1939.

Sin Wen Pao (Evening Edition) of August 3 published the
following comment :-

Concern Over Rising Price of Rice

According to Press reports yesterday, the
price of rice in Shanghai has increased and has exceeded
the limit of $14 per picul and there is every tendency
that the price will still rise. This is a matter that
should be given careful attention.
It will be recalled that a serious shortage
of rice occurred in Shanghai last year after the withdrawal
of the Chinese troops from Shanghai and vicinity. Thanks
to the efforts of the S.M.C. the situation was considerably
relieved and the price of rice was kept stable until
communications with the interior were restored.
Now the price of rice has again passed the
limit of $14 per picul. At a time when the cost of living
is already very high, this increased price of rice will
have serious effects on the livelihood of the poorer
classes of the community.
As the authorities have placed a limit of
$14 on the price of rice, we hope that vigorous measures
will be adopted to enforce observance of this limit so
as to prevent rice merchants from deliberately raising
the price of rice. At the same time, the authorities
should, as quickly as possible, regulate the source of
rice supplies to Shanghai or order large consignments of
foreign rice from abroad to meet local requirements.
Under no circumstances whatever should the authorities
allow the price of rice to be increased beyond $14 per
picul while, on the other hand, rigid measures should be
adopted to deal with those who are hoarding rice in the
hope of making larger profits. If this suggestion is
carried out, it will be possible to stabilize the price
of rice and to avert a panic amongst the general public
through fears of a shortage of rice.
As this is a matter that is closely connected
with the livelihood of the people as well as with the
maintenance of peace and order, the authorities should
pay special attention to this matter.

8月3日出版的《新闻报》（晚报）刊登了如下评论：

关注米价上涨

据昨日新闻报道，上海米价上涨，已超过每担14元的限价，且仍有继续上涨的趋势。此事应予以密切关注。
回想去年中国军队从上海及周边地区撤退后，上海曾发生严重的米荒。得益于工部局（S.M.C.）的努力，局势得到极大缓解，米价保持稳定，直至与内地的交通恢复。
如今米价再次突破每担14元的限价。在生活成本已经很高的情况下，米价上涨将对社会中较贫困阶层的生活产生严重影响。
既然当局已将米价限定为14元，我们希望采取有力措施强制执行这一限价，以防止米商故意抬高米价。同时，当局应尽快规范上海的米源供应，或从国外订购大批洋米以满足本地需求。无论如何，当局都不应允许米价超过每担14元，另一方面，应采取严厉措施打击那些囤积居奇、企图牟取暴利的奸商。如果采纳此建议，就能稳定米价，避免公众因担心缺粮而引发恐慌。
鉴于此事与民生及维持治安秩序密切相关，当局应特别重视此事。

February 15, 1940. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Shun Pao, National
Herald, Central China Daily News :-

INCREASE IN PRICES OF RICE AND FLOUR : SETTLEMENT
AUTHORITIES TO TAKE ACTION

After the rice market re-opened for business on
February 13, the price of rice was increased by $6 or $7
as compared with that before the China New Year holidays.
Yesterday, the price of foreign rice was further increased
by $2 and the highest sale price was $50 per "zar" and the
lowest $47.60. The price is $10 over the price limit on
Chinese rice. (In reality, the price is $16 over the usual
price.) This has broken all previous records. It is
reported that the best broken rice was sold at $40 per "zar",
an increase of $2. Very few transactions were done yesterday.
The Settlement authorities did not place a
price limit on the price of foreign rice when the price
limit on Chinese rice was laid down due to the foreign
exchange. This gave a chance to unscrupulous merchants to
speculate and raise the price of foreign rice. It will be
noted that the foreign rice now on sale arrived in Shanghai
before the time of the price limit placed on Chinese rice
(at that time, the foreign rice was sold at $34 per "zar").
At the request of the general public, the Settlement
authorities have attached much importance to the situation
and are studying measures to deal with the matter. If
necessary, more effective measures will be adopted.
However, the residents hope that the Settlement authorities
will organize a Price Readjustment Committee to discuss
the prices of all daily necessities so as to prevent the
activities of unscrupulous merchants:
On February 14, flour was privately sold at
$13.50, an increase of $2.50. Such an increase broke all
previous records. The prices of wheat and beans are also
on the increase.
Local poor people were much benefitted by the
cheap sale of rice managed by the Rice Cheap Sale Committee.
The cheap sale was suspended over China New Year.
In an interview with our reporter yesterday,
Mr.Yang (楊), secretary of the Rice Cheap Sale Committee,
made the following statement :- "After the Committee
began to raise funds, people in various walks of life made
ample contributions. In view of the sharp increase in
the price of rice for the past few days, members of the
Committee have decided to hold a general meeting some time
this week to discuss matters regarding the continuance
of the cheap sale of rice. The report to the effect
that the Committee will resume cheap sale of rice as from
February 23 is untrue for the date will have to be decided
upon by the Committee meeting and arrangements will have to
be made with the Rice Shop Owners' Guild. At all events,
the cheap sale of rice will be resumed in the near future."

《中美日报》、《大美晚报》、《申报》、《国民新闻》、《华中日报》：

米面价格上涨：租界当局拟采取行动

2月13日米市复市后，米价较春节假期前上涨了6至7元。昨日，洋米价格又上涨2元，最高售价为每“扎”（zar）50元，最低为47.60元。该价格比华米限价高出10元。（实际上，该价格比平常价格高出16元。）这打破了以往的所有记录。据报道，最好的碎米以每“扎”40元售出，上涨2元。昨日成交量极少。
当初制定华米限价时，由于外汇原因，租界当局并未对洋米价格设定限制。这给不法商人提供了投机并抬高洋米价格的机会。值得注意的是，目前上市的洋米是在对华米实施限价之前运抵上海的（当时洋米售价为每“扎”34元）。
应公众要求，租界当局高度重视这一情况，正在研究应对措施。如有必要，将采取更有效的措施。然而，居民希望租界当局组织一个价格调整委员会，讨论所有日常必需品的价格，以防止不法商人的活动：
2月14日，面粉私下售价为13.50元，上涨2.50元。这种涨幅打破了以往的所有记录。小麦和豆类的价格也在上涨。
本地贫民从米价平抑委员会管理的廉价售米活动中受益良多。廉价售米活动在春节期间暂停。
杨先生（楊），米价平抑委员会秘书，昨日在接受本报记者采访时发表如下声明：“委员会开始筹款后，各界人士慷慨捐助。鉴于近日米价急剧上涨，委员会成员决定本周内召开全体会议，讨论有关继续廉价售米的事宜。关于委员会将从2月23日起恢复廉价售米的报道不实，具体日期需由委员会会议决定，并需与米业公会作出安排。无论如何，廉价售米将在不久的将来恢复。”

February 15, 1940.                                  Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News (brief comment) :-

Increased Prices of Rice and Coal.

Every morning and evening, hundreds of people
are to be seen waiting on the roadside of Avenue Edward VII
for the distribution of cooked rice. During the past
two days, the prices of rice and coal briquettes increased
considerably. The price of rice is over $50 per "zar",
while that of coal briquettes is over $6 per hundred catties.
In consequence of this, the number of people who die of
hunger will increase day by day.
It is learned that last year rice and coal
briquette merchants did very good business. A certain
coal concern made a profit of some $17,000,000. This is
inhuman and we do not desire to give them any further
advice.
It is to be hoped that the administrative
authorities will make a strict investigation into undesirables
who endanger the existence of the residents and will punish
them accordingly. The public should from time to time
disclose the activities of these people. In this way,
millions of poor people may have some little hope of
existence.

1940年2月15日。                                  晨间译稿。

《中美日报》（简评）：

米价与煤价上涨。

每天早晚，可见数百人在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）路边等待分发熟饭。过去两天，米价和煤球价格大幅上涨。米价超过每“扎”50元，而煤球价格超过每百斤6元。因此，饿死的人数将日益增加。
据悉，去年米商和煤球商生意兴隆。某煤炭公司获利约17,000,000元。这是不人道的，我们不想再给他们任何建议。
希望行政当局对危害居民生存的不法分子进行严格调查，并依法惩处。公众应不时揭露这些人的活动。这样，数百万穷人或许能有一线生机。

CHINA PRESS

JAN 1 7 1940

Flour And Wheat

The price of native flour continued
high yesterday, registering a gain of $0.20,
as compared with the previous close. On
account of high costs of raw materials,
the mills restricted their sales to outport
dealers. Reacting to brisk demand from
South Sea and North China traders, the
unofficial rate thus soon advanced to
$10.70 quoted for native products while
foreign flour was sold at $10.85, and Jap-
anese flour at 10.50 per bag.
Trading in native wheat came to a
stand-still yesterday when the price reach-
ed the new high of $18 per bag. Dealers,
therefore, were unwilling to transact busi-
ness with the exception of Swatow traders,
who bought six carloads of Soochow and
Wusih wheat at the high rate.

面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉价格持续高企，较前一收盘价上涨0.20元。由于原材料成本高昂，磨坊限制向埠外交易商销售。受南洋和华北交易商强劲需求的推动非官方汇率很快升至国产产品报价10.70元，而洋面粉售价为每袋10.85元，日本面粉为10.50元。
昨日国产小麦交易陷入停滞，价格达到每袋18元的新高点。因此，除汕头交易商以高价购买了六车皮苏州和无锡小麦外，其他交易商不愿进行交易。

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :- 16.12.39 (AM)

RICE STOCKS IN WUSIH

At a meeting held by the Rice Price Adjustment
Committee at the Magistrate's Office at Wuish at 2 p.m.
December 11, it was resolved to make an investigation into
rice stocks in the Hsien and to prevent rice from being
transported outside Wusih Hsien so that the food supplies
of the people may be preserved.

无锡米粮库存

12月11日下午2时，在无锡县公署举行的米价调整委员会会议上，决议对全县米粮库存进行调查，并禁止大米运出无锡县境，以保障民众食粮供应。

page_data.en:
DEC 16 1939
Rice Market

Although only 1,600 bags of white rice arrived yesterday, the rates declined on slack demand. Reacting to the rice riots during the last three days, wholesale merchants were reluctant to replenish their stocks, and local dealers bought only fractionally. As a result, the prices receded $1.00 with the exception of the rate of first grade Changshu rice which remained unchanged at $44.0 per picul. The day's turnover was estimated at 3,000 bags of various qualities.

Dull conditions prevailed on the market for foreign rice yesterday. The wholesale operators were unwilling to take up foreign cereals, while selling offers from rice holders coupled with the arrival of another 10,000 bags served to dampen sentiment. As supplies thus exceeded demand, the rate of Saigon rice dropped $1.40, while a total of about 2,000 bags was traded in.

Changshu               $44.00
Changchow              $42.00
Kunshan                $41.50
Kooli                  $38.50
Wusih "sharp"          $38.00
Kiangpeh "sharp"       $33.50
Saigon                 $35.00

Flour And Wheat

Following the restrictions of sales by the mills, only slight business in native flour was witnessed yesterday. Local buyers absorbed second grade product at $8.70 in cash per bag, while North China and South Sea traders were not in the market because of the high rates. The price of the "Fishman" brand moved up $9.00 quoted to outport dealers. Concerning the business on the outside market no reports were received during the day.

Selling offers arrested the upward trend of the rates of native wheat yesterday and the quotations remained unchanged throughout the day. The Foh Sing flour mill bought 8,000 bags of various kinds of native wheat, and the Fou Foong mill 8,000 bags, while local buyers took up two carloads.

page_data.zh:
1939年12月16日
米市

尽管昨日仅到埠白米1,600包，但因需求疲软，行情下跌。受近三日米骚动影响，批发商不愿补进存货，本地商贩亦仅零星购买。结果，除一等常熟米价格维持在每担44.0元不变外，其余米价均下跌1.00元。当日成交量估计为各种等级大米共3,000包。

昨日洋米市场气氛沉闷。批发商不愿购进洋米，而持米者抛售，加之另有10,000包到埠，致使市场情绪低落。由于供过于求，西贡米价格下跌1.40元，总成交量约为2,000包。

面粉与小麦

继各面粉厂限制销售之后，昨日国产面粉交易清淡。本地买家以每包现金8.70元的价格吸纳二等面粉，而华北及南洋客商因价格高昂未入市。“渔人”牌面粉报价向外地经销商上调9.00元。关于外盘交易情况，当日未收到报告。

昨日卖盘遏制了国产小麦价格的上涨趋势，全天报价保持不变。福新面粉厂购入各种国产小麦8,000包，阜丰面粉厂购入8,000包，本地买家则购进两车皮。

page_data.en:
December 11, 1939.
Morning Translation

FOREIGN MUNICIPAL COUNCILS TAKE ACTION AGAINST
RICE PROFITEERING AND HOARDING

The "Chinese-American Daily News," "Sin
Wan Pao," "Shun Pao," "National Herald," "Ta Mei Pao,"
"Hwa Pao," "Circulation Daily News" and "Central China
Daily News" reproduce the joint proclamation issued by
the Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal
Council on December 10 warning against rice hoarding and
profiteering.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun
Pao, National Herald, Hwa Pao, Circulation Daily News :-

Purchase of Foreign Rice

At a meeting held on December 9 the Bean
and Rice Trade Guild decided to write to the authorities
of the two Settlements, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
and Mr. Yu Ya Ching requesting them to purchase foreign
rice for sale at a cheap price.
According to information secured by our
reporter, this suggestion has received the support of
the authorities and other influential bodies and
individuals and a meeting of various public bodies will
be called in a few days to discuss the purchase of
foreign rice.

Negotiations With Japanese Authorities

Local rice dealers have requested the
Settlement authorities to open negotiations with the
Japanese authorities in conjunction with the Consular
Body for permission to rice merchants to transport rice
freely and to reduce the taxes on rice. This action
is necessary because unscrupulous rice merchants are
in the habit of taking advantage of the frequent
Japanese interference with rice supplies to Shanghai
to raise the price of rice, thereby placing the rice
market in a state of great confusion.
On December 9 the Japanese authorities
prohibited a quantity of rice, wheat and cereals, which
were transported by train to Shanghai, from being
removed into the Foreign Settlements. They have
also posted up the following notice at the North Railway
Station:- "In future when rice arrives in Shanghai,
whether by train or by boat, the owner must call at
North Szechuen Road (?) for registration. He is not
allowed to remove the rice into the Foreign Settlements
until he has secured permission to do so, otherwise he
will only be permitted to dispose of the rice in Hongkew."
The Bean and Rice Trade Guild has
resolved to request the authorities of the two Settlements
to take the following steps :-
(1) To endeavour immediately to
facilitate the transportation of Chinese rice to
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月11日。
晨间译稿

外国市政当局采取行动打击米商囤积居奇及牟取暴利

《中美日报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民新闻》、《大美晚报》、《华报》、《循环日报》及《华中日报》均转载了上海公共租界工部局与法租界公董局于12月10日联合发布的公告，警告不得囤积大米及牟取暴利。

《中美日报》、《大美晚报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民新闻》、《华报》、《循环日报》：-

购买洋米

豆米业同业公会于12月9日召开会议，决定致函两租界当局、上海总商会及虞洽卿先生，请求他们购买洋米并以低价出售。
据本报记者获悉的消息，此建议已得到当局及其他有影响力的团体和个人的支持，数日内将召集各公共团体开会讨论购买洋米事宜。

与日本当局交涉

本地米商请求租界当局会同领事团与日本当局进行谈判，允许米商自由运输大米并降低米税。此举实属必要，因为不法米商惯于利用日本频繁干扰上海大米供应之机抬高米价，致使米市陷入极大混乱。
12月9日，日本当局禁止一批经火车运抵上海的大米、小麦及谷物进入外国租界。他们还在北站张贴了如下告示：“今后凡有大米经火车或轮船运抵上海，货主必须前往北四川路(?)登记。在未获准之前，不得将大米移入外国租界，否则只准在虹口地区处置该批大米。”
豆米业同业公会已决议请求两租界当局采取以下步骤：
(1) 立即设法便利中国大米运抵上海。

page_data.en:
December 11, 1939. Morning Translation

(2) To call a meeting of various public bodies
to discuss the purchase of foreign rice.
(3) To make arrangements to secure "transportation permits" for 50,000 to 100,000 bags of Wuhu "See Mee" so as to enable the rice dealers to make purchases and arrange for transportation.

Influential Bodies Ask Foreign Councils To Take Action

Recently, owing to the big increase in the price of rice, an emergency meeting was held by the Bean and Rice Trade Guild, at which it was resolved to comply with the instructions of the S.M.C. and to place a temporary limit on the price of "Kan Mee" at $45 per picul as the highest and that of "See Mee" at $38. However, the opinion of the general public is that this limit is still too high for the ordinary class of people who depend upon their small monthly earnings for their livelihood for this restriction would fail to put a check on the activities of rice hoarders. Consequently, it is to be hoped that the authorities of the Foreign Settlements as well as the rice trading circles will take into consideration the hardships of the people and fix a lower limit for the price of rice so as to check manipulation and hoarding by speculators, thereby preserving the prosperity and peace and order of the Settlements.

It is sincerely hoped that the authorities of the Foreign Settlements will give favourable consideration to the views of the majority of local residents and reconsider the price limit.

Recently the Shanghai First Special District Citizens' Federation wrote to the Municipal authorities asking them to devise ways and means to protect the food supplies of the people.

A joint petition has now been sent to the authorities by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Native Bankers' Guild, the Bar Association, the Chartered Accountants' Association, the Thrift Committee and various other local public bodies asking them to take rigorous suppressive measures against manipulation of rice markets and to adopt immediate and effective measures to curtail the price of rice so as to preserve the supply of food-stuffs.

Many People Leaving Shanghai Owing to High Cost Of Living

The question of future food supplies for the people has been a serious one ever since the heavy rise in the price of rice. At present the authorities are endeavouring to suppress rice speculation and to punish unscrupulous rice merchants. However, according to a census recently taken by the authorities of the two Settlements, about 13,000 persons left Shanghai during the last week and this is an ample proof that the public are unable to maintain their living under the highly increased cost of commodities.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月11日。晨间译稿

(2) 召集各公共团体开会讨论购买洋米事宜。
(3) 安排获取50,000至100,000包芜湖“细米”的“运输许可证”，以便米商进行采购并安排运输。

有影响力团体要求外国市政当局采取行动

近期，由于米价大幅上涨，豆米业同业公会召开紧急会议，决议遵行上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）的指示，暂时限定“粳米”最高价格为每担45元，“细米”为每担38元。然而，公众舆论认为，对于依靠微薄月薪维持生计的普通民众而言，此限价仍然过高，且此限制未能有效遏制囤米者的活动。因此，希望外国租界当局及米业界能体恤民众疾苦，制定更低的米价上限，以遏制投机商的操纵和囤积行为，从而维护租界的繁荣与和平秩序。

诚望外国租界当局能充分考虑当地大多数居民的意见，重新审议价格上限。

近期，上海第一特区市民联合会致函市政当局，要求其设法保护民众食粮供应。

目前，上海总商会、钱业公会、律师公会、会计师公会、节约委员会及各地方公共团体已联合向当局呈递请愿书，要求对操纵米市的行为采取严厉的压制措施，并采取即时有效的措施压低米价，以保障食品供应。

许多人因生活成本高企而离开上海

自米价大幅上涨以来，民众未来的粮食供应问题一直十分严峻。目前当局正努力打击大米投机并惩罚不法米商。然而，根据两租界当局最近进行的人口统计，上周约有13,000人离开上海，这充分证明在商品价格高度上涨的情况下，公众已难以维持生计。

page_data.en:
December 11, 1939. Morning Translation

It is to be anticipated that a number of
people living in the two Settlements, who are unable to
maintain their living due to increases in prices of
commodities, are likely to become desperate and resort
to acts of violence, as witness the frequent occurrence
of robberies lately. The situation will become more
aggravated should the unscrupulous rice merchants
continue their profiteering activities.

Ta Mei Pao (Comment) :-

The High Price of Rice

Recently, we published an article in which
we expressed our hope that the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements would take into consideration the maintenance
of peace and order in their respective districts and
adopt immediately suppressive measures against activities
of hoarding and manipulation by the rice merchants. Later
we read in the newspapers an order issued by the S.M.C.
instructing its Legal Department to devise ways and means
in conjunction with the Shanghai First Special District
Court for strict suppression of such activities. This
proves that the authorities are now adopting a wise stand
and giving support to the poor residents in their
hardships.

However, the rice merchants do not take this
action of the authorities seriously; they seem to be of
the opinion that the most the authorities will do is to
make an investigation to be followed by a warning or by
a compulsory order for disposal. They are of the
opinion that they can still make handsome profits if
they get some strong supporters at their back.

Consequently we hope that our Government
authorities will likewise take some action against these
traitorous merchants. Though there exist in Shanghai
many extraordinary circumstances, the city is still part
and parcel of Chinese territory and the residents here
are still Chinese. An order has now been issued by
the Military Affairs Commission of the National Government
calling for severe punishment of traitorous merchants in
Shanghai for manipulation of prices of commodities. It
emphasizes that whoever is ascertained by concrete proof
to have been engaged in such activities will be dealt
with as having committed the offence of disturbing the
financial market and manipulating food provisions during
the time of the war of resistance and will be executed.
In spite of this, the price of rice has marked a further
increase to as high as $48 per picul. Whereas we regret
that the rice merchants could have been so heartless, we
certainly admire their bravery.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月11日。晨间译稿

可以预见，居住在两租界内的一些人因商品价格上涨而无法维持生计，可能会铤而走险，诉诸暴力行为，正如近期抢劫案频发所见证的那样。若不法米商继续其牟取暴利的活动，局势将更加恶化。

《大美晚报》（评论）：-

米价高昂

近日，本刊发表文章，表达了我方希望外国租界当局考虑到各自辖区内的治安维护，立即对米商囤积和操纵活动采取压制措施。随后，我们在报上看到上海公共租界工部局发布命令，指示其法务处与上海第一特区法院合作，制定严厉镇压此类活动的方法。这证明当局目前采取了明智的立场，并在困境中支持贫困居民。

然而，米商并未认真看待当局的这一行动；他们似乎认为当局最多只会进行调查，随后发出警告或强制处理令。他们认为，如果有强有力的后台支持，仍可获得丰厚利润。

因此，我们希望我国政府当局也能对这些奸商采取行动。尽管上海存在许多特殊情况，但该市仍是中国领土不可分割的一部分，此处居民仍是中国人。国民政府军事委员会现已发布命令，要求严惩上海操纵商品价格的奸商。命令强调，凡有确凿证据证实从事此类活动者，将被视为在抗战期间犯有扰乱金融市场及操纵军需民食罪，并处死刑。尽管如此，米价仍进一步上涨至每担高达48元。虽然我们遗憾米商如此狠心，但我们确实佩服他们的“勇气”。

page_data.en:
December 11, 1939.
Morning Translation

National Herald (Comment) :-

Increase in the Cost of Commodities

The prices of daily necessities in Shanghai have reached an all-time high. The rent of a room above a kitchen which used to be $6 a month is now more than $30, while the price of rice which used to be about $12 per picul has risen to over $45. The prices of all other commodities have increased from 400% to 500%. The poorer people can hardly maintain their living.

People are drawing the same pay as before. Exchange shops demand the payment of 50 cents for the exchange of a $10 or $5 banknote. The exchange of a $1 banknote or a 50-cent note costs 5 cents at the exchange shops. This is another charge on the income of residents.

The prices of commodities are abnormal, while the local financial situation is in confusion; this is a fatal blow to the poor people. Unfortunate incidents will naturally arise should this abnormal situation be allowed to go on.

Taking advantage of this unusual situation, the Japanese spread propaganda to the effect that it is the natural consequence of China's war of resistance, while those in favour of compromise will say that it is time for a compromise between China and Japan. The Japanese may also say: "Neither Britain nor France is in a position to maintain the position of the Foreign Settlements and everything should be handed over to Japan." People in favour of compromise will then say: "The Foreign Settlements belong to China and should immediately be handed over to the City Government."

Residents in Shanghai will realize from the following that it is the "friendly nation" that has created the present abnormal situation :-
(1) The high increase of the house rent in the Foreign Settlements is due to the fact that people cannot live in Japanese occupied areas and also that people who used to live in the fallen districts now collect in Shanghai.

"(2) The price of rice is going up rapidly because of detention of rice and grain by the Japanese soldiers in occupied areas and of the transportation of rice to Japan.

(3) The establishment of Customs sub-stations in occupied areas and the blockade of harbours by the Japanese forces are responsible for the sharp increase in the cost of all commodities.

It is known to the public that the Japanese collection of brass and nickel coins and $1 banknotes has resulted in the confusion of the local financial situation. In a word, all this extraordinary situation in Shanghai was created by the Japanese and those in favour of compromise as a "gift" to the 4,500,000 residents.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月11日。
晨间译件

《国民新闻》（评论）：-

商品价格上涨

上海的生活必需品价格已创下历史新高。过去每月租金为6元的灶披间，现在已超过30元；而过去每石约12元的大米，现已涨至45元以上。所有其他商品的价格均上涨了400%至500%。贫苦民众几乎难以维持生计。

人们的薪水仍与从前相同。兑换店要求兑换10元或5元纸币时支付5角手续费。在兑换店兑换1元纸币或5角纸币需花费5分。这是对居民收入的又一重盘剥。

物价异常，本地金融局势混乱，这对贫苦百姓来说是致命打击。如果任由这种异常状况持续下去，不幸事件自然会发生。

日本人利用这一不寻常局势散布宣传，称这是中国抗战的自然后果，而主张妥协的人则会说，现在是中日妥协的时候了。日本人还可能说：“英国和法国都无力维持外国租界的地位，一切应移交给日本。”主张妥协的人随后会说：“外国租界属于中国，应立即移交给市政府。”

上海居民将从以下事实中认识到，正是“友邦”造成了目前的异常局面：
(1) 外国租界房租大幅上涨，是因为人们无法在日军占领区生活，以及原先居住在沦陷区的人们现在聚集于上海。

“(2) 由于日军在占领区扣留稻米粮食并将大米运往日本，米价迅速上涨。

(3) 日军在占领区设立海关分卡并封锁港口，导致所有商品价格急剧上涨。

公众皆知，日本人收集铜镍硬币和1元纸币，导致了本地金融局势的混乱。总之，上海所有这些异常状况都是日本人和主张妥协者送给450万居民的“礼物”。

page_data.en:
December 11, 1939.
Morning Translation

There are certain evildoers among the residents
of Shanghai, who are engaged in speculation and manipulation;
they are supporters of Japan and people favouring compromise.
Of course, it depends upon the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements to deal with this class of people, but the
residents should assist the Settlement authorities in this
respect.
We hope that employers who have a conscience
and who love their country will grant an increase of wages
to their employees according to the circumstances.

Chinese-American Daily News (comment) :-

The price of rice has now reached an
unprecedented figure, while the price of cakes and fried
flour fritters has risen to three cents per piece.
Those who are already unable to live on rice will now
have to satisfy their hunger with the north-westerly wind.
The end of the year is fast approaching and peace and
order in this isolated city of Shanghai is already being
constantly menaced.
Yesterday an order was issued jointly by the
authorities of the two Foreign Settlements warning against
manipulation of the rice market by traitorous rice
merchants. Although such a step should have been taken
earlier, it is welcomed with satisfaction by the public.
As a matter of fact, the only way to check the activities
of traitorous merchants who care nothing but for their
own pockets is to apply the law against them.
The authorities of the Foreign Settlements
have worked strenuously to suppress terroristic
activities. Whereas the activities of terrorists are
aimed at a handful of persons only, the machinations of
rice profiteers are liable to give rise to a serious
situation for they menace the livelihood of the entire
population. Therefore, their activities are a hundred
times more grave than the acts of terrorists.
We hope that the public will immediately
inform the authorities of any case of rice hoarding or
profiteering that comes to their knowledge. Upon
receipt of such information the authorities should
start an immediate investigation with a view to bringing
about the exposure of the culprits who should be
punished. Only by such measures can the situation be
ameliorated and public indignation be appeased.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月11日。
晨间译件

上海居民中有一些败类，从事投机倒把和操纵市场；他们是日本的支持者和主张妥协的人。当然，如何处理这类人取决于外国租界当局，但居民应在这一方面协助租界当局。
我们希望有良知且爱国的雇主根据情况给雇员增加工资。

《中美日报》（评论）：-

米价现已达到前所未有的水平，而糕点和油墩儿的价格已涨至每件三分。那些已经无法靠米饭果腹的人，现在只能喝西北风充饥。年终将至，这座孤岛上海的和平与秩序正不断受到威胁。
昨日，两个外国租界当局联合发布命令，警告奸商不得操纵米市。虽然这一步骤本应更早采取，但公众对此表示欢迎。事实上，遏制那些只顾自己腰包、不顾其他的奸商活动的唯一途径，就是依法惩处他们。
外国租界当局一直在努力镇压恐怖活动。然而，恐怖分子的活动仅针对少数人，而米贩子的阴谋却可能引发严重局势，因为他们威胁到全体居民的生计。因此，他们的活动比恐怖分子的行径严重百倍。
我们希望公众一旦获悉任何囤积居奇或哄抬米价的案件，立即向当局举报。当局收到此类信息后，应立即展开调查，以揭露罪犯并予以惩处。只有采取此类措施，才能改善局势，平息公愤。

INCREASE IN THE PRICE OF RICE

In view of the continued increase in the
price of rice, the Bean and Rice Trade Guild held a
meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday at its office, No. 15 Avenue
Edward VII, to discuss measures to remedy the situation.
Ying Ts-kong (邢志剛) was in the chair.
The following resolutions were discussed and
passed :-
(1) That the opinion of the S.M.C. be accepted and that
as a temporary measure, the price of best quality
rice be not more than $45 per "zar" and the price
of foreign rice and "See Mee" be not more than $38
per "zar". A circular notice will be issued to
enforce the above limited prices of rice as from
December 10 and the Control Committee will see that
the merchants carry on their business accordingly.
The Settlement authorities will be requested to deal
with any merchant who violates the order.
(2) That delivery of Chinese rice or foreign rice or
"See Mee" must be made within three days. Violators
will be severely punished.
(3) That the general public be requested to do their
best to disclose unscrupulous rice manipulators and
hoarders and to request the authorities to punish
them.
(4) Yesterday, rice, grain and provisions arriving here
by trains were prohibited from being transported
into the Foreign Settlements.
That the Settlement authorities be requested to
remedy the situation in order to relieve the distress
of the general public; that as the price of rice at
Wuhu is about $15 per "zar", the Settlement authorities
be requested to apply for certificates for the
transportation of 50,000 to 100,000 bags of "See
Mee" from Wuhu to Shanghai; that the price of this
rice be fixed by the Settlement authorities.
(5) That a suggestion be made that the Settlement
authorities, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce and
Mr. Yu Ya-ching hold a meeting of public bodies
to discuss orders of foreign rice so as to increase
the sources of supply; that the Chamber of Commerce
notify bankers to give loans to those desirous of
ordering Chinese or foreign rice.
(6) That the Chamber of Commerce and Mr. Yu Ya-ching
be requested, as in the previous case, to petition
the Ministry of Finance at Chungking to allow an
order of 50,000 bags of foreign rice at the
Government rate of exchange so as to enable a cheap
sale of rice.

In view of the fact that the continued
increase in the price of rice is liable to menace peace
and order in the Settlement, Mr. T.K. Ho, Deputy
Secretary of the S.M.C., at 1 p.m. yesterday summoned

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
275911
DEC 9 1939

New Record Price
Quoted for Rice
Grain Reaches $46 A Zan
On Local Market ; Permits
Withheld by Japanese

Rice for the bowls of China in Shanghai reached the new high mark of $46.50 per "zah" in the local Rice Market yesterday despite an ample stock of both the regional grain and the Saigon importation. The soaring of the price caused a general feeling of anxiety among the Chinese population, and special measures were being discussed last night to deal with the problem.

In some cases the rate was quoted at $48 per "zah," it was reported from the Rice Market, whose Control Committee hurriedly called a meeting to apply whatever internal remedy was available. Chinese circles believed, however, that only some degree of official control could avert an aggravation of the situation.

The "North-China Daily News" learned last night that a special meeting of the Food and Fuel Supply Committee of the Shanghai Municipal Council had been called for next Monday to discuss the emergency. This Committee would be in a position to recommend to the Council any remedial measures thought appropriate at this time. It may be recalled that the S.M.C. and the French Municipal Administration last July approved the following warning to be posted in the Rice Market:

"After consultation between the Rice Guilds and the Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal Administration, the price, until further notice, of first-grade rice is not to exceed $20 per zah, and the price of See Mee is not to exceed $16 per zah.

"Any prices over and above these prices will not be recognized by the Guilds and should be reported to the Police." ("Municipal Gazette," July 21, 1939.)

Japanese Hold up Rice

Investigation by the "North-China Daily News" revealed last night that some 600 bags of rice destined for the Shanghai market had been held up by the Japanese authorities on the Soochow Creek in the vicinity of the former Government Mint for more than two days. This rice is in boats, ready for entrance into the local market.

It is further learned that since the first of this month the Japanese military have withheld all permits for the entry of rice from the hinterland via the important shipping centres of Quinsan, Wuhu and Sungkiang. The shipment now stopped on the Soochow Creek is rice for which a permit was issued before December, it is learned.

Tension reigned in the Shanghai Rice Market yesterday for as soon as it was opened the price of $46 was called. Seeing that the problem must be tackled quickly, the control committee held a meeting at noon at which it was decided that actual cargo must be delivered in three days and not 10 days in all transactions held in the market. It was hoped that this decision would discourage manipulation by unscrupulous merchants who may hoard cargo and wait for higher prices. In many cases, it was learned, disputes took place between sellers and buyers when goods were not delivered on time.

Rice Merchants Warned

An announcement was issued by the committee after the meeting warning all rice merchants against violating the new rule, explaining that the former 10-day delivery period would only cause more trouble to the already confused market. Those who violate the rule will be punished by the committee. It was stated that no speculation should be allowed and that in all dealings actual rice must be possessed by sellers. Suspension of business was threatened in the announcement should any member of the market be found violating the rule which will go into effect today.

Steady increase of the price of rice surprised all Chinese here as they believed that while the supply had been arriving continuously there should never be such unprecedented upward trend in price. Several days ago, one rice merchant saw the possibility of the price going up to the $50 mark, asserting that when the new crop of rice was arriving the price should not be quoted at $40 the price then prevailing in the market. Before the rice increases started many months ago the normal price fluctuated around $13 per picul.

It was authoritatively learned yesterday that an assistant Municipal Advocate of the Shanghai Municipal Council had conferred, in a private capacity, with judges of the First Special District Court for the purpose of devising some methods of dealing with those who are manipulating the rice market.

The Chinese and foreign press in Shanghai have unanimously expressed the opinion that official quarters should do something before it is too late. In addition to the increase registered in the rice market, prices of other commodities in every-day use have gone up during the past few days causing extreme concern to the majority of people here.

"Shoot the Profiteers!"

General Ku Tsu-lung, a route army commander who is directing operations of the Chungking forces in Chekiang, has been ordered by General Chiang Kai-shek to investigate the price increase "racket" in Shanghai and to shoot those merchants who co-operate with the Japanese in manipulating markets, according to a Chungking message published by a Chinese evening paper here last night. All organizations having relations with the Military Affairs Council were said to have received the order.

（手写签名：Ku Tzu Lung）

《字林西报》。
275911
1939年12月9日

米价创纪录新高
谷物在本地市场
达到每石46美元；
许可证被日方扣留

尽管地区存粮及西贡进口米货源充足，上海本地米市的米价昨日仍创下每“石”46.50美元的新高。价格的飙升在中国民众中引起了普遍的焦虑情绪，昨晚各方正在讨论采取特别措施以应对这一问题。

据米市报告，在某些情况下报价高达每“石”48美元，米市管制委员会为此紧急召开会议，试图采取一切可行的内部补救措施。然而，华人界认为，只有某种程度的官方管控才能避免局势恶化。

《字林西报》昨晚获悉，上海公共租界工部局粮食燃料供应委员会已定于下周一召开特别会议，讨论这一紧急情况。该委员会将有权向工部局推荐其认为此时适当的任何补救措施。人们或许还记得，去年七月，工部局与法公董局批准在米市张贴如下警告：

“经米业公会与上海公共租界工部局及法公董局协商，一等米价格在另行通知前不得超过每石20美元，‘See Mee’（音译）米价格不得超过每石16美元。

“任何高于上述价格的价格均不被公会承认，并应向警方举报。”（《市政公报》，1939年7月21日。）

日方扣留大米

《字林西报》昨晚的调查显示，约600袋 destined for 上海市场的大米已被日本当局在靠近前政府造币厂的苏州河段扣留了两天多。这些大米装在船上，准备进入本地市场。

另悉，自本月一日起，日军已扣留所有经由昆山、芜湖和松江等重要航运中心从内地进入的大米许可证。据悉，目前在苏州河被截停的这批大米，其许可证是在十二月之前签发的。

昨日上海米市气氛紧张，开市伊始便喊出46美元的价格。鉴于必须迅速解决这一问题，管制委员会于中午举行会议，决定市场上所有交易的实物货物必须在三天内交付，而非原来的十天。希望这一决定能遏制不法商人囤积居奇、待价而沽的操纵行为。据了解，在许多情况下，因货物未能按时交付，买卖双方发生了纠纷。

警告米商

会后，委员会发布公告，警告所有米商不得违反新规，解释说原有的十天交货期只会给已经混乱的市场带来更多麻烦。违者将受到委员会的处罚。声明指出，不允许进行投机，所有交易中卖方必须持有实物大米。公告威胁称，若发现市场任何成员违反将于今日生效的规定，将对其处以停业惩罚。

米价的持续上涨令在沪所有华人感到惊讶，因为他们认为，既然供应源源不断，价格就不应出现如此前所未有的上涨趋势。几天前，一名米商看到价格可能涨至50美元大关，断言当新米上市时，价格不应像当时市场 prevailing 的那样报出40美元。在数月前提价开始之前，正常价格在每担13美元左右波动。

昨日有权威消息人士透露，上海公共租界工部局的一名助理公诉人以私人身份与第一特区地方法院的法官进行了会晤，旨在 devising 一些应对操纵米市者的方法。

上海的中外报刊一致表示，官方机构应在为时过晚之前采取行动。除了米市记录到的价格上涨外，过去几天其他日常用品的价格也上涨，引起了此地大多数人的极大担忧。

“枪毙奸商！”

据本地一家中文晚报昨晚刊登的重庆消息，蒋介石将军已命令指挥浙江战区重庆部队作战的陆军将领顾祝同（Ku Tsu-lung，音译）调查上海的涨价“骗局”，并枪决那些与日本人勾结操纵市场的商人。据说，所有与军事委员会有关联的组织都收到了这一命令。

（手写签名：Ku Tzu Lung）

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
1939

Rice Of Shanghai
Taken By Nippon
Shipment To Homeland
In Full Swing;
Prices Rise

"Of course there's profiteering in rice, if you can call taking a profit on what you have bought for sale such. There's profiteering in any business." This is what the Shanghai Evening Post was told today, when making inquiries into the rice situation, and Chinese allegations that a huge holdup by speculators is responsible for the present high prices.

"If Chinese merchants hadn't been determined to do business, and ventured their capital on purchasing rice despite the terrific handicaps imposed by Japanese occupation of the hinterland, but had sat instead with their hands folded, there wouldn't be any rice in Shanghai, and we'd all be starving. It's a normal thing to buy stocks of rice when the crop is in, for sale later. If a merchant who has put out capital for stocks later has to take a kick in the pants and sell at a loss, nobody weeps for him"

In Full Swing
With the Japanese program of exporting China's rice to their homeland now in full swing, arrivals of the grain in Shanghai have almost entirely halted, with the result that prices have crept up, while at the same time the price of the imported Saigon grain have also risen, Evenpost was told. Prices have reached the level of $45 a zah for domestic grain, while Saigon rice is still selling at cheaper than this, around $42 This despite a ten percent increase in the price of rice in Saigon and a ten percent drop in exchange, making a difference of roughly 20 percent higher cost for Shanghai sales.

Crop Interval
Japan is buying 300,000 tons of Saigon rice, and has now completed about one-third of this program. In addition, India is also buying from Saigon. This explains part of the higher cost in the Indo-China port, where the old crop is now finishing.

From the end of this to the beginning of the new crop there will be an interval of four weeks, and it will not be until February that the new Saigon crop will be in fit condition for export.

Japanese System
As already pointed out by Eve-post, the Japanese are purchasing rice in the interior at their own prices, and paying for it in their own notes, for export to Japan, where the rice crop has been a great failure, and for feeding the Nipponese troops in China.

As an example of the way the Japanese have been running things in the countryside, a monopoly has been set up in the Sungkiang area, the most important source of rice supply to Shanghai.

"Unauthorized"
Operating under the name of the Cheng Kee Company, the Japanese outfit has notified the local rice hongs there that they may not sell any rice to "unauthorized" persons but only to that company. By cornering the stock—buying at the utmost $20 per zah —that firm exports partly to Japan and partly to Shanghai, making fat profits.

The firm obviously has the support of the local Japanese military as the sentries along the Sungkiang highway have been ordered to stop all kinds of rice movements, except those weighing less than half a zah and those coming into Sungkiang. Monopolies of the same kind are said to exist in practically all rice producing centers. All kinds of farm products and cocoons are being controlled in like manner.

日本运走上海大米
运往本土计划
全面展开；
价格上涨

“当然，米业存在牟取暴利，如果你把对买入待售商品赚取利润称为暴利的话。任何行业都存在暴利。”这是《上海晚邮报》今日调查米市情况时得到的答复，针对华人方面指责巨额囤积投机导致当前高价的言论，有人如是说。

“如果中国商人没有决心做生意，没有在日军占领内地造成的巨大障碍下冒险出资购米，而是袖手旁观，那么上海就不会有大米，我们都得挨饿。在收获季节购入米 stock 以备日后出售是正常现象。如果一位出资囤货的商人后来不得不忍气吞声亏本出售，没人会为他流泪。”

全面展开

随着日本将中国大米出口至其本土的计划全面展开，运抵上海的大米几乎完全停止，导致价格攀升，同时进口西贡米的价格也随之上涨，《晚邮报》获悉。国产米价格已达到每石45美元的水平，而西贡米售价仍低于此，约为42美元。尽管西贡米价上涨了百分之十，且汇率下跌了百分之十，使得在上海销售的成本大致高出20%。

作物间隙期

日本正在购买30万吨西贡米，目前已完成该计划的约三分之一。此外，印度也在从西贡购买。这解释了印度支那港口部分成本较高的原因，那里的旧作即将结束。

从本季结束到新作物上市之间将有四周的间隔期，直到二月，新的西贡作物才具备出口条件。

日本体制

正如《晚邮报》此前指出的那样，日本人正以其自定价格在内地购买大米，并用其自己的军票支付，用于出口到日本（那里稻作严重歉收）以及供养在华日军。

以日本人在乡村运作方式为例，在松江地区——上海最重要的米源供应地——建立了一个垄断机构。

“未经授权”

这家日本机构以“成记公司”（Cheng Kee Company，音译）的名义运作，通知当地的米行不得向“未经授权”的人员出售任何大米，只能卖给该公司。通过囤积库存——以最高每石20美元的价格买入——该公司部分出口至日本，部分销往上海，赚取丰厚利润。

该公司显然得到了当地日军的支持，因为松江公路沿线的哨兵已奉命阻止各种大米运输，除非重量小于半石或进入松江的大米。据说，实际上所有大米生产中心都存在类似的垄断。各类农产品和蚕茧也正以同样方式受到控制。

ecember 4, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

National Herald, Sin Wan Pac, Shun Pao, Chinese-American
Daily News, Hwa Pao, Ta Mei Pao :-

FURTHER RISE IN PRICE OF RICE

In recent days the price of rice has risen
again. One "zar" of rice now costs over $40. Rice
speculators are very active in the purchase of rice for
a good profit. At noon yesterday the price of rice
set a new record of $43.50 per "zar". The best quality
cost $44 to $45 while the inferior quality was sold
at $37. According to a provision dealer, the rice in
stock in Shanghai is sufficient to meet any demand of
the market and the local authorities are earnestly
requested to cope with the situation created by the
rice manipulators.
According to information from a reporter
of the Sin Sung News Agency, foreign concerns in this
locality have purchased 300,000 bags of Saigon rice;
120,000 bags are en route to Shanghai by water and
40,000 bags are expected to reach here to-day.
During the course of the next few days, it is further
stated, a substantial quantity of Saigon rice can be
obtained.

1939年12月4日。
下午译文。

《国民新闻》、《新晚报》、《申报》、《中美日报》、《华报》、《大美报》：-

米价进一步上涨

近日米价再次上涨。一“石”米现在价格超过40美元。米业投机者在购米以获取丰厚利润方面非常活跃。昨日中午，米价创下每“石”43.50美元的新纪录。优质米价格为44至45美元，而劣质米售价为37美元。据一位杂粮商称，上海库存大米足以满足市场的任何需求，恳请地方当局认真应对由米市操纵者造成的局面。
据《新声通讯社》记者提供的信息，本地的外国商行已购买30万袋西贡米；其中12万袋正通过水路运往上海，预计另有4万袋将于今日抵达。
报道进一步称，在未来几天内，可以获得大量西贡米。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
DEC 4 1938
Mounting Prices
Stir Chinese
High Levels Predicted for
Chief Foodstuffs ; Official
Action Sought

Lack of official attention is blamed
for the unprecedented economic trou-
bles facing the Shanghai people in a
news article published yesterday in
the commercial section of a leading
Chinese newspaper which asserts that
"difficulties of the Shanghai people
are nobody's business. The uncontrol-
led increase of prices is the subject
of many reports and press comments
and is also the curse in every Chinese
family. Hope is freely expressed
that official quarters should do some-
thing.
Most strongly worded criticisms
have been published by the Chinese
press during the past few days against
the unscrupulous merchants and
manipulators in the market but their
words were not heeded. It is pointed
out that in some cases it is excusable
that prices have been increased but
in most cases the alarming situation
is said to be the result of profiteering
because no control over merchants
has been effected as was done in the
past by the Bureau of Social Affairs.
It is generally admitted that the
changed situation has also caused diffi-
culties that can only be settled by
official quarters as public sanction is
of no use.
A rice merchant interviewed says
that he sees the possibility of the
price of rice soaring to the $50 or
even $60 mark a few months later if
no preventive measures are carried
out now. The price of the grain per
picul now is again fluctuating around
$41. He points out that the serious-
ness of the situation lies in the fact
that this is a time when the good
crop of rice is being sold and foreign
rice is arriving continuously. Un-
restricted hoarding is said to be one
of the chief reasons of the price in-
crease.

Further Increases Anticipated
Prices of flour and wheat have also
gone up during the past few days,
leaving more than doubled compared
with the pre-war figures. A bag of
flour is quoted at less than $8 but it
is predicted that it will eventually
reach that mark in the next few days.
The price of wheat is $13 per bag.
The most important increase in addi-
tion to the increase of price of rice
is registered in the bean oil market.
This oil is needed by even a most
humble Chinese family for cooking
vegetables. It is $103 per barrel.
Most of the Chinese here have dis-
carded peanut oil, the price of which
they can not afford to pay.
The "Shun Pao" indicates that it
may be beyond the ability of local
people here to control the price of
oil which mostly comes from the north.
The report asserts that Germany has
been buying beans from Manchoukuo
in large quantities having reached an
agreement with the Japanese. The
purchase of 1,000,000 tons of beans
having been agreed to, the much
needed cargo is said to be reaching
Germany by rail via Siberia. Oil
merchants in Shanghai have been
hoarding the oil too and as a result
the bean oil from Tsingtao surpassed
the $100 mark on Saturday last.
The Chinese press pin their hope
on Mr. Yu Ya-ching in doing away
with the rice market racket. He is
quoted as saying that the way out
of the present difficult situation is
to again start a "collective purchase"
movement. He has promised to hold
a meeting with representatives of
public bodies concerned in order that
they may again collectively buy
Saigon rice to offset local prices.

《字林西报》，
1938年12月4日
物价上涨
引发华人关注
主要食品价格预计将处于高位；寻求官方行动

昨日一家主要中文报纸商业版刊登的一篇新闻文章指责，上海民众面临前所未有的经济困境是由于缺乏官方关注。该文章声称，“上海民众的困难无人过问”。物价失控上涨是许多报告和媒体评论的主题，也是每个中国家庭的痛楚。人们普遍希望官方机构能采取一些措施。
过去几天，中文报刊对市场上无良商人和操纵者发表了措辞最严厉的批评，但这些言论未受重视。有人指出，在某些情况下，价格上涨是可以原谅的，但在大多数情况下，这种令人担忧的局势据称是投机倒把的结果，因为不像过去由社会局那样对商人实施了管控。
人们普遍承认，局势的变化也造成了只有通过官方机构才能解决的困难，因为公众的谴责毫无用处。
一位受访米商表示，如果现在不采取预防措施，他看到几个月后米价有可能飙升至50美元甚至60美元。目前每担（picul）粮食的价格又在41美元左右波动。他指出，局势的严重性在于，眼下正值新稻上市且洋米持续运抵之时。据说，不受限制的囤积是价格上涨的主要原因之一。

预期进一步上涨
过去几天，面粉和小麦的价格也有所上涨，与战前水平相比增加了一倍多。一袋面粉的报价低于8美元，但预计在未来几天内最终将达到这一价位。小麦价格为每袋13美元。
除了米价上涨外，最重要的涨幅出现在豆油市场。即使是最贫寒的中国家庭烹饪蔬菜也需要这种油。其价格为每桶103美元。
这里的大多数中国人已经弃用花生油，因为他们无力支付其价格。
《申报》指出，控制油价可能超出了当地居民的能力，因为油主要来自北方。报道断言，德国已与日本达成协议，大量从满洲国购买大豆。据悉，在同意购买100万吨大豆后，这批急需的货物正通过西伯利亚铁路运往德国。上海的油商也在囤积豆油，结果上周六青岛豆油突破了100美元大关。
中文报刊将消除大米市场投机的希望寄托在于亚青先生身上。据引述他的话称，摆脱当前困境的办法是重新启动“集体采购”运动。他承诺将与有关公共团体的代表举行会议，以便他们再次集体购买西贡米，以抵消本地价格。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
NOV. 30 1939
Japan Buying Causes
Rice Price Increase
Bayonets, Paper “Money” Force Rice Growers
To Sell; Small Remaining Shipments
For Shanghai Heavily “Taxed”

With the price of rice showing still further increases, the vernacular press has been making strong criticism of manipulators in the local market, although it does not appear on closer examination that they are to blame, but the Japanese, who have brought about a remarkable state of affairs.

“No official intervention” states a morning paper, indicating possibly that the Shanghai Municipal Council has done nothing about the situation, although inquiries tend to show that there is little that can be done by the SMC. Measures reported in the Chinese press, as having been adopted by Chinese trading groups, such as “To request buyers and sellers and brokers in the market to be considerate of the livelihood of the poor and to warn them against disturbing peace and order for selfish interests” are entirely beside the point and would have no effect on the market.

Not Due To Hoarding
The high price of rice in Shanghai is not in the least due to hoarding by Chinese merchants, but can be laid completely to Japan. This statement is the result of investigations into the situation made by the Shanghai Evening Post.

“The situation is entirely impossible at present” was one of the comments heard by the investigator. “When Saigon rice works out at slightly cheaper than the native product, despite the bad exchange rate, no more comment is necessary.”

Good Harvest
The rice crop in the Yangtze valley this year was not as good as it would have been in normal political conditions. Despite this, it was still good, and should have been sufficient to provide Shanghai with rice from six to eight months from the harvest in September, that is to say, until April/May/June.

The rice, however, has not come the way of this city as it should. For this there is a set of reasons, which all add up to one thing, the presence of the Japanese army in China.

Japan Crop Bad
In Japan this year the rice crop was 40 percent below normal. First of all, Mother Nature did not come up to scratch. Secondly, the peasants who should have attended to the harvesting were mostly in the army. Thirdly, the girls who work in the fields are now in the munition factories.

A bad crop in Japan has always been estimated at 20 percent below normal. This year’s crop showed twice that deficiency. In normal times, Japan turns to Korea when the crop is bad. This year Korea’s crops were also bad, and no help could be expected from that quarter.

Colored Paper
As a result there was only one thing for Japan to do, and that was to print a large number of nice pieces of colored paper and call them Yen, Hua Hsing notes, or anything else, and for the Japanese army to go with these into the huge rice producing area from Wuhu to the Tai Hu lake. There was the solution to Japan’s rice troubles. Soldiers armed with bayonets and paper “money” do the trick.

The rice is not only needed for Japan itself. The Japanese army has a million men in the field in China, and they need rice too. If the old saying “one soldier, one camp follower” be considered, this million probably totals up to very much more to be fed on army rice.

Residue
What is left of the crop has been finding its way to Shanghai, through a maze of transportation difficulties and “taxes” imposed at barriers where “officials,” accompanied by Japanese soldiers, take their toll at this place and the other.

In the interior rice at present costs $18 to $20 a zah (of 80 kilograms. By the time it has come to Shanghai the cost will have been increased to $35, thanks to the charges en route. Allowing for loss of weight in transit, and for a small profit, the rice then sells at around the $40 mark. Rice imported from Saigon, with shipping charges and unfavorable exchange, actually works out at a little lower than this.

Cost Of Living
The average Chinese eats about 2lb. of rice per day. Altogether, a family would average about 6 lb. per day. This works out at around $40 a month ... and the pay of an average Chinese is around $35.

“The situation is absolutely impossible” said one of Evepost’s sources of information. “But don’t blame the Chinese rice merchant and say he is hoarding. Thank God for him and his keenness to do business; some how and bring what he can into Shanghai. Without him we’d be starving.”
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》
1939年11月30日
日本购买导致
米价上涨
刺刀和纸“币”迫使稻农
出售；运往上海的剩余 shipments
遭受重“税”

随着米价显示进一步上涨，中文报刊一直强烈批评本地市场的操纵者，尽管仔细审查后看来他们并非罪魁祸首，而是日本人造成了一种非凡的局面。

一家晨报称“没有官方干预”，这可能表明上海公共租界工部局对此局势无所作为，尽管调查倾向于显示工部局能做之事甚少。中文报刊报道的中国贸易团体所采取的措施，如“要求市场上的买卖双方和经纪人顾及穷人生计，并警告他们不要为私利扰乱治安”，完全不得要领，对市场不会产生任何影响。

并非由于囤积
上海米价高昂绝非由于中国商人囤积所致，而应完全归咎于日本。这一说法是《上海晚邮报》对局势进行调查的结果。

“目前的局势完全不可能”是调查员听到的一种评论。“尽管汇率不利，但当西贡米算下来比国产米稍便宜时，就无需多言了。”

丰收
今年长江流域的稻作收成不如正常政治条件下那么好。尽管如此，收成仍然不错，本应足以从九月收获起向上海供应六至八个月的稻米，也就是说，直到四月/五月/六月。

然而，稻米并未按应有的方式进入本市。对此有一系列原因，归结起来就是一点：日军在中国的存在。

日本收成不佳
今年日本的稻作收成比正常水平低40%。首先，天公不作美。其次，本应从事收割的农民大多在军队中。第三，在田间劳作的女孩们现在都在军火工厂里。

日本收成不好通常估计比正常水平低20%。今年的收成显示出两倍的不足。在正常时期，当收成不好时，日本会转向朝鲜。今年朝鲜的收成也很差，无法指望从那方面得到帮助。

彩色纸张
因此，日本只有一件事可做，那就是印制大量漂亮的彩色纸片，称之为日元、华兴票据或其他任何东西，并让日军带着这些进入从芜湖到太湖的巨大产米区。这就是解决日本大米问题的办法。手持刺刀和纸“币”的士兵起到了作用。

稻米不仅日本自身需要。日军在中国战场有一百万人，他们也需要稻米。如果考虑“一个士兵，一个随营人员”的老话，这一百万人可能需要供养的人数恐怕要多得多，都靠军粮度日。

剩余部分
剩余的收成正穿过迷宫般的运输困难和在关卡征收的“税费”流向上海，在这些地方，由日本士兵陪同的“官员”在此处和彼处收取他们的份额。

目前内地稻米价格为每扎（zah，80公斤）18至20美元。当它到达上海时，由于途中的费用，成本将增加到35美元。考虑到运输过程中的重量损失和微薄的利润，稻米随后的售价在40美元左右。从西贡进口的稻米，加上运费和不利的汇率，实际算下来比这略低。

生活成本
普通中国人每天大约吃2磅米。总的来说，一个家庭平均每天大约吃6磅。这算下来每月大约40美元……而普通中国人的月薪大约在35美元左右。

“局势绝对不可能”，《晚邮报》的一位消息人士说。“但不要责怪中国米商，说他囤积居奇。要感谢他和他的经商热情，想方设法把能弄到的东西带进上海。没有他，我们就要挨饿了。”

THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW
Nov.25, 1939.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL S. B. REGISTRATION S. D.）
Drought Cuts Korean Rice Crop by
42 Per Cent; Japan Faces Shortage

U. S. MARINES GUARD LOCAL RICE
HONGS AFTER NIPPON VISITS
Guards furnished by the U. S. Fourth Marines were patrolling outside two rice hongs in Shanghai's Sinza district on Monday of this week, following a visit to the premises last Saturday by three Japanese (one a gendarme and two others employees of a transportation firm) who allegedly were searching for "smuggled rice." The Japanese nailed up the rear doors of the hongs and locked the main entrances. Informed of the visits, the Shanghai Municipal Police posted guards, while the Marines, in whose defense sector the two hongs are located, reinforced the police.
The Japanese action is believed linked with the rice shortage in Japan, some quarters suggesting that Japanese in the interior are tightening control of China's rice supply with a view to exporting large stocks to Japan. Reports of such exports and unfavorable crop reports from the hinterland caused the local price of rice to jump from $28 to $35 a picul last week-end.

JAPAN'S economic difficulties, intensified by the prolongation of the war in China which fails to bring anything like adequate returns for the huge investment in life and treasure, have now extended to the staple diet of her people, according to reports which indicate that the country is shortly to face a serious shortage of rice.
According to a United Press dispatch from Tokyo on Nov. 17, it is highly likely that Japan will be forced to import considerable quantities of the grain next summer from Siam, French Indo-China and Burma to meet a threatened shortage.

Korean Output Halved
Although Japan produces annually close to 320 million bushels of rice, her people eat about 365 million bushels. The shortage is usually made good by imports from the Japanese colonies of Korea and Formosa. But this year, Korea suffered a serious drought which cut the country's output by an estimated 42 per cent. There is consequently not sufficient rice for Korea's own needs, and the 30 to 40 million bushels usually exported to Japan will now have to be sought elsewhere.
The drought in Korea this year has not only made rice exports to Japan impossible, but it also reduced crops below the level required to meet the needs of the Korean people. This fact was shown last week in a resolution presented to the Ministry of Agriculture in Tokyo by members of the Social Masses Party, demanding that cereals be sent to Korea immediately from Manchukuo and Japan to "secure an even supply of food."
While Korea's rice crop was severely curtailed by drought, a Domei report from Seoul on Nov. 19 indicated that the wheat and barley crops for the current fiscal year had risen by 6,887,400 bushels over last year's crops. This year's total, it was stated, amounted to 65,687,940 bushels.

Must Drink Less Sake
So serious has Japan's rice shortage become, that the Government is planning to deprive the sake brewing industry in Japan and colonies of some 2,000,000 koku of rice which normally they would be using. Last year, the rice allotted to sake brewing was cut by 10 per cent, but this further cut is now deemed necessary, according to the Asahi Shimbun.
Not only will the Japanese people have to content themselves with less sake, but they henceforth will pay higher prices for their cigarettes. A 14 per cent increase in price was decreed on Nov. 16, effective immediately. Tobacco is a Government monopoly, and the increased price is intended to furnish additional revenue. Government officials estimated, according to Domei, that the increase would yield an additional Yen 15,000,000 for the national treasury this fiscal year, and a total revenue increase of Yen 60,000,000 for the 1940-41 fiscal year.
At the last-day session of the ordinary general meeting of the Imperial Agricultural Association in Tokyo on Nov. 10, a lengthy discussion took place on the food situation. A number of recommendations to the Government were adopted, among them being a proposal that complete preparations be made for the introduction of a "ticket rationing system" for the future distribution of foodstuffs.

"A Contemptible Invention"
The more Japan's people are compelled to tighten their belts in order to keep the Japanese war machine in the field in China, the more sensitive their rulers become to the propagandist use made of Japan's economic difficulties by the Chinese. An example of this was a statement last week by Rear-Admiral Seiichi Iwamura, newly-appointed Japanese Naval Resident Officer in Shanghai, who in an interview with Japanese newspapermen "flayed" Chungking propaganda to the effect that Japan's measures for controlling economy indicated that her resources were insufficient for prolonged hostilities.
"A contemptible invention" was the description which the Admiral applied to this propaganda, at the same time pointing out that there was "a country in Europe" (evidently meaning Germany) which imposed more stringent economic regulations than were enforced in Japan.

《密勒氏评论报》
1939年11月25日。
（印：上海公共租界工部局注册处特别分部）
干旱使朝鲜米产量减少42%；日本面临短缺

日军探访后，美国海军陆战队守卫本地米行
本周星期一，在美国第四海军陆战队提供的卫兵巡逻下，上海新闸区两家米行外有士兵驻守，此前上周六有三名日本人（一名宪兵和两名运输公司员工）访问了该处所，据称他们正在搜寻“走私米”。日本人钉上了米行的后门并锁住了正门。得知此次访问后，上海公共租界工部局警务处部署了警卫，而这两家米行位于其防区内的海军陆战队则增援了警方。
日本人的行动被认为与日本的米荒有关，一些方面暗示，内地的日本人正在加强对中国米源的控制，以便向日本出口大量库存。此类出口的报告以及来自内地的不利作物报告，导致上周末本地米价从每担28美元跳涨至35美元。

据报道，日本的经济困难因在华战争的延长而加剧，这场战争未能为巨大的人力和财力投资带来任何像样的回报，如今已波及到其人民的主食，迹象表明该国即将面临严重的米荒。
根据11月17日从东京发出的合众社电讯，日本很可能被迫明年夏天从暹罗、法属印度支那和缅甸进口大量谷物，以应对迫在眉睫的短缺。

朝鲜产量减半
虽然日本每年生产近3.2亿蒲式耳的米，但其人民消耗约3.65亿蒲式耳。短缺通常通过从日本殖民地朝鲜和台湾进口来弥补。但今年，朝鲜遭受严重干旱，估计使该国产量减少了42%。因此，没有足够的米满足朝鲜自身的需求，通常出口到日本的3,000万至4,000万蒲式耳现在必须从其他地方寻求。
今年朝鲜的干旱不仅使对日米出口成为不可能，而且还将作物产量降低到无法满足朝鲜人民需求的水平以下。上周，社会大众党成员向东京农林省提交了一项决议，要求立即从满洲国和日本向朝鲜运送谷物，以“确保粮食供应均衡”，这一事实便显示了上述情况。
虽然朝鲜的米产量因干旱而严重缩减，但11月19日从首尔发出的一则同盟社报道指出，本财政年度的小麦和大麦产量比去年增加了6,887,400蒲式耳。据报道，今年的总量达到65,687,940蒲式耳。

必须少喝清酒
日本的米荒已变得如此严重，以至于政府计划剥夺日本及殖民地的清酒酿造业约2,000,000石的米，这些米通常是供他们使用的。据《朝日新闻》报道，去年分配给清酒酿造的米减少了10%，但现在认为有必要进一步削减。
日本人不仅将不得不满足于喝更少的清酒，而且今后还将为香烟支付更高的价格。11月16日颁布法令，价格上涨14%，立即生效。烟草是政府专卖品，涨价旨在提供额外收入。据同盟社报道，政府官员估计，涨价将在本财政年度为国库增加1,500万日元的收入，并在1940-41财政年度使总收入增加6,000万日元。
11月10日，在东京举行的帝国农会普通总会最后一天的会议上，就粮食状况进行了 lengthy 讨论。通过了一些向政府提出的建议，其中包括一项提议，即为未来食品分配实施“票证配给制度”做好充分准备。

“卑鄙的捏造”
日本人民越是被迫勒紧裤带以维持日本战争机器在中国战场的运转，其统治者对中国利用日本经济困难进行宣传的做法就越敏感。上周新任日本海军驻沪专员岩村清一少将在接受日本记者采访时“痛斥”重庆方面的宣传，即日本的控制经济措施表明其资源不足以支持长期敌对行动，这就是一个例子。
这位少将形容这种宣传是“卑鄙的捏造”，同时指出“欧洲有一个国家”（显然指德国）实施了比日本更严格的经济管制。

《字林西报》

大量米
被转运
至虹口

据昨晚知名的华商贸易界人士称，从产区运抵此地的数千袋米已被转运至虹口地区，并重新装运至华北港口。
虽然目前尚无法确定如此转运至虹口的米的确切数量，但同一消息来源估计，在过去两周内，超过50,000袋米被“挪用”。
昨晚贸易界普遍认为，除非遏制租界库存的这一损失，否则这里几乎不可能缓解米危机。

根据昨日的交易报告，上等米仍以每担约40美元的价格出售，从而达到了自去年8月危急日子以来的最高价格峰值。

据报道，昨日几个贸易团体正在考虑对米市操纵行为采取“压制措施”。据说这些团体决定的措施包括以下内容：
1. 提请本地银行界注意，必须大幅减少或完全停止以米为抵押的贷款，以防止此类贷款被不法商人利用；
2. 要求市场上的买卖双方和经纪人顾及穷人的生计，并警告他们不要为了私利扰乱和平与秩序；
3. 公开要求所有知情方揭露操纵者，以便将其绳之以法；
4. 呼吁租界当局采取明确政策保护粮食状况，并对负责操纵市场的人施以严厉惩罚；
5. 分别向此地的中国法院、市商会、米业公会和中国钱业公会请愿，要求与外国当局联合组织一个上海粮食保护委员会，并被赋予处理粮食问题的最高权力。

Move to Check Rise
In Rice Prices
Local Public Bodies to
Petition Authorities For
Action Against Profiteers
Some Chinese public bodies in
Shanghai are reported to have met
during the past few days and resolved
upon a number of measures which
they will petition official quarters to
carry out in order to put an end to
the manipulation which is alleged to
be responsible for the sudden increase
in the price of rice during the past

They have decided upon "preven-

this end, it is stated, they will request
bankers not to lend money to
merchants who depend on hoarding
rice for obtaining a profit. They will
persuade merchants and commission
men in the rice market not to increase
their prices unreasonably, and also
encourage people to report secretly
on the activities of manipulators.
The most important decision reached
at the meetings is a joint committee
to be organized by the Chinese courts
in the foreign areas, the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce, the Rice
Dealers' Association, the Shanghai
Bankers Association and the Settle-
ment and Concession authorities for
the purpose of regulating the price of
rice. The joint committee will be the
highest arbitration organization in any
rice dispute between the public and
unscrupulous merchants. It is under-
stood that the public bodies con-
cerned will carry out their decisions
by petitioning the official quarters
affected.
Only about two weeks ago the price
of rice was gradually returning to

遏制米价上涨的行动
本地公共团体将
请愿当局采取行动打击奸商
据报道，上海的一些中国公共团体在过去几天内举行会议，并决议采取若干措施，他们将请求官方部门执行这些措施，以结束据称导致过去几天米价突然上涨的操纵行为。
他们已决定将“预防”和“公众制裁”作为摧毁这一非法勾当的最佳手段。为此，据悉，他们将请求银行家不要向依赖囤积大米获利的商人贷款。他们将劝说米市中的商人和掮客不要不合理地提高价格，并鼓励人们秘密举报操纵者的活动。
会议上达成的最重要决定是，由租界内的中国法院、中华总商会、米业同业公会、上海银行公会以及租界和公董局当局组织一个联合委员会，目的是调节米价。该联合委员会将成为公众与不法商人之间任何米纠纷的最高仲裁机构。据悉，相关公共团体将通过向受影响的官方部门请愿来执行其决定。
就在大约两周前，米价才逐渐恢复正常。一等米曾报价仅为每担26美元，但在过去几天里，它又跳涨至35美元的水平。

CHINA PRESS

NOV 22 1939

S. M. C. Asked
To Probe Rice
Price Hikes

Settlement authorities have been petitioned to investigate into the causes leading to the sharply mounting cost of rice in the foreign areas, a large Chinese rice dealer told THE CHINA PRESS in an interview yesterday.

“The speculators are entirely responsible for this state of affairs,” he added. “Dealers are powerless unless the authorities lend us their assistance.”

It could not be ascertained last night whether such a petition had been received by the Council. It was learned earlier in the day that the Council had received official information that a large quantity of rice had been ordered from Saigon, while arrivals from the growing areas nearby were considered satisfactory.

A high official of the Council informed THE CHINA PRESS that the principal task of the Council rice control body is to facilitate the importation of the grain here wherever possible and it is not primarily concerned in the regulation of prices.

It was recalled, however, that when price increases had reached such a stage as to threaten “public welfare”, the Council would as on former occasions, step in and put into effect some sort of regulations.

Meanwhile, traders’ reports last night stated that the amount of rice which arrived here yesterday totalled about 8,000 bags. Together with the existing stock in Shanghai, dealers saw no alarm for any serious shortage in the near future.

（批：Liu）
（批：C 92 / 11）

《字林西报》

1939年11月22日

要求工部局
调查米价
上涨原因

一位中国大米商人在昨日接受《字林西报》采访时称，已 petitioned 租界当局调查导致外国区域米价急剧上涨的原因。

“投机商应对这种局面负全部责任，”他补充道。“除非当局给予我们协助，否则商人无能为力。”

昨晚无法证实工部局是否收到了此类请愿书。早些时候获悉，工部局已收到官方消息，称已从西贡订购大量大米，而来自附近产区的到货情况令人满意。

工部局一位高级官员告诉《字林西报》，工部局米粮管制机构的主要任务是尽可能便利粮食进口本市，其主要关注点并非调节价格。

然而，值得注意的是，当价格上涨达到威胁“公共福利”的程度时，工部局将像以往一样介入并实施某种形式的管制。

与此同时，商人昨晚的报告称，昨日抵达此处的米量总计约8,000包。结合上海现有库存，商人认为近期不会出现严重短缺的恐慌。

（批：刘）
（批：C 92 / 11）

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
NOV 20 1938

Rice Price Up;
Japan Hand
Seen

Rumors Of Big
Exports Cause
Rates To Soar

Wusih Gendarme Calls
On Hongs, Indicate
Tight Control

MARINES, POLICE
PROTECT STORES

$7-Increase Recorded
In Weekend; Stock
Shows Decline

US Marines are aiding the
Shanghai Municipal Police
in guarding two rice hongs
in the Sinza district, which
were visited Saturday night
by three Japanese in search
of smuggled rice. The Japan-
ese nailed up the back door
and locked the front door of
one of the premises.

Altogether three hongs were
visited, the third in the Louza dis-
trict. This last was visited for a
second time yesterday morning,
when the Japanese found an SMP
on guard, who interrogated the
trio.

Wusih Gendarme

The three hongs are situated at
13 Lane 344 Burkill Road, 208
Avenue Road and 377 West Soo-
chow Road. It was the latter
which was visited twice by the
Nipponese, who apparently com-
prise a gendarme from Wusih and
two members of a transportation
firm.

The Japanese were apparently
checking up on rice shipped from
Wusih to Shanghai on a forged
permit, but what exactly they in-
tended to do regarding the stocks
in the three hongs is not clear,
neither is their action in closing
up the Burkill Road hong.

Independent

It is believed, however, that
the Japanese in the interior are
tightening the control of rice with
the view of switching large stocks
to Japan where there is a short-
age of supply.

The SMP were informed by the
three concerns of the Saturday
night visit, and guards were im-
mediately posted. As the Burkill
and Avenue Roads hongs are in
the US Marine sector, squads of
Marines were called in to supple-
ment the Police pickets.

The action of the Japanese gen-
darme from Wusih in pursuing
independent investigations without
asking for SMP assistance is as-
cribed in some quarters to his
ignorance of local conditions. No
official complaint has as yet been
laid with the SMP regarding rice
illegally acquired, and the whole
situation is at present being
studied by SMP Headquarters.

Reports of huge exports of rice
to Japan to relieve the shortage
there and unfavorable crop re-
ports from the interior combined
to force the price of rice from
$28 to $35 per picul during the
weekend. Rice business circles
are reticent concerning the re-
ported exports to Japan although
it is admitted that there have been
large withdrawals from the local
rice stock during the last few
days.

Stocks Fall Slightly

An official of the SMC told the
Evening Post this morning that
there had only been a slight
falling off in the total stocks held
in godowns and retail rice shops,
and estimated that the present
stock in the city amounted to
around 224,000 piculs.

The official revealed that this
was considerably higher than the
total of only 50,000 piculs in
Shanghai last September, when
rice prices rose to over $50 per
picul.

He also declared that since the
recent improvement in foreign ex-
change, a number of orders had
been placed for the purchase of
rice from Saigon, one order hav-
ing been placed by a firm here
this week for importation of 500
tons of Saigon rice, while several
other orders had also been enter-
ed.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
1938年11月20日

米价上涨；
疑似日本
插手

大量出口谣言
导致行市飙升

无锡宪兵走访
洋行，显示
管控收紧

海军陆战队、警察
保护仓库

周末记录到
$7涨幅；库存
显示下降

美国海军陆战队正在协助上海公共租界工部局警务处守卫新闸区两家米行，周六晚有三名日本人前往这两家米行搜寻走私大米。日本人将其中一处场所的后门钉死，并锁上前门。

共有三家米行被走访，第三家位于老闸区。昨日上午，日本人第二次走访最后这家米行，发现有一名警务处警员在站岗，遂对这三名日本人进行了讯问。

无锡宪兵

这三家米行分别位于伯基尔路344弄13号、爱文义路208号和苏州西路377号。后者被日本人两次走访，这些人显然包括一名来自无锡的宪兵和一家运输公司的两名成员。

日本人显然是在检查凭伪造许可证从无锡运往上海的大米，但他们究竟打算如何处理这三家米行的库存尚不清楚，他们关闭伯基尔路米行的举动也不明就里。

独立行动

然而，人们认为，内地的日本人正在加强对大米的控制，目的是将大量库存转运至供应短缺的日本。

这三家公司已将周六晚间的走访情况告知警务处，随即部署了警卫。由于伯基尔路和爱文义路的米行位于美国海军陆战队防区，因此召来海军陆战队小分队以补充警察哨位。

某些方面将无锡日本宪兵在不寻求警务处协助的情况下进行独立调查的行为归咎于其对当地情况的不了解。目前尚未就非法获取大米一事向警务处提出正式投诉，警务处总部目前正在研究整个局势。

有关为缓解日本国内短缺而向日本大量出口大米的报道，以及来自内地的不利作物报告，共同导致周末米价从每担$28涨至$35。尽管承认过去几天本地大米库存有大量提取，但大米商界对报道中的对日出口一事保持缄默。

库存小幅下降

工部局一位官员今早告诉《晚邮报》，仓库和零售米店持有的总库存仅有小幅下降，并估计本市当前库存约为224,000担。

该官员透露，这一数字远高于去年9月上海仅有的50,000担的总量，当时米价涨至每担$50以上。

他还宣称，自近期外汇状况改善以来，已下达多笔从西贡购买大米的订单，本周本地一家公司已下达一笔进口500吨西贡大米的订单，此外还下达了其他几笔订单。

page_data.en:
Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Chinese-American Daily
News, Hwa Pao, Ta Ying Yeh Pao, China Evening News, etc. :-

20.11.39 (AM) S.M.C. REQUESTED TO PREVENT HOARDING OF RICE

At this time of the year when there is a
continuous arrival of new rice, there is still no sign
of a drop in the price of rice; on the contrary an increase
has been marked during the past seven days.
Consequently a meeting was held by the Rice
Mart Control Committee at the Tsing Lieh Koo Tea Shop
(青蓮閣) on Foochow Road yesterday afternoon at which
the following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
(1) That the members of the Committee be
requested to advise the rice merchants to check further
increases in the price of rice.
(2) That efforts be made to prevent rice
brokers from manipulation for profiteering on the rice
mart; that severe measures be adopted against them if they
are found to be engaged in such activities.
According to a certain leading rice merchant,
the present increase in the price of rice is due to
manipulation and hoarding on the part of certain elements
who are doing this with the deliberate intention of
disturbing the rice market.
It is learned that petitions have been sent
to the S.M.C. and the Chamber of Commerce by the Shanghai
First Special District Citizens' Federation and other local
public bodies requesting them to devise ways and means to
put a stop to the activities of manipulation and at the
same time to accelerate the construction of granaries so
as to avoid a shortage of rice supplies for the people.

1939年11月20日（上午）请求工部局防止囤积大米

值此新米持续上市之际，米价仍无下跌迹象；相反，过去七天出现上涨。因此，米业管理委员会昨日下午在福州路青莲阁茶馆举行会议，讨论并通过以下决议：-
(1) 请委员会成员劝告米商遏制米价进一步上涨。
(2) 努力防止米经纪人在米市操纵牟利；如发现其从事此类活动，将采取严厉措施。
据某知名米商称，目前米价上涨是由于某些分子操纵和囤积所致，这些人故意扰乱米市。
据悉，上海第一特区市民联合会及其他地方公共团体已向工部局和总商会提交请愿书，请求他们制定办法制止操纵活动，同时加速粮仓建设，以避免民众出现大米供应短缺。

page_data.en:
S. M. C. MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. C. REGISTRY
No. S. M. C. D. 80397/576
Date 21 / 11 / 39

Hwa Pao, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Chinese-American
Daily News: 21.11.39 (AM)

REASONS FOR THE HIGH PRICE OF RICE

Due to the unreasonably rapid increase in the
price of rice during the past few days, the question of
rice supplies to local residents will again become as
serious as it was two months ago. This is evidently
due to manipulation and hoarding on the part of certain
elements and it is deemed necessary that investigations
should be made and punishment be meted out upon such
elements.

The following information has been secured by
the Dah Chung News Agency ( 大中社 ):-
At this time when the S.M.C. and various local
authoritative bodies are planning the construction of
granaries for the storage of rice as a means to prevent
a shortage of rice supplies in spring next year, the price
of the "Kan Mee" has suddenly gone up to over $40 per
picul during the past three or four days. This sharp
increase in the price of rice is undoubtedly not due to
obstruction or to shortage of stocks, as rice supplies
are still pouring into Shanghai continuously from the
suburban areas. Moreover, according to a high official
of the S.M.C., there are at present at least 224,000 piculs
of rice in stock in Shanghai. It is therefore quite
evident that the recent sharp increase in the price of rice
is due to manipulation on the part of certain elements
who are doing this purposely for the sake of profiteering.

It is learned that with a view to preventing
a shortage of rice supplies for residents as well as for
the purpose of maintaining peace and order, the S.M.C. is
making discreet enquiries into the actual facts responsible
for this rapid increase and will take severe measures
against such activities as soon as definite proof has been
established.

The authorities of the Foreign Settlements have
been requested by the Citizens' Federation to pay special
attention to such activities, while the Chamber of Commerce
and the Rice Trade Guild have been asked by the local
authoritative banking and industrial circles to take
effective measures against activities of manipulation and
hoarding so as to appease the anxiety of the public. It
is hoped that by doing this the avarice for profits of the
traitorous merchants will be somewhat checked.
page_data.zh:
工部局警务处
工部局档案室
编号 S. M. C. D. 80397/576
日期 1939年11月21日

《华报》、《申报》、《新闻报》、《大美晚报》、《中美日报》：1939年11月21日（上午）

米价高昂之原因

由于过去几天米价不合理地快速上涨，本地居民的米粮供应问题将再次变得如同两个月前那样严峻。这显然是由于某些分子的操纵和囤积所致，认为有必要对此类分子进行调查并予以惩罚。

大中社已获得以下信息：-
正值工部局及各地方权威机构计划建造粮仓以储存大米，作为防止明年春季大米供应短缺的手段之际，“粘米”价格在过去三四天内突然涨至每担$40以上。米价的急剧上涨无疑并非由于阻碍或库存短缺，因为郊区的大米仍在源源不断地运入上海。此外，据工部局一位高级官员称，上海目前至少有224,000担大米库存。因此，最近米价急剧上涨显然是由于某些分子为了牟利而故意操纵所致。

据悉，为了防止居民大米供应短缺以及维持治安，工部局正在谨慎调查导致此次快速上涨的实际事实，并在确立确凿证据后立即对此类活动采取严厉措施。

市民联合会已请求租界当局特别注意此类活动，而地方权威银行界和工业界已要求总商会和米业公会采取有效措施对付操纵和囤积活动，以平息公众的焦虑。希望以此能稍微遏制奸商的贪利之心。

page_data.en:
According to two local leading rice merchants,
there is no explanation for the sudden rise of the price
of rice during the past few days other than that of
manipulation for profiteering on the part of certain
elements. The reports that this increase is due to non-
arrivals of rice and shortage of rice stocks or due to
the shortage of rice supplies in Japan are simply intended
to mislead the public. At present between seven and eight
thousand bags of rice arrive in Shanghai every day, while
the daily consumption in Shanghai is only 7,000 bags.
Moreover, there are sufficient stocks of rice in Shanghai.
In connection with the report that the Japanese
are making purchases of rice in the interior, it will be
noted that most of the purchases they make consist of the
Wuhu "see-mee;" this in no way affects the rice supplies
to Shanghai as the rice transported here from the regions
along the Nanking-Shanghai Railway comprise mostly "kan-mee."
It is, therefore, not difficult to see why there has
prevailed a sharp rise in the price of rice of this category.
When asked by the reporter of the news agency
about the truth of the rumour that a company had been
established jointly by certain speculators with the object
of undertaking large-scale manipulation of the rice mart,
the two rice merchants replied that they were in ignorance
but stated that the rice trading circles were now making
discreet enquiries into this fact and were devising ways
and means to put a stop to future trouble in connection
with the question of rice supplies.
It will be remembered that on November 19 a
meeting was held by the Rice Mart Control Committee, at
which it was resolved that efforts be made to prevent rice
brokers from engaging in deliberate enhancement of the
price of rice at the rice mart. This action on the part of
the Committee has checked somewhat the activities of the
unscrupulous elements.
More than 7,000 bags of rice arrived here
yesterday and, thanks to this, the price of all grades of
"kan-mee" marked a drop of about $2 per picul yesterday,
while that of the "see-mee" showed a decline of about $1.30
per picul.
page_data.zh:
据两位本地米业巨头称，近日米价突然上涨，除某些分子为牟取暴利而进行操纵外，别无其他解释。有关此次涨价是由于大米未运抵、库存短缺或日本大米供应不足的说法，纯属误导公众。目前，每天运抵上海的大米在七千至八千包之间，而上海的日消费量仅为7,000包。此外，上海的大米库存充足。

关于日本人在内地采购大米的报道，值得注意的是，他们采购的大部分是芜湖“细米”；这丝毫不影响对上海的稻米供应，因为从京沪铁路沿线地区运往此处的大米主要为“粳米”。因此，不难理解为何此类大米的价格会出现急剧上涨。

当通讯社记者就有关某些投机商联合成立一家公司、旨在大规模操纵米市的传闻真实性进行询问时，这两位米商表示他们并不知情，但指出米业界目前正在谨慎调查此事，并正在设法制定措施，以杜绝未来在大米供应问题上可能出现的麻烦。

需指出的是，11月19日米市管制委员会召开了一次会议，会上决议努力防止米经纪人在米市故意抬高米价。委员会的这一行动在一定程度上遏制了不法分子的活动。

昨日运抵此地的大米超过7,000包，得益于此，昨日各级“粳米”的价格每担下跌约2美元，而“细米”的价格每担下跌约1.30美元。

26780

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

Rising Rice Shortage
Alarms Nippon People

The shortage of rice in Japan is increasing and the masses
of the Nipponese people now are seriously worried on this be-
half, the Tokyo paper "Asahi" reveals. The paper is openly con-
tradicting the Japanese Minister of Agriculture and Forestry,
who in the latest meeting of the Tokyo Cabinet assured his col-
leagues that there was no reason to fear an immediate rice short-
age, and that the food supply situation in Japan was well in hand.
At present the supply of rice in Japan is short in many
places and anxiety is being felt over the situation, the "Asahi"
points out. The so-called "drive for economizing in the consump-
tion of rice" has had a bad psychological effect upon the people
and resulted merely in more speculative buying, so that at pre-
sent there is great confusion as regards the general distribution
of stocks, the paper says.
The summer and autumn drought in Korea has been much
more severe than Japanese officials originally admitted. The rice
harvest in Korea, as a result of the drought, has been cut
by no less than 42 percent, the Nipponese vice-minister for Agricul-
ture and Forestry, Mr. Yasushi Hasumi, was compelled to admit
in a interview with a representative of the "Asahi." In these
circumstances, Korea will be unable to export rice to Japan dur-
ing the current rice year, if the Koreans themselves are not to
be starved.
The new Japanese Rice Control Law was officially enforced
as from November 1, but many difficulties delay its operation in
practice, so that the beginning of the new governmental rice con-
trol in Japan cannot be expected before next months, the Tokyo
Government announced.
page_data.zh:
26780

《上海晚邮报与水星报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）。

大米短缺加剧
令日本民众恐慌

东京报纸《朝日新闻》披露，日本的大米短缺情况日益严重，日本民众对此深感忧虑。该报公开反驳日本农林大臣，后者在最近的东京内阁会议上向同僚保证，没有理由担心立即出现大米短缺，且日本的粮食供应局势完全在掌控之中。

《朝日新闻》指出，目前日本许多地方大米供应短缺，人们对局势感到焦虑。该报称，所谓的“节约大米消费运动”对民众产生了不良的心理影响，仅导致了更多的投机性购买，致使目前库存的总体分配陷入极大混乱。

朝鲜夏季和秋季的干旱比日本官员最初承认的要严重得多。日本农林次官莲见康 (Yasushi Hasumi) 先生在接受《朝日新闻》代表采访时被迫承认，由于干旱，朝鲜的水稻收成减少了至少42%。在这种情况下，如果不想让朝鲜人自己挨饿，朝鲜在当前稻米年度将无法向日本出口大米。

新的日本《大米管制法》已于11月1日正式实施，但在实际操作中遇到许多困难而延误，因此东京政府宣布，日本政府对新的大米管制预计要到下个月才能开始。

Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao and Central China Daily News :- 23.10.39 (PM)
CITIZENS' FEDERATION SUGGEST S.M.C. CONSTRUCT GRANARIES
FOR THE STORAGE OF RICE

The following joint letter was sent to the
Shanghai First Special District Citizens' Federation by
the 15th, 36th and 37th Branches of the Federation yesterday:
"The rise of commodity prices, especially the
price of rice, has seriously affected the livelihood of
the people. This is a question that is closely connected
with peace and order of the community. Since the outbreak
of the hostilities, Shanghai has become a big refugee
centre and the population here is said to total 5,000,000.
Therefore, in order to be able to prevent any shortage of
food supplies to the people, it is necessary to devise
some adequate measures to deal with the problem.
"We, therefore, suggest that the authorities of
the two Foreign Settlements be requested to take advantage
of the rich harvest in the interior to make large purchases
of rice from the inland districts and to establish public
granaries in the Settlements for the storage of these
purchases. Thus, there will arise no public alarm despite
a shortage of rice supplies in the future.
"As this is a matter that closely affects the
livelihood of the people and the maintenance of peace and
order, we hope that a letter be sent to the two municipal
authorities requesting acceptance of this proposal for
enforcement."

《新闻报》、《申报》及《华中日报》：1939年10月23日（下午）
市民联合会建议工部局建造粮仓
用于储存大米

昨日，该联合会的第15、36和37支会向上海第一特区市民联合会发送了以下联名信：
“物价上涨，尤其是米价上涨，已严重影响民众生计。这是一个与社区和平秩序密切相关的问题。自战事爆发以来，上海已成为一个大型难民中心，据说此地人口总数达500万。因此，为了能够防止民众出现粮食供应短缺，有必要制定一些适当的措施来应对这一问题。
“因此，我们建议请求两个外国租界的当局利用内地的丰收，从内陆地区大量采购大米，并在租界内建立公共粮仓以储存这些采购的大米。这样，即使未来出现大米供应短缺，也不会引起公众恐慌。
“由于此事 closely 关系到民众生计及和平秩序的维护，我们希望致函两个市政当局，请求接受并执行此提议。”

Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Chinese-American

has increased. This though is partly because of

据一份由日本人煽动的报道昨晚称，几大批大米已运抵杨树浦地区。然而，报道未说明这些粮食是供日军使用还是供一般消费。
