SHANGHAI TIMES.
25860
OCT 18 1939

Large Drop In Price Of
Rice Is Registered

Heavy Shipments From Inland Areas Coupled With
Desire Of Dealers To Unload Accounts For
Drop; Price Still Too High For Poor

Heavy continuous shipments of
rice from the inland areas to
Shanghai, coupled with the pre-
vailing bearish feeling in the local
rice market, precipitated a down-
ward wave in price yesterday. The
price for first cereals closed at $27
per zar, second grade at $26, and
lower grade cereals at $17, it was
reported yesterday.
Available stocks of rice in
Shanghai up till yesterday were
reported to total more than 100,000
bags, and this is being steadily
swollen by steady arrival of fresh
shipments.
The market had been quiet dur-
ing the past few days, with dealers
and big operators anticipating fur-
ther decline in prices, while hold-
ers had continued to unload heav-
ily, according to the report.
Judging from present conditions,
there was no ground for anxiety
over a shortage of stocks in the
immediate future, local rice mer-
chants circles declared yesterday.
Restrictions Lifted
The restriction which had been
enforced against the free shipment
of rice from Wuhu and other in-
land areas to Shanghai was also
reported to have been lifted by the
authorities concerned. This report
had a further dampening influence
upon the appetite of local rice deal-
ers who were generally inclined
to adopt a "watch and wait" atti-
tude.
The general working classes, how-
ever, were said to be still not in
a position to benefit much from the
prices ruling yesterday. These
prices were still beyond the reach
of the poor, most of whom had
been compelled to subsist on wheat
flour instead, it was stated.
The crisis which several weeks
ago had precipitated the series of
rice riots in the International
Settlement and the French Conces-
sion was felt to have passed, and
the general trend was said to por-
tend better days ahead for Shang-
hai's teeming Chinese population.

Liu
C 15/10
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）。
25860
1939年10月18日

米价大幅
下跌

来自内地的沉重 shipments 加上商人
抛售意愿导致价格
下跌；价格对穷人来说仍然太高

从内地向上海持续大量运抵大米，加上本地大米市场普遍存在的看跌情绪，导致昨日价格出现下跌浪潮。据报道，昨日一级谷物收盘价为每 zar 27美元，二级为26美元，低级谷物为17美元。（注：zar 应为 picul/石 的误植或特定单位，照实译出或保留）
截至昨日，上海可用的大米库存据报道总计超过10万包，并且随着新货的稳定到达，库存正在稳步增加。
据报道，过去几天市场一直平静，经销商和大运营商预期价格会进一步下跌，而持有者则继续大量抛售。
本地米商界昨日宣称，从目前的情况来看，没有理由担心近期会出现库存短缺。
限制解除
据报道，有关当局也解除了此前对从芜湖和其他内陆地区向上海自由运输大米的限制。这一报告进一步抑制了本地米商的胃口，他们普遍倾向于采取“观望”态度。
然而，据说普通工人阶级仍无法从昨日的现行价格中受益多少。据说，这些价格仍然是穷人力所不及的，其中大多数人被迫改以小麦粉为生。
几周前引发公共租界和法租界一系列米骚乱的危机被认为已经过去，据说总体趋势预示着上海拥挤的中国人口将迎来更好的日子。

Liu

OCT 15 1939

Rice Market

The day's arrivals amounted to 5,000
bags of white rice, coming by truck and
rail while no junks arrived on account of
the heavy rainfall. Small business was
recorded during the session and the rates
ruled steady. Best quality Changshu rice
was not traded, while first grade Chang-
shu rice was being quoted at $30 per
picul. First grade qualities of the new
crop stood at $28, while second grade
products fetched $26.50. The price of
"sharp" rice ranged from $21 to $23 per
picul.

On account of poor demand, the rate
of provincial rice dropped by $0.30 in
the market yesterday. Fresh shipments
received totaled 4,000 bags. The local
dealers were hesitant to buy, and the
business transacted in the session amounted
to 3,000 bags of various cereals. Nanking
rice was being offered at from $18.50 to
$19.60, while the price of Wuhu rice ranged
from $18 to $19.60, and that of Kiangpen
products from $18.50 to $18.80 per picul.

大米市场

当日到货量为5,000包白米，由卡车和铁路运抵，因大雨无米船到达。交易期间成交量小，价格平稳。优质常熟米未成交，而一级常熟米报价为每石30美元。新粮一级品价格为28美元，二级产品售价为26.50美元。“尖”米价格在每石21至23美元之间。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 1 4 1939

Rice Market

On account of large arrivals, the rates
of white rice remained unchanged in the
market yesterday. Best quality Chang-shu
rice stood at $33, and first grade Chang-shu
rice at $31. Soochow rice was being
quoted at $28, and best quality of newly
harvested rice sold at $28. Second grade
qualities of newly harvested rice were
offered at $26, "sharp" rice at $23, while
Kiangpeh rice fetched $18.30, and poorer
qualities $17 per picul. The day's arrivals
amounted to several junkloads and 5,000
bags.
The prices of provincial rice registered
a gain of $1 on behalf of rumors that
the Japanese authorities would interfere
with the transportation again. With arri-
vals having declined considerably the total
traded in aggregated around 3,000 bags
of Nanking, Wuhu and Kiangpeh rice.
Prices varied from $18 to $19.50 per picul.

大米市场

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

OCT 12 1939

Price of Rice Shows
Further Decline

Superior Grade Now $4
Cheaper Than Before

With the arrival of further large
shipments, the market price of rice
declined considerably in Shanghai
yesterday.
Kan mee, the superior quality of
the grain, registered a drop of $4
per zah. This grade o' rice was
selling at prices ranging from $28

1939年10月12日

米价显示
进一步下跌

优等米现在比之前
便宜4美元

随着更多大批货物的到达，昨日上海大米市场价格大幅下跌。
“勘米”（Kan mee，音译，即优等米），这种优质谷物，每 zah 下跌4美元。该等级大米的售价范围为每 zah 28至34美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

Rice Market

On account of large shipments of newly-harvested rice the rate showed a downward trend on the market yesterday. The day's arrivals amounted to 8,000 bags. Only small business was done during the entire session.
Best quality Changshu rice was being quoted at $33, while first grade products were being offered at $31. Soochow rice stood at $30, while best quality of newly-harvested rice was being offered at $29. Foonking rice was being sold at $26, and first grade "sharp" rice at $23. Wuhu rice stood at $18.70, Kiangsu rice at $17, while poorer qualities fetched $16 per picul.
Large arrivals of provincial rice dampened sentiment yesterday, with operators adopting an awaiting attitude. Fresh shipments received amounted to 7,900 bags. 大米市场

由于新收大米大量装运，昨日市场价格呈下跌趋势。当日到货量为8,000包。整个交易期间成交量很小。
优质常熟米报价为33美元，而一级产品报价为31美元。苏州米价格为30美元，而优质新收米报价为29美元。奉化（Foonking，音译）米售价为26美元，一级“尖”米为23美元。芜湖米价格为18.70美元，江苏米为17美元，而较差品质售价为每石16美元。

OCT 12 1939

Flour And Wheat

The market for native flour was ruling firm yesterday with the rate still being quoted at $7,000 in cash per bag. North China dealers absorbed a considerable quantity of "Gunboat" flour at $6.70, while South Sea and Hongkong dealers bought a few thousand bags of "Red and Blue Foong Sing" flour at $6.60. Business on the official market was very small, while most transactions took place on the outside market.

The market for native wheat ruled steady yesterday. Wheat holders were reluctant to offer their supplies at the official rate while the mills showed a very poor appetite. As a result, the local dealers bought 5 carloads of Kweitien, Soochow and Wushih products at prices varying from $9.60 to $10 per bag, and the Pooh Sing and Fou Foong flour mills absorbed a few hundred bags at prices ranging from $9.68 to $9.80.

1939年10月12日

面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉市场坚挺，每袋现金报价仍为7,000元。华北商人以6.70元的价格吸纳了大量“炮舰牌”（Gunboat）面粉，而南洋和香港商人则以6.60元的价格购买了数千袋“红蓝凤兴”（Red and Blue Foong Sing）面粉。官方市场的交易量很小，大部分交易在场外市场进行。

昨日国产小麦市场平稳。持粮者不愿按官方价格出售存货，而磨坊的购买意愿极低。因此，本地商人在场外以每袋9.60元至10元不等的价格购买了5车皮来自贵甸（Kweitien）、苏州和无锡的产品，宝兴（Pooh Sing）和福丰（Fou Foong）面粉厂则以9.68元至9.80元不等的价格吸纳了数百袋。

page_data.en:
PRESS
OCT 10 1939

Rice Market

The rate of white rice continued to rule weak on yesterday's market. Only small business was transacted during the day and all quotations registered losses. Best quality Changshu rice was being sold at $37, and first grade cereals were being quoted at $34 per picul. Soochow rice stood at $32, and newly-harvested Soochow rice at $30. Foongking rice was being offered at $31, and best quality "sharp" rice fell to $22. Wuhu rice sold as from $18.20 to $20, while Kiangpeh rice fetched $18.50, and poorer qualities $16.80.

On account of large arrivals of provincial rice the rate declined although the local dealers showed brisk demand. The total turnover amounted to 4,000 bags of various products, traded in at between $18.20 to $20 per picul.

File
C 1%
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年10月10日

大米市场

昨日白米市场行情持续疲软。全天交易量稀少，所有报价均出现下跌。优质常熟米售价为37元，一等谷物报价为每担34元。苏州米价格为32元，新收苏州米为30元。奉化米（Foongking rice）报价为31元，优质“尖”米（sharp rice）跌至22元。芜湖米售价在18.20元至20元之间，江北米售价为18.50元，较差品质的为16.80元。

由于外省大米大量到货，尽管本地商人需求旺盛，价格依然下跌。总成交量为4,000袋各类产品，交易价格在每担18.20元至20元之间。

档案
C 1%

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

Flour And Wheat

Small business in native flour was done
yesterday while second grade products were
all being quoted at $7 in cash per bag.
Many local dealers bought in the outside
market where a cheaper rate was ruling.
"Gunboat" flour was being sold at $6.55,
and red and blue cart brands fell to $6.70
per bag. Japanese flour was being offered
at $6 per bag but only slight business was
recorded.
Trading in native wheat was narrow
in yesterday's market. The mills were
reluctant to buy, and the local dealers
were not in the market. The Foo Foong
and Fook Sing flour mills absorbed 4,500
bags of Soochow, Changchow, Wuhu and
Taiyang wheat, the prices ranging from
$9.65 to $9.80 per bag.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉交易量较小，二等产品均报价为每袋现金7元。许多本地商人在场外市场买入，那里价格较低。“炮舰牌”面粉售价为6.55元，红蓝车牌面粉跌至每袋6.70元。日本面粉报价为每袋6元，但成交寥寥。

昨日国产小麦市场交易清淡。磨坊不愿购买，本地商人也未入市。福丰（Foo Foong）和福兴（Fook Sing）面粉厂吸纳了4,500袋来自苏州、常州、芜湖和太阳（Taiyang，音译）的小麦，价格在每袋9.65元至9.80元之间。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

OCT 7 1939

Rice Situation Shows
Improvement
Other Commodities Dearer, But
Grain Getting Cheaper

Chinese banks in Shanghai have
now received orders from the
Ministry of Economics at Chungking
requiring them to enlarge the scope
of "commodity mortgage" activities
so as to prevent unscrupulous mer-
chants from hoarding goods which
fact is said to be chiefly responsible
for the increase of prices in Shanghai.
According to a Chinese report the
institutions are required to send re-
ports to the Ministry regarding this
matter.
Meanwhile, advertisements of in-
creasing prices of many kinds of
commodities continue to appear in
the Chinese press but Chinese re-
ports indicate that the rice situation
here has definitely improved. Al-
though the present prices are still
very high, it is predicted that with
the continuous arrival of supply no
upward trend will be followed in the
immediate future.
The new crop of rice in Chekiang,
Kiangsu and Anhwei is now ready
for the market. Merchants have ne-
gotiated for free transportation of rice
to Shanghai. Rice has been arriving
here by train and boats during the
past few days from Quinsan, Chang-
chow, Kashing, Wuhu and Sungkiang.
It is estimated that about 8,000 bags
or sometimes 15,000 bags of the grain
are arriving here daily. Prices have
therefore dropped.
This rice, however, comes from
Kiangpeh and is an inferior kind of
the grain. It is called "hsien mei"
but as to the better grade of rice
there has been little improvement in
the situation. The "pai en" or the
first grade rice is still priced between
$32 and $35 per picul.

Lil
C 7/10
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年10月7日

大米局势显示
改善
其他商品更贵，但
粮食变得更便宜

据中文报道，上海的中国银行现已收到重庆经济部的命令，要求扩大“商品抵押”业务的范围，以防止无良商人囤积货物，据说这是导致上海物价上涨的主要原因。据报道，各机构需就此事项向部里提交报告。

与此同时，中文报刊上继续刊登各种商品涨价的广告，但中文报道指出，这里的大米局势已明确好转。虽然目前价格仍然很高，但预计随着供应持续到达，近期不会出现上涨趋势。

浙江、江苏和安徽的新稻米现已上市。商人们已协商好将大米免费运往上海。过去几天，来自昆山、常州、嘉兴、芜湖和松江的大米已通过火车和船只抵达这里。估计每天约有8,000袋，有时甚至15,000袋粮食运抵此处。因此价格有所下降。

然而，这些大米来自江北，属于劣质品种。它被称为“籼米”（hsien mei），但对于优质大米而言，局势几乎没有改善。“白恩”（pai en，音译）或一等大米的价格仍在每担32至35元之间。

Lil
C 7/10

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

OCT 7 1930

Rice Market

A drop of $2 to $1 was registered by
the market yesterday as the result of large
arrivals and small demand. The ship-
ments received consisted of about 4 junk-
loads and 6,000 bags. Best quality Chang-
shu rice remained unchanged at $41, and
first grade quality at $40. Soochow rice
stood at $34, while best quality of newly-
harvested rice was being sold at $32.
Foongking rice was being quoted at $28.
The price of "sharp" rice declined to $24
per picul.
Increased arrivals of provincial rice
depressed the market yesterday. A total
of about 3,500 bags was traded in at
prices ranging from $18 to $20.20. Wuhu
rice stood at $19.50. Kiangpeh rice was
being offered at from $19.70 to $20.20,
while poorer qualities fetched $18 per
picul.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1930年10月7日

大米市场

由于大量到货和需求低迷，昨日市场价格下跌1至2美元。收到的货物包括约4船和6,000袋。优质常熟米价格保持不变，为41美元，一等品质为40美元。苏州米价格为34美元，而新收优质米售价为32美元。奉化米（Foongking rice）报价为28美元。“尖”米（sharp rice）价格跌至每担24美元。

外省大米到货量增加，导致昨日市场低迷。总成交量约为3,500袋，价格在18美元至20.20美元之间。芜湖米价格为19.50美元。江北米报价在19.70美元至20.20美元之间，而较差品质的每担售价为18美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
OCT 7 1989

Flour And Wheat
The market for native flour continued
to rule easy yesterday. As the mills were
still quoting their price at $7 in cash,
trading shifted to the outside market
where brisk business was done at a lower
rate. Blue and red cart brands declined
to $6.75, while Japanese flour was being
sold at $6.40 per bag.
Dull trading was witnessed in the market
for native wheat on account of decreased
buying interest shown by dealers and
mills. The Fooh Sing and Fou Foong
Flour Mills bought only 2,500 bags of
Wuhu and Changshu wheat, the rate being
the same as that of the previous close.
Local dealers absorbed five carloads.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1989年10月7日

面粉与小麦
昨日国产面粉市场持续疲软。由于磨坊仍报价为现金7元，交易转向场外市场，那里以较低价格成交活跃。红蓝车牌面粉跌至6.75元，而日本面粉售价为每袋6.40元。

由于商人和磨坊购买兴趣降低，国产小麦市场交易沉闷。福兴（Fooh Sing）和福丰（Fou Foong）面粉厂仅购买了2,500袋芜湖和常熟小麦，价格与前一日收盘价相同。本地商人吸纳了五车皮。

25468
CHINA PRESS. OCT 6 1939
Rice Market
On account of fresh arrivals the rate
of white rice dropped in yesterday's
market. The supplies received by truck
and rail mounted to 6,000 bags, while no
rice junks arrived. Local dealers were
hesitant to buy and as a result losses
ranged from $1 to $4 per picul. Best
quality Changshu rice declined to $41,
first grade quality was being quoted at
$40, while Soochow rice stood at $37.
Newly-harvested rice of first grade quality
was being offered at $35, and Foong King
rice at $34. First grade "sharp" rice
was being sold at $29, Kiangpeh rice at
$21, and Wuhu rice at $21.50. Poorer
qualities stood at $19.50 per picul.
The market for provincial rice was
ruling weak yesterday with arrivals
amounting to 5,000 bags. The business
transacted amounted to 3,300 bags of
Nanking, Wuhu, and Kiangpeh rice, the
rates varying from $19.50 to $21.50 per
picul.
Liu
Cyo
page_data.zh:
25468
《字林西报》。1939年10月6日
大米市场
由于新鲜货源到达，昨日白米价格下跌。通过卡车和铁路收到的供应量达到6,000袋，而没有米船抵达。本地商人犹豫不决，不愿买入，导致每担损失在1至4美元之间。优质常熟米跌至41美元，一等品质报价为40美元，而苏州米价格为37美元。一等新收米报价为35美元，奉化米（Foong King rice）为34美元。一等“尖”米（sharp rice）售价为29美元，江北米为21美元，芜湖米为21.50美元。较差品质的价格为每担19.50美元。

昨日外省大米市场走势疲软，到货量为5,000袋。南京、芜湖和江北米的成交量为3,300袋，价格在每担19.50美元至21.50美元之间。
Liu
Cyo

page_data.en:
2543
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
OCT 5 1939

More Rice Arriving
In Shanghai
Merchants Act to Prevent
Manipulation

Shanghai rice merchants have made strenuous efforts to obtain a big supply in rice-producing districts in the occupied areas and when the question of obtaining "removal certificates" has been settled the rice they have bought will be transported to this city in large quantities, Chinese reports state. About 5,000 bags of rice have been arriving here from railway districts daily during the past few days and indications are that prices will drop.

Meanwhile, further efforts are being made by rice merchants to regulate the Shanghai rice market so that no merchants can hold transactions outside the market which fact is responsible for the confusion that has troubled the local populace to a great extent during the past few months as manipulators have been active outside the market disregarding the official prices. To this end, representatives of several rice merchants' public bodies met three days ago and drafted a set of regulations. No speculation will be allowed and all merchants must possess rice while carrying out transactions in the market.

Liu
C S
10
page_data.zh:
2543
《字林西报》
1939年10月5日

更多大米运抵
上海
商人采取行动防止
操纵

据中文报道，上海米商已努力在被占领区的产米区获取大量供应，一旦获得“迁移证”的问题得到解决，他们购买的大米将大量运往本市。过去几天，每天约有5,000袋大米从铁路沿线地区运抵此处，迹象表明价格将下跌。

与此同时，米商们正进一步努力规范上海大米市场，以便没有商人可以在市场之外进行交易，这一事实导致了过去几个月严重困扰当地民众的混乱局面，因为操纵者在市场外活动，无视官方价格。为此，几个米商公会的代表三天前开会，起草了一套规章。不允许投机，所有商人在市场进行交易时必须持有实物大米。

Liu
C S
10

page_data.en:
25366
CHINA PRESS.
Aug 4 1939

Rice Market
Easy Despite
Saigon Ban

Prices Register Another
Small Drop As New
Grain Arrives

Despite the export ban on rice
in Saigon, the rice market in
Shanghai yesterday was steady
while the cost of the grain regis-
tered another small decline.
Changshu rice and Soochow rice,
which were quoted respectively at
$40 and $36 per picul, continued
to pour into Shanghai in large
quantities, yesterday's imports to-
talling approximately 20,000 bags.
Together with these two kinds
of rice, large shipments were also
said to be on the way here from far-
ther up the Yangtse River, includ-
ing Wuhu and Hankow. Several
thousand bags of Hankow rice
have already arrived here, it was
learned.
Traders yesterday were unable to
explain the Saigon ban in view of
the record production of the grain
in the French colony. It was re-
garded as likely that the French
Government was reserving the
grain for emergency use, occasioned
by the new European conflict.
Despite the ban, local merchants,
public organizations and residents
continued to sign up with the
Shanghai Chartered Accountants
Association for the purchase of
Saigon rice. Already, registration
for the purchase of more than
15,000 bags has been received, ac-
cording to the Association.
Officials of the Association be-
lieved that the ban would soon be
lifted and that the importation of
Saigon rice would be resumed.

Liu
8/10
page_data.zh:
25366
《字林西报》。
1939年8月4日

大米市场
尽管西贡禁令
行情疲软

随着新粮到达
价格再次小幅
下跌

尽管西贡实施大米出口禁令，上海大米市场昨日保持平稳，而粮食成本再次小幅下降。分别报价为每担40元和36元的常熟米和苏州米继续大量涌入上海，昨日进口总量约为20,000袋。

据悉，除了这两种大米外，还有大量货物正从长江上游包括芜湖和汉口等地运往此处。据了解，已有数千袋汉口米运抵此处。

鉴于该法国殖民地粮食产量创纪录，交易商昨日无法解释西贡禁令。人们认为法国政府很可能因新的欧洲冲突而储备粮食以备紧急之需。

尽管有禁令，本地商人、公共组织和居民继续在上海会计师公会登记购买西贡大米。据该公会称，已收到超过15,000袋的购买登记。

公会官员相信禁令很快会解除，西贡大米的进口将恢复。

Liu
8/10

page_data.en:
25309
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUN 2 1939

Coal Shows Slight
Decrease
Supplies from India Help
To Ease Situation ; Saigon
Rice Ban Reported

The price of coal here is expected
to follow a downward trend since
there is enough coal here for four
months' consumption, says a Chinese
report. Quoting an executive of the
Shanghai Coal Dealers Association,
the report explains that about 40,000
tons of coal is stored in Shanghai
which needs 5,000 tons of coal
monthly for household use.
Recently more than 20,000 tons of
coal arrived here which fact is
responsible for the drop in price by
$4 per ton. In addition to the
newly arrived coal from India, there
is already about 20,000 tons of coal
stored in various shops and open
godowns here, it is stated. It is
pointed out that coal shop managers
already reduced their prices during
the Mid-autumn Festival celebration
when they wanted to obtain as much
cash as possible.

Rice Orders Held Up
Authorities in Saigon have placed
an embargo on rice, which fact has
caused Chinese public bodies and
individuals here to postpone placing
orders with Saigon rice merchants,
it is reported. So far more than
100 Chinese public bodies and
individuals here have signified their
wish to buy 15,718 bags of Saigon
rice.
They have been registering with
the Shanghai Chartered Accountants'
Association for buying the Saigon
rice as prices of the rice here are
too high to be paid. The registration
is still continued and as soon as the
embargo is lifted the association
will notify all registered buyers to
hold a meeting, the report states.
Prices of the first grade rice arriv-
ing here from Qulnsan, Changshu
and Soochow still range between
$37.50 and $42 per picul. According
to the "Shun Pao," most of the rice
from Wuhu has been sent to Hong-
kew. The situation leaves much to
be desired as the rice thus priced is
still beyond the reach of the poor.

（批：Lil. C. 2/10）
page_data.zh:
25309
《字林西报》，
1939年6月2日

煤炭显示轻微
减少
来自印度的供应有助于
缓解局势；据报道
西贡大米禁令

据一份中文报道，由于这里的煤炭足够四个月消耗，预计煤炭价格将呈下降趋势。该报道引用上海煤业公会一位高管的话解释说，上海储存了约40,000吨煤炭，而每月家庭用煤量为5,000吨。

最近有20,000多吨煤炭运抵此处，这导致每吨价格下跌4元。据报道，除了刚从印度运到的煤炭外，这里各家店铺和露天仓库已储存了约20,000吨煤炭。指出的是，煤店经理在中秋节庆祝期间为了尽可能多地获取现金，已经降低了价格。

大米订单受阻

据报道，西贡当局对大米实施禁运，导致这里的中国公共团体和个人推迟向西贡米商下订单。到目前为止，这里有超过100个中国公共团体和个人表示希望购买15,718袋西贡大米。

由于这里的大米价格太高而无法支付，他们一直在上海会计师公会登记购买西贡大米。报道指出，登记仍在继续，一旦禁运解除，公会将通知所有登记买家召开会议。

从昆山、常熟和苏州运抵此处的一等大米价格仍在每担37.50至42美元之间。据《申报》称，大部分芜湖米已送往虹口。局势仍不尽如人意，因为以此价格计算的大米仍然是穷人无法负担的。

（批：Lil. C. 2/10）

page_data.en:
24945

CHINA PRESS.

SEP 18 1939

Chinese Dollar Slump
Sends Prices Up

As a result of the devaluation of
Chinese dollar in the local black
market and the tense situation in
Europe, numerous commodities have
their prices increased during the
month of August, all according to
Shun Pao released by China News
and Views Digest.
According to reports on news-
papers, no less than 162 different
kinds of commodities increased their
prices, representing an increase of
14 when compared with the month
of July.
According to the compilation of
the Shun Pao, of these 162 com-
modities, 48 were foodstuffs, 17
were other daily necessities, 16 were
transportation facilities, 14 were
electric apparatus or metals, 11
were printing and printing articles.
The increase of prices of food-
stuffs have greatly affected the
livelihood of the poor people of this
city. The price of rice increased to
the record high of $50 per picul
during the month. The price of
bean-curd, which was consumed in
large quantities by the poor people
every day increased also.

FILE
(批：8/9)
page_data.zh:
24945

《字林西报》。

1939年9月18日

中国法币暴跌
推高物价

据《新闻文摘》发布的《申报》消息，由于本地黑市中国法币贬值以及欧洲局势紧张，8月份多种商品价格上涨。

据报纸报道，不少于162种不同种类的商品价格上涨，与7月相比增加了14种。

根据《申报》的汇编，在这162种商品中，48种为食品，17种为其他日用品，16种为交通设施，14种为电器或金属，11种为印刷品及印刷器材。

食品价格的大幅上涨极大地影响了本市穷人的生计。本月大米价格涨至每担50元的历史新高。穷人每天大量消费的豆腐价格也上涨了。

档案
（批：8/9）

page_data.en:
September 17, 1939.
Morning Translation.

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Hwa Pao :-

THE RICE SITUATION

Yesterday was the first day of the cheap
sale of the 8,000 bags of foreign rice. The sale
commenced at 8 a.m. By 5 a.m. a large number of people
had already collected at the sale places.
At the first place of cheap sale, 100 bags
of rice were sold by 2 p.m. At the second place, 100
bags of rice were sold by noon, and a second lot of 100
bags was sold by 2 p.m., so a third lot of 100 bags was
issued. The 100 bags of rice at the third place were
sold by noon, but as the situation there was very
disorderly, there was no sale in the afternoon. At the
fourth place, a tragic incident occurred due to
overcrowding of people, and no sale was made in the
afternoon. The 100 bags of rice at the fifth place
were sold by noon.
The 4th place of cheap sale of rice is
located in the Shantung Guild, No. 249, Rue Porto de
l'Ouest in the French Concession, and was undertaken by
the Rice Shop Owners' Guild. The hour was fixed at
8 a.m., but long before that hour, some 5,000 to 6,000
people, including young and old, had already collected
at the place and the policemen could not maintain order.
Some 300 people rushed into the Shantung Guild, whereupon
the policemen hurriedly closed the iron gate. Owing
to the large number of people, the main iron gate of
the building was opened, and the people in front of the
gate fell and great disorder reigned at the place.
People from behind rushed forward and cries were heard
from the people on the ground.
Upon receipt of a report, a large party of
French Police arrived and succeeded in restoring order.
An old woman of about 60 years of age was seriously
injured and died soon afterwards. Two brothers named
Dong Chin-sun (董金生) and Dong Ah-san (董阿三) were
seriously injured in the chest. In addition, many
people received slight injuries or had their clothing torn.
Upon learning of this, Mr. Yu Ya-ching
arrived at the scene to console the injured. The rice
at this place was sold by 3 p.m.
Disorder also occurred at other places.

1939年9月17日。
晨间译件。

《申报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《华报》：

米市情况

昨日是8,000包洋米平价发售的第一天。发售于上午8时开始。至凌晨5时，已有大量人群聚集在各发售点。
在第一处平价发售点，至下午2时已售出100包米。在第二处，至中午已售出100包米，下午2时前又售出第二批100包，因此发出了第三批100包。第三处的100包米于中午前售罄，但因现场秩序极为混乱，下午未再发售。在第四处，因人群过度拥挤发生了一起悲剧事件，下午未进行发售。第五处的100包米于中午前售罄。
第四处米粮平价发售点位于法租界西爱咸斯路（Rue Porto de l'Ouest）249号山东会馆，由米业公会承办。原定时间为上午8时，但在此时间之前很久，已有约五六千名男女老幼聚集在该处，警察无法维持秩序。约300人冲入山东会馆，警察随即匆忙关闭铁门。由于人数众多，大楼的主铁门被打开，门前的人群跌倒，现场陷入极大混乱。后面的人群向前涌去，听到倒地者的哭喊声。
接到报告后，大批法国警察赶到并成功恢复了秩序。一名约60岁的老妇人受重伤，不久后死亡。两名分别名为董金生和董阿三的兄弟胸部受重伤。此外，许多人受轻伤或衣服被撕破。
获悉此事后，虞洽卿先生赶到现场慰问伤者。该处的米于下午3时售完。
其他地点也发生了混乱。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 16 1939

The Food Racket:
More Alleged Profiteering

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—There have been numerous
letters in your paper of late regard-
ing the "rent racket"—but few re-
garding the "food racket" until the
one appearing this morning re a
sugar episode in a Russian store.
How long are the people of this city
prepared to pay the piper of "high
price war on the masses." There are
a "chosen few" in Shanghai who re-
ceive U. S. dollar and sterling salar-
ies—and whilst it is true that in some
cases numerous others have received
some "compensation for the high cost
of living," nevertheless what they
have received is soon swallowed up.
In a little private war of our own we
have been attempting to refrain from
buying Japanese goods in an effort to
help our own country's commodities—
but if the Chinese storekeepers don't
change their tactics—I am afraid that
more and more people will be going
over to Hongkew to make their pur-
chases! Strange how the goose that
lays the golden egg is so often killed
isn't it?
It would be interesting to know
how many others have been victimiz-
ed.
AUSSIE.
Shanghai, Sept. 15.

（批：Recd 16/9）
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年9月16日

食品投机案：
更多涉嫌牟取暴利的指控

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——贵报近期刊登了许多关于“房租投机案”的信件，但关于“食品投机案”的却寥寥无几，直到今早出现了一封关于一家俄国商店糖事件的来信。本市居民准备忍受这种“针对大众的高价战争”还要多久？上海有“少数特权阶层”领取美元和英镑薪水——虽然确实在某些情况下，许多其他人也得到了一些“生活高昂费用的补偿”，然而他们所得到的很快就被消耗殆尽。在我们自己的一场小规模的私人战争中，我们一直试图 refrain from（注：此处原文为英文，意为“避免”）购买日本货，以努力支持本国商品——但如果中国店主不改变他们的策略——我担心会有越来越多的人转去虹口购物！下金蛋的鹅常常被杀掉，这不是很奇怪吗？
若能知道还有多少人受害，将会很有趣。
AUSSIE.
上海，9月15日。

（批注：1939年9月16日收悉）

page_data.en:
September 15, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

China Evening News :-

THE RICE PROBLEM

Up to the present, uneasiness over the problem of food supplies for the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai has not been allayed. A large number of refugees are returning to the interior and the number of vacant houses will be on the increase.

There has been no appreciable decline in the price of rice, although prices usually register a sharp decline with the marketing of the new crop. The public is very much concerned for they do not know whether the stability of the price is due to manipulation by unscrupulous merchants or to cessation of supplies.

Page 472, Volume 39, of the Municipal Gazette, contains some passages explaining the rise in the local cost of living. One of the factors is trade manipulation which has tended to intensify the rise in prices.

As regards rice, a thorough investigation should be conducted to ascertain whether this commodity is being manipulated by unscrupulous merchants. In this connection, the Chinese residents in the Foreign Settlements earnestly hope that the authorities will enforce full control over foodstuffs, thereby maintaining an effective check on prices.

The cheap sale of the 8,000 bags of foreign rice will commence on September 16. It will be undertaken by the Rice Shop Owners' Guild, but the rice will be on sale at 5 places only. On this account, opinion is being expressed that the general public will not benefit. It will be of great help to the poor class of people if the sale is undertaken by all the rice shops.

As matters now stand, the decision of the Rice Shop Owners' Guild is being regarded by a large number of people, as a measure to protect its own interests and to prevent a violent reduction in the price of rice.

It is earnestly hoped that charitable bodies will continue to purchase large quantities of rice to alleviate the sufferings of poor people.
page_data.zh:
1939年9月15日。下午译件。

《大美晚报》：

米荒问题

截至目前，上海公共租界粮食供应问题引起的不安情绪尚未平息。大量难民正返回内地，空置房屋的数量将会增加。

尽管通常在新粮上市时价格会急剧下跌，但米价并未出现明显下降。公众对此非常关切，因为他们不知道价格的稳定是由于奸商操纵还是供应中断所致。

第39卷第472页的《工部局公报》中包含一些解释本地生活成本上升的段落。其中一个因素是商业操纵，这往往加剧了价格上涨。

关于大米，应进行彻底调查，以确定该商品是否正被奸商操纵。在这方面，公共租界的中国居民恳切希望当局对食品实施全面管制，从而有效地抑制价格。

8,000包洋米的平价发售将于9月16日开始。这将由米业公会承办，但仅在5个地点发售。鉴于此，有舆论表示普通民众将无法受益。如果由所有米店进行发售，将对贫困阶层大有裨益。

就目前情况而言，米业公会的决定被许多人视为保护自身利益并防止米价剧烈下跌的措施。

恳切希望慈善团体继续购买大量大米，以减轻穷人的苦难。

page_data.en:
TAIRIKU SHIMPO 14.9.39

CHINESE MOSQUITO PAPERS SUSPENDED BY S.M.C.

A number of Chinese mosquito
papers which have been well received by many Chinese
residents in the Foreign Settlements on the south side
of the creek, are reported to have been suspended by
the S.M.C. The action of the S.M.C. is likely to
give rise to an issue over the question of the freedom
of publication for such freedom is being improperly
suppressed by the S.M.C. which seems to have some sort
of understanding with unscrupulous rice dealers.
At the end of August the
"Crystal" and the "Wei Pao" were ordered to suspend
publication; on September 3, the Cheng Pao"; on September 12,
the "Shanghai Daily News". All these newspapers were
ordered to suspend publication for 20 days. This is a
death sentence to these small papers because they were
already in financial difficulties.
These papers were suspended because
they had published articles exposing the evil conduct of
rice dealers who had secretly purchased rice with a view
to raising the price, especially as the papers published
true reports regarding the activities of the Bank of
China, the Central Bank of China, and of Wu Wen Tsai,
general manager of the King Chung Bank, Tsu Hsu Tang,
manager of the Shanghai Bank, who had stocked large
quantities of rice, in disregard of the hardships
of the poor class people. Between the Special Branch
of the S.M.P. and the above mentioned bankers some sort
of secret transaction is reported to have been made.
The unduly strong measures
adopted by the S.M.C. to suppress the mosquito papers
in compliance with the wish of some evil merchants are
being criticized because the S.M.C. has all along shown
its insincerity regarding the suppression of newspapers
which are publishing anti-Japanese articles, under the
pretext that freedom of publication must be respected.
page_data.zh:
《大陆新报》 1939年9月14日

工部局查封中文小报

据报道，工部局已查封数份在苏州河以南公共租界受到许多中国居民欢迎的中文小报。工部局的这一行动可能会引发关于出版自由的问题，因为这种自由正遭到工部局的不当压制，而工部局似乎与不法米商达成了某种默契。
8月底，《晶报》和《威报》被勒令停刊；9月3日，《诚报》；9月12日，《上海日报》。所有这些报纸均被勒令停刊20天。这对这些小报来说是死刑判决，因为它们已经处于财务困境中。
这些报纸被停刊是因为它们发表了揭露米商恶行的文章，这些米商秘密收购大米以抬高价格，特别是因为这些报纸发布了关于中国银行、中央银行以及京钟银行总经理吴文哉、上海银行经理徐旭堂囤积大量大米、不顾贫困阶层疾苦的真实报道。据报道，工部局警务处政治部与上述银行家之间进行了某种秘密交易。
工部局顺应一些不良商人的意愿，采取过分严厉的措施压制小报，此举正受到批评，因为工部局一直以必须尊重出版自由为借口，对刊登反日文章的报纸表现出镇压上的不诚意。

page_data.en:
September 14, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:

THE RICE SITUATION

The first batch of foreign rice, consisting
of 18,000 bags, ordered by various public bodies from
Saigon, has arrived in Shanghai. 10,000 bags will
be used for the relief of refugees, the remainder to be
sold at a cheap price by the Rice Trade Guild.
Interviewed by a reporter of the Sing Sing
News Agency (新声社) yesterday, Chang Yen-hsi
(张鑫培), Chairman of the Rice Trade Guild, stated that
five cheap rice sales depots in the Foreign Settlements,
to which necessary alterations had been completed, would
start functioning on September 16.
At the request of various public bodies, the
Chartered Accountants' Guild recently undertook the
registration of persons desiring to purchase foreign rice.
Up to yesterday, 11,000 bags of rice to be ordered from
Saigon were registered.
The public are of opinion that the purchase
of foreign rice and sale of same at a cheap price will
prove much help to the relief of poor people. As there
appears only a slight fall in the price of rice, and the
serious situation has not yet been completely remedied,
it is hoped that orders of foreign rice will be continued
and that cheap rice sales depots will be established in
as many places as possible. By so doing, not only poor
people will enjoy great benefit in the purchase of rice,
but the price of rice will fall. At present no sign of
an appreciable fall in the price of rice is apparent.
An investigation should be made so as to ascertain whether
there are persons manipulating the rice market.
As a result of the market manipulation by rice
merchants, the Japanese authorities have issued a
proclamation at Wusih, Changshu, Soochow and Quinsan to
the effect that the ban on the transportation of rice
supplies has been lifted and that merchants are allowed
to transport freely.
However, since heavy taxes are imposed on
rice supplies to be transported, rice merchants are
finding it difficult to keep prices down.

The "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" of September 13
reports that owing to manipulation and hoarding on the part
of certain persons as well as interference by Japanese
authorities with rice boats coming to Shanghai, the
question of rice supplies has become more serious for there
is no sign of a drop in the price of rice despite the
efforts of charitable organizations and the authorities of
the Foreign Settlements in purchasing foreign rice and in
regulating rice supplies. Unless ways and means are
devised to relieve the situation, the situation may
become dangerous.
Local benevolent associations and public bodies
have submitted a joint petition to the authorities of the
Foreign Settlements requesting that negotiations be opened
with the Japanese authorities for the free passage of rice
boats to Shanghai. At the same time, arrangements are
being made for the further purchase of rice from abroad.
Local public bodies are also making an investigation into
the manipulation and hoarding of rice by traitorous
merchants and requests will be made to the authorities of
the Foreign Settlements to adopt effective measures
to deal with these elements.
page_data.zh:
1939年9月14日。下午译件。

《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《申报》、《华报》：

米市情况

由各公共团体从西贡订购的第一批共计18,000包洋米已抵达上海。其中10,000包将用于救济难民，其余部分将由米业公会平价出售。
米业公会主席张鑫培昨日接受新声社记者采访时表示，公共租界内五个已完成必要改造的平价米店将于9月16日开始营业。
应各公共团体的要求，会计师公会最近承担了登记欲购买洋米人员的工作。截至昨日，已登记将从西贡订购的米量达11,000包。
公众认为，购买洋米并平价出售将对救济穷人大有帮助。由于米价仅略有下降，严峻局势尚未完全缓解，希望继续订购洋米，并尽可能多地设立平价米店。这样做，不仅穷人在购米方面将获得巨大利益，米价也会下降。目前，米价尚未出现明显下跌的迹象。应进行调查，以确定是否有人操纵米市。
由于米商的市場操纵，日本当局已在无锡、常熟、苏州和昆山发布公告，宣布解除对米粮运输的禁令，允许商人自由运输。
然而，由于对运输中的米粮征收重税，米商发现难以压低价格。

9月13日的《华美晚报》报道称，由于某些人的操纵和囤积，以及日本当局对驶往上海的米船进行干扰，粮食供应问题变得更加严重，尽管慈善组织和公共租界当局努力购买洋米并调节粮食供应，但米价仍无下降迹象。除非想出办法缓解局势，否则情况可能会变得危险。
本地慈善团体和公共团体已向公共租界当局提交联合请愿书，请求与日本当局就米船自由通行至上海一事展开谈判。同时，正在安排进一步从国外购买大米。
本地公共团体也在调查汉奸米商对大米的操纵和囤积行为，并将要求公共租界当局采取有效措施对付这些分子。

CHINA PRESS
SEP 12 1939

Rice Market

Prices in the rice market yesterday
opened strong, and gains of $1 were
recorded. Trading interest, however, was
seen to narrow down, causing the rate
to decline $0.50 for best quality. While
only 5 rice junks arrived yesterday, 6,000
bags were brought in from various pro-
ducing districts. A total of 7,000 bags
was sold to local rice dealers. Best
quality Changshu rice was being sold at
$39.50 per picul, while first grade Chang-
shu rice remained unchanged at $38.
Kaishing newly-harvested rice was being
offered at $37, and second qualities fetched
$32.
After opening firm the market for
provincial rice was subsequently depressed
by the arrivals of 5,000 bags of newly-
harvested Kiangpeh rice and a consider-
able amount from Wuhu and Nanking.
At the final bell the rates registered
losses from $0.30 to $0.50 per picul. The
turnover amounted to 8,000 bags of rice.
Wuhu rice was being quoted at $28, or
$0.50 below last Saturday's final rate,
and Kiangpeh newly-harvested rice stood
at from $25.50 to $27.

《大美晚报》
1939年9月12日

米市

昨日米市开盘强劲，录得1美元涨幅。然而，交易兴趣趋于狭窄，导致优质米价格回落0.50美元。虽然昨日仅有5艘米船抵达，但从各产区运入6,000包米。共计7,000包米售予本地米商。优质常熟米售价为每担39.50美元，而一级常熟米价格保持不变，为38美元。嘉兴新米报价为37美元，二等米成交价为32美元。
外省米市场开盘坚挺，随后因5,000包江北新米以及来自芜湖和南京的大量大米到货而受压。收盘时，价格每担下跌0.30至0.50美元。成交量为8,000包米。芜湖米报价为28美元，比上周六最终收盘价低0.50美元，江北新米价格在25.50至27美元之间。

8039A/15
6 9 39

Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao 1- 5.9.39 PM

SUDDEN RISE IN THE PRICE OF RICE

After the arrival at Shanghai of the news of outbreak of war in Europe, the condition of the rice market here grew tense. Rice hoarders thought that after the outbreak of war in Europe, there would be a difficulty in obtaining foreign rice in Shanghai and therefore the price would rise. The rice shops purchased large quantities of rice and as a result the price of rice went up by $5 per picul, to $35 for first grade rice and $32 per picul of "see mee".

Upon being questioned by a reporter, Mr.Wu Zien-kung (符前耕), Chairman of the Rice Market Control Committee, expressed the opinion that the rise in the price of rice yesterday was caused only by speculation which could not be suppressed by the Committee. It was also said that when the people were calmer, the market would naturally stabilize.

As the nations in the Orient are adopting a neutral attitude towards the European War, the purchase of foreign rice will not be obstructed. Besides the Norwegian vessels that are carrying rice also belong to a neutral Power. The first batch of 18,000 bags of foreign rice coming to Shanghai has already passed Hongkong.

Another quarter reports that on September 2, 4,000 bags of rice dispatched to Shanghai from Hangchow by rail was detained by the Japanese in Hongkew. This rice was sold under compulsion to the Japanese at $20 per picul, thus the rice dealers had reluctantly to sacrifice the rice at a price below the cost.

Up to the present, a requisition for 4,286 bags of foreign rice has been registered for purchase with the Chartered Accountants Guild by various concerns.

5
8039A/15
6 9 39

《中美日报》、《申报》、《新闻报》 1939年9月1日至5日下午

米价突然上涨

欧洲爆发战争的消息传至上海后，本地米市形势趋于紧张。米商囤积者认为，欧洲战事爆发后，上海将难以获得洋米，因此价格会上涨。米店大量购进大米，导致米价每石上涨5元，一等米涨至每石35元，“西米”（see mee）涨至每石32元。

米业同业公会主席吴前耕先生（音译）在接受记者询问时表示，昨日米价上涨纯属投机行为所致，公会无法压制。据称，待民众情绪平复后，市场自然会稳定。

由于东方各国对欧洲战争采取中立态度，购买洋米不会受到阻碍。此外，运载大米的挪威船只也属于中立国。首批运抵上海的18,000袋洋米已通过香港。

另有消息报道，9月2日，由杭州经铁路发往上海的4,000袋大米被日军在虹口扣留。这批大米被迫以每石20元的价格卖给日本人，因此米商不得不亏本忍痛出售。

截至目前，各商号已向会计师公会登记申请购买洋米4,286袋。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
SEP 1 1939.

Cost Lowest
Since Recent
Price Crisis

S.M.C. Denies Rumors
Of Heavy Holdings
Of Cereal

CO-OPERATION OF
JAPANESE LAUDED

Council Said Paying
Special Attention
To City's Poor

The price of rice yesterday sank
to a new low since the recent price
crisis when the $31-per-picul mark
was registered in local grain
markets.
The downward trend was first
noted earlier this week when over
the weekend large shipments of
rice reached Shanghai from the
rice growing areas.
Timely relief from Chungking
further relieved the tension here
when the National Government
purchased 18,000 bags of Saigon
rice with £10,000 supplied to dealers
here at the Government rate of ex-
change.
Ban Relaxed
Since the ban on rice export from
the growing areas was relaxed by
the Japanese, it was stated in in-
formed quarters, the stock of the
grain in the Settlement has greatly
increased.
A slight setback was said to have
been suffered by the rice market
here during the past few days when
the storm prevented the regular
arrival of the grain from Wuhu,
Changshu and other parts of
Kiangsu and Chekiang provinces.
But both officials of the Shanghai
Municipal Council and rice dealers
gave assurances that new ship-
ments will reach Shanghai with
the return of good weather.
Statement Issued
In an official statement yesterday,
the Council denied rumors that the
Council had large quantities of rice
at its disposal. It also discredit-
ed earlier reports that the price of
rice had been forced up as a result
of private hoarding.
Commenting on the proposal
that the Council import rice from
foreign producing areas for the
relief of the tension here, the Coun-
cil stated:
"Circumstances have been very
different from 1937 when the
Council imported rice from Saigon.
The importation at the ruling rate
of exchange of a sufficient quantity
of rice to supply Shanghai for any
considerable period would have in-
volved serious financial risk."

（批：Liu C¼）
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年9月1日

自近期
价格危机以来
成本降至最低

工部局否认
持有大量谷物
的谣言

赞扬日本方面
的合作

据悉工部局正特别关注
本市贫民

昨日，随着本地粮市录得每石31元的价格，米价跌至近期价格危机以来的新低。
本周早些时候已注意到这一下跌趋势，当时周末有大量大米从产米区运抵上海。
重庆方面的及时救济进一步缓解了这里的紧张局势，国民政府购买了18,000袋西贡米，并按政府汇率向本地经销商提供了10,000英镑。
禁令放宽
据知情人士称，自从日本方面放宽了对产米区的大米出口禁令后，租界内的粮食库存已大幅增加。
据说过去几天本地米市遭受了轻微挫折，风暴阻碍了来自芜湖、常熟以及江苏和浙江其他地区的粮食定期运抵。
但上海公共租界工部局官员和米商均保证，随着天气好转，新的大批货物将运抵上海。
发表声明
工部局在昨日的一份官方声明中，否认了有关工部局掌握大量大米的谣言。它还驳斥了早先关于米价因私人囤积而被推高的报道。
在评论有关工部局从国外产区进口大米以缓解本地紧张局势的提议时，工部局表示：
“情况与1937年工部局从西贡进口大米时大不相同。按现行汇率进口足够供应上海相当长一段时间的大米，将涉及严重的财务风险。”

（批注：Liu C¼）

page_data.en:
Representations Made
"Moreover, it has throughout the
period of crisis been clear that the
only solution of the problem was a
free supply of rice from the hinter-
land. Representations were ac-
cordingly made to the Japanese
authorities to facilitate the im-
portation of rice from areas under
their control.
"These representations obtained
sympathetic co-operation and have
already resulted in a mark
amelioration of what was becoming
a grave situation.
"The Council has throughout the
period of anxiety maintained re-
gular contact with all bodies and
persons who were likely to be able
to assist in implementing the arrival
of rice into Shanghai. The co-
operation of those to whom the
Council has appealed for help is
gratefully acknowledged.
Poor Affected
"The steep rise in prices na-
turally weighed most heavily on the
poorer classes of the Chinese com-
munity. To this aspect of the
problem the Chinese members of
the Council have naturally devoted
special attention, and in particular
one of their members (Mr. Yu Y
Ching) arranged for the financing
of a shipment of 1,800 tons of
Saigon rice to meet the immediate
needs of the refugees and poorer
classes."
The Council specifically com-
mented on the complete co-opera-
tion which it had received from
the French authorities here.
page_data.zh:
提出交涉
“此外，在整个危机期间，很明显，解决这一问题的唯一办法是来自内地的自由大米供应。因此，向日方当局提出交涉，要求便利从其控制区进口大米。
“这些交涉获得了同情的合作，并已使原本日益严峻的局势得到显著改善。
“在焦虑期间，工部局一直与所有可能有助于实现大米运抵上海的组织和个人保持定期联系。对于向工部局提供援助的那些人的合作，谨表感激。
贫民受影响
“价格的急剧上涨自然对中国社区较贫困阶层的影响最为沉重。工部局华董自然特别关注问题的这一方面，其中一位董事（余亚庆先生）特别安排融资运送1,800吨西贡米，以满足难民和贫困阶层的迫切需求。”
工部局特别评论了其在此地获得的法国当局的全面合作。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

SEP 1 1939

CHEAP RICE BY CITY
GOVERNMENT

Special Arrangement To
Sell 450 Piculs Each
Day At $15

The following information has been received from the office of Mayor Fu Siao-en of the City Government of Greater Shanghai:
"At present, the effect of the accumulation and hoarding of rice by the profiteers, in order to raise the price of rice as high as forty to fifty dollars local currency per picul, has made the scarcity of food a vital problem of the multitude. Mayor Fu Siao-en has had great sympathy and understanding to such hardship of the community so he has given strict orders to all the rice merchants that no hoarding and accumulating of rice for profiteering purposes is allowed to be carried out under his jurisdiction and that the sale price of the rice should not be in access of more than fifteen dollars per picul. Such policy has been approved by the Japanese Authorities to avail the transportation facilities from the rice growing districts in order to standardize the price of rice to a moderate level. Sincere promise and hearty co-operation to work for the general welfare have been secured so that the multitude of the community will not be hard pressed by the costly price and scarcity of this daily staple commodities.
"There will be hundred thousands of piculs of native rice to be imported from time to time from the different rice producing districts. The first shipment of rice from Wuhu has already arrived to this City yesterday. The City Government of the Greater Shanghai has got the allotment of 450 piculs of rice which has been transferred to the Bureau of Social Affairs for cheap sale. Thus, the selling price of the said rice, will be fifteen dollars per picul. Anybody may purchase 5 shen every day and the selling price is limited to 15 cents per shen. This daily cheap sale of such alloted 450 piculs of rice will be carried out by the Bureau of Social Affairs of the City Government of Greater Shanghai as long as the shipments are available. All the subsidiary expenses for the transportation of the said rice will be borne by the Japanese Authorities.
"At this critical moment, the price of the rice is at its high pitch. Now there will be a constant supply of great quantity of rice to Shanghai every day so that the evil practice of hoarding and accumulation of this staple commodity will leave no effect to the market and the trend of lowering the sales price can be readily predicted The lowering of the price and the getting of a constant supply of rice by Mayor Fu Siao-en and the sincere assistance and hearty co-operation of the Japanese Authorities will no doubt be highly appreciated by the community of Greater Shanghai."
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》

1939年9月1日

市政府提供
廉价大米

特别安排每日
以15元价格出售
450石

以下信息收自大上海特别市政府市长傅筱庵办公室：
“目前，奸商为了将米价抬高至每石四十至五十元法币而囤积居奇，导致粮食短缺成为广大民众的重大问题。傅筱庵市长对社区的这种苦难深表同情和理解，因此严令其管辖范围内的所有米商不得为牟取暴利而囤积大米，且大米售价不得超过每石十五元。此项政策已获日本当局批准，以便利用产米区的运输设施，将米价稳定在适度水平。已获得真诚承诺和热心合作，致力于公共福利，从而使广大社区民众不再受此日常主食高昂价格和短缺的重压。
“将有数十万石国产大米不时从不同产米区进口。首批来自芜湖的大米已于昨日抵达本市。大上海特别市政府已获得450石大米的配额，并已移交社会局进行平价销售。因此，上述大米的售价为每石十五元。任何人每天可购买5升，售价限制为每升15分。只要货源充足，大上海特别市政府社会局将持续进行这每日450石配给大米的平价销售。上述大米运输的所有附属费用均由日本当局承担。
“在此关键时刻，米价处于高位。现在每天将有大量大米持续供应上海，因此囤积居奇这一恶习将对市场不再产生影响，且销售价格下降的趋势可以预见。傅筱庵市长降低米价并确保大米持续供应，以及日本当局的真诚协助和热心合作，无疑将得到大上海社区的高度赞赏。”

page_data.en:
CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 1 1939

Rice Price Fixed
By City Govt.
Large Shipments of
Staple Food Said
Arriving Here

The price of rice has been fixed
at $15 per picul in all territories
under the control of the "City Gov-
ernment of Greater Shanghai", ac-
cording to a statement issued by
Mayor Fu Siao-en's offices yesterday,
and individual purchases may not
exceed five shen per day at a price
of 15 cents per shen

Hundreds of thousands piculs of
rice will be brought to Shanghai
from the Interior from time to time,
the statement continues and the
Bureau of Social affairs of the City
Government will continue to sell at
a cheap price as long as the present
amount which has been allotted for
this purpose, lasts.

All expenses connected with the
transportation of the rice to Shang-
hai from the Interior, the statement,
continues, will be borne by the Japan-
ese military authorities who are co-
operating fully with Mr. Fu Siao-en
in his attempt to alleviate the seri-
ous condition of the local rice
market.
page_data.zh:
《中国日报》

1939年9月1日

市政府固定
米价
据悉大量主食
正运抵此处

根据傅筱庵市长办公室昨日发表的声明，在“大上海特别市政府”控制的所有地区，米价已固定为每石15元，个人购买量每天不得超过5升，价格为每升15分。

声明继续称，将有数十万石大米不时从内地运抵上海，只要为此目的分配的现有数量尚存，市政府社会局将继续以低价出售。

声明接着称，将大米从内地运至上海的所有相关费用将由日本军方承担，他们正与傅先生充分合作，试图缓解本地米市的严峻状况。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

SEP 1 1939

Flour And Wheat

The business in native wheat was dull
in yesterday's market, and the selling
price remained unchanged at $6.20 per
bag of second-rate product. The dealers
were reluctant to buy for their stocks,
as they had a large amount of this flour
in hands. The selling rate in the outside
market has been irregularly low during
the last few days with outport dealers
reluctant to buy so that the selling price
fell further to $5.95. While the North
China dealers were not interested in
further shipments during the flood in
Tientsin. With reference to the cheaper
rate of native wheat, the rate of native
flour was expected to drop in a day or
two according to a report from the mar-
ket yesterday.
On account of a limited production of
native flour by the local Chinese flour
mills, the price of native wheat continued
dull in the market yesterday. The wheat
holders refused to sell their goods at a
low rate, but the buyers and Chinese flour
mills were not in the market, so that no
official rate was quoted in the session.
The Japanese dealers and flour mills
bought a considerable amount of this
wheat at $8.57, or $0.80 below the pre-
vious final rate.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年9月1日

面粉与小麦

昨日市场上国产小麦交易清淡，二等品售价保持在每袋6.20元不变。经销商不愿补货，因为他们手中已有大量此类面粉。过去几天，外埠市场的售价不规则地偏低，外地经销商不愿购买，导致售价进一步跌至5.95元。鉴于天津发生洪水，华北经销商对进一步发货不感兴趣。关于国产小麦价格较低的情况，据昨日市场报告，预计国产面粉价格在一两天内将会下跌。
由于本地华商面粉厂国产面粉产量有限，昨日市场上国产小麦价格持续低迷。持麦者拒绝低价出售货物，但买家和华商面粉厂未入市，因此该时段未报出官方价格。日本经销商和面粉厂以8.57元的价格购买了相当数量的小麦，比前一最终价格低0.80元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

SEP 1 1939

Rice Market

The selling rate of white rice was irregularly low in the early session at yesterday's market, because the market has received 6,000 bags of fresh rice supplies from the growing centers in the interior, and another 400 bags of white rice were transported here by steamer. No demand was seen for purchases, and the rate fell by $1 per picul as compared with the preceding day's final closing rate.
The local dealers bought a considerable amount of this rice, and the retail shops purchased a small quantity of rice for selling, while the selling rate moved up by $0.50. As a result, the best quality of Changshu white rice was quoted at $31.50 per picul; Wuh white rice sold at $29; Quinsan white rice noted at $28 and the low-grade white rice sold at $25 per picul. The total sales in the day were estimated at a few thousand bags of different kinds of white rice.
Because of over-supplies of fresh provincial rice in the market yesterday, the rice holders submitted to the market for selling, while the buyers were uninterested to buy in the morning session. The selling price dropped by $2 for liquidation. The local dealers bought fractionally and trading for the retail shops was very dull. The business done in the day amounted to 3,000 bags of various kinds of provincial rice. The newly-harvested Kiangsu provincial rice was liquidated at $24; Kaishing newly-harvested provincial rice sold at $22; Wuhu stocked provincial rice stood at $25 and the low-grade of provincial rice dropped to $18.70 per picul.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年9月1日

米市

昨日市场早盘白米售价不规则走低，因为市场收到了来自内地产粮中心的6,000袋新鲜大米供应，另有400袋白米由轮船运抵此处。未见采购需求，价格较前一日最终收盘价每石下跌1元。
本地经销商购买了相当数量的大米，零售店购买了少量大米用于销售，随后售价上涨了0.50元。结果，最好的常熟白米报价为每石31.50元；芜湖白米售价29元；昆山白米 noted at 28元（注：原文如此，意为报价28元），低级白米售价为每石25元。当日总销量估计为数千袋各类白米。
由于昨日市场上外省新米供应过剩，持米者提交市场出售，而买家在上午时段无意购买。抛售导致价格下跌2元。本地经销商零星购买，零售店交易非常清淡。当日成交量为3,000袋各类外省米。新收获的江苏省米以24元清算；嘉兴新收获外省米售价22元；芜湖库存外省米维持在25元，低级外省米跌至每石18.70元。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

SEP 1 1939

Dr. H. H. Kung, President of the
Executiv. Yuan, has authorized the
civic organizations in Shanghai to
purchase 20,000 piculs of Saigon
rice to relieve the urgent food
shortage in Shanghai. He has
granted foreign exchange allotment
amounting to £10,000, at the
official rate, to finance the shipment.
Dr. Kung has also agreed to exempt
duty on arrival at Shanghai. The
arrangements were made through
Messrs. Yu Ya-ching, Li Ming and
other Shanghai civic leaders.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》

1939年9月1日

行政院院长孔祥熙博士已授权上海的民间组织购买20,000石西贡米，以缓解上海紧迫的粮食短缺。他已按官方汇率批准了总计10,000英镑的外汇配额，以资助此次运输。
孔博士还同意免除抵达上海时的关税。这些安排是通过虞洽卿、李明及其他上海民间领袖进行的。

page_data.en:
Eastern Times, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Central China Daily
News, Chinese-American Daily News :- 31.8.39(PM)

THE PURCHASE OF SAIGON RICE

To relieve the rice situation, Messrs Yu
Ya-ching, Li Min and Hsu Chi-ching sent a telegram to
Dr. H.H. Kung, President of the Executive Yuan, requesting
an allotment of exchange at the rate quoted by the
Central Bank of China and the Bank of Communications for
the purchase of 20,000 bags of foreign rice. In reply
Dr. Kung approved the request and in addition waived the
import duty. For this, the people are grateful to the
National Government.

During the past few days, many concerns
and trade guilds have registered their rice requirements
with the Chartered Accountants' Society in the Pootung

Guild Building for the purchase of foreign rice. The
Accountant's Society will pay at the rate
of 7d. to the dollars but at the exchange rate prevailing
in the unlawful exchange market in Shanghai.

Yesterday a reporter called on Mr. Yu Ya-ching
and asked him about the purchase of foreign rice.
Mr. Yu made the following statement :-
"I personally can see a shortage of food supplies in
Shanghai. The authorities should regulate the importation
of rice and the price should also be lowered to enable
poor people to buy. Now the first consignment of
foreign rice is being shipped by Norwegian vessels from
Saigon for Shanghai and will arrive here in about 8 or
9 days. The proper price of this rice should be $30 per
picul but it has cost only a little over $20 because of
the favourable exchange. About 10,000 bags will be
used for the relief of refugees and the remaining 8,000
bags will be sold by rice merchants at cheap prices.
I have also advised various trades to purchase foreign
rice so that the present consignment may last some time.
The second consignment of rice will be purchased when the
amount registered by various public/reaches 20,000 bags."
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《华中日报》、《中美日报》：1939年8月31日（下午）

购买西贡大米

为缓解米荒，虞洽卿、李敏和徐寄庼三位先生致电行政院院长孔祥熙博士，请求按中国银行和交通银行所报汇率拨付外汇，用于购买两万包洋米。孔博士复电批准该请求，并额外免除进口关税。民众对此对国民政府深表感激。

过去数日，许多商号和同业公会在浦东公会大楼的会计师公会登记了购买洋米的所需数量。会计师公会将以每美元7便士的比率支付，但汇率参照上海非法外汇市场的现行汇率。

昨日，一名记者拜访了虞洽卿先生，询问有关购买洋米的情况。虞先生发表如下声明：“我个人看到上海食品供应短缺。当局应管制大米进口，价格也应降低，以便穷人能够购买。目前第一批洋米正由挪威船只从西贡运往上海，预计约8或9天后抵达此处。这批大米的合理价格应为每担30元，但由于汇率有利，成本仅略高于20元。其中约一万包将用于救济难民，其余八千包将由米商以低价出售。我也建议各行业购买洋米，以便使目前的这批货物能维持一段时间。当各方登记的总量达到两万包时，将购买第二批大米。”

page_data.en:
August 30, 1939.

MAINICHI

PRICE OF RICE DECLINING : SUCCESS OF TIMELY
MEASURES BY JAPANESE AUTHORITIES ; S.M.C. STARTS
ADJUSTMENT OF RICE SUPPLY

Due to desperate efforts made by various
authorities concerned, the importation of rice from the
interior is being gradually resumed. The public demand
will be met whilst the price of rice is decreasing day
by day, to our great satisfaction.

Having become conscious of the discontent
of the populace, the S.M.C. recently convened a meeting
of the Municipal Council and the Food Affairs Committee.
They discussed the matter of food supply and issued a
proclamation to the effect that the S.M.C. had found
that the report of large stocks of rice being hoarded
was a complete fabrication; at the same time, they set
out to bring about the transportation of rice from the
interior.

Thus, the unprecedented high price of rice
has now been checked by the effective measures taken by
our authorities, the Shanghai City Government and the
S.M.C.
page_data.zh:
1939年8月30日。

《每日新闻》

米价下跌：日本当局及时措施奏效；工部局开始调整大米供应

由于各有关当局的竭力努力，从内地进口大米正逐渐恢复。公众需求将得到满足，同时米价逐日下降，令我们深感欣慰。

意识到民众的不满情绪后，工部局最近召开了市议会和粮食委员会会议。他们讨论了粮食供应问题，并发布公告称，工部局发现关于大量囤积大米的报道纯属捏造；与此同时，他们着手安排从内地运输大米。

因此，前所未有的高米价现已因我方当局、上海市政府和工部局采取的有效措施而得到遏制。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

AUG 30 1939

Price Of Rice
Drops To $36

Committee For Control
Of Staple Food
In Formation

Announcement by the Shanghai
Municipal Council that rice ship-
ments into Shanghai would again
function normally following the
cooperation of the Japanese mili-
tary authorities, and fears that
the present "typhoon season"
which usually lasts until mid-
September might cause "cargo-
damages", were contributing causes
toward a further decline of from
two to four dollars in the price
of rice, with this morning's prices
quoted around $36 per picul for
first grade rice.

In a formal statement issued
to the local press yesterday, the
SMC declared that rice has been
entering Shanghai during the past
few days at a sufficient rate to
cater to the city's normal con-
sumption, which is approximately
10,000 piculs per week.

A denial was issued in the state-
ment that the SMC had made pur-
chases of rice stocks, while rumors
that rice had been hoarded by pri-
vate interests in the Settlement
was also refuted in the statement.

According to the communique, a
rice dealers' guild is likely to be
formed shortly as a result of
negotiations between the Japanese
Residents' Corporation, the Jap-
anese Chamber of Commerce and
Industry and local Japanese rice
merchants.

（批：80349/5(8)）
（批：Lile C 31/8）
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1939年8月30日

米价
跌至36元

主食管制
委员会
正在组建

上海公共租界工部局宣布，在日本军方的合作下，运入上海的大米 shipments 将再次正常运行；加之人们担心通常持续至九月中旬的当前“台风季节”可能导致“货物受损”，这些因素共同促使米价进一步下跌两至四元，今晨一级大米的报价约为每担36元。

在昨日向本地媒体发布的正式声明中，工部局宣称，过去几天进入上海的大米数量足以满足城市正常消费，即每周约一万担。

声明中否认了工部局曾购买大米库存的说法，同时也驳斥了有关租界内私人利益集团囤积大米的谣言。

据公报称，作为日本居留民团、日本商会及工业会以及当地日本米商之间谈判的结果，一个米业同业公会可能很快成立。

（批注：80349/5(8)）
（批注：Lile C 31/8）

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

AUG 31 1939

Price Of Rice
Drops As Kung
Grants Relief

Grain Quoted At $36
Per Picul In City
During Day

Timely relief from Dr. H. H.
Kung, President of the Executive
Yuan and concurrently Minister of
Finance, yesterday caused the
price of rice here to drop another
$2. The price was quoted at $36
per picul.

The relief came in the form of a
special sanction granted to local
rice dealers by Dr. Kung, which
allows the purchase of 20,000 bags
of Saigon rice with £10,000 supplied
to them at the Government rate of
exchange.

The same sanction also provided
that the rice might be imported to
Shanghai duty free.

According to Reuter, Dr. H. H.
Kung, in granting the exchange,
blamed the Japanese for having
caused the rice crisis here. Japanese
authorities were said to have inter-
fered with the transportation of
foodstuffs to Shanghai and have
caused the overpopulation of this
city as a result of their invasion of
Kiangsu and Chekiang.

Dr. Kung also pointed out, Reuter
said, that while Shanghai is facing
a shortage of rice, the Chinese
Government is worrying about the
slump in the rice price in "free"
China, on account of good harvests.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1939年8月31日

随着孔氏
提供救济
米价下跌

日间市内
谷物报价
为每担36元

行政院院长兼财政部长孔祥熙博士昨日提供的及时救济，导致此地米价再跌2元。报价为每担36元。

此项救济的形式是孔博士给予本地米商的一项特别许可，允许他们以政府汇率获得的1万英镑资金，购买两万包西贡大米。

同一许可还规定，该批大米可免税进口至上海。

据路透社报道，孔祥熙博士在批准外汇时，指责日本人造成了此地的米荒危机。据说日本当局干扰了运往上海的粮食运输，并因其入侵江苏和浙江而导致本市人口过剩。

路透社称，孔博士还指出，虽然上海面临大米短缺，但中国政府正因丰收而担忧“自由”中国地区的米价暴跌。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
AUG 31 1939

Rice Conditions
Grow Better
Dr. H. H. Kung to Provide
Exchange for Purchase of
Supplies From Saigon

As a new encouraging factor in the
serious rice situation in Shanghai,
Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance
at Chungking, has replied to a tele-
gram recently sent by Chinese civic
leaders here allowing them to obtain
£10,000 foreign exchange at the
Government rate for buying Saigon
rice for the public here. Dr. Kung
mentions in his telegram that 20,000
piculs of Saigon rice should be
quickly bought to relieve the situa-
tion Customs duty is also exempted.

Dr. Kung shows great concern over
the populace here expressing the
opinion that the rice shortage in
Shanghai is a result of the restric-
tions placed on transportation by the
Japanese and "puppets." He asserts
that a good rice crop has been re-
ported from both Chekiang and
Kiangsu. He suggests that with the
£10,000 foreign exchange granted by
him Chinese public bodies in Shang-
hai should purchase 20,000 piculs of
Saigon rice jointly.

The Minister's reply has been re-
ceived by Messrs. Yu Ya-ching,
doyen of Chinese members of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, Li Ming,
of Shanghai Bankers Association and
Hsu Chi-chuan, acting chairman of
Chinese Ratepayers Association of the
International Settlement who jointly
telegraphically petitioned Dr. Kung
for relief on August 24.

Meanwhile, registration of Chinese
public bodies and individuals for
buying Saigon rice is still going on
and it is expected that the sums given
by buyers have reached a big
amount orders for Saigon rice will at
once be placed. There is no doubt
now that the rice situation here is
improving with prices gradually
dropping but it must be pointed out
that prices quoted by rice shops at
present are still beyond the ability of
small salaried individuals and poor to
pay. The present price of $35 or
more per picul is more than double
when compared with the figure
quoted only about four months ago.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年8月31日

大米状况
好转
孔祥熙博士将提供外汇
用于从西贡购买物资

作为上海严峻米荒局势中的一个新鼓舞因素，重庆财政部长孔祥熙博士回复了此地中国各界领袖近期发出的电报，允许他们以政府汇率获得1万英镑外汇，为本地公众购买西贡大米。孔博士在电文中提到，应迅速购买两万担西贡大米以缓解局势，海关关税亦予免除。

孔博士对本地民众表示深切关注，他认为上海的大米短缺是日本人和“伪政权”对运输施加限制的结果。他断言，据报道浙江和江苏均获大米丰收。他建议，利用他批准的1万英镑外汇，上海的各中国公共团体应联合购买两万担西贡大米。

上海公共租界工部局华董领袖虞洽卿先生、上海银行公会李明先生以及国际租界华人纳税会代理主席徐寄庼先生已收到部长的回复，他们曾于8月24日联名致电孔博士请求救济。

与此同时，中国公共团体和个人登记购买西贡大米的工作仍在进行，预计买家提供的金额已达巨大数目，西贡大米的订单将立即下达。毫无疑问，此地米荒状况正在改善，价格逐渐下跌，但必须指出的是，目前米店报价仍超出小薪阶层和贫困人口的支付能力。目前每担35元或以上的价格，与仅约四个月前报价相比，已增加了一倍多。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
AUG 31 1939

SAIGON RICE FOR
SHANGHAI
Chungking Permission Is
Given For Foreign
Exchange
CHUNGKING, Aug. 30.—Receiving a petition from prominent Chinese leaders in Shanghai for assistance in connection with the present rice situation in Shanghai, Dr. H. H. Kung, President of the Executive Yuan and concurrently Minister of Finance, to-day gave special permission for the purchase of £10,000 for importing 20,000 piculs of Saigon rice, to be exempt from import duty.
In his reply, however, Dr. Kung points out that while Shanghai is facing a shortage of rice, the Chinese Government is worrying about the slump in the rice price in "free" China on account of good harvests.
He lays the blame for the rice situation in Shanghai on Japanese restrictions regarding the transportation of foodstuffs to Shanghai, and on the over-population in that city due to Japanese military operations in Kiangsu and Chekiang provinces.
—Reuter.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年8月31日

供上海之
西贡大米
重庆准许
使用外汇
重庆，8月30日电。——收到上海著名中国领袖关于协助解决当前上海米荒局势的请求后，行政院院长兼财政部长孔祥熙博士今日特别批准购买1万英镑外汇，用于进口两万担西贡大米，并免除进口关税。
然而，孔博士在回复中指出，虽然上海面临大米短缺，但中国政府正因丰收而担忧“自由”中国地区的米价暴跌。
他将上海米荒归咎于日本对运往上海的粮食运输施加的限制，以及因日军在江苏和浙江省的军事行动导致该市人口过剩。
——路透社。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

AUG 31 1939

Rice Market

On account of the typhoon and the
heavy rain yesterday, no fresh rice supplies
were brought here by steamer from the
growing centers in the interior, and only
2,000 bags of white rice were received by
the market, coming by truck and rail.
The selling price in yesterday's session
was weak in purchases, or $2 below the
last final rate. The business in the day
was slight, because most of the dealers
were absent.

According to the market record, the
first-grade white rice was quoted at $32,
and the second-grade of the same rice
was sold at $29 per picul. Changshu
white rice was liquidated at $30, while
the Kiangpeh newly-harvested rice noted
at $25 and the low grade of white rice
at $24.

The market has received only a small
shipment of provincial rice from the in-
terior, because of the Typhoon and the
rain and the selling price continued dull
in the market for selling. According to
reliable information the Japanese authori-
ties would allow the Wuhu provincial rice
to be regularly transported to Shanghai
without any delay, so that the rate of the
rice would drop in a day or two.

As a result, the rate of provincial rice
weakened by $1. The total sales in the
day were estimated at 3,000 bags of
different kinds of provincial rice, while
the Nanking provincial rice was sold at
$30, and the Wuhu Provincial rice was
quoted at $28. The Kiangpeh newly-har-
vested provincial rice sold at $24 per picul.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1939年8月31日

大米市场

由于台风和昨日的大雨，没有新的大米供应通过轮船从内地种植中心运抵此处，市场仅收到通过卡车和铁路运来的两千包白米。昨日交易时段的买盘疲软，售价比最后成交价低2元。当日交易量稀少，因为大多数商人缺席。

根据市场记录，一级白米报价为32元，同级二级白米售价为每担29元。常熟白米以30元成交，而江北新米报价为25元，低级白米为24元。

由于台风和降雨，市场仅收到少量来自内地的外省大米，且市场卖价持续低迷。据可靠消息，日本当局将允许芜湖外省大米定期无阻地运往上海，以便米价在一两天内下跌。

因此，外省大米价格下跌1元。当日总销量估计为各种外省大米三千包，其中南京外省大米售价为30元，芜湖外省大米报价为28元。江北新产外省大米售价为每担24元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

AUG 31 1939

Flour And Wheat

The business in native flour was slight
and the selling rate was weak in the
market yesterday. Owing to the recent
low rate of white rice no brisk demand
for flour was shown by the local and
retail shops, and even the North China
and South Sea buyers were not interested
to buy for transportation, so that the
selling rate of second-grade dropped by
$0.20, and the official rate stood at $6.20
in cash. The total turnover in the ses-
sion amounted to 30,000 bags of native
flour.
Slight trading of native wheat was seen
in yesterday's market. On account of
typhoon and heavy rain, the market has
received no fresh wheat from the growing
centers in the interior. Following the
cheap rate of native flour, the Chinese
flour mills were inactive in absorbing for
their further stocks, so that no official
price was quoted in the market yesterday.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1939年8月31日

面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉交易稀少，市场售价疲软。由于近期白米价格低廉，本地零售店对面粉并未表现出旺盛需求，甚至华北和华南买家也无兴趣购买转运，导致二级面粉售价下跌0.20元，官方现金报价维持在6.20元。该时段总成交量为国产面粉三万包。

昨日市场可见少量国产小麦交易。由于台风和大雨，市场未收到来自内地种植中心的新小麦。继国产面粉价格低廉之后，中国面粉厂在吸收进一步库存方面表现不活跃，因此昨日市场未报出官方价格。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
AUG 30 1939
Further Drop
In Price Is
Anticipated
Shipments Reported Now
Entering From Nippon
Controlled Areas
RECENT “FAMINE”
IS EXPLAINED
Tribute Paid To Time
Devoted By Council
Members To Problem
Shanghai's rice shortage shows
distinct signs of easing, an official
communique issued yesterday by
the Shanghai Municipal Council
stated. While the price of rice is
still "too high to be considered
satisfactory" the statement declar-
ed there was reason to hope for a
further decline.
Rice shipments to this city
from the Japanese - governed
growing areas have been almost
non-existent for several weeks
now due to a virtual export em-
bargo maintained by the mili-
tary. During the past week
large shipments have been per-
mitted to enter the city with a
consequent drop in price from
the peak of $50 per picul sev-
eral days ago to $35 on yester-
day's market.
Explaining the financial impos-
sibility of importing foreign rice at
the present high rate of exchange,
the Council statement yesterday
declared that throughout the period
of crisis it had been clear that the
only real solution of the problem
was a free supply of rice from the
hinterland.
Appeal Made
Accordingly representations were
early made to the Japanese au-
thorities to facilitate importation of
the cereal. These were always
given "sympathetic consideration"
and are believed directly responsible
for a "marked amelioration of
what was becoming a grave situa-
tion."
The communique further acknow-
ledged the assistance of all bodies
and persons who co-operated with
it in the solution of the problem.
The Chinese members of the Coun-
cil devoted much attention to the
effect of a shortage among the
poorer members of the Chinese
community and Mr. Yu Ya-ching,
a Council member, arranged for the
financing of a shipment of 1,800
tons of Saigon rice.
A total of 15,000 bags of rice ar-
rived here yesterday from the Wuhu
and Klangshah ports, and while
trading was dull on the local mar-
ket due to the hope of dealers that
a further drop in price will even-
luate during the week, the price
of first grade Changshu white rice
was quoted $35 per picul, $3 below
Monday's close. Low grade cereal
sold at $25 per picul, about $5 below
Monday's price.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》（China Press）
1939年8月30日

预计价格将进一步下跌
据报道，来自日本控制区的稻米 shipments 现已进入
近期的“粮荒”得到解释
对工部局董事为解决该问题所投入的时间表示敬意

上海公共租界工部局昨日发布的官方公报称，上海的米荒显示出明显的缓解迹象。公报宣称，虽然米价仍然“高得令人无法满意”，但有理由希望价格会进一步下跌。

由于军方实际上维持着出口禁令，过去几周从日本管辖的产米区运往本市的稻米几乎为零。在过去的一周里，大量稻米获准进入本市，导致价格从几天前每担50美元的峰值跌至昨日市场的35美元。

工部局昨日的声明解释说，在目前的高汇率下进口外国大米在财务上是不可能的，并宣称在整个危机期间，很清楚问题的唯一真正解决办法是来自内地的自由供应的大米。

提出呼吁

因此，早期已向日本当局提出交涉，以便利谷物的进口。这些交涉始终得到“同情的考虑”，并被认为直接导致了“原本日益严重的局势的显著改善”。

公报进一步感谢所有在该问题的解决过程中与之合作的团体和个人。工部局的华籍董事非常关注米荒对中国社区贫困阶层的影响，工部局董事虞洽卿先生安排为一批1,800吨的西贡大米提供资金。

昨天共有15,000袋大米从芜湖和长沙（Klangshah，音译）港口抵达此处，虽然由于商人希望本周内价格会进一步下跌，本地市场交易清淡，但一等常熟白米的报价为每担35美元，比周一收盘价低3美元。低等谷物以每担25美元出售，比周一的价格低约5美元。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES

AUG 20 1939

Large Drop In Local
Rice Prices Seen As
Big Shipments Arrive

Big Operators Reported To Be Unloading After
S. M. Council And Japanese Reach Under-
standing On Free Entry Of Cereals

COUNCIL ISSUES EXPLANATION ON
SITUATION; NO SHORTAGE SEEN

Unable to sustain its position in face of heavy shipments of
rice arriving from the inland areas yesterday, coupled with a
dull market, a further wave of downward trend was precipit-
ated in the local rice market, with the result that prices for
various grade of cereals registered further loss of from $2 to $5.
Following favourable reports dur-
ing the past few days, and the an-
nouncement that the S. M. C. had
reached some understanding with
the Japanese authorities for the free
entry of cereals into Shanghai, local
big operators continued to unload
heavily their stocks in an attempt
to cover. This tendency also per-
vaded the ranks of local rice dealers,
but the market remained quiet dur-
ing the day, as buyers were few
and failed to come to terms in an
anticipatory mood.
Arrivals yesterday were reported
to total more than 20 junkloads, and
several thousand more bags by rail
and more than 8,000 bags by
steamers from the Yangtze regions.
The storm in the local "rice crisis"
was generally believed to have
blown over. A return of confidence
among local rice merchants circles
generally, and an optimistic outlook
in the future has constrained the big
rice operators and rice dealers gen-
erally to adopt a "watch and wait
attitude," while attempts have been
made generally to unload their avail-
able stocks. Barring profiteering
and speculation, it was hinted that
before long Shanghai would be
glutted with cereals, although mer-
chants generally displayed a guard-
ed optimism, fearing that a contrary
reaction might again set in to arrest
the downward trend.
The present downward trend,
however, has not yet sufficiently
developed to bring direct benefit to
the poorer classes of Chinese, as the
wholesale price of $35 per picul of
first grade cereals, and $36.20 retail,
is still beyond their reach. Medium
and lower grade cereals were quoted
respectively at $34.50 and $32 whole-
sale, and at from $0.50 to $1.20 more
at retail prices.
S. M. C. Statement
A statement on the rice situation
was issued by the S. M. C. yester-
day as follows:—
During the last few days rice has
been coming into Shanghai at a rate
sufficient to cater for normal con-
sumption. Prices have dropped,
and although they are still too high
to be considered satisfactory, there
is reason to hope that they will
soon drop further.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》（Shanghai Times）

1939年8月20日

随着大批货物抵达，本地米价大幅下跌

据报道，在工部局与日本就谷物自由进入上海达成谅解后，大运营商正在卸货

工部局就局势发表说明；未见短缺

面对昨天从内陆地区运抵的大量大米，加上市场疲软，本地大米市场无法维持其地位，引发了新一轮的下跌趋势，结果各种等级的谷物价格又下跌了2至5美元。

继过去几天的有利报道，以及宣布工部局已与日本当局就谷物自由进入上海达成某种谅解之后，本地大运营商继续大量抛售库存以图保本。这种倾向也蔓延到本地米商的行列，但由于买家寥寥无几，且未能以预期的心态达成交易，市场在当天保持平静。

据报道，昨天的到货总量超过20船（junkloads），另有数千袋通过铁路运抵，还有8,000多袋通过轮船从长江流域地区运抵。

人们普遍认为，本地“米荒”的风暴已经过去。本地米商圈子普遍恢复信心，以及对未来的乐观展望，迫使大米大运营商和一般米商普遍采取“观望态度”，同时普遍试图抛售现有库存。有人暗示，除非出现囤积居奇和投机行为，否则不久上海将会谷物充斥，尽管商人们普遍表现出谨慎的乐观，担心可能会出现相反的反应，从而阻止下跌趋势。

然而，目前的下跌趋势尚未发展到足以使中国贫困阶层直接受益的程度，因为一等谷物每担35美元的批发价和36.20美元的零售价仍然超出他们的承受能力。中等和下等谷物的批发价分别为34.50美元和32美元，零售价则高出0.50至1.20美元。

工部局声明

工部局昨日就米市情况发表声明如下：—

在过去几天里，进入上海的稻米数量足以满足正常消费。价格已经下跌，虽然仍然高得令人无法满意，但有理由希望它们很快就会进一步下跌。

page_data.en:
It is not always possible or expedient, when important negotiations are in progress and various alternative plans are under consideration to issue statements explaining the Council's position. Throughout the past weeks the Council has been anxiously observing the rice situation, which has been under constant discussion not only by Members of Council and Council officials but also by the Food and Supplies Sub-Committee under the Chairmanship of Sir Robert Calder-Marshall. There is no truth in the rumour that the Council has at any time had rice stocks at its disposal, nor, according to the Council's investigations, has the shortage of rice been due to hoarding by private interests in the Settlement. Daily reports have been received of stocks in the Settlement and all supplies in godowns, etc., have been carefully checked from time to time. There has been complete co-operation between the French authorities and the Council.

Difficult Circumstances
Circumstances have been very different from 1937 when the Council imported rice from Saigon. The importation at the ruling rate of exchange of a sufficient quantity of rice to supply Shanghai for any considerable period would have involved serious financial risk. Moreover, it has throughout the period of crisis been clear that the only real solution of the problem was a free supply of rice from the hinterland. Representations were accordingly made to the Japanese authorities to facilitate the importation of rice from areas under their control. These representations obtained sympathetic consideration and have already resulted in a marked amelioration of what was becoming a grave situation.
The Council has throughout the period of anxiety maintained regular contact with all bodies and persons who were likely to be able to assist in implementing the arrival of rice into Shanghai. The co-operation of those to whom the Council has appealed for help is gratefully acknowledged. The steep rise in prices naturally weighed most heavily on the poorer classes of the Chinese community. To this aspect of the problem the Chinese Members of Council have naturally devoted special attention, and in particular one of their number arranged for the financing of a shipment of 1,800 tons of Saigon rice to meet the immediate needs of the refugees and poorer classes.

Rice Dealer's Guild
A rice dealers' guild was expected to be formed as the result of consultations among leaders of the Japanese Residents' Corporation, Japanese Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Japanese rice merchants, in order to check price increases, according to the Shanghai "Mainichi."
The Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions held a meeting of its executive sub-committee at the Nippon Club Monday afternoon to discuss a plan for bringing down the price of rice.
Japanese military authorities recently provided facilities for the transportation of rice to Shanghai from interior points, the paper recalled.

当重要谈判正在进行且各种替代方案正在考虑之中时，发布声明解释工部局的立场并不总是可能或权宜之计。在过去的几周里，工部局一直焦急地观察着米市情况，这不仅由工部局董事和官员不断讨论，也由罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士（Sir Robert Calder-Marshall）担任主席的食品与供应小组委员会不断讨论。有关工部局随时拥有可支配的大米库存的谣言毫无根据，而且根据工部局的调查，大米短缺也不是由于租界内私人利益集团的囤积所致。工部局每天都收到关于租界内库存的报告，并时不时仔细核查仓库等处的所有供应品。法国当局与工部局之间有着充分的合作。

困难的环境

情况与1937年工部局从西贡进口大米时大不相同。按现行汇率进口足够供应上海相当长一段时间的大米，将涉及严重的财务风险。此外，在整个危机期间，很清楚问题的唯一真正解决办法是来自内地的自由供应的大米。因此，已向日本当局提出交涉，以便利从其控制区进口大米。这些交涉得到了同情的考虑，并已使原本日益严重的局势得到显著改善。

在整个焦虑时期，工部局一直与所有可能有助于实现大米进入上海的团体和个人保持定期联系。工部局对其求助对象的配合表示感激。价格的急剧上涨自然给中国社区的贫困阶层带来了最沉重的负担。中国籍工部局董事自然特别关注问题的这一方面，其中一位董事特别安排为一批1,800吨的西贡大米提供资金，以满足难民和贫困阶层的迫切需求。

米业公会

据上海《每日新闻》（Mainichi）报道，作为日本居留民团、日本工商会和日本米商领导人之间磋商的结果，预计将成立一个米业公会，以抑制价格上涨。

日本各街道联合会联盟执行小组委员会周一下午在日本俱乐部举行会议，讨论降低米价的计划。

该报回顾说，日本军方最近为从内地向上海运输大米提供了便利。

AUG 30 1939

Fall in Rice Prices Follows
Arrival of Supplies

Further Decline to More Reasonable Level is
Expected: Council Explains Situation

CHINESE press reports yesterday unanimously predicted that
prices of various grades of rice will continue to follow a
downward trend in view of the sympathetic attention aroused
among the various influential and official quarters in Shanghai.
The price of the first grade rice which last week soared to the
$45 mark is now sold at a price less than $40. (between $35 and
$38) while the movement led by Mr. Yu Ya-ching for buying
Saigon rice has big support.

According to a statement issued yes-
terday by the Shanghai Municipal
Council, during the last few days
rice has been coming into Shanghai
at a rate sufficient to cater for
normal consumption. Prices have
dropped, and although they are still
too high to be considered satisfactory,
there is reason to hope that they will
soon drop further.

It is not always possible or expedi-
ent, when important negotiations are
in progress and various alternative
plans are under consideration to
issue statements explaining the Coun-
cil's position. Throughout the past
weeks the Council has been anxious-
ly observing the rice situation, which
has been under constant discussion
not only by Members of Council and
Council officials but also by the Food
and Supplies Sub-Committee under
the Chairmanship of Sir Robert
Calder-Marshall. There is no truth
in the rumour that the Council has
at any time had rice stocks at its
disposal, nor, according to the
Council's investigations, has the short-
age of rice been due to hoarding by
private interests in the Settlement.
Daily reports have been received of
stocks in the Settlement and all
supplies in godowns, etc., have been
carefully checked from time to time.
There has been complete co-operation
between the French authorities and
the Council.

Circumstances have been very
different from 1937 when the Council
imported rice from Saigon. The im-
portation at the ruling rate of ex-
change of a sufficient quantity of rice
to supply Shanghai for any consider-
able period would have involved
serious financial risk. Moreover, it
has throughout the period of crisis
been clear that the only real solution
of the problem was a free supply
of rice from the hinterland. Repre-
sentations were accordingly made to
the Japanese authorities to facilitate
the importation of rice from areas
under their control. These repre-
sentations obtained sympathetic con-
sideration and have already resulted
in a marked amelioration of what
was becoming a grave situation.

1939年8月30日

供应到达后米价下跌

预计将进一步回落至更合理的水平：工部局解释局势

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

AUG 30 1939

Cheaper Rice
The rice situation, which has caused great distress among Shanghai's 3,900,000 population has improved appreciably during the past few days. Prices of Chinese rice have declined several dollars per bag and well-informed sources believed that this downward tendency will continue until a more reasonable level is reached consonant with wages. The reason for this is the arrival of larger supplies from Wuhu, the great Central China rice port, and the promise of even greater supplies in the near future through the co-operation of the Japanese authorities in whose controlled territory this great rice-producing area is located. Amidst a large volume of complaints, speculations and accusations regarding the cause of the unusual situation caused in Shanghai, a satisfactory explanation is still lacking to show why rice at Wuhu is $14 and in Shanghai it has touched over $50. Political obstacles arising from the peculiar relationships between the Japanese authorities controlling the hinterland around Shanghai, and speculation and hoarding by manipulators have been variously quoted, but little heed has been paid to the fact how near Shanghai is to starvation. At one point, the city's stocks were estimated at 70,000 bags which represents a week's supply at the daily average consumption of 10,000 bags. Whatever is the reason the seriousness of conditions, which resulted in raids on rice shops, has received the urgent attention of the foreign municipal authorities for a huge city like Shanghai cannot be left to exist on meagre driblets of subsistence when abundance is within easy reach. Shanghai has many difficult problems but none is more important than that of filling the rice bowl. And the way the Shanghai Municipal Council, the French Concession authorities and others have co-operated to ameliorate conditions is described by the Council's statement issued yesterday and published on another page.

《字林西报》，

1939年8月30日

米价下跌

过去几天里，令上海三百九十万居民深感痛苦的米荒局势已显著改善。中国大米的价格每袋下降了数美元，消息灵通人士认为，这种下降趋势将持续下去，直至达到与工资水平相称的更合理水平。造成这一情况的原因是，来自华中重要米港芜湖的大批供应已经抵达，而且由于日本当局的合作——该主要产米区位于其控制领土内——近期有望获得甚至更多的供应。尽管关于造成上海这一异常局势的原因存在着大量的抱怨、猜测和指责，但仍缺乏令人满意的解释来说明为何芜湖的大米价格为14美元，而在上海却已超过50美元。人们列举了各种原因，包括因控制上海周边内地的日本当局之间特殊关系而产生的政治障碍，以及操纵者的投机和囤积行为，但很少有人注意到上海离饥荒有多么近。在某一时刻，据估计全市库存仅为7万袋，按日均消耗1万袋计算，这仅够维持一周的供应。无论原因如何，导致冲击米店的严峻局势已引起外国市政当局的紧急关注，因为像上海这样的大城市，在物资充裕且易于获取的情况下，不能仅靠微薄的生存配给度日。上海面临许多难题，但没有比填满饭碗更重要的了。工部局、法租界当局及其他方面为改善局势所进行的合作，已在工部局昨日发表并刊登于另一版的声明中予以描述。
