30 8 39

AUG 29 1939

Price Of Rice
Shows Decline

Buyers Awaiting Drop
To Still Lower
Figure

With the price of first grade rice
dropping a further three dollars
from yesterday afternoon's quota-
tion of $44 per picul, an SMC offi-
cial this morning told the Evening
Post that the situation at present
was "very much easier."

"We are no longer alarmed," the
Council official declared this morn-
ing, adding that "the supply of
rice is again coming into Shang-
hai in normal quantities."

Official Statement

An official communique by the
Shanghai Municipal Council, ex-
plaining the shortage of rice and
the acute situation which prevailed
during the past fortnight, will be
prepared for release to the press
this afternoon, an official of the
SMC stated this morning.

However, despite the fact that
the price of the grain has fallen
almost 10 dollars since Saturday
morning, Chinese householders
continued to make only small pur-
chases today, probably expecting
the price to drop still lower.

Deliveries

Since Sunday, approximately
6000 bags of rice have arrived in
Shanghai from the interior, most-
ly from Wuhu, while deliveries
were also received from Saigon.
It was estimated this morning
that the present stock of first
quality rice in the city is between
60,000 to 70,000 bags.

Lile

C. 39.

1939年8月30日

1939年8月29日

米价
显示下跌

买家等待价格
进一步降至
更低水平

随着一级大米价格从昨天下午每担44美元的报价再跌3美元，工部局（SMC）一名官员今晨告诉《晚报》（Evening Post），目前的局势“大大缓和”。

“我们不再感到恐慌，”该工部局官员今晨宣称，并补充说，“大米供应正再次以正常数量进入上海。”

官方声明

工部局一名官员今晨表示，一份解释大米短缺及过去两周普遍存在的紧急局势的工部局官方公报，将于今天下午准备发布给新闻界。

然而，尽管自周六早晨以来粮价已下跌近10美元，中国家庭主妇今天仍只进行小额购买，可能是预期价格会进一步下跌。

交货情况

自周日以来，约有6000袋大米从内地运抵上海，主要来自芜湖，同时也有来自西贡的交货。今晨估计，市内一级大米的现有库存介于6万至7万袋之间。

Lile

C. 39.

August 29, 1939. Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper)
publishes the following article:

The Rice Question

The sharp drop in the value of legal tender notes
is a sign of the financial collapse of the Kuomintang
Government, while the acute increase in the prices of rice
and other things is the natural sign following the drop in
the value of the legal tender notes. The arbitrary
manipulation of the rice market by unscrupulous merchants
and the impossibility on the part of the authorities of the
Foreign Settlements to deal with the situation are also
connected with the increase in the price of rice.
The price of rice should not be so high for it
is closely concerned with the living of the general public.
People become disturbed without rice and cases of robbery
of rice have arisen. It is the authorities of the
Foreign Settlements who are held responsible for this
situation because they have failed to devise ways and means
of coping with the demand before the situation had become
too grave nor could they control the increase of the price
of rice once it had begun to rise. It seems that
besides collecting taxes from the Chinese, they do not care
for the public security or the livelihood of the general
public. When the situation has become serious, they bring
machine guns into action or arrest people and put them into
prison. Only poor Chinese are affected.
The authorities of the Foreign Settlements should
be held responsible for all tragic incidents in the
Settlements arising from the increase in the price of rice.
Unscrupulous merchants are supported by the Settlement
authorities and enjoy the latter's protection. So if we
wish to overthrow unscrupulous merchants, we must also
overthrow the Settlement authorities that protect these
unscrupulous merchants.
In view of the sharp increase of the price of
rice, the people will face starvation and the security of
the general public will be endangered, the "Reformed Government"
has ordered 100,000 "zah" of rice from Wuhu, to be transported
to Shanghai for sale at a moderate price. Within one or
two days, it will arrive in Shanghai. This is why the
price of rice has now dropped from $53 per picul to $38
according to yesterday's newspapers. This shows how the
"Reformed Government" holds a serious view to the foodstuffs
of the people and in the meantime it reveals the evil
intention of the Settlement authorities and unscrupulous
merchants. The new regime aims at protecting the general
public.
From the increase of the price of rice, we may
understand that the Kuomintang Government is creating
unnecessary wars, the Settlement authorities shelter
unscrupulous merchants and unscrupulous merchants are doing
their best to carry out their evil intention. The people now
understand the crimes of the Kuomintang Government and the
Settlement authorities for the increase of the price of rice
and understand that they give no consideration to the interests
of the general public. Henceforth, we should give every
support to our "Reformed Government" that loves us, effect
the return of the Foreign Settlements and overthrow the
Kuomintang Government.

1939年8月29日。晨间译稿。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）刊登以下文章：

米价问题

法币价值的急剧下跌是国民党政府财政崩溃的标志，而大米及其他物品价格的急剧上涨则是法币贬值后的自然现象。不法商人对米市的任意操纵，以及租界当局无力应对局势，也与米价上涨有关。
米价不应如此之高，因为它与公众的生活息息相关。无米则人心惶惶，抢米案件时有发生。租界当局应对此局势负责，因为他们未能在局势变得过于严重之前想出办法来应对需求，也无法在米价开始上涨后控制其升势。看来，除了向中国人征税外，他们并不关心公共安全或公众的生计。当局势变得严重时，他们就出动机枪或逮捕人员投入监狱。受影响的只有贫穷的中国人。
租界当局应对租界内因米价上涨而发生的所有悲剧事件负责。不法商人得到租界当局的支持并享受其保护。因此，如果我们希望推翻不法商人，我们也必须推翻保护这些不法商人的租界当局。
鉴于米价急剧上涨，人民将面临饥饿，公共安全将受到威胁，“维新政府”已从芜湖订购10万“石”大米，运往上海以适中价格出售。一两天内即可抵达上海。这就是为什么据昨日报纸报道，米价已从每担53美元跌至38美元。这表明“维新政府”严肃对待人民的粮食问题，同时也揭露了租界当局和不法商人的邪恶意图。新政权旨在保护公众。
从米价的上涨中，我们可以看出国民党政府制造不必要的战争，租界当局庇护不法商人，而不法商人则极力实施其邪恶意图。人民现在明白了国民党政府和租界当局对米价上涨所犯的罪行，并明白他们不考虑公众的利益。今后，我们应该全力支持爱护我们的“维新政府”，实现收回租界，并推翻国民党政府。

大米进口
降低价格

随着昨日货物抵达
局势正在改善

随着来自外围地区和内陆地区的运输量增加，以及有报道称日本当局已承诺协助工部局（S.M.C.）实现大米自由进入上海，本地大米市场的前景昨日受到新的提振。
因此，昨天所有等级的谷物批发价格每担均下跌略超过1美元。
一则未经证实的消息称，根据日本当局的指示，维新政府正从芜湖向上海发运大批货物，后续还将有更多货物跟进。据报道，约10万担芜湖谷物昨日已抵达虹口，并由上海特别市政府以低价零售给苏州河以北地区的中国居民。
预计日本当局不久还能将另一大批芜湖谷物带给工部局，以便在国际租界区域内的零售米店进行分销。
另一个正在发挥作用的有利因素是，由俞亚清先生和其他本地中国商界领袖订购的1800吨外国大米即将抵达。
昨天，本地商品市场因庆祝孔子诞辰而休市，

CHINA PRESS.
16 28 1939
808723-

Rice Dearth
Here Continues
To Be Acute

Puppet Regime Claims
100,000 Bags Cereal
Sent To Shanghai

JAPANESE REPORTS
OFFICIAL'S SPEECH

Nippon Agencies Would
Play Good Samaritan
Role Here

A Domei report that 100,000 piculs
of Wuhu rice have been imported
to Shanghai within the past two
days by the Japanese authorities,
was denied yesterday from a source
close to the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

Increased optimism has been
shown on the local market here
during the past few days with arri-
val of larger shipments of rice from
the interior growing center. The
optimism, declared the above quoted
source, was entirely unfounded as
the rice which the Japanese au-
thorities have permitted to trickle
through their embargo each day
has been less than sufficient to feed
Shanghai for the respective 24-hour
periods. According to the same
source, the feeling of hope is deli-
berately being strengthened in order
that when the city's fast dwindling
stocks are finally depleted, the reac-
tion of a disappointed public will
know no limits of reason.

The Domei report stated that to
relieve the shortage of rice in
Shanghai the "Nanking Reformed
Government" after consultation with
Japanese authorities, had obtained
large quantities of rice from Wuhu
and had dispatched them to Shang-
hai. The statement was attributed
to Chen Chun, "Minister of the
Interior" for the puppet govern-
ment.

The "Minister," Domei continued,
stated that the first 100,000 had
already arrived here and was being
distributed among the inhabitants
of the city at a low cost.

Chen in further reported as
declaring that successive consign-
ments will be sent to Shanghai
to be distributed in the Settlement
and Concession by the Japanese
authorities, while in the areas
under the jurisdiction of the Spe-
cial Municipality the rice will be
distributed by the Bureau of Social
Affairs of that Municipality.

Meanwhile the local settlement
population no longer able to afford
the exorbitant rice prices, are
switching to a flour diet. At the
same time a group of Shanghai
Chinese business men has been
formed to purchase Saigon rice to
stave off the impending lack of
rice in the city.

《大美晚报》。
1939年8月28日
808723-

此地米荒
持续严峻

傀儡政权声称
10万担谷物
已运抵上海

日本报道
官员讲话

日本通讯社将在沪
扮演好撒玛利亚人角色

对于同盟社报道日本当局在过去两天内向上海进口了10万担芜湖大米一事，一位接近工部局的消息来源昨日予以否认。

随着来自内地种植中心的大批大米运抵，过去几天本地市场显示出增强的乐观情绪。上述消息来源宣称，这种乐观情绪完全毫无根据，因为日本当局允许每天通过其封锁线零星流入的大米，不足以维持上海相应24小时期间的食用需求。据同一消息来源称，这种希望感是被刻意强化的，目的是当城市迅速减少的库存最终耗尽时，失望的公众的反应将失去理智的界限。

同盟社的报道指出，为缓解上海的米荒，“南京维新政府”在与日本当局协商后，已从芜湖获得大量大米，并将其发往上海。该声明归因于傀儡政府的“内政部长”陈春。

同盟社继续报道，“部长”称首批10万担已抵达此地，并正以低成本向城市居民分发。

据进一步报道，陈春还宣布，后续批次将发往上海，由日本当局在租界和法租界进行分发，而在特别市管辖区域内，大米将由该市的社会局进行分发。

与此同时，本地租界居民已无力承担高昂的米价，转而食用面粉。同时，一群上海中国商人已组建起来，购买西贡大米，以抵御城市迫在眉睫的缺米危机。

（批注：档案 6/28）

CHINA PRESS
AUG 27 1939

Rice Market

The rice crisis in Shanghai was eased during the last few days, because some leading Chinese businessmen had organized the "maintaining Rice For Chinese Relief Society", which has offered a large amount of Saigon Rice in Indo-China, so that the selling price of native white rice was lowered. The market has also received a considerable amount of fresh rice supplies from the growing centers in the interior yesterday, coming by truck rail and steamer.

With a large shipment of newly-harvested white rice in the market for selling, the rate in yesterday's session dropped from $1 to $2 per picul, as the local rice dealers and the retail shops were not interested in buying, and only fractional purchases were displayed in the entire session, and no brisk demand was shown by the buyers. The first-grade white rice was quoted at $37.50 per picul, and Kiangsu white rice sold at $37. Quinsan and Soochow rice was liquidated at $35 to $36 per picul. The Southern Sorts newly-harvested rice, original price of which stood at $37 per picul, dropped irregularly in yesterday's trading, and the official price stood at $35 per picul. Owing to lacking of supplies, the low-grade white rice was not in the market for liquidation.

The low tendency of provincial rice was still seen in the market yesterday. The selling rate weakened as the dealers were reluctant to buy, on account of the high rate. The market supplied a large amount of Kiangpeh newly-harvested provincial rice which was brought here recently. The price of this rice heavily dropped by $2 below the previous final rate and even the Wuhu and Nanking provincial rice was low by $0.50 cash.

The total business done in provincial rice in yesterday's market was estimated at 4,000 bags of different kinds of rice. The Nanking provincial rice was sold at $31.50, and the Wuhu provincial rice stood at $32. The Kiangpeh newly-harvested provincial rice was quoted from $31 to $33 per picul, with reference to a report that the rate of provincial rice would be cheap in early part of next week.

8 27/8

《大美晚报》
1939年8月27日

米市

上海的大米危机在过去几天有所缓解，因为一些中国商界领袖组织了“维持华赈米会”，提供了大量来自印度支那的西贡米，使得本地白米的售价降低。昨日，市场还收到了来自内地产粮中心的大量新鲜大米供应，这些大米通过卡车、铁路和轮船运抵。

随着大量新收获的白米进入市场销售，昨日交易期间的价格每担下跌了1至2美元，因为本地米商和零售店无意购买，整个交易期间仅出现零星采购，买方未表现出强劲需求。一级白米报价为每担37.50美元，江苏白米售价为37美元。昆山和苏州米以每担35至36美元的价格清算。南方品种新米原价为每担37美元，昨日交易中不规则下跌，官方价格定为每担35美元。由于缺乏供应，低级白米未在市场进行清算。

昨日市场上仍可见外省米价格走低的趋势。由于价格高企，经销商不愿购买，导致卖价走弱。市场供应了大量近期运抵这里的江北新收外省米。这种米的价格较之前的最终价格大幅下跌2美元，甚至芜湖和南京的外省米也低了0.50元现金。

昨日市场外省米的总成交量估计为各种大米共4,000包。南京外省米售价为31.50美元，芜湖外省米价格为32美元。江北新收外省米报价为每担31至33美元，据报下周初外省米价格将更便宜。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
AUG 27 1930
Improvement
Seen In Local
Rice Market
Slight Drop in Price
Noted; No More
Riots Staged
An optimistic report circulated in
the rice market yesterday that
provincial rice will go lower in
price beginning with the early part
of the coming week. As a fore-
runner of hope the price of first
quality cereal dropped by $1 per
picul to $37.
Although the Japanese have not
indicated their official willingness
to lift the ban on rice shipments
from growing centers, and parti-
cularly Wuhu to Shanghai, larger
quantities of rice have been flow-
ing into the city during the week
than previously, a fact which
amounts to virtual lifting of the
ban.
Reflecting a glimmer of con-
fidence on the part of the poorer
classes that the situation may con-
tinue to improve, mob storming of
rice shops which appeared to be
growing in violence at the begin-
ning of the week, have shown no
signs of becoming a major problem.
No riots have been reported within
the past two days.
A further factor pointing to
slight amelioration in the rice
situation here, yesterday, was the
drop by $2 in the price of newly
harvested Klangpeh provincial rice
to $31 a picul. A considerable
quantity of this poor quality pro-
duct has been brought here re-
cently but although the cheapest
rice on sale it sold very little in
the market.
While Saigon rice remained in
the vicinity of $50 per picul, it was
reported that a large shipment
arrived yesterday. A group of
local Chinese business men were
said to be forming a committee to
purchase Saigon rice in case the
city should be reduced to absolute
lack of this necessity.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1930年8月27日
本地米市
现见改善
注意到价格
小幅下跌；
不再发生
骚乱

昨日米市流传着一份乐观报告，称从下周初开始，外省米价格将下降。作为希望的先兆，一级谷物的价格每担下跌1美元，至37美元。

尽管日本人尚未表示愿意正式解除对从产粮中心（特别是芜湖）向上海运送大米的禁令，但本周流入该市的大米数量比以往更多，这一事实相当于实际上解除了禁令。

这反映出贫困阶层对局势可能继续改善抱有一丝信心，本周初看似暴力升级的冲击米店行为，并未显示出成为重大问题的迹象。过去两天内未报告发生骚乱。

昨日这里米市状况略有改善的另一个因素是，新收获的江北外省米价格下跌2美元，至每担31美元。最近有大量这种劣质产品运抵此处，但尽管它是市面上最便宜的大米，在市场中的销量却很少。

虽然西贡米价格保持在每担50美元左右，但据报道昨日有一大批货物抵达。据说一群本地中国商人正在组建一个委员会，以便在城市陷入绝对缺乏这种必需品的情况下购买西贡米。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
2390

Rice Prices Fall
Suddenly
Large Quantity of Grain
Received from Kiangsu ;
Manipulators Caught

As local Japanese authorities are
reported to be willing to allow free
importation of rice from the interior
to Shanghai and as large quantities
of the grain are being brought into
foreign settlements, prices of various
grades of rice here suddenly dropped
yesterday, to the relief of all.
The "Sin Shun Pao" reported that
the Japanese military authorities
would allow free importation of rice
into Shanghai from the interior
even to the extent of sacrificing
part of the grain that the military
authorities wished to reserve for
their own use. The paper quoted a
military officer as saying this.
Meanwhile, some Chinese rice
merchants who are not manipulators
have got in touch with the Kuomintang
governor of Kiangsu province,
General Han Deh-ching, telling him
of the serious rice situation here.
The governor immediately promised
to send rice to Shanghai. Already
3,800 piculs of Kiangsu rice arrived
here yesterday and the news shocked
the rice manipulators.
Many firms and shops and
individuals have registered with Mr.
Yu Ya-ching, who is leading a
movement of buying Saigon rice to
relieve the local shortage. People
wishing to buy 50 bags of Saigon
rice may register, so that one big
order may be placed at one time.
Only two days ago the first grade
rice was sold at $40 or even more
for one picul, but yesterday the
price dropped to $35. It was
reliably learned that the newly
arrived Kiangsu rice was bought by
local merchants at only $18 per
picul including transportation fee.
The price therefore is expected to
follow a downward trend if the rice
is continuously arriving.

Lily
Coy
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
2390

米价突然
下跌
大量谷物
从江苏运抵；
投机者被擒

据报道，由于当地日本当局愿意允许从内地自由进口大米到上海，且大量谷物正被运入租界，这里各级大米的价格昨日突然下跌，令所有人松了一口气。

《新闻报》报道，日本军方当局将允许从内地自由进口大米到上海，甚至不惜牺牲部分军方希望留作自用的谷物。该报引用了一位军官的话证实了这一点。

与此同时，一些非投机性的中国米商与江苏省政府主席韩德勤将军取得了联系，向他通报了这里严峻的大米形势。省主席立即承诺向上海运送大米。昨日已有3,800担江苏米运抵此处，这一消息震惊了大米投机者。

许多商行、店铺和个人已在虞洽卿先生处登记，他正领导一场购买西贡米以缓解本地短缺的运动。希望购买50包西贡米的人可以登记，以便一次性下达一个大订单。

就在两天前，一级米每担售价还高达40美元甚至更多，但昨日价格跌至35美元。据可靠消息，新运抵的江苏米被本地商人以每担18美元的价格购入，含运费。因此，如果大米持续运抵，预计价格将呈下降趋势。

Lily
Coy

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
AUG 20 1939
Local Rice Situation Now
Showing Big Improvement
Observers Believe That Prices Of First-Grade Rice
Will Drop To As Low As $20 Per Picul; S.M.C.—
Japanese Co-operation Responsible

A distinctly improved outlook
regarding the local rice situation
was shared by rice merchants' cir-
cles yesterday following the steady
downward trend during the past
two days, these observers intimat-
ing that there was reason to believe
that first-grade rice would return
to as low a level as $20 per picul
as a result of a number of favour-
able factors operating.

The reported satisfactory progress
that has been made in the nego-
tiations conducted by the Shang-
hai Municipal Council with the
Japanese authorities for the free
entry of rice into Shanghai has had
a most reassuring effect in the local
rice market. Meanwhile, it was
reliably reported that the Chairman
of the Kiangsu Provincial Govern-
ment, Mr. Han Teh-ching, has
agreed to the unrestricted exporta-
tion of rice produced in the North
Kiangsu areas to Shanghai, follow-
ing successful negotiations with
local Chinese rice merchants.

A total of 3,800 piculs of rice from
North Kiangsu arrived in Shang-
hai yesterday. It was intimated in
local rice circles yesterday that in
North Kiangsu prices for first grade
cereals are being quoted at as low
a price as $16 per picul. These
cereals were being quoted at less
than $36 per picul in the local mar-
ket.

Losses Of $5

For the two days ended yester-
day, first grade rice sustained losses
of about $5, and stood at the level
of a little over $35 per picul yes-
terday, as compared with $39.80
last Wednesday. Medium and lower
grade cereals, likewise, recorded
further losses.

Large quantities of rice were re-
ported also to have been brought
into Shanghai from the Pootung and
outlying areas throughout yester-
day. A daily average of about 10,-
000 bags of rice were reported to
have arrived in Shanghai during the
past two days. If this favourable
trend persists, there is hope that
prices for first grade cereals would
drop to the low level of $20 per
picul, the price officially fixed for
the local unofficial open market
transactions by the two foreign
municipal authorities. This de-
velopment was a possibility, barring
speculation and profiteering by the
big rice operators, local Chinese
rice merchants declared yesterday.

A big shipment of Saigon rice is
also expected to arrive in Shanghai
by early September. The registra-
tion of intending buyers among
local Chinese business houses, fac-
tories and shops at the Chinese
Public Accountants Association in
the premises of the Pootung Resid-
ents Guild on Avenue Edward VII,
continued to be brisk yesterday.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年8月20日
本地米市现状
显示大幅改善
观察人士认为一级米价格
将跌至每担低至20美元；工部局—
日本合作对此负责

继过去两天价格稳步下行后，米商圈子昨日对本地米市前景持明显乐观态度，这些观察人士暗示，有理由相信，由于多种有利因素的作用，一级米价格将回落至每担低至20美元的水平。

据报道，上海公共租界工部局与日本当局就大米自由进入上海进行的谈判取得了令人满意的进展，这对本地米市产生了极大的安抚作用。同时，有可靠消息称，江苏省政府主席韩德勤先生在与本地中国米商成功谈判后，已同意 unrestricted（无限制地）出口苏北地区生产的大米至上海。

昨日共有3,800担苏北大米运抵上海。昨日本地米界透露，在苏北，一级谷物的报价低至每担16美元。这些谷物在本地市场的报价低于每担36美元。

损失5美元

截至昨日的两天内，一级米损失约5美元，昨日价格维持在每担略高于35美元的水平，而上周三为39.80美元。中低级谷物同样录得进一步损失。

据报道，昨日全天也有大量大米从浦东及周边地区运入上海。据报道，过去两天平均每天约有10,000包大米运抵上海。如果这一有利趋势持续下去，一级谷物的价格有望跌至每担20美元的低水平，这是两个外国市政当局为本地非官方公开市场交易正式固定的价格。本地中国米商昨日表示，除非大型米业经营者进行投机和牟取暴利，否则这一发展是有可能实现的。

预计大批西贡米也将于9月初运抵上海。昨日，在爱多亚路浦东同乡会会所内的中国会计师公会，本地中国商号、工厂和店铺有意购买者的登记工作继续活跃。

CHINA PRESS

AUG 27 1939

Flour And Wheat

The selling price of native flour in
the outside market weakened gradually
during the last two days, because the
North China dealers were reluctant to
buy for transportation, owing to the flood
accident in the Tientsin areas, and
some of the local retail shops bought the
flour directly from the mills, so that the
unofficial rate was low.
On account of the shortage of
white rice during the last few
weeks, the mills prepared a big
amount of flour for local Chinese. When
any retail shops, or flour dealers asked
any flour for stocks or selling, the flour
mills delivered to the buyers immediately.
Therefore the local sellers were not in
need of any outside market flour. The
selling price of second-grade product re-
mained unchanged at $6.40 per bag, paid
in cash, but the mills still refused to accept
orders from outport dealers. Satisfactory
business was done in the market yester-
day. The unofficial price of "Gun"
native flour was still quoted at $6.50, but
the "Warship" flour fell to $6.35 per
bag. On account of the fresh improve-
ment of the foreign exchange, the rate of
foreign flour went down to $6.45.
Business in native wheat was dull in
the market yesterday, as the buyers were
inactive and the Chinese flour mills were
not interested in absorbing for further
stocks. These conditions lowered the
price of middle quality of native wheat,
and the rate of the best quality was
steady. Both the Fooh Sing and Fou
Foong Flour Mills bought 12,000 bags of
Nanking, Wushih and Soochow native
wheat.

（批：Liu C8/8）
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1939年8月27日

面粉与小麦

过去两天，外盘本地面粉的售价逐渐走弱，因为华北经销商由于天津地区的水灾事故不愿进货运输，且一些本地零售店直接从磨坊购买面粉，导致非官方汇率较低。

由于过去几周白米短缺，磨坊为中国本地人准备了大量面粉。当任何零售店或面粉经销商要求库存或销售面粉时，磨坊立即向买家交货。因此，本地卖家不需要任何外盘面粉。二级产品的售价保持不变，为每袋6.40美元，现金支付，但磨坊仍拒绝接受外地港埠经销商的订单。昨日市场交易良好。“Gun”牌本地面粉的非官方价格仍报价为6.50美元，但“Warship”牌面粉跌至每袋6.35美元。由于外汇状况最新改善，洋面粉价格降至6.45美元。

昨日本地小麦市场交易清淡，因为买家不活跃，且中国面粉厂对进一步吸纳库存不感兴趣。这些情况降低了中等质量本地小麦的价格，而最佳品质的价格保持稳定。福新和阜丰面粉厂均购买了12,000包南京、无锡和苏州本地小麦。

（批：Liu C8/8）

page_data.en:
24138
CHINA PRESS.
AUG 26 1939
Shanghai Rice
Market Shows
Some Optimism
Whether Shanghai has enough
rice to eat a week hence is now a
race of Time against the low stock
of cereal in the city and harvesting
of the new crop expected within
ten days.
However optimism reined on the
rice market as the price of first
grade white dropped by $1.50 to
$38 per picul. Lowest grade rice
sold at $30 per picul but the Saigon
product soared again from yester-
day's $48 to $53 a picul.
Although the Shanghai Municipal
Council could report no progress in
its negotiations with the Japanese
military authorities concerning the
Wuhu rice blockade, it was pointed
out that rice had been trickling
into the city from interior growing
points in larger quantities this week
than it has for some time past.
Yesterday more than 9,000 bags
entered the city.
Quiet Rules
Following scattered rice riots
during the past week, yesterday
presented a peaceful picture with-
out a single outbreak reported here.
Among the poorer classes it is re-
ported that due to the high cost
of rice a general switch over to a
flour noodle diet is in progress. The
City Chamber of Commerce is said
to have appealed to the Flour Mill
Owners Guild not to boost prices
at this crucial time.
A cargo of 18,000 bags of Saigon
rice bought by Mr. Yu Ya-ching
prominent local merchant is report-
ed due today when it may be ex-
pected that the local price of the
cereal will drop further.
Many Arrests
Rice riots at Settlement rice
hongs have resulted in dozens of
arrests. First rioters to appear in
court was yesterday morning when
two men, Mei Ching-ken and Lu
Se-tsing, received a light suspended
sentences of three months each.
The riot occurred at the Kwang
Hwa Rice Hong at 206 Stonebridge
Road. At 7.15 Thursday night a
gang of 100 mobsters surrounded
and broke into the hong but before
they could steal much, cries of help
from the shopkeepers brought a
few police who frightened away the
men. Two however were slow on
their feet and found themselves
nabbed by the police.
Later it was found that $200 worth
of rice and grains were seized by
the mob.
page_data.zh:
24138
《字林西报》。
1939年8月26日
上海米市
显现些许乐观情绪

上海是否有足够的稻米供一周后食用，目前是一场时间与城市低谷物库存及预计十天内新粮收割之间的竞赛。

然而，米市弥漫着乐观情绪，一级白米价格每担下跌1.50美元，至38美元。最低等级大米售价为每担30美元，但西贡米价格再次飙升，从昨日的每担48美元涨至53美元。

尽管上海公共租界工部局报告称，在与日本军方当局就芜湖大米封锁问题进行的谈判中未取得进展，但有人指出，本周从内地产区流入城市的稻米数量比过去一段时间要多。

昨日进入城市的稻米超过9,000袋。

平静局面

继上周发生零星的米骚乱后，昨日呈现出一片和平景象，此处未报告发生一起爆发事件。

据报道，在贫困阶层中，由于米价高昂，普遍转向以面粉面条为主食的转变正在进行中。据悉，上海总商会已呼吁面粉业公会在此关键时刻不要抬高价格。

据报，当地著名商人虞洽卿先生购买的一批18,000袋西贡大米将于今日抵达，届时预计该谷物的本地价格将进一步下跌。

多人被捕

在租界米行发生的米骚乱导致数十人被捕。首批出庭的骚乱者于昨日上午受审，两名男子梅景根（Mei Ching-ken，音译）和陆世清（Lu Se-tsing，音译）各被判处三个月缓刑，刑罚较轻。

骚乱发生在石路桥路206号的光华米行。周四晚7点15分，一群100名暴徒包围并闯入该米行，但在他们窃取大量财物之前，店主的呼救声引来了几名警察，吓退了这些人。然而，有两人行动迟缓，发现自己被警察抓获。

后来发现，暴徒抢走了价值200美元的米粮。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

AUG 26 1939

Rice Situation
Greatly Eased

Price Reduced After
Shipment Arrives

With the arrival yesterday of
5,000 bags of rice and another ship-
ment of 1,800 tons due here before
the end of the month, the rice
situation in Shanghai has somewhat
improved and the price declined by
$1 per picul yesterday. Rice riots
did not occur as most shops were
able to sell the quantities required
by customers.
While the normal average daily
consumption is 10,000 bags, it was
pointed out by reliable circles that
since the increase in the price, this
figure has been somewhat reduced.
The 1,800 ton shipment due at the
end of the month was ordered in
Saigon by Mr. Yu Ya-ching and
while most of it will be distributed
to refugees, it was understood that
a part of the shipment would be
sold to the poorer classes who are
hardest hit by the high cost of the
staple food.
Further shipments are expected in
September and thus it may be
safely said that the difficult rice
situation here has come to an end.
inasmuch as that there is enough
stock in this city at present to last
until further substantial shipments
will arrive here.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，

1939年8月26日

米荒局势
大大缓解

货物抵沪后
价格下调

随着昨日5,000袋大米的抵达，以及另一批1,800吨大米预计在本月底前运抵，上海的米荒局势有所改善，昨日米价每担下跌1美元。未发生米骚乱，因为大多数商店能够出售顾客所需的数量。

虽然正常的日均消费量为10,000袋，但可靠人士指出，自价格上涨以来，这一数字已有所减少。

月底即将抵达的1,800吨货物是由虞洽卿先生在西贡订购的，虽然大部分将分发给难民，但据了解，部分货物将出售给受主食高价打击最严重的贫困阶层。

预计9月份将有更多货物运抵，因此可以稳妥地说，此地的困难米荒局势已经结束，因为目前本市的库存足以维持到下一批大量货物抵达。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
AUG 26 1939
Improved Situation Is Seen
In Local Rice Markets
Prices Take Downward Trend As Shipments Of
Grain Reach Shanghai; Apprehension Less On
Part Of Chinese Though Cost Is High
An easier tendency continued to rule in the local rice market yesterday, with wholesale prices fluctuating by between $1 to $2, while retail prices recorded losses of about a few to 30 cents. Shipments of rice from the inland areas also recorded a slight increase, with the result that general apprehension was visibly relieved.
Commencing yesterday, registrations of Chinese firms and factories, the intending buyers of foreign rice, were taken at the Shanghai Chartered Public Accountants' Association on the third floor of the Peotung Residents' Guild, on Avenue Edward VII. The response was declared to be great.
Arrivals from the inland areas during yesterday were reported to total about 25 junkloads, and about 6,000 bags by rail and steamers. Reacting to this, the market took on a distinctly improved tone, although transactions remained quiet, only between 3,000 to 4,000 bags were reported to have changed hands.
Retail Prices
Retail prices quoted by Chinese merchants yesterday were as follows: — First grade, $38.80; medium, $37.60; and lower grade, $34 per bag of 160 catties.
The increased shipment of cereals noted yesterday had the effect of calming down general apprehensions among rice operators who attempt to unload their stocks, but buyers were generally unwilling to trade on the ruling prices, with the result that wholesale prices sustained a further loss of about $1, while medium and lower grade cereals recorded losses of from $1 to $2.
Other factors precipitating the downward trends were attributed to reports that negotiations carried on between the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Japanese authorities for the free entry of rice from the inland areas to Shanghai were proceeding satisfactorily. The concrete measures now being-adopted by local Chinese public bodies to import large quantities of foreign cereals also has had a most reassuring effect generally.
Downward Trend
Taken all in all, local rice merchants circles yesterday expressed the belief that the factors contributing to a general downward trend would continue to operate, but a return to normal conditions was not to be expected pending some tangible results being reached between the S.M.C. and the Japanese authorities. A real solution of the "rice crisis" should take into consideration the welfare of the poorer classes of people, as the better-circumstanced classes of Chinese and the Chinese shops and factories are generally better able to meet the situation. Yet, they declared, it was precisely for the benefit of the poorer classes that the competent authorities should attempt to solve the rice problems, in the interest of public peace and social order.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年8月26日
本地米市局势 seen 改善
随着谷物运抵上海，价格呈下降趋势；华人虽感成本高企，但忧虑减轻

昨日本地米市继续呈现宽松态势，批发价格在1至2美元之间波动，而零售价格则下跌了约几角至30角。来自内地的稻米运输量也略有增加，结果是普遍的担忧明显缓解。

从昨日起，有意购买外国大米的华商和工厂的登记工作在上海爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）浦东同乡会三楼的上海公证会计师公会进行。据悉响应热烈。

据报道，昨日来自内地的抵达总量约为25船载量，另有约6,000袋通过铁路和轮船运抵。对此，市场气氛明显改善，尽管交易依然清淡，据报道仅有3,000至4,000袋易手。

零售价格

昨日华商报价的零售价格如下：一级，38.80美元；中级，37.60美元；低级，每袋160斤34美元。

昨日 noted 的谷物运输量增加，起到了平息试图抛售库存的米商普遍担忧的作用，但买家普遍不愿按现行价格交易，结果是批发价格进一步下跌约1美元，而中低级谷物价格下跌1至2美元。

促成下降趋势的其他因素归因于以下报道：上海公共租界工部局与日本当局就内地大米自由进入上海事宜进行的谈判进展顺利。本地华人公共团体为进口大量外国谷物所采取的具体措施也产生了普遍的安抚效果。

下降趋势

总而言之，昨日本地米商圈子表示相信，导致普遍下降趋势的因素将继续发挥作用，但在上海公共租界工部局与日本当局达成某些实质性结果之前，不应期待恢复正常状况。“米危机”的真正解决应考虑贫困阶层的福祉，因为境遇较好的华人阶层以及华人商店和工厂通常更有能力应对局势。然而，他们宣称，正是为了贫困阶层的利益，主管当局才应尝试解决大米问题，以维护公共和平与社会秩序。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
2454
AUG 26 1939

The Rice Shortage:
A Correspondent's Anxiety

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—The recent rise in price of
rice has badly hit the already wretch-
ed Chinese residents of this city,
especially those of middle and lower
classes. A picul of rice costing $36
or so is unprecedented and is cer-
tainly beyond the average buying
power of the man in the street.
As we generally know, a great
portion of the present Shanghai re-
sidents are refugees from the in-
terior. These people have been liv-
ing either on their previous savings
or by the support of their relatives
or friends. That their conditions
are pitiful is too well-known to
need mentioning. Ever since the
beginning of this year, a number of
these people have been returning to
their native towns on account of the
high cost of living prevailing in this
city. This exodus is observed to
have come to its crowning point dur-
ing the past several months. Ac-
cording to a recent report published
in the local papers, the number of
residents in the International Settle-
ment and French Concession in
Shanghai has been reduced by one
million since the beginning of this
year and further reduction is ex-
pected towards the end of current
year. The huge reduction in number
of residents will probably give one
some impression as to the seriousness
of the local economical condition.
In this connection, it might as well
be pointed out that residents in
Hongkew and Yangtsepoo districts
have been greatly increased since the
beginning of this year. This is un-
doubtedly due to the cheaper rent
and lower price of daily necessities
prevailing in these areas compared
with those in the Settlement and
Concession. The reduction in num-
ber of residents in the Settlement and
Concession has given rise to some
anxiety among the local business and
financial circles. Business in general
was flourishing last year. Some busi-
ness is said to have reaped such a huge
profit that they have had never en-
joyed before. Further, a considerable
number of new shops have sprung
up last year to meet the increasing
demand on the part of population.
A contrast of conditions of current
year to that of last leads one to
worry very much about the future
of this metropolis. As a sequel to
the reduction of residents in the
Settlement and Concession business
firms are the first to suffer. The fall
in value of Chinese dollars has in-
creased the prices of various com-
modities to such a degree that they
are generally beyond the reach of
working class. Among those the most
hard hit one are, of course, the im-
port firms. Some import firms have
practically no business to do since
the fall of dollar, and as the time is
going on there seems no alternative
for them but to close up the business.
Firms other than this category
though are less unfortunate, but the
difference is only in degree.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
2454
1939年8月26日

米荒：
一位通讯员的焦虑

致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——近期米价的上涨严重打击了本市本已悲惨的中国居民，尤其是中下层阶级。每担米 costing 36美元左右是前所未有的，肯定超出了普通市民的平均购买力。

正如我们所知，目前上海居民中有很大一部分是来自内地的难民。这些人要么靠以前的积蓄生活，要么靠亲戚或朋友的接济。他们的处境之悲惨众所周知，无需赘述。自今年年初以来，由于本市生活费用高涨，这些人中已有不少人返回家乡。据观察，这种外流在过去几个月达到了顶峰。根据当地报纸最近发表的一份报告，自今年年初以来，上海公共租界和法租界的居民人数减少了100万，预计在今年年底还将进一步减少。居民人数的巨大减少可能会让人对本地经济状况的严重性产生某种印象。

在这方面，不妨指出，自今年年初以来，虹口和杨浦区（Yangtsepoo）的居民人数大幅增加。这无疑是由于与租界和法租界相比，这些地区的租金更便宜，日常必需品价格更低。租界和法租界居民人数的减少引起了本地商业和金融界的一些焦虑。去年商业总体繁荣。据说有些生意获得了前所未有的巨额利润。此外，去年涌现了大量新店以满足人口日益增长的需求。将今年的状况与去年对比，让人非常担心这座大都市的未来。作为租界和法租界居民减少的后果，商业公司首当其冲。法币贬值使各种商品的价格上涨到工人阶级普遍无法承受的程度。其中受影响最严重的当然是进口商行。自法币下跌以来，一些进口商行实际上无生意可做，随着时间的推移，他们似乎别无选择，只能停业。其他类别的公司虽然不那么不幸，但也只是程度不同而已。

page_data.en:
24155

The situation is aggravated by the
recent rise in price of rice, which is
the prelude to the general increase
in price of practically every kind of
commodity. With the exception of a
few wealthy class, most people are
unable to afford the sky-high price
and are being in a state of disaster.
Notwithstanding the pains we suffer,
the prices of rice and other com-
modities show no sign of dropping
down: instead there is every pos-
sibility of their going up. The
ultimate result will be that there
will be no buying power on the
part of population to meet the
high price. If the present situa-
tion were allowed to continue
unabated the time would not be long
before the business world in Shang-
hai come to a general depression, if
not bankruptcy.
In speaking of this, I have no in-
tention to exaggerate the situation. I
simply bring the grave situation to
the notice of those responsible for
the maintenance of peace and order
of this city. I doubt if our City
Fathers are giving due attention to
this matter and devising ways and
means to relieve the present string-
ency.
LI CHUN.
Shanghai, Aug. 24.
***The correspondent may rest
assured that the City Fathers are
anxiously seeking the best remedy for
the existing situation, and that every-
thing possible will be done to alleviate
it, but it is necessary to remember
that to find a solution is not likely to
prove so easy as was the case of the
rice shortage shortly after the out-
break of hostilities.—Ed.
page_data.zh:
24155

近期米价上涨加剧了局势，这几乎是所有种类商品价格普遍上涨的前奏。除少数富裕阶层外，大多数人无力承担天价，正处于灾难状态。

尽管我们遭受痛苦，但大米和其他商品的价格没有显示出下跌的迹象：相反，它们完全有可能继续上涨。最终结果将是人口没有购买力来应对高价。如果允许目前的局势不受遏制地持续下去，不久之后上海的商业界将陷入普遍萧条，甚至破产。

说到这一点，我无意夸大局势。我只是提请负责维护本市和平与秩序的相关人士注意这一严峻局势。我怀疑我们的“城市父老”（City Fathers）是否给予了此事应有的关注，并正在 devising 方法和手段来缓解目前的紧张状况。

李春。
上海，8月24日。
***通讯员可以放心，“城市父老”们正在焦急地寻求解决现有局势的最佳良方，并将尽一切可能加以缓解，但有必要记住，找到解决方案并不像战事爆发后不久出现的米荒那样容易解决。——编者

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
24130
8039 A./5
AUG 25 1939

Rice Price Goes
Over $59; Riots
· Kept In Check

Situation Easing Seen
By Chairman
Of SMC

YU YA-CHING
PURCHASE DUE

Market Expecting New
Crop To Arrive
In Ten Days

Causing further tensity to the acute rice situation now prevailing in Shanghai, the price of first grade rice rose over $50 per picul this morning, probably the first time the grain has ever reached such a high level in the history of Shanghai, as rice dealers in the two foreign areas of the city quoted from $51 to $53 per picul.
Rioting, however, has subsided somewhat since yesterday, the last outbreak occurring at 7.25 o'clock last night, when about 100 Chinese attacked the Kwong Wo Rice Hong at 206 Stone Bridge Road and stole the entire stock of seven piculs of rice stored in the shop, after causing minor damage to the shop's furniture. The rioters fled before an alarm could be raised, but Probationary Sergeant L. J. Ellis of Sinza Police Station succeeded in arresting one of the mob, while another was subsequently apprehended by a Chinese constable. Both men were brought up in the First Special District Court and were given suspended sentences of three months' imprisonment.

Easing-Up Seen
The Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Mr. Cornell S. Franklin, informed the Evening Post this morning that he expected the present acute rice situation would ease up shortly.
Meanwhile, reports that the next rice crop will be ready in about 10 days have caused belief among the local authorities that the present shortage will be relieved to a great extent.

Yu Ya-ching Purchase
About 1800 tons of Saigon rice, purchased by Mr. Yu Ya-ching, noted Chinese philanthropist and shipping magnate, is expected to arrive in Shanghai this afternoon or early tomorrow morning.
It was reported this morning that the rice would mostly be given to local Chinese refugees and other charitable groups in the city.

Lila

1939年8月25日

米价突破59美元；骚乱
得到控制

工部局主席认为
局势正在缓和

虞洽卿
采购在即

市场预计新粮
将于十日内抵达

上海目前严峻的米荒局势进一步加剧，今晨上等米价格涨至每石50美元以上，这可能是上海历史上米价首次达到如此高位，因为本市两个外侨区域的米商报价为每石51至53美元。
然而，自昨天以来，骚乱已有所平息，最后一次爆发发生在昨晚7点25分，当时约100名中国人袭击了位于石桥路206号的广和米行（Kwong Wo Rice Hong），在对该店家具造成轻微损坏后，偷走了店内储存的全部7石大米。骚乱者在警报发出前逃散，但新闸捕房的见习巡佐 L. J. Ellis 成功逮捕了一名暴徒，另一名随后被一名华捕抓获。两人均被提解至第一特区法院审理，并被判处三个月监禁，缓刑执行。

局势有望缓和

上海公共租界工部局主席科尼利厄斯·S·富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）先生今晨告知《晚邮报》，他预计目前的严峻米荒局势将很快得到缓解。
与此同时，有关下一季稻米将在约10天内上市的消息，使地方当局相信目前的短缺状况将在很大程度上得到缓解。

虞洽卿采购

由著名华人慈善家及航运巨头虞洽卿先生购买的约1800吨西贡米，预计将于今天下午或明天清晨抵达上海。
今晨有报道称，这批大米将主要提供给本地的中国难民及城内的其他慈善团体。

Lila

日本米价
持续上涨
政府可能被迫
实施管制
东京，8月24日电。
由于需求超过供应，米价持续稳步上涨，已达到每斛40日元的新高位。
因此，米价统制委员会在昨晚召开的特别会议上，审议了援引《米价统制法》第4条的事宜，该条款将赋予政府对米价的完全控制权。
《米价统制法》授权主管当局向米商或其代理人发布有效管控大米分销所需的命令，从而为确保价格适宜和流通顺畅，实现限制销售价格以及禁止囤积居奇的目的。——路透社。

Chinese-American Daily News:

Rice Riots Unchecked in Pootung and Nantao

Several cases of rice riots in the Foreign Settlements are reported to have taken place during the past few days. Even in the occupied district of Nantao, more than 20 cases of rice stealing took place yesterday. At 9 a.m. yesterday three piculs of rice were plundered from No.383 Seward Road, Hongkew. A large number of poor people in Yangtszepoo are living on potatoes, hence the price of potatoes has risen from $3.00 to $4.50 per picul.

At 7.50 p.m. yesterday, more than 100 poor people rushed into the Wang Wu Rice Hong (王弘米行) at No.20, Lane 51, Sinza Road and carried off 7 piculs of rice. One person was arrested.

Yesterday afternoon, some 100 men and women plundered several rice shops in the busy section of Tung Chong Road, Pootung. At Yang Ka Tu several tens of women and children rushed into the Wang Tsun Kee Rice Shop (王尊記) to plunder rice and several of them were arrested.

On August 23, thousands of people completely plundered several rice shops in Sungkiang.

Yesterday various villages in Sungkiang were ordered by the Chinese Guerrilla Warfare Zone Hsien Government to sell rice at $0.10 per catty(equivalent to $16 per picul) and each person was allowed to buy only 3 catties at a time. The rice thus purchased would first be soaked in water before it is allowed to be taken away. This is done to prevent hoarding.

《中美日报》：

浦东与南市米荒骚乱未止

据报道，过去几天内，外国租界内发生了数起米荒骚乱事件。即便在被占领的南市地区，昨天也发生了20多起偷米案件。昨天上午9时，虹口华德路383号遭抢，损失大米三石。杨树浦的大量贫民以土豆为生，因此土豆价格已从每石3.00美元涨至4.50美元。

8月23日，成千上万的人将松江的几家米店洗劫一空。

昨天，松江各村庄奉中国游击战区县政府命令，以每斤0.10美元（相当于每石16美元）的价格出售大米，每人每次限购3斤。购得的大米在允许带走之前需先在水中浸泡。此举旨在防止囤积。

August 25, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Shun Pac (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper):

RICE SNATCHING IN SHANGHAI

Yesterday more than ten cases of highway
robbery of rice by poor people took place in the Foreign
Settlements. Two of them occurred in the vicinity of
Rue Kraetzer and Luzon Road, four in the vicinity of Rue
du Marche and Rue du Pere Froc, one in Rue Gaston Kahn,
seven in the Western District in the International
Settlement and two in Sinza Road.
Pedestrians were sympathetic towards the rice
snatchers, while in some of the cases policemen did not
chase after the snatchers but smiled, because they also
were sympathetic towards these poor people for they were
driven to this by poverty.
As their loss was not heavy, the victimized
rice shops did not make any report to the Police, because
they know that it would not be of any use if they did so.
As a result of these rice riots, rice shops
closed their iron grilles or remained only half open for
business.

《新顺帕克报》（Sin Shun Pac，日资中文报纸）：

上海抢米事件

昨天，外国租界内发生了十多起穷人拦路抢米案件。其中两起发生在克勒策尔路（Rue Kraetzer）和吕宋路附近，四起发生在马立斯路（Rue du Marche）和神父路（Rue du Pere Froc）附近，一起发生在嘉斯顿·康路（Rue Gaston Kahn），七起在国际租界西区，两起在新闸路。
路人同情抢米者，而在某些案件中，警察并未追赶抢米者，而是面带微笑，因为他们也同情这些因贫困所迫而不得不如此做的穷人。
由于损失不大，受害米店并未向警方报案，因为他们知道报案也无济于事。
受这些米荒骚乱影响，米店纷纷拉下铁栅栏门，或仅半开门营业。

AUG 25 1939
Rice Situation
Serious Here
Improvement Likely
Within Few Days ;
Prices Advance
Notwithstanding the fact that the
price of rice advanced by a further
$4 per picul yesterday, reliable quar-
ters indicated yesterday that within
a few days a satisfactory solution to
the whole problem would be found
and that in the meanwhile existing
stocks in Shanghai are quite sufficient
to cope with the normal demand.
Police both in the Settlement and
the Concession are on the look-out
for trouble-makers, however, as they
wish to prevent any further riots
being staged in front of rice shops,
the operators of which, it is pointed
out, can only sell what they have,
and cannot be expected to sell rice
when they have none left. A riot
was staged at a rice shop at 383 Ward
Road yesterday morning when a
small crowd attacked the premises
and managed to carry away two and
a half piculs of rice, before a police
party from Yulin Road Station
arrived on the scene to disperse the
demonstrators.
A small shipment of 537 bags of
rice arrived here yesterday afternoon
and was unloaded on the Bund, being
subsequently taken away by a fleet
of trucks. As police precautions had
been taken at the Bund, no untoward
incident occurred.

尽管昨天米价又上涨了每石4美元，但可靠方面昨天表示，整个问题将在几天内找到令人满意的解决方案，同时指出上海现有的库存足以应付正常需求。
然而，租界和法租界的警方都在警惕滋事分子，因为他们希望防止在米店门前发生进一步的骚乱。有人指出，米店经营者只能出售现有存货，不能指望他们在无米可卖时继续出售。昨天上午，华德路383号的一家米店发生骚乱，一小群人袭击了该处，并在榆林路捕房的警队赶到现场驱散示威者之前，抢走了两石半大米。
昨天下午，一批537袋的小批量大米运抵此处，在外滩卸货，随后由一队卡车运走。由于警方在外滩采取了预防措施，未发生任何意外事件。

Cereal Hits
Record High
Price Of $48
Shop On Stone Bridge
Road Looted By Mob
Of 100 Persons
WARD ROAD SCENE
OF FRESH TROUBLE
Japanese Hold Only
Key To Solution Of
Problem
Although the price of rice con-
tinued to mount in Shanghai yes-
terday, reaching the high figure of
$48, attacks against rice shops
lessened considerably compared
with the number of such disturb-
ances staged by mobs of the poorer
classes on Wednesday.
Only two riots were reported
yesterday in the International
Settlement against five on the
the previous day while no
serious disturbances occurred in
the French Concession.
About 40 persons attacked a
small rice shop at 383 Ward
Road at 9.15 a.m. yesterday and
stole two and one-half piculs of
rice. The mob was subsequent-
ly dispersed by the police.
The next riot reported occurred
at the Kwong Wo Rice Shop, Lane
51, House 206, Stone Bridge Road.
More than 100 rioters stormed the
place and looted it of seven piculs
of the cereal, all the stocks that
the merchant had.
Japanese Hold Key
A solution to the rice shortage
here can be solved now only by a
change in attitude of the Japanese
authorities north of the creek. It
was learned from a semi-official
source yesterday.
Declaring that one week's supply
of rice remains in the city, the
same source foresaw an early
change in attitude of local Japanese
authorities who control the flow of
supplies to the city. This predic-
tion was based on the conciliatory
tone of press conference yesterday
given here by Lt. General Hikozo
Yamada, Commander-in-Chief of
the Japanese Expeditionary force in
Central China.
Should a let-up in the ban on rice
supplies for the city fail to
eventuate, it was pointed out, the
Japanese could at the last minute
"save" the city's starving millions
by distributing low cost rice.

1939年8月2日
谷物价格
创48美元
历史新高
石桥路店铺
遭百人暴徒
洗劫
华德路再现
新冲突
日本人掌握
解决此问题
的关键

尽管昨天上海米价继续攀升，达到48美元的高位，但与周三由较贫困阶层暴徒制造的骚乱数量相比，针对米店的袭击大幅减少。
昨天国际租界内仅报告了两起骚乱，而前一天为五起，法租界内未发生严重骚乱。
昨天上午9点15分，约40人袭击了华德路383号的一家小米店，偷走了两石半大米。暴徒随后被警方驱散。
接下来报告的骚乱发生在石桥路51弄206号的广和米店。100多名暴徒冲击该地，抢走了该商人所有的全部库存，即7石谷物。

日本人掌握关键

据一位半官方消息人士昨天透露，此处米荒问题的解决，现在只能依靠苏州河北岸日本当局态度的改变。
该消息人士宣称市内仅剩一周的大米供应，并预见控制流入该市物资供应的当地日本当局的态度将很快发生变化。这一预测基于日本华中派遣军司令山田乙二中将昨天在此举行的记者招待会上所表现的和解语调。
有人指出，如果对城市大米供应的禁令未能放松，日本人可以在最后一刻通过分发低价大米来“拯救”城市中数百万饥民。

page_data.en:
24318

No Hoarding

It was learned from the same
quarter that there is no large-scale
hoarding of rice in the city, a fact
which seems to be borne out by
the failure of the police to sub-
stantiate reports yesterday that one
dealer was hoarding several
thousand bags of the cereal.

While scattered rice riots con-
tinued to be reported yesterday and
the price of rice soared to the
sensational height of $48 per picul
it was learned that the Shanghai
Municipal Council, which has inter-
mittantly been reported as con-
sidering the purchase of foreign
rice, is quite without funds to do
so. With 10,000 bags a day con-
sumed here it would cost the city
$3,000,000 a week to feed the
population and even the credit of
the Council which is strong would
not stand up long under such a
drain considering the unsound
status of the Chinese dollar.

Japanese Buying Rumored

Rumors circulated yesterday that
much of the rice being bought up
by Japanese from surrounding areas
of Shanghai is being transported to
Japan where the crop has been
poor due to the shortage of farmers
recalled to the colors and farm girls
doing factory work.

Mr. Yu Ya Ching, prominent local
merchant was reported to have
held a conference with other rice
dealers on the subject of forming a
committee to purchase foreign rice
should the crisis here continue.
page_data.zh:
24318

无囤积行为

从同一消息来源获悉，市内并无大规模囤积大米的行为，这一事实似乎得到了证实，因为警方未能核实昨天关于一名商人囤积数千袋谷物的报道。

虽然昨天仍零星报道有米荒骚乱，且米价飙升至每石48美元的惊人高度，但据悉，间歇性有传闻称正在考虑购买外国大米的上海公共租界工部局，实际上并无资金进行此类采购。按每天消耗1万袋计算，供养全市人口每周需花费300万美元，考虑到法币地位不稳，即使工部局信誉良好，也难以长期承受如此巨大的资金流失。

谣传日本人购买

昨天流传着这样的谣言：日本人在上海周边地区购买的大量大米正被运往日本，由于农民被征召入伍以及农家女孩进入工厂工作，导致劳动力短缺，日本国内收成不佳。

据报道，本地著名商人虞洽卿先生已与其他米商举行会议，商讨如果此处危机持续，则组建委员会购买外国大米事宜。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,
AUG 25 1939
SHANGHAI'S ECONOMIC
DIFFICULTIES
The further substantial rise in the
price of market and fresh food supplies
yesterday, the beginning of what might
develop into much more serious rice
riots, the suggestion by the British
Residents' Association that the Council
should form a Rental Adjustment Com-
mittee to arbitrate on disputed cases, the
big increase which the Shanghai Power
Company has been compelled to make in
its surcharge in order to meet the ever-
increasing cost of coal—these are only
some of the facets of a local economic
and financial situation which is bearing
ever more heavily upon almost the whole
community. Rice has soared to over $40
per bag and unless further supplies are
soon received the price is bound to go
higher and stocks become insufficient to
meet the needs of the population. There
are many differently viewed reasons and
factors behind the actual shortage of
grain, but it must still be hoped that
before a really critical stage is reached
new supplies will come into the foreign-
controlled areas. The Council is no doubt
exerting its best efforts in this direction,
and its decision not to buy rice from
Saigon to ease the shortage, as it did
when the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke
out here two years ago, must have been
made in the expectancy that local
difficulties will be overcome. If it is not
the great fall in the exchange value of
the dollar which is the major factor
behind the rice price problem it is all too
true that the dollar's slump explains the
great majority of other financial difficul-
ties. Owing to the crisis in Europe there
has been some improvement in the rate
of exchange these past two days, but it
ought clearly to be understood that this
is not a real appreciation of our own
currency but a temporary position
brought about by reconversions into local
dollars by those who think that war might
break out in which practically all currency
values will be affected. The fact which
we in Shanghai have to bear constantly
in mind is that the dollar is worth no
more than what it will buy, and we see
that that is getting less and less. The
rising price of compradore stores and
provisions, rising rentals, increased
electricity charges, the greatly increased
price of gasoline, and everything which
is imported as well as local produce, tell
their own plain story, which is that what
we are pleased to call "a dollar" is
merely a piece of paper possessed of no
inherent or intrinsic worth but only of a
value which others are prepared to
accept.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年8月25日
上海的经济困境

昨日市场及新鲜食品价格进一步大幅上涨，这可能演变为更为严重的米骚乱的开端，英国侨民协会建议工部局成立租金调整委员会以仲裁争议案件，以及上海电力公司因煤炭成本不断攀升而被迫大幅提高附加费——这些仅仅是当地经济和金融局势的几个侧面，该局势正日益沉重地压在整个社区几乎所有人的身上。大米价格已飙升至每袋40元以上，除非很快收到更多供应，否则价格势必继续上涨，库存将不足以满足人口需求。造成实际粮食短缺的原因和因素众说纷纭，但仍须希望在真正危急阶段到来之前，新的供应能进入外国控制区。工部局无疑正在此方向尽最大努力，其决定不像两年前中日敌对行动在此爆发时那样从西贡购买大米以缓解短缺，这一定是基于地方困难将被克服的预期。如果不是美元汇价的大幅下跌是米价问题背后的主要因素，那么美元暴跌解释了绝大多数其他金融困难也是千真万确的。由于欧洲危机，过去两天汇率有所改善，但显然应理解，这不是我们本国货币的真正升值，而是由那些认为战争可能爆发、几乎所有货币价值都将受到影响的人将资金重新兑换成当地美元所造成的暂时局面。我们在上海必须时刻牢记的事实是，美元的价值仅在于它能买到什么，而我们看到这种购买力正变得越来越少。买办商店商品和生活物资价格上涨、租金上涨、电费增加、汽油价格大幅上涨，以及所有进口商品和本地产品的价格，都清楚地说明了一个事实：我们乐于称为“一美元”的东西仅仅是一张纸，没有任何固有或内在价值，只有他人愿意接受的价值。

page_data.en:
When landlords, compradores, retail-
ers, and public utility concerns which
have to buy their raw materials at
present rates of exchange increase their
charges they are, in very many cases,
doing only what they must do unless they
are going either into bankruptcy or down
to penury. When it is said that a workman,
or a servant, gets $30 a month (let us
say) it sounds not so bad, because we
have always thought that that was about
a fair figure. But the fact of the matter
is that that workman or servant is getting
about 10/- a month, which is fast
becoming tragically ridiculous. What
Shanghai as a whole is faced with is the
necessity of general revision in terms of
the dollar's real worth. If we were all
as wise as theory ought to make us, if
we could learn the lesson which has been
so painfully experienced by others else-
where when a currency has gone almost
to nothing, we should quickly re-assess
everything we use, eat, or have to pay
for in terms of the dollar's current buying
capacity. As matters are, vast numbers
of people are becoming more and more
impoverished, less able to buy what they
did formerly, unable to save even a
copper, and, in many cases, being forced
to dig into savings and capital. This is a
situation which cannot persist for long
without having a serious effect upon the
economy of the community of the city as
a whole, and, as is already so well known,
upon the financial position of the Adminis-
tration. It is becoming clear that with
the dollar at its present rate of exchange
Shanghai cannot go on without revising
its ideas of what "a dollar" means.
Chungking has said that it never did see
the necessity of maintaining the currency
value in the Settlements and Concessions
and occupied areas where there are
speculators, luxury importers, and those
who hasten to convert national currency
into other currencies, but that can be
little consolation in face of the need for
us all to buy life's necessities, many of
which either have to be imported or have
a price which is almost immediately
affected by rates of exchange. There is
no guarantee that the dollar will stay
even at its present low level; if and when
it goes lower we shall be more than ever
"up against it."

Considerations like these come to
mind when thinking over Britain's
decision not to co-operate with Japan on
the currency question, for it is hard to
see how the position can be prevented
going from bad to worse—eventually, if
not immediately. If another European
war should come, the chances of outside
aid for Chungking's currency will
dwindle down to zero and the whole of
what might be called "occupied China"
will quite likely be left to take pot luck
by the Chungking régime. It will, or
should, be the task of someone to see that
coastal China has a worthy currency, and
co-operation with the de facto authorities
to that end strikes one as being a reason-
able course to take. Maybe, there would
be many preliminary difficulties to clear
away and a strict understanding to be
reached regarding equal treatment and
facilities for all, but the economic health
and productivity of many millions of
people would be safeguarded.

page_data.zh:
当房东、买办、零售商以及必须以当前汇率购买原材料的公用事业公司提高收费时，在许多情况下，他们只是在做必须做的事，否则他们将面临破产或陷入贫困。当人们说一名工人或仆人每月收入30元（比方说）时，听起来并不太糟，因为我们一直认为这是一个相当公平的数额。但事实是，这名工人或仆人的月收入约合10先令，这正迅速变得可悲且荒谬。上海整体所面临的是必须根据美元的实际价值进行全面修订的必要性。如果我们都像理论所期望的那样明智，如果我们能吸取他人在货币几乎变得一文不值时所痛苦经历的教训，我们就应根据美元当前的购买力迅速重新评估我们要使用、食用或支付的一切费用。就目前情况而言，大量人群正日益贫困，越来越无力购买以前能买到的东西，甚至无法存下一枚铜板，并且在许多情况下被迫动用储蓄和资本。这种情况若持续下去，不久必将对整个城市社区的经济产生严重影响，并且正如众所周知的那样，也将影响行政当局的财政状况。显而易见，在美元处于当前汇率的情况下，上海若不修正其对“一美元”含义的看法，将无法维持下去。重庆方面曾表示，它从未认为有必要在存在投机者、奢侈品进口商以及急于将法币转换为其他货币的人群所在的租界、通商口岸及占领区维持货币价值，但在我们所有人都需要购买生活必需品——其中许多要么必须进口，要么价格几乎立即受汇率影响——的需求面前，这几乎不能带来什么安慰。无法保证美元即使维持在目前的低水平；如果且当它进一步下跌时，我们将更加“陷入困境”。

在思考英国决定不在货币问题上与日本合作时，这类考量浮现在脑海中，因为很难看出如何防止局势恶化——即使不是立即，最终也会如此。如果另一场欧洲战争爆发，重庆法币获得外部援助的机会将缩减至零，整个所谓“被占领的中国”很可能被重庆政权听天由命。某人的任务，或者说应有的任务，是确保中国沿海地区拥有有价值的货币，为此目的与实际当局合作似乎是一条合理的途径。也许会有许多初步困难需要清除，并在平等待遇和各方设施方面达成严格谅解，但数千万人的经济健康和生产力将得到保障。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
AUG 25 1939

The Rice Shortage :
Swift Action Wanted

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—The rice problem which confronts this community is serious and its seriousness may be far-reaching. In normal time local government cannot remain indifferent. In this abnormal time its responsibility must become so much greater. But what is proposed for either or both of the Municipal Councils to do?
The Shanghai Municipal and the French Municipal Councils, methinks, can join hands and heads together for whatever should be done. An emergency advisory committee, for example, may be appointed jointly and in accordance with one of the advices which must be forthcoming, an international relief committee on food may be organized. The latter committee ought to do one of the possible things very soon and that is to sell rice and, if necessary, other commodities supplementary to or substitute for rice at cost or at a price which will break the psychology of panic on one hand and on the other the practice of profiteering either by speculative merchants or unusual speculators. Appeal for grant of aid as well as of standard rate of foreign exchange may succeed, depending on the honesty, standing, ability and experience of those who will constitute the Committee.
Members of both Councils must look ahead and labour for the welfare of all who come to live and trade and work under their control. Security and order in a community can be maintained so much better from every point of view only when there is no danger of starvation—no pretext for riot—no incentive for violence. It pays for the Councils to act without any more delay.
C. H. LEE.
Shanghai, Aug. 24.

《字林西报》，
1939年8月25日

米荒：
亟需迅速行动

致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——本社区面临的米粮问题十分严重，其严重性可能影响深远。在正常时期，地方政府不能漠不关心。在这个非常时期，其责任必然更加重大。但是，提议两个市议会中的任何一个或两者共同做什么呢？
我认为，上海公共租界工部局和法公董局可以携手合作，共同谋划应采取的行动。例如，可以联合任命一个紧急咨询委员会，并根据必将提出的建议之一，组织一个国际粮食救济委员会。后一委员会应尽快做一件可能的事情，即以成本价或足以打破一方面恐慌心理、另一方面遏制投机商人或异常投机者牟取暴利做法的价格出售大米，以及在必要时出售大米的补充品或替代品。申请援助拨款以及标准外汇汇率能否成功，取决于组成该委员会人员的诚实、地位、能力和经验。
两个市议会的成员必须放眼未来，为所有在其管辖下生活、贸易和工作的人的福祉而努力。只有当没有饥饿的危险——没有骚乱的借口——没有暴力的诱因时，从各方面来看，社区的安全和秩序才能得到更好的维护。市议会不再拖延地采取行动是符合其利益的。
C. H. 李 (音译)
上海，8月24日。

CHINA PRESS.

AUG 25 1939

Rice Market

The selling price of white rice remained unchanged at yesterday's market, and slight business was done during the entire session, as all dealers and retail shops were reluctant to buy at the highest rate. Owing to the uncertain market selling rate, the Executive Committees of the Rice and Bean Guild have decided upon a new maximum price of $40 for any kind of best quality of white rice, which was the rate already effective in yesterday's market. The market has received 1,500 bags of white rice from the growing centers in the interior, coming by truck and rail and another 15 junkloads of fresh rice supplies were brought here by steamer.
Because of mob disturbances the rice shops, located in the International Settlement and French Concession, and many of the retail shops bought only a small amount of white rice to prevent further robbing. No brisk demand was thus seen in the market throughout the session. The following price was noted at yesterday's market: newly-harvested Wusih first-grade white rice at $40; Soochow white rice, at $38.50; Stocked Wuhu white rice at $36, and the low-grade white rice from $30 to $31 per picul.
The high tendency of provincial rice was steady in yesterday's market, and the business turnover was narrow by the operators, because the market has reserved a considerable amount of provincial rice. According to a reliable source, Mr. Fu Ya-ching, one of the members of the Chinese Executive Committee of the Shanghai Municipal Council and a well-known Chinese business leader in Shanghai, have organized a "Maintaining Rice For Chinese Relief Society" with some other Chinese leading traders, and have ordered a large shipment of Saigon Rice from Indo-China to Shanghai.
The turnover of provincial rice in the session was very narrow, because the operators awaited the further improvement, the total purchases in the day were estimated at 2,000 bags of different kinds of provincial rice, and the selling rate was unchanged as compared with last final rate, while high-grade Nanking provincial rice was sold at $36 per picul. The Saigon rice in the session was quoted at $45 per bag of 220 lbs., but no business was done.

《大美晚报》。

1939年8月25日

米市

昨日米市白米售价保持不变，全天交易清淡，因为所有商行和零售店都不愿以最高价买入。由于市场售价不确定，米豆业同业公会执行委员会决定任何种类的最佳品质白米的新最高价格为40元，这也是昨日市场已生效的价格。市场收到来自内地产粮区通过卡车和铁路运来的1,500袋白米，另有15船新鲜大米供应由轮船运抵此处。
由于发生民众骚乱，位于公共租界和法租界的米店以及许多零售店仅购买了少量白米以防止进一步抢劫。因此，整个交易期间市场未见旺盛需求。昨日市场记录的价格如下：新收无锡一级白米40元；苏州白米38.50元；库存芜湖白米36元，低级白米每担30至31元。
外省米的高位趋势在昨日市场中保持稳定，由于市场储备了大量外省米，经营者的交易量狭窄。据可靠消息来源，上海公共租界华董委员之一、上海著名华商领袖傅雅清 (音译) 先生与其他几位华商领袖组织了一个“维持华赈米社”，并已订购大批西贡米从印度支那运往上海。

本次交易中外省米的成交量非常狭窄，因为经营者等待进一步改善，当日各类外省米的总采购量估计为2,000袋，售价与上次最终价格相比未变，而高等级南京外省米以每担36元售出。本次交易中西贡米报价为每袋（220磅）45元，但未达成交易。

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 25 1939

Flour And Wheat

Business in native flour was quiet and
featureless. The market rate was kept
firm by the mills. A keen demand was
displayed in the session by the dealers
and rice retail shops, because the dealers
were greatly interested in buying flour in-
stead of white rice during the period of
the rate of rice. The mills have sup-
plied a big amount of ready flour for
purchases to local buyers. The selling
price in the session was noted at $6.10
in cash for the second-grade product.
The outport dealers were not allowed
to take any action in the market, because
the mills did not offer for transportation
to North China and South Sea, so that
some of the outport dealers bought their
flour outside and the price was always
$0.20 higher compared with the official rate.
Owing to the European situation the out-
port dealers were reluctant to absorb,
while the selling rate fell to $6.50 per bag.
Satisfactory business in native wheat
was seen in the market yesterday. The
selling rate was increased by the holders,
but the Chinese flour mills continued to
buy for their stocks. There were 10,000
bags of various kinds of native wheat
being bought by both Fooh Sing and Foo
Foong Flour Mills, and the local dealers
absorbed 2 carloads of the same wheat.

《大美晚报》。
1939年8月25日

面粉与小麦

国产面粉交易平静且无特色。市场价格由磨坊保持坚挺。交易期间，商行和米零售店表现出强烈需求，因为在米价高企期间，商行对购买面粉而非白米极大感兴趣。磨坊已向本地买家供应大量现货面粉以供购买。本次交易中二级产品的现金售价记录为6.10元。
外埠商行不被允许在市场采取任何行动，因为磨坊不提供向北华和南洋地区的运输服务，因此一些外埠商行在外部购买面粉，价格总是比官方价格高0.20元。由于欧洲局势，外埠商行不愿吸纳，而售价跌至每袋6.50元。
昨日市场国产小麦交易令人满意。持有者提高了售价，但中国面粉厂继续为其库存购买。福兴和福丰面粉厂购买了10,000袋各种类型的国产小麦，本地商行吸收了2车皮同类小麦。

THE HIGH PRICE OF RICE

The Chamber of Commerce yesterday sent the
following letter to the S.M.C. :-
"The high price of rice in this city has broken
all records and the inhabitants are becoming uneasy.
During the past two years, prosperity was returning to the
areas under your jurisdiction, but if this uneasiness is
allowed to continue, the good results brought about by the
Council's efforts will disappear.
"The present situation is due to reduced
importation of rice for there was a very rich harvest last
autumn. Therefore, the regulation of rice importation is a
most important question. When ample quantities of rice
are imported, the price will naturally drop. It is hoped
that the S.M.C. will exercise its authority to cause the
rice market to return to normalcy and investigation be
made to ascertain the identity of all persons who are
hoarding rice or who are causing the price of rice to go
up."

Ta Ying Yeh Pao and Ta Mei Wan Pao (21/8), Chinese-American
Daily News, Central China Daily News, Sin Wan Pao and
Shun Pao :-

17 RICE SHOPS IN NANTAO RANSACKED IN ONE DAY

There are many refugees in the Refugee
Zone in Nantao who pose as original inhabitants chiefly
because no rent is being demanded, whilst there are about
50 or 60 rice shops selling rice at about $25 per picul.
Three days ago, some 30 persons were
gathered to plunder rice from rice shops though they each
took a quantity only sufficient for one day's supply for
a family. Since then rice shops have often been attacked
and loafers have become very active. Rice shops have
closed their doors and do trade through a small apperture
in the door.
Yesterday, loafers in various districts,
leading groups of 30 to 40 persons each, carried out a large
scale plundering of rice shops. With the group of some
40 persons lying in wait, one of them would pretend to
buy a picul of first grade rice and ask to be allowed
to examine samples, paying in advance $30. The rice shop
employees opened the doors of the shop which was completely
ransacked by the crowd. Yesterday 17 rice shops were
plundered in a similar manner.

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Hwa Pao, Chinese-American Daily News :-

Chinese Ratepayers' Association Writes to the S.M.C.
on the Question of Rice Supplies

The following letter was sent to the S.M.C.
by the Chinese Ratepayers' Association yesterday:-
"The question of rice supplies has now
become a grave one, and unless immediate relief is
forthcoming, serious consequences such as those which
took place during the reign of King Louis XVI, in connection
with the question of the supply of bread, will arise. The
cause of the present shortage of rice is due to ... non-
arrivals owing to disruption of communications and hoardings
for better prices. As the Council is known for its curious
interest in the livelihood of the people and as the rice
problem is an important question, we therefore request that
the Council quickly adopt the following suggestions:-
"(1) Regulate the supplies of rice.
"(2) Make detailed purchase of rice for
storage and enforce public sale at a reasonable price.
Efforts should be made to secure loans to meet immediate
losses. These loans may be liquidated later.
"(3) Make a detailed investigation into the
rice stocks held in the godowns owned by various banks
and thereafter make known to the public the result of
the enquiries. If the rice stocks are owned by rice hongs
or shops, they should be ordered to dispose of same within
a specified time and at a fixed price and in the case of
hoardings by private individuals, they should be forced
to sell their rice at half price or else appropriate action
be taken against them.

南市一日之内十七家米店遭劫

南市难民区内有许多难民冒充原住居民，主要因为此处不收取租金，而那里约有五六十家米店，以每担约25元的价格出售大米。三天前，约三十人聚集起来从米店抢米，虽然每人只拿取足够一家人一日食用的数量。自那以后，米店屡遭袭击，游手好闲之徒变得非常活跃。米店已关闭大门，仅通过门上的小孔进行交易。
昨日，各区的无业游民各自率领三四十人的团伙，对米店进行了大规模抢劫。其中一伙约四十人埋伏在外，一人假装购买一担上等米，并要求查看样品，预先支付30元。米店店员打开店门，店铺随即被人群彻底洗劫。昨日共有十七家米店以类似方式遭劫。

《申报》、《新闻报》、《华报》、《中美日报》：

华人纳税会就大米供应问题致函工部局

华人纳税会昨日致函工部局如下：
“大米供应问题现已变得十分严峻，除非立即采取救济措施，否则将出现如同路易十六统治时期因面包供应问题所引发的严重后果。目前大米短缺的原因是……由于交通中断导致大米无法运抵，以及为了获取更高利润而进行的囤积。鉴于工部局以对民众生计的奇特关注而闻名，且大米问题至关重要，因此我们请求工部局迅速采纳以下建议：
“(1) 调节大米供应。
“(2) 详细采购大米进行储备，并以合理价格强制公开销售。应努力争取贷款以弥补即时损失。这些贷款可日后偿还。
“(3) 对各银行拥有的仓库中持有的大米库存进行详细调查，随后向公众公布调查结果。如果大米库存属于米行或商店所有，应命令其在指定时间内以固定价格处理；如果是个人囤积，应强迫其以半价出售大米，否则对其采取适当行动。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
Mayor Fu Asks Co-operation in
Curbing Rice Speculation
AUG 22 1939
No. 5 - 23934
Official Claims Best Way to Stop Profiteering
Is to Hand Over Courts to Ta Tao Authorities

MAYOR Fu Siao-en, in a letter to the Consular Body and the
Shanghai Municipal Council, yesterday urged co-operation
with the City Government of Greater Shanghai in order to
prohibit speculation in rice by war profiteers. The most effective
way to curb this profiteering, according to the Mayor of the Ta
Tao regime, would be to hand over the jurisdiction of the First
and Second Special District Courts to the Ta Tao authorities. The
full text of the letter follows:—

With reference to our letter dated

Isolation Favoured
NANKING, Aug. 21.—Measures to
isolate the Shanghai International
Settlement or return it to the
jurisdiction of Chinese authorities
were being advocated by Reformed
Government officials and anti-
British organizations here to-day.
Desire for such drastic action was
rooted in the growing resentment
being felt here against the Shanghai
Municipal Council because of the
numerous incidents and outbreaks
of violence in the Shanghai Settle-
ment, which reached a climax
Saturday night in a clash between
police of the Settlement and the
Shanghai Special Municipality.
Mr. Wang Tsan-tzu, Director of
the Political Affairs Bureau of the
Reformed Government's Foreign
Ministry, left here this morning for
Shanghai to take part in the inves-
tigation of the gun battle, in which
two Special Municipality policemen
were slain and several others
wounded by machine-gun bullets
fired by Probationary Sergeant
W. L. Kinloch, of the S.M.P.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
held a special meeting to-day to
discuss measures in connection with
the latest Shanghai incident. A
decision was deferred until such a
time as a report is received from
Mr. Wang.

of the Executive Yuan, took a per-
sonal hand in the deliberations to-
day. He summoned Mr. Hsia Chi-
yeng, Minister of Foreign Affairs, to
the offices of the Executive Yuan to
discuss "counter-measures" against
the Shanghai Municipal Council.—

SHANGHAI TIMES,
AUG 22 1939

Rice Situation Becoming
Steadily Worse Here

Prices Still Soaring And Zenith Not Yet In Sight;
Parallel Drawn With Situation In Paris
Just Before French Revolution

The local rice situation took an ugly turn yesterday when prices advanced further from $6 to $10 as compared with last Saturday, following the resumption of unofficial open market transactions after a three-day suspension. First-grade rice was quoted at the unprecedented price of $42, and medium and lower quality cereals reached the new levels of $38 and $36 respectively.

General apprehension of social unrest was felt by responsible Chinese circles yesterday. Taking a serious view of the rice situation, the Settlement Chinese Ratepayers' Association yesterday addressed a letter to the Shanghai Municipal Council urging that immediate action be taken to remedy the abnormal situation. The letter recalled the "bread riot" during the reign of Louis XVI and pointed out that an analogous situation exists in Shanghai at the present time, and that there is a distinct possibility of the Parisian scene being enacted in this city if the present "rice crisis" should persist, in view of the fact more than 6,000,000 people, mostly refugees, are residing in Shanghai.

The restrictions which are being placed upon the free entry of rice from the inland areas into Shanghai, and general hoarding by big rice operators were given as the two chief factors now aggravating the "rice crisis." The Council is urged to devise proper measures to aid the unrestricted importation of rice into Shanghai, to make large purchases of foreign rice on its own account for relief purposes, and to carry out an investigation into the available stocks.

Rice shops, the letter urged, should be compelled to sell their stocks to the general public within a definite period of time, while private individuals who are hoarding large quantities of rice should be ordered to dispose of their stocks at half the market price, or be severely dealt with by such measures as the Council may deem it fit to take.

Unprecedented Prices

Yesterday's maximum price levels were said to be unprecedented in Shanghai. Owing to low stocks, big rice operators generally were disinclined to unload, but on the contrary, continued to absorb during the morning sessions. More than 10,000 bags of rice of various grades were reported to have been traded. Arrivals of rice from the inland areas continued to be in small quantities; only slightly more than 4,000 bags were reported to have arrived by junks, rail and steamers yesterday. During the past three days between 2,000 to 5,000 bags only were reported to have been shipped into Shanghai, but larger quantities than these were said to have been imported into the Hongkew areas.

Following the riot at the Yue Yuan Sing Rice Shop, at 89 Changping Road, on Sunday, special police patrols have been assigned to guard all the rice shops within the Settlement and Concession areas beginning from yesterday, at the request of the Rice Merchants Guild.

An unconfirmed Chinese report last night stated that French Municipal Police authorities were investigating into the alleged hoarding of more than 40,000 bags of rice by a rice shop situated at the corner of Rue Chapsal and Rue du Pere Froc, following the receipt of private information. The rice shop was suspected of engaging in profiteering.

Foreign Rice Bought

Following the example set by Mr. Yu Ya-ching and others in recently placing an order for 18,000 bags of Saigon rice for relief purposes, many local Chinese public organizations were reported last night to be making preparations to purchase large quantities of foreign rice to relieve the local rice situation.

The closest contact is understood to have been maintained between the French Municipal Administration and the Shanghai Municipal Council, but no immediate action, pending further careful study of the matter, is contemplated regarding the rice situation.

Local rice merchants' circles yesterday forecast a further rising trend in the market, it being stated that, at the most, less than 5,000 bags of rice had found their way into Shanghai during the past few days, whereas the normal daily consumption would require about 10,-000 bags. The only remedy to the situation, they averred, was effective control over prices and the ensuring of the free entry of rice into Shanghai from the inland areas. If these two problems could be thoroughly tackled by the City Fathers, it would go a long way towards fundamentally solving the rice problems.

1939年8月22日

本地米价形势日益恶化

价格仍在飙升，顶点尚不可见；
与法国大革命前夕巴黎的局势相类比

随着非官方公开市场交易在中断三天后恢复，昨日本地米价形势出现恶化，价格较上周六进一步从6美元涨至10美元。一级大米报价达到前所未有的42美元，中低品质谷物分别达到38美元和36美元的新高位。

昨日，中国各界负责人士对社会动荡普遍感到担忧。鉴于米价形势严峻，租界华人纳税会昨日致函上海公共租界工部局，敦促立即采取行动纠正这一异常状况。信函回顾了路易十六统治时期的“面包暴动”，并指出上海目前存在类似情况，鉴于上海居住着600多万人口（大多为难民），如果当前的“米荒”持续下去，巴黎的一幕极有可能在本市重演。

限制内地大米自由进入上海，以及大米大商人的普遍囤积，被认为是目前加剧“米荒”的两个主要因素。信中敦促工部局制定适当措施，协助大米 unrestricted（无限制）进口到上海，自行大量购买外国大米用于救济，并对现有库存进行调查。

信函敦促，应强制米店在规定期限内向公众出售其库存，同时应命令囤积大量大米的个人以市场价格的一半处理其库存，否则将受到工部局认为合适的严厉措施处置。

前所未有的价格

据说昨日的最高价格水平在上海是前所未有的。由于库存低，大米大商人普遍不愿抛售，相反，在上午的交易时段继续吸纳。据报道，各种等级的大米交易量超过1万包。来自内地的大米到货量依然很少；昨日通过驳船、铁路和轮船抵达的大米仅略多于4,000包。据报道，在过去三天里，运入上海的大米仅在2,000至5,000包之间，但据说有比这更多的数量进口到了虹口地区。

继周日昌平路89号悦元兴米店发生骚乱后，应米业公会请求，从昨日起，已指派特别巡逻队守卫租界和法租界区域内的所有米店。

昨晚一份未经证实的中文报道称，法国公董局警务当局在收到私人情报后，正在调查位于 Chapsal 路和 Pere Froc 路拐角处的一家米店涉嫌囤积超过40,000包大米的行为。该米店被怀疑从事牟取暴利活动。

购买外国大米

据悉，继虞洽卿等人近期订购18,000包西贡大米用于救济之后，昨夜报道许多本地中国公共团体正准备购买大量外国大米，以缓解本地米价形势。

据了解，法国公董局与上海公共租界工部局之间保持着最密切的联系，但在对该问题进行进一步仔细研究之前，不打算就米价形势采取立即行动。

本地米商圈子昨日预测市场行情将进一步上涨，据称，在过去几天里，进入上海的大米最多不到5,000包，而正常的每日消费量则需要约10,000包。他们断言，解决这一局面的唯一办法是对价格进行有效控制，并确保内地大米自由进入上海。如果市政当局能够彻底解决这两个问题，将从根本上大大推动米价问题的解决。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
AUG 22 1939
Rice Riots Occur
In Nantao
17 Shops Robbed by Mobs
On Sunday; Gangsters
Are Seen Behind Trouble
While one big rice riot has already
broken out in the Settlement it was
reported yesterday that similar riots
have been terrorizing rice shop man-
agers in Nantao for several days and
that on Sunday alone 17 shops were
victimized by hungry mobs. First
grade rice has been sold for about
$25 per picul in Nantao but although
the price is lower by seven or eight
dollars, as compared with that quoted
in foreign settlements, it is still con-
sidered too high for the people living
in the native city, most of whom are
poor.
Those who live in the Nantao Re-
fugee Zone were said to have been
exempted from paying rents but
owing to the decrease of employment
many of them can hardly make a
living. The zone is at present
crowded with people, it was stated,
and the density of population is
almost comparable to the condition
existing prior to the hostilities. Rice
shops outside the zone were victim-
ized long ago and in view of this
there have been only rice hawkers
outside the zone.
Four days ago, it was stated, about
30 hungry people robbed many rice
shops of rice but they only tried to
fill up the cans and baskets in which
they meant to carry rice. Since then
rice shop robberies have been daily
staged. At present, rice shops in
Nantao leave only a small opening in
their doors through which shop
assistants transact business.
But the desperate people had their
way on Sunday. The gangster type
of people gathered together 30 or 40
persons and asked one of them to buy
rice at a shop. This representative
of the rice buyers usually carried
some money with him and did not
appear to be a rioter. He demanded
to see the "sample" of rice and when
he was allowed to go into the shop
the others dashed up and stole all
rice they could. In this way, 17 shops
were robbed.
Rice Market Reopens
After three days' recess, the Shang-
hai Rice Market was opened to
business yesterday but very little
business was done and confusion con-
tinued to reign. The market has
been neglected for a long time by
merchants who have been obtaining
their quota outside the market. The
official price has not been followed
outside the market. Those who did
business in the market yesterday
were required to register and to name
the shops to which their rice had
been sold.
The eight persons, several of them
women, who are suspected of having
participated in Sunday evening's rice
riot in Changping Road were brought
before the First Special District Court
yesterday and after a short hearing
they were remanded in custody. It
was alleged that 20 bags of flour were
seized from the detained persons.
They were alleged to have been stolen
from the Yu Yuan Hsing Rice Shop
in Changping Road. The suspects
were charged with robbery but the
judge reserved his decision pending
further investigations.
239.3
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年8月22日
南市发生米骚乱
周日17家店铺遭暴徒抢劫；
幕后可见流氓身影

虽然公共租界内已经爆发了一起大规模米骚乱，但昨日据报道，类似的骚乱已在南市恐吓米店经理数日，仅周日一天就有17家店铺成为饥饿暴徒的受害者。南市一级大米售价约为每担25美元，虽然比外国租界报价低七八美元，但对于生活在华界的人们来说仍然被认为太高，他们大多数是穷人。

据说住在南市难民区的人免付租金，但由于就业机会减少，他们中许多人难以维持生计。据称，该区目前人口拥挤，人口密度几乎可与战事发生前的状况相比。该区外的米店早已受害，因此该区外只有米贩在经营。

据称，四天前，约30名饥饿者抢劫了许多米店的大米，但他们只是试图装满他们打算用来装米的罐子和篮子。从那以后，抢劫米店的事件每天都在上演。目前，南市的米店只在门上留一个小口，店员通过这个小口进行交易。

但在周日，绝望的人们得逞了。流氓类型的人聚集了三四十人，让其中一人去一家米店买米。这位买米代表通常带着一些钱，看起来不像暴徒。他要求查看大米“样品”，当他被允许进入店内时，其他人冲上前去，偷走了所有能拿到的大米。通过这种方式，17家店铺遭到抢劫。

米市重新开市

休市三天后，上海米市昨日重新开市，但成交量极少，混乱局面依旧。长期以来，商人一直在市场外获取配额，因而忽视了该市场。市场外的交易并未遵循官方价格。昨日在市场进行交易的人被要求登记，并指明其大米卖给了哪些店铺。

涉嫌参与周日晚昌平路米骚乱的八人（其中几名为女性）昨日被提审至第一特区法院，经过简短听证后，被还押候审。据称，从被拘留者身上搜出了20袋面粉。据称这些面粉是从昌平路的悦元兴米店偷窃的。嫌疑人被控抢劫罪，但法官保留判决，以待进一步调查。
239.3

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 22 1939
Rice Price
Here Makes
Big Jump

The rice market re-opened yes-
terday a three-day shutdown only
to find the cereal price had soared
by $6 to be $39 a picul. This
abnormal rise took place despite
the fact that more than 11,000 bags
of rice were reported to have
reached Shanghai from the in-
terior growing centers.

While the rice shops did a fast
business the city remained on a
war famine basis with known stock
supplies less than sufficient to feed
the population for nine days. As
yet the Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil has received no word from the
Japanese military authorities in
reply to its note asking that re-
strictions be eased on shipment of
rice to Shanghai from Wuhu and
other centers.

The unusually large shipment
which arrived yesterday came most-
ly by steamers from points lower
on the coast. Only 3,000 bags were
received from the immediate in-
terior.

Wuhu rice which closed on
Thursday's market at $29 a picul
sold yesterday at $33, the lowest
price quoted for any rice during
the day. But even at the high
rates prevailing a total of 4,000
bags changed hands during the
trading period. Most of this busi-
ness was carried on outside the
market, however. Saigon rice was
quoted at $40 a picul.

Police On Watch

Police continued to keep a close
watch on rice and flour shops
throughout the Settlement fearing
riots yesterday following the storm-
ing on Sunday of a small flour
shop on Changping Road. An
angry mob on that occasion broke
into the shop premises and looted
more than 100 bags of flour incited
by rumors that the price was going
higher and that a shortage was
imminent throughout the city.
The Council has not yet taken
any action in the matter of secur-
ing further rice supplies for the
city other than their present re-
presentations to the Japanese in
regard to lifting the ban on rice
exports.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年8月22日
米价
在此
大幅跳涨

大米市场在休市三天后于昨日重新开市，却发现粮价已暴涨6美元，达到每担39美元。尽管据报道有超过11,000袋大米从内地产粮区运抵上海，这种异常上涨仍然发生。

虽然米店生意兴隆，但全市仍处于战时饥荒状态，已知库存不足以为人口提供九天的口粮。截至目前，上海公共租界工部局尚未收到日本军方的回复，以回应其要求放宽从芜湖及其他中心向上海运输大米限制的照会。

昨日抵达的异常大量货物大多由轮船从沿海较低处的港口运来。仅有3,000袋来自邻近内地。

周四市场上以每担29美元收盘的芜湖米，昨日售价为33美元，这是当日任何种类大米报价中的最低价。但即使在普遍的高价位下，交易期间仍有总计4,000袋易手。然而，大部分交易是在市场外进行的。西贡米报价为每担40美元。

警方监视

警方继续严密监视租界内的米店和面粉店，因担心继周日昌平路一家小面粉店遭冲击后，昨日会发生骚乱。当时，受谣言煽动，愤怒的人群闯入店铺 premises 并抢劫了100多袋面粉，谣言称价格将上涨且全市即将出现短缺。

除目前就解除大米出口禁令一事向日本人进行交涉外，工部局尚未为确保城市进一步的大米供应采取任何行动。
