2255.
AUG 1 2 '37

Municipal Council Debates Action To Be
Taken On Threatening Shortage Of Rice Here

Representations Made
To Japanese To Lift
Export Embargo

The Rice Supplies Sub-Committee,
only emergency body of the
Shanghai Municipal Council to
survive the 1937 hostilities, met
yesterday in a tense session to
discuss the increasingly serious
problem of securing this city's
basic food from its Japanese con-
trolled growing centers.

The meeting was held following
several weeks in which rice on the
local market has been going to
progressively higher rates both
because shipments from the port of

Wuhu have been irregular and
because of the aggravated Chinese
currency situation. Reports from
all districts of Shanghai yesterday
attested to the fact that high
quality rice was impossible to buy
in shops although a plentiful
supply of the low grade product was
available.

The day previous to yesterday's
committee meeting, the S.M.C. had
made representations to the local
authorities in Wuhu asking that the
present ban of three weeks stand-
ing be lifted. No reply had been
received at the time of the meeting
yesterday. The embargo has been
in force during the past months for
periods of one and two weeks at a

time but has usually been lifted in
time to preclude any serious rice
shortage here. The present ban is
said to be the longest imposed this
year.

Questioned yesterday on possible
steps the S.M.C. would take to
force release of large stocks of rice
held here by bank godowns, T. W.
Cubb, Deputy Secretary of the
Council and rice expert, declared
that there was no cause for alarm
concerning the city's immediate
rice stocks and that consistently de-
creasing supplies in the godowns
were proof that the rice is not being
hoarded by unscrupulous specula-
tors. The fundamental problem, he
said, is to get the new rice, now

being harvested in the growing
centers, to Shanghai.

A further meeting of the Supplies
Sub-Committee will be held Monday,
Mr. Cubb said. The question of
raising the maximum price from $20
per picul may come up for discus-
sion. Then the maximum was im-
posed on the local market several
weeks ago by the S.M.C. and
French Municipal Council jointly in
an effort to eliminate speculation

《大美晚报》
2255.
1937年8月12日

工部局辩论针对此地大米短缺威胁应采取的行动

向日本方面提出交涉
要求解除出口禁令

大米供应小组委员会是上海公共租界工部局在1937年战事中幸存下来的唯一紧急机构，昨日召开了一次气氛紧张的会议，讨论从其日本控制的种植中心获取本市基本粮食这一日益严重的问题。

此次会议是在本地市场大米价格因芜湖港发货不规则以及中国货币局势恶化而逐步攀升数周之后举行的。昨日来自上海各区的报告证实，尽管低等级产品供应充足，但商店中已无法买到高质量大米。

在昨日委员会会议的前一天，工部局已向芜湖地方当局提出交涉，要求解除已持续三周的现行禁令。在昨日开会时，尚未收到回复。过去几个月里，该禁令曾以一周或两周为期限实施，但通常会在导致此地出现严重大米短缺之前及时解除。据说目前的禁令是今年实施时间最长的一次。

昨日，当被问及工部局可能采取何种步骤迫使释放由银行仓库在此持有的大量大米库存时，工部局副秘书兼大米专家T. W. Cubb先生宣称，对于本市目前的大米库存无需惊慌，仓库中持续减少的供应证明大米并未被无良投机者囤积。他说，根本问题在于将目前正在种植中心收割的新米运到上海。

Cubb先生说，供应小组委员会将于周一举行进一步会议。可能会讨论将最高价格从每担20美元提高的问题。几周前，工部局和法公董局联合在本地市场实施了这一最高限价，旨在消除投机行为

（批注：4/8 C 12/8）

以及不公平的价格。中国商界认为，两个管理机构将提高最高限价，以努力使 diverted 到非法私人渠道的贸易回归市场。有人指出，实际上，由于中国货币贬值，提高最高限价仅仅是纸面上的增加。

据昨日中文报纸报道，一个米商委员会已起草了几项遏制本地米价上涨的建议。其中一项要求强制执行经销商的大米销售，另一项要求惩罚违反官方规定的经销商。报道称，这些建议将提交给市政当局。

据当地一家通讯社的另一则报道，经销商伪造了本市储存的大米数量登记。据该消息来源称，现有库存总量超过240,000包，而非官方公布的133,094包。

Rice Market

As some of the transporting rice ports
in the interior were closed by the Jap-
anese authorities there, on the occasion
of the second anniversary of Sino-Japanese
Hostilities in Shanghai, the selling price
of white rice was high again for pur-
chases yesterday, as the market received
only a small amount of fresh rice supplies
from the growing center.

On account of lacking of stocks, a large
demand of rice was seen by the retail
shops in the market, while most of the
operators were awaiting further improve-
ment. The price of first-grade white
Changshu rice was quoted at $28 per picul,
or $8 above the maximum price established
by the authorities of Shanghai Municipal
Council. According to market reports
there were only limited stocks, and if
the high rate of rice remained for a day
or two, the price would reach $30 per
picul.

Business in provincial rice was firm in
yesterday's market, although the price of
this rice was irregularly high for pur-
chases, while the retail dealers were greatly
interested in buying. There came no
fresh rice supplies from Nanking and
Wuhu. As a result, the selling price
in the outside mark stood at $23 per
picul, or $6 high compared with the
maximum price.

Owing to shortage of provincial rice,
some of the great local rice dealers and
rice hongs intended to order Saigon rice
from Indo-China. But on account of the
high rate of foreign exchange no agree-
ment was reached between rice dealers
and foreign rice brokers in Shanghai.
According to yesterday's exchange rate,
one bag of Saigon rice would be quoted
at $35 of Chinese national currency.
page_data.zh:
20845

大米市场

由于内地一些大米运输港口被日本当局关闭，正值上海中日敌对行动两周年之际，昨日采购的大白米售价再次高企，因为市场仅从产区收到少量新鲜大米供应。

由于缺乏库存，市场上的零售店面临巨大的大米需求，而大多数经营者则在等待进一步改善。一级常熟白米的报价为每担28美元，比上海公共租界工部局当局制定的最高限价高出8美元。据市场报告称，库存有限，如果米价高位维持一两天，价格将达到每担30美元。

昨日市场上外省大米交易坚挺，尽管采购价格不规则地偏高，而零售经销商购买兴趣浓厚。没有来自南京和芜湖的新鲜大米供应。因此，场外市场的售价为每担23美元，比最高限价高出6美元。

由于外省大米短缺，一些本地大型米商和米行打算从印度支那订购西贡大米。但由于外汇汇率高企，上海的米商与外国大米经纪人之间未能达成协议。根据昨日的汇率，一包西贡大米的报价为35元法币。

CHINA PRESS.

AUG 1 3 1939

Rice Market

The shortage of rice was the serious problem in Shanghai. Although the Executive Committee of the Rice and Bean Guild had held several emergency meetings with the authorities of Shanghai Municipal Council, concerning the new maximum price of white rice no satisfactory result was gained. According to a reliable information, some of the rice ports in the interior had been closed for transportation by the Japanese authorities. There were 3,600 piculs of white rice arrived here by truck and rail.
On account of an investigation by the local authorities, 133,000 bags of white rice were stocked in the various godowns yesterday, except the rice stocks of the retail shops and private persons. If the rice growing centers continued to be blockaded after the second anniversary of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities in Shanghai, rice supplies would be probably short, because the newly-harvested rice would not be in the market before the middle of September.
In yesterday's market, the price of white rice was again irregularly high for selling. First-grade Changshu white rice moved up by $29 per picul, even the low-grade of white rice was noted at $25 against the maximum price of $20 per picul. No brisk demand was recorded in the entire session.
According to a latter report yesterday, the committees of the Shanghai Chinese General Chamber of Commerce and Rice and Bean Guild submitted a petition to the Shanghai Municipal Council and asked settlement of the rice problem for public relief.
Due to lacking of stocks, the price of provincial rice was higher again, but some of the retail shops kept the maximum price for selling at $20 per picul. The most part of that provincial rice was lowest-grade instead of Wuhu rice. The rate of Nanking provincial rice was quoted at $25 per picul in the outside market, and the Wuhu rice was noted at $23. On account of the high rate of foreign exchange, the rate of Saigon Rice stood at $31 per bag of 220 lbs.

Lil.
C 13/8

23319

《字林西报》（China Press）。

1939年8月13日

大米市场

大米短缺是上海的严重问题。尽管米豆业同业公会执行委员会与上海公共租界工部局当局就大白米的新最高限价举行了多次紧急会议，但未取得令人满意的结果。据可靠消息，内地一些大米港口已被日本当局封闭运输。有3,600担白米通过卡车和铁路运抵此地。

由于地方当局进行了调查，昨日除零售店和个人的大米库存外，各仓库储存了133,000包白米。如果在上海中日敌对行动两周年后，大米产区继续被封锁，大米供应可能会短缺，因为新收获的大米在九月中旬之前不会上市。

在昨日的市场上，白米售价再次不规则地高企。一级常熟白米涨至每担29美元，甚至低级白米也录得25美元，而最高限价为每担20美元。整个交易期间未记录到旺盛的需求。

据昨日稍晚的报道，上海总商会和米豆业同业公会的委员会向上海公共租界工部局提交请愿书，要求解决大米问题以救济公众。

由于缺乏库存，外省大米价格再次上涨，但一些零售店保持每担20美元的最高限价出售。大部分外省大米是最低等级的，而非芜湖米。南京外省大米在场外市场的报价为每担25美元，芜湖米为23美元。由于外汇汇率高企，西贡大米的价格为每包（220磅）31美元。

Lil.
C 13/8

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
24047
AUG 2 + 1939

Rice Shortage in Shanghai
Raises Acute Problem

Minor Disturbances Caused in Concession by Mobs ;
Japanese Regret Inability to Import Cereal

TWO minor riots occurred in French Concession rice shops yes-
terday, and nine rice shops in the Chengtu Road district had
to close up because they had completely sold out their stocks as
this city was facing an unprecedented shortage in this most vital
of all food-stuffs. The two minor riots, which occurred on Route
Frelupt and Rue Gaston Kahn, were the result of the impatience
of queues of prospective customers who eventually were pushed
into the shop by those standing behind, with the result that minor
panics ensued and that the police dispersed the 100 odd disgruntled
customers.
Nevertheless, precautions are being taken in both the Settle-
ment and the Concession, with a view to preventing any further
riots. Thus the Settlement police are carefully watching all
developments on the rice market, while constables of the Conces-
sion police who are on their regular beats near rice hongs, have
been instructed to be on the alert so that they may intervene in
the event of any trouble.

Rioting over rice broke out in
two sections of the International
Settlement last night. Police from
Pootoo Road station answered a call
to 1053 Ferry Road at 7.27 p.m. when
it was reported that a large crowd
of people, led by a group of loafers,
were attempting to storm a rice shop
at that address. The police dispersed
the mob and returned to the station,
only to be turned out again at 8.11
p.m. to the same address when it was
learned that the trouble had resumed.
Second Call
Again the police dispersed the mob,
this time arresting six suspects.
Windows in the rice shop were smash-
ed by the crowd, who were stoning
the place when the police arrived
on the scene. It was revealed that
the people wanted to buy rice and
that the shop was closed and the
proprietor refused to open up to do
business. After being held for ques-
tioning, the six arrested men were
released by the police.
At 8.15 last night police on duty
at Yulin Road station received their
report that there was considerable
trouble outside a medicine shop at
502 Ward Road. Riot squads raced
to the scene to find a large crowd
of threatening Chinese gathered out-
side the medicine shop. The rumour
had been circulated in the neighbour-
hood that the Shanghai Rice Shop
at 490 Ward Road had stored 300
piculs of rice in the medicine shop.
The police examined the medicine
shop, found no rice on the premises,
and dispersed the mob. They return-
ed to the station but again the alarm
was raised at 9 p.m. and the riot
squads were ordered back to the same
medicine shop. This time the mob
had apparently got out of hand. The
advertising signs in front of the shop
had been torn down, windows were
broken, and part of the crowd were
in the act of smashing in the door
when the police arrived. This time
the police arrested two of the men
who were trying to break into the
shop and, after showing a representa-
tive group from the crowd that there
was no rice in the shop, they dis-
persed the mob. The two arrested
men will probably be charged this
morning.

Liu
Coy

24047
1939年8月2日

上海大米短缺
引发严峻问题

暴民在租界引起小规模骚乱；
日本人对无法进口谷物表示遗憾

昨日法租界米店发生两起小规模骚乱，成都路地区的九家米店因库存售罄而不得不关门，因为本市正面临这种最重要食品前所未有的短缺。这两起发生在弗雷吕普路（Route Frelupt）和加斯顿·卡恩路（Rue Gaston Kahn）的小规模骚乱，是由于排队 prospective 顾客的不耐烦所致，后面的人最终将前面的人推进店内，导致发生小规模恐慌，警察驱散了100多名不满的顾客。

尽管如此，公共租界和法租界都在采取预防措施，以防止任何进一步的骚乱。因此，公共租界警察正在仔细监视大米市场的所有动态，而在米行附近常规巡逻的法租界巡捕已接到指令保持警惕，以便在发生任何麻烦时进行干预。

昨晚国际公共租界两个区域爆发大米骚乱。普陀路警署的警察于晚上7点27分响应渡江路1053号的呼叫，据报道，一大群人由一群游手好闲者带领，试图冲击该地址的一家米店。警察驱散了暴民并返回警署，但在晚上8点11分又因得知骚乱恢复而被再次派往同一地址。
第二次出警
警察再次驱散暴民，这次逮捕了六名嫌疑人。当警察到达现场时，人群正在向该处投掷石块，米店的窗户被砸碎。据悉，人们想买米，但店铺已关门，店主拒绝开门营业。经过拘留讯问后，这六名被捕男子被警察释放。

昨晚8点15分，榆林路警署的值班警察接到报告，称华德路502号一家药店外发生严重骚乱。防暴队迅速赶往现场，发现一大群具有威胁性的中国人聚集在药店外。附近有谣言流传，称位于华德路490号的上海米店将300担大米储存在该药店内。警察检查了药店，在现场未发现大米，并驱散了暴民。他们返回警署，但在晚上9点警报再次响起，防暴队被命令返回同一家药店。这次暴民显然已失控。店前的广告牌被撕下，窗户被打破，当警察到达时，部分人群正在砸门。这次警察逮捕了两名试图闯入店内的男子，并向人群中的代表展示店内没有大米后，驱散了暴民。这两名被捕男子可能将于今晨被起诉。

Week's Stocks Here
Opinions voiced by rice experts yesterday indicated that a most grave situation might develop in Shanghai within a week, since the rice situation here is now completely beyond the control of the Settlement authorities. They pictured a most gloomy future for the rice situation, attaching little importance to the present negotiations between the Settlement and Japanese authorities which, it was stated, would be of no use at the present time. The price of the "nominal" first grade rice is $40 per picul, but it was predicted that it would jump to $45 if no abundant supply is forthcoming. The price is more than double the one quoted a few months ago.
Despite the Japanese denial, it was stated that much rice arriving in Hongkew from the interior had been bought in the Japanese-controlled parts of the Settlement. Some supply had been forthcoming to other parts of foreign settlement, but it had been too scanty to meet the demand of more than 10,000 piculs needed daily. One expert complained that there is no real expert on the special committee created by the Shanghai Municipal Council to deal with the question, and that expert suggestions had not been carried out by the authorities.

Foreign Purchases Now Too Late
The suggestion of buying foreign rice was made long ago to the authorities but it was not accepted, it was stated. The merchants with big capital did not want the authorities to pay, but they merely wanted them to guarantee against possible losses. It was too late to do anything now to offer an immediate remedy to the situation and in the next few days anything might happen, as the poor may become desperate. Large-scale rioting would have broken out long ago had it not been for the extra precautionary measures carried out by the authorities, not against the serious rice situation but because of political tension, it was asserted.
It was suggested that it would be better for merchants to carry out negotiations with the Japanese direct in order to have more supply, as the Japanese would likely make it a political issue when approached by Settlement authorities. Even experts were mystified as to the ever increasing price of the rice, stating that a picul of rice in Wuhu was worth only $12. When it reached Hongkew the price would be quoted at $35. It was also pointed out that it would be a great disadvantage to allow the information about the abnormal rice situation here to leak out to the people, especially guerrilla bands in the interior. More tax collected in the interior on the rice would further aggravate the situation.

Japanese "Regrets"
The "so-called shortage of rice" in Shanghai was greatly regretted by the Japanese authorities, stated Col. Mabuchi, head of the Japanese army press bureau, when speaking at the Japanese press conference yesterday evening. He wondered, however, whether the term "shortage" was wholly correct.
To him the situation seemed to be not so much an actual shortage of rice supplies as the fact that speculators, and even the Municipal Council, had stored away huge quantities of rice. Since extremely high prices were now being charged for rice it was creating great hardship among local Chinese.

本周本地库存

昨日大米专家发表的意见表明，鉴于本地大米局势目前已完全超出公共租界当局的控制，上海在一周内可能会出现极其严重的局面。他们描绘了大米局势极其黯淡的未来，认为公共租界与日本当局目前的谈判无足轻重，并称这些谈判在目前毫无用处。“名义上”的一级大米价格为每担40美元，但据预测，如果没有充足的供应，价格将跳涨至45美元。该价格是几个月前报价的两倍多。

尽管日本人予以否认，但据称从内地抵达虹口的许多大米是在公共租界的日本控制区购买的。其他外国租界区域也有少量供应，但太少，无法满足每日超过10,000担的需求。一位专家抱怨说，上海公共租界工部局为处理此问题而设立的特别委员会中没有真正的专家，且专家的建议未被当局采纳。

现在购买外国大米为时已晚

据称，很久以前就曾向当局提出购买外国大米的建议，但未被接受。拥有大量资本的商人不想让当局付款，而只是希望当局担保可能的损失。现在做任何事情来提供 immediate remedy 为时已晚，在接下来的几天里，任何事情都可能发生，因为穷人可能会变得绝望。据称，如果不是当局采取了额外的预防措施，大规模骚乱早就爆发了，但这些措施并非针对严重的大米局势，而是出于政治紧张局势。

有人建议，商人最好直接与日本人进行谈判以获得更多供应，因为如果由公共租界当局出面，日本人可能会将其作为一个政治问题。甚至连专家也对大米价格不断上涨感到困惑，指出芜湖的一担大米仅值12美元。当它到达虹口时，报价将为35美元。还有人指出，让关于本地异常大米局势的信息泄露给民众，特别是内地的游击队，将是一个巨大的不利因素。内地对大米征收更多的税将进一步加剧局势。

日本人的“遗憾”

日本陆军新闻局局长马渊大佐（Col. Mabuchi）在昨晚的日本记者招待会上发言时表示，日本当局对上海“所谓的大米短缺”深感遗憾。然而，他怀疑“短缺”一词是否完全正确。
对他来说，这种情况似乎不完全是大米供应的实际短缺，而是投机者，甚至公共租界工部局，囤积了大量大米的事实。由于目前大米收取极高的价格，这给当地中国人造成了巨大的困难。

He thought that the problem should
be solved by efforts on the part of
the Shanghai Municipal Council and
merchants, who had resorted to
questionable practices for their own
profit. Should the Settlement au-
thorities be unable to solve the prob-
lem and should there occur a gen-
eral outbreak of rice riots as a re-
sult, then the Japanese authorities,
since they were responsible for the
maintenance of peace and order in
Shanghai, would feel bound to take
proper measures for a solution of the
rice problem.
Even if riots did not occur, since
rice was the staple diet of the Chinese
people, the Japanese authorities would
undertake a solution from the stand-
point of humanitarian principles. If
the Settlement authorities failed then
it would be time for the Japanese to
step-in.
Settlement Blamed
One way to alleviate the situation
was to allow rice to enter the Settle-
ment quite freely and that could also
be said of other goods, but in view of
the numerous barriers in the form
of differences between the Settlement
authorities and the Japanese military
authorities, the latter felt that the
first steps towards an improvement
in the situation would be an improve-
ment of the atmosphere inside the
Settlement.
If the situation became acute then
something, of course, would have to
be done to relieve the situation. He
added that even the Japanese army
were having difficulties in obtaining
a supply of the commodity in the
occupied areas. While the conditions
were fairly good last year, the crop
had been considerably below normal
this year owing to wartime condi-
tions.
He concluded by saying that plenty
of rice had been planted in these

他认为，这一问题应由上海公共租界工部局和那些为谋取私利而采取可疑手段的商人努力解决。如果租界当局无法解决这一问题，并因此导致大规模的米骚乱爆发，那么日本当局由于负责维持上海的和平与秩序，将感到有义务采取适当措施来解决大米问题。

即使没有发生骚乱，鉴于大米是中国人的主食，日本当局也会从人道主义原则出发着手解决。如果租界当局失败，那就是日本人介入的时候了。

归咎于租界

缓解局势的一种方法是允许大米相当自由地进入租界，其他商品也是如此，但鉴于租界当局与日本军方当局之间存在诸多障碍形式的分歧，后者认为，改善局势的第一步将是改善租界内部的气氛。

如果局势变得严峻，那么当然必须采取措施来缓解局势。他补充说，就连日军在占领区也难以获得该商品的供应。虽然去年的情况相当好，但由于战时条件，今年的收成远低于正常水平。

他最后说，这些地区种植了大量水稻，并已完全成熟。然而，由于到了收割时节却无人从事这项工作，因此无法收获庄稼。

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 2, 1935
Seven Shops
Stormed By
Angry Mobs
During Day
Widespread Rumors Of
Profiteering Cause
Fresh Trouble
WAYSIDE POLICE
ARREST RIOTERS
Reports Of Excessive
Hoarding Denied
By Officials
Rice riots to a high degree
of seriousness swept through
Shanghai's International Set-
tlement last night as rumors
that huge stocks of the cereal
have been stored in the city
by profiteering merchants
continued to spread.
The riots extended from the
District in the eastern area of
the Settlement to Ferry Road
in the western district. Five
shops are reported to have been
stoned and looted by as many
different mobs ranging in size
from 75 to 200 persons. Two
riots occurred in French Con-
cession.
The continued increase in the
price of rice is credited with having
been partially responsible for the
activities of the hunger rioters.
Costs of the grain rose yesterday
afternoon from $40 to $45 per picul.
Ferry Road Riots
Two riots were carried out against
the same rice shop at 1053 Ferry
Road within the short space of one
hour. About 150 rioters stormed the
establishment at 7.30 p.m. and after
stealing small quantities of the
grain, they decamped with the
police not far behind. Another mob
attacked the shop at 8.10 p.m. and
were dispersed by the police.
The next riot reported to the
police occurred at a rice shop on
Yates Road. The place was in the
process of being looted when the
police arrived. The rioters scatter-
ed and did not return.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）.
1935年8月2日
七家店铺
白天遭愤怒暴民冲击
关于囤积居奇的广泛谣言
引发新麻烦
巡捕逮捕骚乱者
官员否认过度囤积的报道

昨晚，随着投机商人将大量谷物储存在城内的谣言继续传播，严重的米骚乱席卷了上海公共租界。

骚乱从租界东部区域延伸至西区渡船路（Ferry Road）。据报道，有五家店铺遭到多达五伙不同暴民的投石袭击和抢劫，每伙人数在75至200人之间。法租界发生了两起骚乱。

大米价格的持续上涨被认为是导致饥饿暴民活动部分原因。昨日午后，每担粮食的价格从40美元涨至45美元。

渡船路骚乱

在一小时内，同一家位于渡船路1053号的大米店遭遇了两次骚乱。晚上7点30分，约150名暴民冲击了该店，在偷走少量谷物后逃窜，警察紧随其后。另一伙暴民于晚上8点10分袭击了该店，并被警察驱散。

向警方报告的下一场骚乱发生在耶茨路（Yates Road）的一家米店。警察到达时，该店正在遭受抢劫。暴民四散而去，未再返回。

Shortly after 9.25 p.m., about 200
Chinese of the poorer classes storm-
ed the Sing Zang Rice Shop at 900
Chengtu Road and were dispersed
by the police. At about the same
time, rioters attacked a medicine
shop at 502 Ward Road. They had
been told that the proprietor of

rice and they intended to seize it.
Wayside police arrived on the scene
and arrested three of the rioters.
Arrests were made in other sec-
tions of the city and it is estimated

Two shops in the French Con-

Furniture Smashed
In the first outbreak, which
occurred in the vicinity of Route

about 7.30 a.m. a mob of 30 to 40
poorer class Chinese ransacked the Da

was broken up by the police and
one of the rioters was arrested.
A few minutes later, another mob
assaulted the Hung Dah rice shop

These rioters also managed to steal

晚上9点25分过后不久，约200名贫困阶层华人冲击了成都路900号的兴昌米店（Sing Zang Rice Shop），并被警察驱散。大约在同一时间，暴民袭击了华德路502号的一家药店。他们被告知店主囤积了300担大米，并意图将其 seizing。巡捕赶到现场，逮捕了三名暴民。

市内其他地区也实施了逮捕，据估计，昨晚约有12名米骚乱者在狱中。由于骚乱，警察预备队整夜大部分时间都处于执勤状态。

法租界的两家店铺在上午遭到袭击，在警察赶到现场驱散暴民之前，两处均遭受了一些损失。

家具被砸毁

第一次爆发发生在上午7点30分左右，地点在阿尔伯特国王大道（Avenue du Roi Albert）附近的弗雷吕普路（Route Frelupt）附近，一伙30至40名的贫困阶层华人洗劫了大兴米店（Da Hsing Rice Shop），砸毁了一些家具，并拿走了少量大米。此事被警察制止，一名暴民被捕。

几分钟后，另一伙暴民袭击了距离第一次事件现场仅几门之隔的鸿达米店（Hung Dah rice shop）。在警察到达现场之前，这些暴民也设法偷走了少量大米。

随后，法租界和公共租界的当局均否认了投机商囤积100万袋大米的谣言。工部局的一名官员宣称，最近的调查显示，目前市内的大米存量不超过7万袋。

谈判进展顺利

同一位发言人补充说，与日本方面就允许更多大米进入外国管理区域的谈判正在进行中。他补充说，这些会谈进展顺利，预计很快会有结果。

昨日还有报道称，由上海著名商人、航运业人士及工部局董事虞洽卿先生购买的一批来自西贡的1,800吨大米，预计将在未来几天内抵达上海。昨晚称，这批大米的大部分将移交给当地的中国战争难民

SHANGHAI TIMES.

AUG 2 1939

MOBS ATTACK RICE
SHOPS IN CITY

Little Damage Done But
Several Arrests Made;
Shortage Responsible

Reflecting the urgency of the current rice shortage in Shanghai a number of small riots occurred in the Settlement and French Concession yesterday, little damage being done but a number of agitators being arrested by the police.

The first took place at about 7 o'clock in the morning in the French Concession and involved the Dah Hsiang Rice Shop at 320 Route Frelupt, and the Hung Dah Rice Shop, at the corner of Route Frelupt and Avenue Du Roi Albert. Small quantities of rice were stolen by rioters, one of whom was taken into custody by French Municipal Police.

At 7.30 in the evening another rice shop, at 1053 Ferry Road, was attacked by a Chinese mob, the attempt to raid the premises being repeated again at 8.11 p.m. Six of the ringleaders were arrested by the police.

A few minutes afterwards a Chinese pharmacy at 502 Ward Road was the scene of another riot, the mob's intention being to break into the Shanghai Rice Shop next door, which was reported to be stocked with 300 piculs of rice. Police quickly arrived on the scene and dispersed the crowd, but when the attack was repeated at 9 p.m. three Chinese were arrested and taken to the station for questioning.

《上海泰晤士报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）.

1939年8月2日

暴民袭击市内
米店

损失轻微但数人被捕；短缺是罪魁祸首

反映了上海当前大米短缺的紧迫性，昨天租界和法租界发生了一些小规模骚乱，损失不大，但警方逮捕了一些煽动者。

第一起发生在早上7点左右，地点在法租界，涉及弗雷吕普路320号的大祥米店（Dah Hsiang Rice Shop）以及弗雷吕普路与阿尔伯特国王大道交汇处的鸿达米店（Hung Dah Rice Shop）。暴民偷走了少量大米，其中一人被法公董局巡捕拘捕。

晚上7点30分，另一家位于渡船路1053号的米店遭到中国暴民袭击， raid 该场所的企图在晚上8点11分再次重演。六名头目被警方逮捕。

几分钟后，华德路502号的一家中国药房成为另一起骚乱的现场，暴民的意图是闯入隔壁据说存有300担大米的上海米店。警察迅速赶到现场驱散人群，但当晚上9点袭击再次发生时，三名中国人被捕并被带到警局接受讯问。

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 24 1939

Local Rice
Famine Hit
By Japanese
Army Spokesman
Sees Possibility Of
Intervention

If the Settlement authorities fail to find a solution to the local rice problem it will be "time for the Japanese to take over," declared Colonel Mabuchi, chief of the Japanese Army Press Bureau in Central China, yesterday.

The Japanese authorities "would feel bound to take appropriate measures for a solution of the rice question, should officials of the International Settlement be unable, or refuse, to do so, thus resulting in an outbreak of riots that might disturb the peace and order in Shanghai and the immediate vicinity, for whose maintenance the Japanese are responsible," declared the spokesman in the course of the Japanese press conference yesterday.

The "so-called rice shortage," Colonel Mabuchi declared, was greatly regretted by the Japanese authorities, but he wondered if the term "shortage" was wholly accurate.

Speculators Blamed

It was not so much a shortage, he stated, as it was a fact that speculators, "and even the Shanghai Municipal Council authorities, have stored away huge quantities of rice. Since the extremely high price was creating suffering," he said, he thought that the "Shanghai Municipal Council authorities and the merchants, who resorted to this questionable practice for their own profit, should solve the question."

Colonel Mabuchi declared that, in his opinion, "even if the difficulty does not go to the extent of riots, since rice is the staple food of the Chinese, the Japanese authorities should undertake a solution if only from a humanitarian standpoint."

In reply to a question, he added that any such measures taken by the Japanese would apply to the International Settlement and "also to the French Concession."

Free Shipments Asked

It was then suggested by a foreign correspondent that one contributory feature towards relieving the current shortage, might be for the Japanese to allow rice to enter Shanghai freely, without heavy taxes, from the Japanese-occupied areas.

Colonel Mabuchi, in reply, admitted that "this is, of course, one possible way of alleviating the shortage of rice and, it may be said, of other goods also." However, he continued, "in view of the numerous barriers which constitute difficulties in the relations between the Settlement and areas outside, the Japanese military authorities feel that the first step towards relieving the situation will be an improvement of the atmosphere within the Settlement."

1939年8月24日

当地米荒
受日军影响
发言人看到
干预的可能性

华中日军报道部部长马渊上校（Colonel Mabuchi）昨日宣称，如果租界当局未能找到解决当地大米问题的办法，那就“轮到日本人接手了”。

该发言人在昨日的日本记者招待会上宣称，“如果公共租界官员无法或拒绝这样做，从而导致可能扰乱上海及其附近地区和平与秩序的骚乱爆发，而维持这些地区的和平与秩序是日本人的责任，那么日本当局将感到有义务采取适当措施来解决大米问题。”

马渊上校宣称，日本当局对“所谓的大米短缺”深感遗憾，但他怀疑“短缺”一词是否完全准确。

归咎于投机商

他表示，这与其说是短缺，不如说是这样一个事实：投机商，“甚至上海公共租界工部局当局，都储存了大量大米。既然极高的价格造成了痛苦，”他说，他认为“上海公共租界工部局当局和那些为谋取私利而采取这种可疑做法的商人应该解决这个问题。”

马渊上校宣称，在他看来，“即使困难没有发展到骚乱的程度，由于大米是中国人的主食，日本当局也应仅从人道主义立场出发着手解决。”

在回答一个问题时，他补充说，日本采取的任何此类措施将适用于公共租界，“也适用于法租界”。

要求自由运输

随后，一名外国记者建议，缓解当前短缺的一个促成因素可能是日本允许大米从日占区免税或轻税自由进入上海。

马渊上校在回答中承认，“这当然是缓解大米短缺以及其他商品短缺的一种可能方式。”然而，他继续说道，“鉴于构成租界与外部地区关系困难的诸多障碍，日本军方当局认为，缓解局势的第一步将是改善租界内部的气氛。”

page_data.en:
Asked whether shipments of
rice from Wuhu and other
places, where there were large
stocks, would be permitted to
enter Shanghai by the Japanese
if there were several millions of
Chinese in actual want, the
Colonel replied:
Transportation Difficulty
"If the situation comes to that,
something would have to be
done to meet it. It is not gen-
erally realized, however, how
difficult it is to effect a move-
ment of supplies from one place
to another, and even the Japan-
ese army suffers from this diffi-
culty."
Nevertheless, he admitted that this
and "similar questions" were now
under consideration by the Japan-
ese authorities.
Colonel Mabuchi stated the rice
crop had been fairly good last year
although he had no statistics to
hand. He believed, however, that
the total amount of rice had been
considerably lower than usual be-
cause of the war. Of the whole
amount he was unable to say "how
much has been used by the army
and how much has been stored by
the Chinese."
He asserted that the rice planted
in battle areas, and even in places
where guerillas operated had reach-
ed full maturity, but in the end had
come to naught because there had
been no one there to harvest the
crops, owing to the evacuation of
the farmers.
Army Trucks Seek Rice
Shanghai's rice situation remained
acute yesterday. Police were inves-
tigating reports of an illegal 100,000
bag hoard and at the same time it
was learned that Japanese army
trucks have been scouring the sur-
rounding countryside within a 200
mile radius of the city for rice.
Conditions inside the foreign
settlement were slightly ameliorat-
ed with the drop of $.50 in the
price of first grade cereal to $38.50
per picul. Poor grade rice went $6
lower to $30 per picul. But nine
rice shops on Chengtu Road closed
for lack of supplies. No riots were
reported in consequence and police
details have not been strengthened
on this account.
According to the market report
more than 10,000 bags arrived yes-
terday from Wuhu despite the con-
tinued embargo maintained by the
Japanese. A further report stated
that a large consignment of rice
being shipped here aboard a Japan-
ese steamer from upriver had been
detained by the Japanese authori-
ties in the Whangpoo.
Good Crop Reported
Because of the unusually good
harvest forecast from Wusih,
Changshu, Nanking and Wuhu the
local market assumed an optimism
which has been foreign to it for
weeks past. Several local dealers
have reported their intention of
going directly to the rice centers
to make their purchases if they
encounter no difficulties it is ex-
pected the cost of rice here will
start an early decline.
While Saigon rice remained at
$45 a bag and the local market
showed a slight turn for the better
it was learned that rice in Hong-
kew was selling at only $25 per
picul.
The price of flour jumped on the
market when 40,000 bags were sold
at $6.40 a piece which was $.20
higher than Tuesday's closing price.
The Noodle Shops Guild was report-
ed to have sent a letter to the City
Chamber of Commerce urging that
the authorities place restrictions on
further advance of flour prices for
the benefit of the public. In ordin-
ary times flour sells at an average
of $4.80 a bag.

当被问及如果数百万中国人确实陷入困境，日军是否会允许来自芜湖及其他拥有大量库存地区的大米运入上海时，这位上校回答说：

运输困难
“如果局势发展到那一步，就必须采取某些措施来应对。然而，人们普遍没有意识到，将物资从一个地方转移到另一个地方是多么困难，甚至日本军队也受困于这一难题。”

尽管如此，他承认日本当局目前正在考虑这个问题以及“类似的问题”。

马渊（Mabuchi）上校表示，去年的稻收成相当不错，尽管他手头没有统计数据。但他相信，由于战争的影响，大米总量比平时低得多。关于总量中有多少被军队使用，有多少被中国人储存，他表示无法说明。

他断言，在战区甚至游击队活动地区种植的水稻虽然已完全成熟，但最终却颗粒无收，因为农民撤离后无人收割庄稼。

军车搜寻大米
昨天上海的米荒依然严峻。警方正在调查有关非法囤积10万袋大米的报告，与此同时获悉，日本军用卡车一直在城市周围200英里半径范围内的乡村四处搜寻大米。

随着一级谷物价格每担下跌0.50美元至38.50美元，租界内的状况略有改善。劣质大米价格下跌6美元，至每担30美元。但是，成都路上的九家米店因缺乏供应而关门。据报未因此发生骚乱，警方也未因此增派警力。

根据市场报告，尽管日本维持着禁运令，昨天仍有超过1万袋大米从芜湖抵达。另有报告称，一批由日本轮船从上游运抵此处的大米被日本当局扣押在黄浦江。

据报道丰收
由于无锡、常熟、南京和芜湖预报收成异常良好，本地市场呈现出数周未见的乐观情绪。几位本地商人报告说，如果没有遇到阻碍，他们打算直接前往大米产地采购，预计这里的大米价格将开始早期回落。

虽然西贡大米价格仍保持在每袋45美元，且本地市场略有好转，但据悉虹口的大米售价仅为每担25美元。

面粉价格在市场上跳涨，4万袋面粉以每袋6.40美元的价格售出，比周二收盘价高出0.20美元。据悉，面馆公会已向市商会致函，敦促当局为公众利益限制面粉价格进一步上涨。在平时，面粉的平均售价为每袋4.80美元。

24057
AUG 24, 1939

Rice Situation In Shanghai
Shows Some Improvement

Confidence In Council's Ability To Provide Relief
Causes Reduction Of Prices; S.M.C. Partly
Blamed For Shortage By Japanese

The local rice market, following a wave of upward trend during the past few days, slightly eased off yesterday on reports of the near-arrival of a big shipment of Saigon rice and on slightly increased shipments of rice from inland areas.

Reacting to generally improved conditions and confidence in efforts of the foreign municipal authorities to devise relief measures, a marginal downward trend was precipitated during the day. As against the new high level of $42 two days ago, first grade cereals returned to the maximum level of $39 per picul yesterday, while medium and lower grade cereals were respectively quoted at between $36 and $37.50 and between $35.20 and $36.

Shipments during the day totaled about four junkloads and more than 4,000 bags by rail and steamer. The market generally ruled firm during the day, but trading was quiet during the morning, both buyers and sellers failing to come to terms. The afternoon's unofficial open market transactions slightly improved, and more than 8,000 bags of rice of various grades were reported to have changed hands.

Chinese Bodies Confer

Meanwhile, various local Chinese public bodies, at the initiation of Mr. Yu Ya-ching, local shipping magnate, were reported to be have exchanged views yesterday for the purpose of purchasing large quantities of Saigon cereals for relief purposes. Intending purchasers among local Chinese business firms, factories and shops were requested to register.

A joint attempt is being made by these public bodies to raise the necessary funds among local Chinese banks, some of which are said to have agreed in principle to advance the required amount of the loan. No definite action, however, will be taken pending unanimous agreement being reached on the best procedure to be adopted for importing foreign rice.

A shipment of 18,000 bags of Saigon rice ordered by Mr. Yu and other industrialists is expected to arrive in Shanghai on September 2, but in view of the largest population in this city, such a small quantity is regarding as unavailable in solving the local acute shortage of rice.

The total available stock of rice in Shanghai up till yesterday was reported to be less than 100,000 bags, just about sufficient to meet local normal consumption for 10 days, barring, of course, the possibility of increased supplies forthcoming. However, it was confidently stated in local rice merchants' circles yesterday that the worst stage in the "rice crisis" had past and that before long large shipments of cereals from the inland areas might be expected following the mid-summer harvest.

Council Blamed

Colonel Mabuchi of the Japanese Army in answering questions on the rice problem in Shanghai at the press conference yesterday stated that the so-called shortage of rice was, of course, greatly regretted by the Japanese, but he wondered if there was really a serious shortage; he believed that the shortage was due to the hoarding of speculators and "even to the Shanghai Municipal Council, who have also stored large quantities of rice, thus creating hardships all around."

The Colonel added that he considered the problem should be solved by the Settlement authorities, and if they should be unable or should refuse to solve the question, thereby causing a general outbreak of riots which might disturb the peace and order of Shanghai and its immediate vicinity, the Japanese would feel bound to take appropriate measures to find a solution, because they were responsible for the peace of Shanghai. He added afterwards that even if riots did not occur, the Japanese should undertake to provide a solution from the viewpoint of humanity, since rice is the staple food of the Chinese.

The Colonel thought that the solution ought to be found by the S.M.C., but if they failed, the Japanese would consider it their duty to try to solve the question. Asked if the Japanese would allow shipments of rice to Shanghai from Wuhu and other places if the situation became acute, Colonel Mabuchi replied that something, of course, would have to be done, but the movement of rice was very difficult, and even the Japanese army had difficulty in supplying its own needs, because of transportation difficulties and also because a great deal of rice was allowed to go waste because there was no one to harvest it.

Asked if he had any statistics on the amount of rice consumed by the Japanese forces in China, the Colonel replied that he had not.

24057
1939年8月24日

上海米荒情况
显示有所改善

对工部局救济能力的信心
导致价格下降；日本人将短缺部分归咎于工部局

本地大米市场在经历了过去几天的上涨浪潮后，昨天因有大批西贡大米即将抵达以及内地大米运量略有增加的消息而略有缓和。

由于总体状况改善以及对外国市政当局制定救济措施的努力充满信心，当天引发了轻微的下跌趋势。与前两天创下的42美元新高相比，昨天一级谷物回落至每担39美元的最高水平，而中等和低等谷物的报价分别在36至37.50美元之间和35.20至36美元之间。

当天的运输总量约为四船驳运量，以及通过铁路和轮船运输的4000多袋。市场全天总体坚挺，但上午交易清淡，买卖双方未能达成交易。下午的非官方公开市场交易略有改善，据报道有超过8000袋各种等级的大米易手。

华人团体磋商

与此同时，据报道，在当地航运巨头虞洽卿先生的发起下，各本地华人公共团体昨天交换了意见，目的是购买大量西贡谷物用于救济。有意购买的本地华商、工厂和商店被要求登记。

这些公共团体正联合尝试向本地华商银行筹集必要资金，据说其中一些银行已原则上同意提供所需贷款金额。然而，在就进口外国大米的最佳程序达成一致之前，不会采取任何具体行动。

由虞先生和其他实业家订购的18,000袋西贡大米预计将于9月2日抵达上海，但鉴于本市人口众多，如此少量的大米被认为无助于解决本地严重的大米短缺问题。

据报道，截至昨天，上海可用的大米总库存不到10万袋，仅够满足本地正常消费10天左右，当然不包括可能增加的供应量。然而，昨天本地米商圈子自信地表示，“米荒”最严重的阶段已经过去，随着仲夏收获的到来，不久有望看到来自内地的大量谷物运抵。

指责工部局

日本陆军马渊（Mabuchi）上校在昨天的记者招待会上回答关于上海大米问题时表示，日本人当然对所谓的大米短缺深感遗憾，但他怀疑是否真的存在严重短缺；他认为短缺是由于投机者的囤积以及“甚至是因为上海公共租界工部局，他们也储存了大量大米，从而造成了普遍的困难。”

上校补充说，他认为这个问题应由租界当局解决，如果他们无法或拒绝解决这个问题，从而导致可能扰乱上海及其附近地区和平与秩序的大规模骚乱爆发，日本人将感到有必要采取适当措施寻求解决方案，因为他们对上海的和平负有责任。他随后补充说，即使没有发生骚乱，从人道主义观点出发，日本人也应承担提供解决方案的责任，因为大米是中国人的主食。

马渊上校认为解决方案应由工部局（S.M.C.）寻找，但如果他们失败，日本人将认为试图解决此问题是他们的责任。当被问及如果局势变得严峻，日本人是否允许从芜湖和其他地方向上海运送大米时，马渊上校回答说，当然必须采取一些措施，但大米的运输非常困难，甚至日本军队也难以满足自身需求，这是因为运输困难，同时也因为大量大米因无人收割而被浪费。

当被问及他是否有关于日军在中国消耗的大米数量的统计数据时，上校回答说他没有任何数据。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
AUG 24 1939
24051
Rice Shortage:
Another Suggestion
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Shortly following the outbreak
of the hostilities in the autumn of
1937, the price of rice in the Shang-
hai mart skyrocketed, causing much
suffering among the Chinese populace.
To alleviate their suffering the
S. M. C. took matter in hand and
bought some rice from abroad for
distribution here at a reasonable
price, thereby putting an end to the
rice shortage.
It is therefore not strange that some
of the Chinese residents expect the
S. M. C. to again come forth to
their assistance and some are under
the impression that there is a supply
of rice on hand available for allot-
ment to those applying. In order to
save unnecessary correspondence on
the part of both the S. M. C. and the
general public may I suggest that
you ascertain the facts and inform
the public at an early date whether
any allotment is to be applied for.
I have read in your esteemed
journal and in your contemporaries
that everything possible is being done
by the S. M. C. to cut down price
of rice, but I am inclined to think
that in view of depreciation of local
currency in terms of foreign monies,
it is now impossible for the S. M. C.
to bring foreign rice to Shanghai at
competitive prices. As an alternative,
I wonder if it is not possible for the
S. M. C. to apply to the United States
or some other country to contribute
such part of their bumper crop as
they could spare to relieve Shang-
hai because the prosperity of
the Settlement and Concession is
dependent upon the ability of
myriads of workers in its mills
and shops to subsist therein.
If these cannot maintain themselves,
they and their dependents must either
migrate from the Settlement and Con-
cession or become destitute, and the
disintegration of Shanghai will have
begun, and once the deteriorating
process has started, its progress will
be steady and rapid.
At least a part of the shortage is
brought about artificially, the avail-
able supply of rice being absorbed by
buying for future requirements by
some of the residents, many of whom
are stocked up for several weeks or
even months ahead. It is no wonder
that the price shot up to $40 per
picul and beyond in a brief period.
The greater the increase in price, the
more frantic the public become to
buy. But the shortage is neverthe-
less real and acute among the ma-
jority of the people who lead a hand-
to-mouth existence and do not have
the wherewithal to buy ahead. I am
sure an assurance from abroad that
in case of need, some adequate food
supply, flour, corn or any other thing
will be made available to Shanghai
residents at a reasonable price will
do much to relieve anxiety and pres-
sure on the little supply of rice that
is now available. Perhaps such an
assurance is all that is required and
its fulfilment may not be necessary.
Will it be sought and given?
KAO KWOK.
Shanghai, Aug. 23.

《字林西报》，
1939年8月24日
24051
米荒：
另一项建议
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——1937年秋战事爆发后不久，上海市场的大米价格飞涨，给中国民众造成极大痛苦。为了减轻他们的痛苦，上海公共租界工部局（S. M. C.）介入此事，并从国外购买了一些大米，以合理价格在此分销，从而结束了米荒。

因此，一些中国居民期望工部局再次伸出援手并不奇怪，有些人甚至认为手头有大米供应可供申请分配者使用。为了避免工部局和公众之间不必要的通信往来，我建议贵报查明事实，并尽早告知公众是否可以申请分配。

我在贵报及同行报刊上读到，工部局正在尽一切努力降低大米价格，但我倾向于认为，鉴于本地货币对外币贬值，工部局现在已不可能以具有竞争力的价格将外国大米运到上海。作为一种替代方案，我想知道工部局是否可以向美国或其他国家申请，将其丰产收成中可节省的部分捐赠出来以救济上海，因为租界和法租界的繁荣取决于其工厂和商店中无数工人的生存能力。

如果这些人无法维持生计，他们及其家属要么迁出租界和法租界，要么陷入贫困，上海的解体就将开始，一旦恶化过程开始，其进展将是稳定而迅速的。

至少部分短缺是人为造成的，现有大米供应被一些居民为未来需求而购买所吸收，其中许多人储备了几周甚至几个月的用量。难怪价格在短时间内飙升至每担40美元以上。价格涨幅越大，公众抢购就越疯狂。但对于大多数靠微薄收入度日、无力提前购买的人来说，短缺仍然是真实且严峻的。我相信，如果国外能保证在需要时以合理价格向上海居民提供充足的食物供应，如面粉、玉米或其他物品，将大大缓解焦虑，并减轻目前有限大米供应的压力。也许这样的保证就是所需要的全部，而其实际履行可能并非必要。

这种保证会被寻求并给予吗？

高国（KAO KWOK，音译）
上海，8月23日。

CHINA PRESS
AUG 24 1939

Rice Market

After the brisk upward trend of the
selling rate of white rice for the past
few weeks, the official rate of white rice
was low in the market yesterday. The
market has received a considerable amount
of fresh rice supplies from the growing
centers. According to a reliable infor-
mation from the local authorities, a large
shipment of 10,000 bags of Wuhu rice
was brought here, and another 2,000 bags
of Soongkiang newly-harvested rice with
1,000 bags of Kaishing rice were delivered
to port for selling.
The opening price of white rice in the
session was quoted at $40 per bag of
best quality of white rice. The operators
and retail shops however were not inter-
ested in buying at the high rate, since
a big amount of rice available for selling
was supplied. As a result the rate fell
in the later session. Only slight business
was done throughout the entire session.
The selling rate dropped from $0.50 to
$1 for different kinds of white rice.
First-grade white rice stood at $38.50 and
low-grade of this rice sold at $30 per
picul.
The selling price of provincial rice was
very firm in the market yesterday, as the
market supplied a big amount of this rice
for purchases. The authorities of Shang-
hai Municipal Council had conferred with
the Japanese authorities concerning the
transportation of Wuhu provincial rice to
Shanghai. Owing to the above fact, the
retail and local dealers were not inter-
ested to buy for their stocks, awaiting a
further price improvement. The sales
in the day amounted to 2,000 bags of pro-
vincial rice. One hundred bags of Saigon
rice were liquidated and the price was
quoted at $45 per bag of 220 lbs.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）
1939年8月24日

米市

在过去几周白米售价 briskly 上涨之后，昨日市场上白米的官方牌价偏低。市场从产区接收了大量新鲜大米供应。据地方当局提供的可靠消息，一批10,000袋芜湖大米运抵此处，另有2,000袋松江新米和1,000袋嘉兴大米已运至港口待售。

开盘时，最上等白米的报价为每袋40元。然而，由于可供销售的大米数量充足，经营者和零售店对以高价买入并不感兴趣。因此，后市价格下跌。全交易日成交寥寥。各类白米的售价下跌了0.50元至1元不等。一级白米价格为38.50元，低级白米售价为每担30元。

昨日外省米的市场售价非常坚挺，因为市场提供了大量此类大米供购买。上海公共租界工部局当局已与日本当局就芜湖外省米运往上海事宜进行了磋商。鉴于上述情况，零售商和本地商人对进货储备不感兴趣，等待价格进一步改善。当日外省米成交量达2,000袋。100袋西贡米被抛售，报价为每袋（220磅）45元。

CHINA PRESS.

AUG 2 4 1938

Flour And Wheat

After the shortage of white rice in
the International Settlement and the
French Concession, the native flour has
become the important daily food for local
Chinese. The Chinese Flour Mills offered
unlimited flour supplies for purchases in
the market instead of rice. Local dealers
and rice retail shops were active in the
session, and bought a large amount of
the second-grade product at $6.40 per
bag, or $0.20 above the last final closing
rate.
With reference to the market report,
every local dealer and retail shop asked
for further flour supplies. The mills issued
a regulation on account of which the
dealers should deliver their orders first
to the market, and then the mills would
send the cargoes to the buyers directly
from their factories. This was done to
prevent the dealers from shipping the
cargoes to outport dealers. The total
purchases in the entire session amounted
to 40,000 bags of various kinds of native
flour. North China and South Sea dealers
were not in the market yesterday.
Because of the foreign exchange crisis,
the rate of native wheat was steady in
selling at yesterday's market. The market
collected an amount of this wheat from
the growing centers in the interior. For-
eign wheat was also transported to the
market for selling, but the price was al-
most the same as that of native wheat,
so that the rate of native wheat remained
unchanged. The Fooh Sing and Fou Foong
Flour Mills bought 10,000 bags of dif-
ferent kinds of native wheat from $9
to $9.40 per bag. No business in foreign
wheat was done in the entire trading.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。

1938年8月24日

面粉与小麦

在国际租界和法租界出现白米短缺后，国产面粉已成为当地中国人的重要日常主食。中国面粉厂在市场上提供无限量面粉供应，以替代大米。本地商人和米店在交易时段内表现活跃，以每袋6.40元的价格购买了大量二级产品，比上一最终收盘价高出0.20元。

根据市场报告，每位本地商人和零售店都要求进一步的面粉供应。面粉厂发布了一项规定，据此经销商应首先向市场提交订单，然后面粉厂将直接从工厂向买家发货。此举旨在防止经销商将货物转运给外埠经销商。全时段各类国产面粉的总采购量达到40,000袋。昨日华北和华南商人未出现在市场上。

由于外汇危机，昨日市场上国产小麦的售价保持稳定。市场从内地产区收集了一定数量的小麦。外国小麦也被运到市场出售，但其价格几乎与国产小麦相同，因此国产小麦的价格保持不变。福新（Fooh Sing）和阜丰（Fou Foong）面粉厂以每袋9元至9.40元的价格购买了10,000袋不同种类的国产小麦。整个交易中没有任何外国小麦的业务成交。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

AUG 1 1 1930

Rice Market in State
Of Confusion

Dealers Said to Be Holding
Back Best Grades

Utter confusion again reigned in the local rice market during the past few days with the price of the first grade rice soaring to the new high mark of $26 per picul and the official price of $20 is no longer in existence. Even at such an unprecedented prices people cannot buy the first grade rice, which is alleged to be stored by manipulators.

It would appear that the rice situation at present is still beyond the control of the authorities who were reported yesterday to be devising means of putting a stop to manipulation. The "China Evening News" reported that officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council met yesterday afternoon and the results of the meeting would soon be announced.

At present few if any people can buy the first grade rice in the Shanghai market and the inferior kind of rice is being sold at $20 or more, which is the officially fixed price for the first grade rice. Even the purchase of the second grade rice is limited. A rice shop would only sell half a picul because, it was announced, its manager could not obtain much rice from the Rice Market. The supply was decreasing, it was stated.

Rice shops have been warned against buying rice from the market in violation of the official regulation and so even of there was first grade rice in the market they did not dare to buy, it. It was reported that the 800 rice shops in town might soon suffer a serious shortage.

1930年8月11日

米市陷入混乱

据称商人囤积最佳等级大米

过去几天，本地米市再次陷入极度混乱，一级米价格飙升至每担26美元的新高点，而20美元的官方价格已不复存在。即使在如此前所未有的价格下，人们也买不到一级米，据称这些大米被投机者囤积。

目前的大米局势似乎仍超出当局的控制范围，据报道，当局昨日正在策划制止操纵的手段。《China Evening News》报道说，上海公共租界工部局的官员昨日下午举行了会议，会议结果将很快公布。

目前，在上海市场上几乎没有人能买到一级米，而劣质米的售价却在20美元或更高，这原本是一级米的官方固定价格。即使是二级米的购买也受到限制。一家米店只肯卖半担米，因为其经理宣布无法从米市获得大量大米。据说供应量正在减少。

米店已被警告不得违反官方规定从市场购买大米，因此即使市场上有一级米，他们也不敢购买。据报道，全市800家米店可能很快就会面临严重短缺。

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 1 1 1939

Rice Situation
Acute As Price
Soars To $25

Stock Ample Here But
Shops Refuse To
Make Purchase

War isolated Shanghai was once
more made conscious of its pre-
carious food supply with the report
yesterday that Kiangsu white rice
is quoted at the prohibitive prices
of $25 a picul on the local market
and is likely to reach $30 before the
end of the month.
Although rice dealers here are
believed to have a considerable
quantity of the first quality cereal
in godowns, it is said they refuse
to sell at the official maximum of
$20 a picul because the excise on
shipments of the product to Shang-
hai from growing centers makes
import prohibitively high.
Actually the stock of high grade
rice available in the growing centers
is reported ample with prices there
quoted at only $9 a picul. Trans-
portation to Shanghai is calculated
at a further $3 a picul and the
military tax is about $4 more.
The price of Kiangsu rice which
is considered amongst the best in
China has been going up steadily
during the past few weeks and is
expected by dealers to go even
higher before the end of the month.
Some believe it will reach a top of
$30 before the new season's crop is
harvested in September. The price
will probably break at that time and
return to normal as a good harvest
is reported.
In the meantime rice shops
which find themselves hard pressed
for stocks are going directly to
individual dealers rather than
through the open market. In this
way they evade the restriction im-
posed by the Shanghai Municipal
Council and the French Municipal
Council which makes $20 the maxi-
mum price per picul. But even in
such purchases it is reported the
good quality rice is often found
mixed with a second grade product.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。
1939年8月11日

米价飙升至25元
米荒形势严峻

本地库存充足但
商店拒绝采购

随着昨日报告称江苏白米在本地市场的报价高达令人望而却步的每担25元，且可能在本月底前达到30元，因战争而与世隔绝的上海再次意识到其粮食供应的脆弱性。

虽然据信这里的米商在仓库中存有相当数量的一等谷物，但据说他们拒绝以每担20元的官方最高限价出售，因为从产区向上海运输该产品的消费税使得进口成本高得令人望而却步。

实际上，据报道产区的优质大米库存充足，那里的报价仅为每担9元。运往上海的运费估算为每担额外3元，军事税约为4元多一点。

被视为中国最好大米之一的江苏米，在过去几周内价格稳步上涨，经销商预计在本月底前价格甚至会上涨得更高。一些人认为，在9月份新季作物收获之前，价格将达到30元的顶峰。据报道届时将迎来丰收，价格可能会在那时崩盘并恢复正常。

与此同时，发现自身库存紧张的米店正直接前往个人经销商处采购，而不是通过公开市场。通过这种方式，他们规避了上海公共租界工部局和法公董局 imposed 的限制，后者规定每担最高价格为20元。但据报道，即使在这样的采购中，优质大米也常常混杂着二级产品。

AUG 1 1 1939

Rice Market
The business in white rice was still deadlocked in the official market yesterday. The market received 1,000 bags of fresh white rice from the growing centers by rail and truck, and 15 junk-loads of rice coming by steamer from the interior. "P-Yong" white rice was quoted at $26 in the market or $0.50 above the previous closing rate, and "Tong-Song" rice stood at $24.50 per picul.
The selling price in the outside market was weak yesterday, and business was also narrow throughout the entire day's trading, because all the retail shops were reluctant to buy. As a result the rate fell by $0.50 below the preceding day's close, except the first-grade Changshu white rice, which was still quoted at $26.
No business in provincial rice was done by operators yesterday, while all dealers awaited the new decision by the authorities of Shanghai Municipal Council and French Concession. Despite the high rate for purchases, slight trading in the outside market was seen in yesterday's turnover, as the dealers abstained from absorbing any more provincial rice for stocks, and the rate of this rice dropped by $0.80 per picul.

米市

昨日官方市场的白米交易仍然僵持。市场通过铁路和卡车从产区接收了1,000袋新鲜白米，另有15船来自内地的轮船运抵的大米。“P-Yong”白米在市场报价为26元，比前一收盘价高出0.50元，“Tong-Song”米价格为每担24.50元。

Flour And Wheat
Owing to small stocks and high costs
of material, the Chinese Flour Mills de-
clared that no native flour was available
for selling in the market yesterday. Big
orders by the outport dealers were re-
fused by the mills. Later, the mills
offered to local wholesale dealers, that 20
bags would be sold to each buyer, and
the price rose by $0.10 above the preceding
day's price, as the official rate stood at
$5.60, in cash payment. The price of for-
eign flour in yesterday's market noted at
$5.80 per bag.
High rates of native wheat were re-
corded in the market yesterday, while all
the buyers were interested in absorbing
for stocks. The Chinese flour mills took
an active part in buying, because there
were only small shipments from the grow-
ing centers available. Both Fooh Sing and
Fou Foong Flour Mills asked 20 carloads
of newly-harvested Nanking and Wuhu
native wheat, and local buyers also bought
another 20 carloads of this wheat. The
price was $0.20 high above the last close.

1939年8月11日

面粉与小麦

由于库存少且原料成本高，中国面粉厂宣布昨日市场上无国产面粉可供销售。面粉厂拒绝了外埠经销商的大额订单。随后，面粉厂向本地批发商提出，每位买家可购买20袋，价格比前一天价格上涨0.10元，官方现金支付价格为5.60元。昨日市场上外国面粉的价格记录为每袋5.80元。

Rice Market
Slight business in white rice was done by some of the operators in the market yesterday, but no major trading was seen during the entire session. Although there was no official market of provincial rice in past few days, on account of the maximum price, unofficial business was done yesterday. The turnover was 2,000 bags of different kinds of provincial rice. The selling rate rose further by $1, compared with the preceding day's close. The first-grade of Nanking provincial rice was sold at $21.50 per picul.

Flour And Wheat

There was only small business done in native flour yesterday. CHINA PRESS.
AUG 9 1939

Rice Market

The trading in white rice was still dead-locked yesterday, since all dealers had received a strict order as to selling at maximum price from the Executive Committees of the Bean and Rice Guild last week. Owing to high costs at the growing centers and heavy transportation fees and new taxes, the rice holders refused to sell at $20 per picul, while the dealers waited for a further improvement of the situation. With lacking supplies, the retail shops took the low-grade rice at maximum price instead of first-grade white Changshu rice.

The outside market, it was reported, showed some activity and the selling price was quoted high again, compared with the preceding day's final closing rate. The high quality of white rice was noted at $25 per picul.

No official trading was recorded yesterday, on account of the new price restrictions by the authorities of Shanghai Municipal Council. Although all operators lacking in stocks the market offered no rice for selling, as the rice holders kept all their goods in stock, awaiting the high selling rate.

According to a rumor that the Wuhu rice port would be reopened for transportation by the Japanese authorities there, it was expected that the rate of provincial rice would be weak at some time next week. The selling rate of this rice at the outside market was further increased and the unofficial trading opened at $22 per picul, or $5 above the previous closing rate.

During the present high rate of provincial rice, some of the great local rice dealers and large rice houses asked the the authorities for import permission of Saigon rice in order to alleviate the shortage, but no official approval was learned yesterday.

（手写批注：Liu R. 9/8）

1939年8月9日

米市

昨日白米交易仍然僵持，因为所有经销商上周均已收到豆米业公会执行委员会关于按最高限价出售的严格命令。由于产地成本高企、运输费用昂贵以及新税开征，持米者拒绝以每担20美元的价格出售，而经销商则等待局势进一步好转。由于供应短缺，零售店以最高限价购进低等级大米，而非一等白常熟米。

据报道，场外市场显示出一丝活跃，与前一日的最终收盘价相比，售价再次走高。优质白米报价为每担25美元。

由于上海公共租界工部局当局实施了新的价格限制，昨日未记录到官方交易。尽管所有经营者都缺乏库存，但市场上没有大米可供出售，因为持米者将所有货物囤积在库，等待更高的售价。

据传闻，芜湖米港将被当地日本当局重新开放运输，预计下周某个时候外省米价将会走弱。该种大米在场外市场的售价进一步上涨，非官方交易以每担22美元开盘，比前一收盘价高出5美元。

在目前外省米价高企之际，一些本地大型米商和大米行号向当局申请进口西贡米的许可，以缓解短缺，但昨日获悉未获官方批准。

（手写批注：Liu R. 9/8）

1939年8月9日

面粉与小麦

昨日市场上本土面粉交易令人满意，尽管本土小麦近期价格创下新高，但 mills（面粉厂）采购的销售费率保持不变。华北、南洋及本地买家在吸纳货源方面表现出浓厚兴趣。估计当日向所有交易商销售的各类本土面粉总量为55,000袋。

本地经营者和内地客商主导了市场，购买了20,000袋二等产品。费率保持在现金5.50美元不变。天津经销商又求购20,000袋二等的“车牌”和“船牌”面粉，一些华北经销商购买了15,000袋四等的“红财神”面粉。这些品质的报价为期票5.90美元。由于缺乏库存，面粉厂不接受来自口岸经销商的大额订单，仅进行了零星销售。

随着中日面粉厂的旺盛需求，新收获的本土小麦的市场售价再次走高，而麦主则保持其售价非常稳定。因此，费率较上一收盘价上涨了0.20美元。福新面粉厂和丰田面粉厂均吸纳了13车皮南京和芜湖本土小麦，而在整个交易时段内，日本商人和一些本地经销商购买了10车皮苏州和太阳牌小麦。

SHANGHAI

AUG 7 1938

PROPOSAL MADE TO
COUNCIL ON RICE

Mr. Ho Suggests Council
Import Cereals To
Relieve Shortage

A request for immediate action
by the Shanghai Municipal Council
to ensure Shanghai obtaining a
steady supply to cereals from the
inland areas was made by represen-
tatives of the Shanghai Beans and
Rice Dealers Association when they
called upon Mr. T. K. Ho, Chinese
Secretary, on Friday afternoon, it
was reported yesterday.

Two main proposals were sub-
mitted to Mr. Ho to be referred to
the Council for consideration. The
first was that the Council under-
take to regulate and to ensure a
steady supply to cereals from Wuhu
by importing them into Shanghai.
The second proposal was to the
effect that the Council should, as a
supplementary measure, undertake
to import foreign rice, such as Sai-
gon cereals, on its own account so
as to relieve any emergency rice
shortage in Shanghai.

By such means, it was submitted,
it was possible to prevent wide
fluctuations in prices in the local
rice and bean market. It was
understood that Mr. Ho assured the
representatives that every effort
would be made by the Council to
prevent profiteering such as by
officially fixing and readjusting the
prices on which unofficial open
market transactions should be con-
ducted, according to the report.

上海
2 N13
1938年8月7日

向工部局提出的
关于大米的建议

何先生建议工部局
进口谷物以
缓解短缺

据昨日报道，上海豆米业同业公会代表于周五下午拜访了华务处长何德奎（T. K. Ho）先生，请求上海公共租界工部局立即采取行动，确保上海从内陆地区获得稳定的谷物供应。

向何先生提交了两项主要建议，供转呈工部局审议。第一项建议是，工部局承诺通过将芜湖谷物进口到上海来调节并确保其稳定供应。第二项建议大意是，作为补充措施，工部局应自行负责进口外国大米，如西贡谷物，以缓解上海任何紧急的大米短缺。

据称，通过此类手段，有可能防止本地米豆市场价格的大幅波动。据悉，何先生向代表们保证，工部局将尽一切努力防止牟取暴利，例如通过官方固定和调整价格，非官方公开市场交易应据此进行。

CHINA PRESS.
6 -, 1939

Rice Market

Since the authorities of Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Concession have maintained strict orders to the local rice dealers and rice hongs here in the past few days, that they must keep the selling price at a maximum rate of $20 per picul for the best quality white rice. There was no possibility to sell at a higher rate in the present market. The market has been receiving large shipments of fresh supplies from the growing centers every day, according to an investigation by the authorities recently.

The selling price in the outside market yesterday was weak or $0.50 below the preceding day's close, but the price in the official market remained unchanged. Low-grade white rice was still quoted at $20 per picul, and the second-grade rice stood at $22, while no best quality and first-grade Changshu rice was seen in the session the market received 1,700 bags of fresh rice from the interior, coming by truck rail and steamer yesterday.

According to the market record, slight business was done throughout the day as all operators were reluctant to buy during the higher quotations, awaiting further improvement. In the outside market, the selling rate of best quality of rice stood at $24 per picul, but no brisk demand was reported.

A rumor circulated in the market that 60,000 bags of provincial rice would be transported to this port from the growing centers at Wuhu. The rice holders continued to keep their selling rate at higher quotations in the market, and slight business was done in the day, as few operators were interested in buying at a high rate. The local dealers and retail shops bought 2,000 bags of provincial rice.

The selling rate of provincial rice dropped by $0.40, below the previous closing rate. Rice in the market yesterday was all low-grade Nanking and Wuhu provincial, but the high quality of this rice was not in the market, the rice holders sold directly to the rice dealers outside the market at $19 per picul.

1939年6月 - ,

米市

鉴于上海公共租界工部局和法租界当局在过去几天里向本地米商和米行下达了严格命令，要求他们必须将最优质白米的售价保持在每担20美元的最高限额。在当前市场上，不可能以更高的价格出售。据当局最近调查，市场每天都从产地接收大量新鲜供应。

昨日场外市场的售价疲软，比前一交易日收盘价低0.50美元，但官方市场的价格保持不变。低等级白米仍报价为每担20美元，二等米为22美元，而当次交易中未见最优质和一等常熟米。市场昨日通过卡车、铁路和轮船从内地收到1,700袋新米。

据市场记录，全天交易量轻微，因为所有经营者在高报价期间不愿购买，等待进一步改善。在场外市场，最优质大米的售价为每担24美元，但据报道需求并不旺盛。

市场流传一种谣言，称将有60,000袋外省米从芜湖产地运抵本埠。持米者继续在市场上维持较高的报价，当日交易清淡，因为很少有经营者有兴趣以高价购买。本地经销商和零售店购买了2,000袋外省米。

外省米的售价下跌了0.40美元，低于前一收盘价。昨日市场上的大米均为低等级的南京和芜湖外省米，但该种大米的高品质并未出现在市场上，持米者以每担19美元的价格直接在场外向米商出售。

Rice Speculators
Here To Be Dealt
With Severely

The authorities in the Interna-
tional Settlement and the French
Concession are determined to era-
dicate all speculative activities in
the local rice market, it was re-
ported yesterday by the Credit
Men's Bulletin. In pursuance of
this policy they will shortly carry
out a thorough investigation of the
rice stocks in the local godowns and
the names of their owners, and
will request the banks to strictly
reduce their grant of mortgage loans
on rice.
In connection with rumors that
the authorities will extend the
restricted price of $20 per picul for
white rice and $16 per picul for
provincial rice, these were reported
to have been denied.
page_data.zh:
在此的
大米投机者
将受到
严厉处置

据《征信新闻报》昨日报道，国际租界和法租界的当局决心根除本地米市的所有投机活动。为了贯彻这一政策，他们不久将对本地仓库中的大米库存及其所有者姓名进行彻底调查，并将要求银行严格减少大米抵押贷款的发放。
针对有关当局将延长白米每担20美元和外省米每担16美元的限价规定的谣言，据报道已被否认。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

Rice Market

Due to an uncertain selling price, the
rice market continued suspension for li-
quidation yesterday, while no operators
offered rice for sale because the price
had been too high recently. Even low-
grade white rice was sold at the maximum
price of $20. Three thousand bags of
fresh rice supplies were brought here
from the growing centers by truck, rail
and steamer, but most of those goods
were directly transported for stock in
godown instead of selling in market.
According to the unofficial rate, first-
grade white rice was quoted at $24 per
picul, but business was done directly
between traders and retail shops. A
rumor circulated in the market that the
committees of the Bean and Rice Guild
would order foreign rice shortly to settle
the rice crisis.
The business in provincial rice was
still slight in the market yesterday, owing
to the maximum price set by the authori-
ties of the Shanghai Municipal Council
and French Concession. The market has
received no fresh rice from the growing
centers at Nanking and Wuhu. The total
sales in the day were estimated at 2,000
bags of low-grade provincial rice at from
$15.50 to $16 per picul.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

米市

由于售价不确定，昨日米市继续暂停清算，由于近期价格过高，没有经营者提供大米出售。即使是低等级白米也以20美元的最高限价出售。三千袋新鲜大米供应通过卡车、铁路和轮船从产地运抵此处，但大部分货物直接运往仓库存储，而非在市场出售。
根据非官方汇率，一等白米报价为每担24美元，但交易直接在贸易商和零售店之间进行。市场流传一种谣言，称豆米业公会委员会将很快订购外国大米以解决大米危机。
昨日市场上外省米交易仍然清淡，这是由于上海公共租界工部局和法租界当局设定的最高限价所致。市场未收到来自南京和芜湖产地的新米。估计当日总销量为2,000袋低等级外省米，价格为每担15.50至16美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

Rice Market

Despite the high rate of white rice
recently, business in white rice came
to a temporary standstill in the market
yesterday, because the authorities of both
Shanghai Concessions continued the pro-
hibition against raising the selling price
above a maximum of $20 a picul for any
kind of white rice. If the dealer asks
over the above price, his business license
is liable to be withdrawn.
All operators were unwilling to exhibit
their rice for selling in the market yes-
terday, because of the price crisis. No
market rate was opened by the
holders yesterday, except the maximum
price, but there were no goods for selling.
The market received 1,400 bags of differ-
ent kinds of white rice from the interior,
by truck, rail and steamer, but most of
those goods were delivered directly for
stocks in godown.
Slight trading of provincial rice was
recorded as the selling rate declared too
high, and all the dealers were reluctant
to buy. Neither the Nanking nor Wuhu
high quality provincial rice were in the
market, even the low-grade of provincial
rice was quoted at $16 per picul. Local
and interior dealers bought 2,000 bags of
this rice for transportations.
Due to the high rate of foreign ex-
change and low quotation of Chinese na-
tional currency, the price of Saigon rice
was irregularly high for purchases, ac-
cording to the market report, the rate
of Saigon rice moved up to $25.50 per
bag, (220 lbs.) but no business was done
throughout the session.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

米市

尽管近期白米价格高企，但昨日市场上白米交易暂时停滞，因为上海两租界当局继续禁止任何种类白米的售价超过每担20美元的最高限额。如果经销商索要高于上述价格，其营业执照可能会被吊销。
由于价格危机，昨日所有经营者都不愿展示大米出售。持米者昨日除了最高限价外未开出其他市场价，但没有货物可供出售。市场通过卡车、铁路和轮船从内地收到1,400袋各类白米，但大部分货物直接交付存入仓库。
由于宣称售价过高，外省米交易记录轻微，所有经销商都不愿购买。南京或芜湖的高品质外省米均未出现在市场上，即使是低等级外省米也报价为每担16美元。本地和内地经销商购买了2,000袋此种大米用于运输。
据市场报告，由于外汇汇率高企和中国法币报价低迷，西贡米的采购价格不规则地偏高，西贡米的价格涨至每袋（220磅）25.50美元，但整个交易时段内未达成交易。

CHINA PRESS

JUL 2 1939

Because of lack of supplies, the selling
price of white rice was irregularly high
yesterday, while a keen demand was evinced
by all operators notwithstanding increas-
ingly warmer weather. The market only
received a few junkloads of white rice
from the growing centers by steamer,
and two thousand bags of fresh rice from
the interior by truck and rail.
With high tax and transportation fees
in the growing centers, the first-grade
Changshu white rice was not offered for
liquidation in the market by the rice
holders, as the selling price would have
been quoted over the maximum price of
$22 per picul, so that no highest grade
rice was seen in the market yesterday.
While all buyers made a large demand
for various kinds of white rice, the rate
of second-grade white rice rose by $0.20
to $0.30, and general-grade moved up to
a maximum price of $20, or $0.30 above
the previous closing level. Local dealers
dominated in the market for purchases
and rice hongs also bought a considerable
amount of rice.
Business in provincial rice displayed
satisfactorily in the market yesterday.
Both local and the interior merchants took
an active interest in buying. Owing to
maximum price of purchases, set by the
authorities of Shanghai Municipal Council
and French Concession recently the price
of provincial rice was similarly increased,
because the first-grade of provincial rice
was not in the market for selling.
There were small shipments of fresh
rice arriving in port from Nanking and
Wuhu yesterday. Local buyers were in-
terested in absorbing for further stocks,
while the rate of Saigon rice was irre-
gularly high during the period of the low
rate of the Chinese national dollar. The
interior dealers also absorbed a consider-
able amount of this rice for transporta-
tion. Total sales in the day were estimated
at 4,000 bags of Nanking and Wuhu
second-grade provincial rice. The former
was noted at maximum price of $16, and
the latter was quoted at $15 per picul.
The low-grade provincial rice stood between
$14.80 to $15, or $0.20 above the previous
close.

《字林西报》

1939年7月2日

由于供应短缺，昨日白米售价异常高涨，尽管天气日益炎热，所有经营者仍表现出强劲的需求。市场仅通过轮船从产区运来少量几船白米，另有两千包新米通过卡车和铁路从内地运抵。

由于产区税费及运输费用高昂，持米商未将一级常熟白米投放市场进行清算，因为售价将超过每担22元的最高限价，因此昨日市场上未见最高等级的大米。虽然各类白米需求旺盛，二级白米价格上涨0.20至0.30美元，普通级大米涨至最高价20美元，较前一收盘价上涨0.30美元。本地商人在采购中主导市场，米行也购买了相当数量的大米。

昨日外省大米在市场交易表现令人满意。本地及内地商人均积极购入。由于上海公共租界工部局和法租界当局近期设定了采购最高限价，外省大米价格同样上涨，因为一级外省大米并未上市销售。

昨日有少量来自南京和芜湖的新米运抵港口。本地买家有兴趣吸纳以备进一步库存，而在中国法币汇率低迷期间，西贡米的价格异常高企。内地商人也吸纳了相当数量的此类大米用于运输。当日总销量估计为4,000包南京和芜湖产的二级外省大米。前者最高价记为16美元，后者报价为每担15美元。低级外省大米价格在14.80至15美元之间，较前一收盘价上涨0.20美元。

CHINA PRESS
21 87

Rice Prices
Expected To
Drop Again

S. M. C., F. M. C. May
Lower Limits In
Near Future

Another reduction in the official
price limit for rice was expected in
Shanghai yesterday as huge quan-
tities of the grain continued to
pour into Shanghai from foreign
and inland ports, it was learned in
authoritative circles yesterday.

The present limits were set by
the Shanghai Municipal Council
and French Municipal Administra-
tion last Monday fixing the price
of first grade rice not to exceed
$20 per shih and of sien mee at $16.

The existing prices represented a
drop of $1 from the previous limit
ruling which prevailed in the for-
eign areas between June 23 and
July 17.

Meanwhile, according to reports,
Shanghai at present has 300,481
bags of rice stored in various go-
downs, representing a decrease of
about 40,000 bags as compared with
the previous week.

As a result of the recent
typhoons, local grain traders were
of the opinion that the rice harvest
for the current year in Kiangsu,
Chekiang and Anhwei would not be
as good as expected before.

2/7
Lilo
Coy

《字林西报》
21 87

米价
预计将
再次下跌

公共租界、法租界可能
在不久的将来
降低限价

据昨日权威人士透露，随着大量大米继续从外国港口和内陆港口涌入上海，预计上海官方大米限价将再次下调。

现行限价由上海公共租界工部局和法公董局于上周一制定，规定一级大米价格每石不超过20美元，仙米（sien mee）价格为16美元。

现行价格代表较此前在6月23日至7月17日期间适用于外侨区域的限价下降了1美元。

与此同时，据报道，上海目前各仓库储存大米300,481包，与上周相比减少了约40,000包。

受近期台风影响，本地粮商认为江苏、浙江和安徽今年的稻米收成将不如此前预期的那样好。

2/7
Lilo
Coy

CHINA PRESS

MAY 26 1959

Rice Market

Rice quotations were irregularly lower during last few days, owing to the advent of warm weather. The opening price of white rice in yesterday's morning market was $0.50 below the previous final rate. Rice supplies brought here during the day totaled eight junkloads and 3,000 bags of white rice, brought by steamer and rail from the interior.

Local dealers are reluctant to buy more rice for their stocks, because of the imminence of the damp season in early part of June, according to the lunar calendar, but the holders offered a handsome discount rate to the buyers, thus attracting business.

Trading in yesterday's market was very satisfactory, with few hundred bags of first-grade white rice quoted around $17 and second-grade at $16.50 by local and outport traders. The third-grade also went down by $0.40 per bag.

The provincial rice displayed weakness, the opening price dropping by $0.40 in liquidation, with small business done throughout the day's session.

《字林西报》

1959年5月26日

米市

由于天气转暖，过去几天大米报价不规则下跌。昨日早市白米开盘价较前一最终成交价低0.50美元。当日运抵此处的大米供应总量为八船白米，以及通过轮船和铁路从内地运来的3,000包白米。

根据农历，六月初潮湿季节即将来临，本地商人不愿再购进大米增加库存，但持货商向买家提供了可观的折扣率，从而吸引了交易。

昨日市场交易非常令人满意，本地和外埠商人报价一级白米约为17美元，二级为16.50美元，仅有数百包成交。三级大米每包也下跌了0.40美元。

外省大米表现疲软，清算时开盘价下跌0.40美元，全天交易清淡。

Ta Ying Yeh Pao dated April 29 :-

THE RICE SITUATION

According to an arrival from Sungkiang
yesterday, Li Shih Tu (米市酒) in the south Whangpoo,
from which place rice supplies were transported to
Shanghai, has been blockaded by the Japanese authorities
since April 27. Some 200 rice boats have been held
up and the rice supplies thereon have been forcibly
bought over by the Japanese at $10.80 per picul despite
the market price being set at $12 per picul.
On the surface, the rice supplies were
purchased by a firm known as the Cheng Kee Company
(誠記洋行). It is learned that the latter in turn sold
them to Japanese merchants. For this reason, the price
of rice in this locality has been increasing again.

Pan
Rks

4月29日《大英夜报》：

米市情况

据昨日来自松江的消息称，位于黄浦江南部、大米由此转运至上海的Li Shih Tu (米市酒)自4月27日起已被日本当局封锁。约200艘米船被扣留，船上的大米供应被日本方面以每担10.80美元的价格强行收购，尽管市场价格定为每担12美元。

表面上，这些大米是由一家名为诚记洋行（Cheng Kee Company）的公司购买的。据悉，该公司随后将其转售给日本商人。因此，该地区的大米价格再次上涨。

Pan

Hwa Mei Chen Pao :-

RICE MERCHANTS BUYING GRAIN FOR JAPANESE

The Japanese authorities are
purchasing provisions and many traitorous merchants, such
as the Heng Nyi Kung (恒義公), Ho Kee Hong (和記行),
etc., have been collecting rice in the hope of making a
profit.

According to information given out by the
rice trade, a strong warning has been received by some
of the local traitorous rice merchants against their
traitorous activities. Though this has created some anxiety
among these merchants, they are continuing their purchases
of rice for the Japanese.

Shanghai Has
Seven Weeks'
Rice Supply

S.M.C. Food Committee
Member Says Dealers
Can Go It Alone

SHORTAGE SEEN,
HOWEVER, IN AUG.

Rice Guild Demanding
Free Movement
Of Grain

There are now approximately
500,000 bags of rice stored in
Shanghai. This is a sufficient
supply for seven weeks. Twenty-
five thousand bags, or 2,500 tons of
this is the property of the Shanghai
Municipal Council, bought duty
free last December when a rice
shortage appeared imminent.
"It is not the intention of the
authorities to import any further
foreign rice. The rice trades should
now be in a position to look out
for themselves," a member of the
S.M.C. Food Committee told THE
CHINA PRESS yesterday.
The daily consumption of rice in
Shanghai is between 8,000 and 9,000
bags. There is a sufficient quantity
of rice coming here daily to satisfy
all immediate requirements. As
long as this supply continues un-
interrupted there can be no question
of a shortage.
"There is prospect of a rice short-
age here at the end of August
should the surrounding areas go
unplanted this summer," one au-
thority said.

Koreans Planting Rice

"I know there are 4,500 Koreans
even now planting rice in Pei Shin,
Chin, near Hungjao, and con-
sequently there will be an ample
supply of rice this fall." Mr. R. K.
Raphael, local rice broker, said
yesterday.
At the present time a sharp con-
troversy is under way between the
local Rice Shop Guild and the Rice
Guild.
The Rice Shop Guild, backed by
powerful foreign and Chinese inter-
ests, are demanding an embargo on
the export of rice from this city,

上海拥有
七周的
大米储备

公共租界工部局粮食委员会
成员称商人可
自力更生

然而，预计八月
将出现短缺

米业公会要求
粮食自由流通

目前上海储存的大米约有500,000包。这足以供应七周。其中25,000包，即2,500吨，属于上海公共租界工部局的财产，是去年12月在米荒看似迫在眉睫时免税购买的。

“当局无意再进口任何外国大米。米业界现在应该能够自谋生路了，”公共租界工部局粮食委员会的一名成员昨日告诉《字林西报》。

上海每日大米消耗量在8,000至9,000包之间。每日运抵此处的大米数量充足，足以满足所有即时需求。只要这种供应持续不断，就不会出现短缺问题。

“如果周边地区今年夏季不种植作物，八月底这里可能会出现大米短缺，”一位权威人士说。

朝鲜人种植水稻

“我知道即使在现在，仍有4,500名朝鲜人在虹桥附近的北新泾（Pei Shin, Chin）种植水稻，因此今年秋季大米供应将十分充足。”本地大米经纪人R. K. Raphael先生昨日表示。

目前，本地米号公会与米业公会之间正在进行激烈的争论。
米号公会在强大的中外利益集团支持下，要求禁止从本市出口大米，

Lack of Interest
The Courts have proved or treated
with complete lack of interest or
sympathy such illegal speculations
and restraints endangering the daily
food of the people and the peace and
good order of community. It is also
a true fact that the Courts in hand-
ling the cases of rental disputes have
displayed inconsistency and incapacity
without reference to any equitable
principle and have created a very
unfavourable impression on the minds
of Chinese as well as foreign tenants
without at the same time giving any
satisfaction to the landlords. In order
to remove these grievances and to
maintain the peace and order of the
Settlement and Concession, these
Courts must be taken over by the
Reformed Government. Moreover,
these Courts being strictly Chinese
Courts must in order to exercise any
effective jurisdiction be under the
direct and sole control of the de
facto authorities as alone in conjunc-
tion with them can the Courts be
backed with the adequate authority.

Repeated Representations
My repeated representations on the
subject of the Courts made to you,
the Consular Body and the Shanghai
Municipal Council, have not produced
any response or expression of opinion,
and it is a matter of great regret to
me and of grave public concern that
this important problem is left in abey-
ance. While I invoke your co-
operation for the welfare of the
people in curbing the speculation of
the rice profiteers and in standardiz-
ing the price of this staple food sup-
ply. I desire to emphasize that the
most effective way of achieving that
end is to enable the Courts to carry
out its functions in that respect under
the control of the only de facto au-
thorities and I would request your
earnest and deepest consideration of
the question and a reply on the sub-
ject at your earliest convenience.
page_data.zh:
23935

缺乏关注

法院已证明或对待此类非法投机和限制行为完全缺乏兴趣或同情，这些行为危及人民的日常食物以及社区的和平与良好秩序。同样属实的是，法院在处理租赁纠纷案件时，表现出前后不一和无能，不考虑任何公平原则，在中国和外国租户心中造成了非常不利的印象，同时也没有给房东带来任何满意的结果。为了消除这些不满并维持租界和法租界的和平与秩序，这些法院必须由维新政府接管。此外，这些法院既然是纯粹的中国法院，为了行使有效的管辖权，必须处于事实上当局的直接和单独控制之下，因为只有与他们结合，法院才能得到充分的权力支持。

反复交涉

我就法院问题向你、领事团和上海公共租界工部局进行的反复交涉未产生任何回应或意见表达，这一重要问题被搁置，令我深感遗憾，也引起公众严重关切。虽然我呼吁你们合作，为了人民福祉，遏制米商投机倒把并规范这种主食供应的价格。我想强调，实现这一目标最有效的途径是使法院能够在唯一的事实上当局的控制下履行其在此方面的职能，我恳请你们对此问题进行认真且深入的考虑，并在方便时尽早就此主题给予答复。

CHINA PRESS

JUL 19 1939

Rice Market

The selling rate of white rice was high
in the market yesterday, but satisfactory
business was done throughout the day's
session. The market has received 8 junk-
loads of white rice from the interior by
steamer and another 2,000 bags of fresh
rice supplies were brought here by truck
and rail from the growing centers.
Due to high rate of foreign ex-
change yesterday, the price of foreign
rice showed strength in the market, while
the rice holders kept their goods for
purchase, and asked a high price of
white rice. As a result, both low-grade
and second-grade of white rice moved up
$0.30 per picul, as compared with the
preceding day's final rate.
Although the weather is hot, all the
operators were still interested in buying,
and absorbed a considerable amount of
first-grade Changshu white rice and the
price was increased to $20, or $0.40 above
yesterday's closing rate.
Despite lower quotations of provincial
rice in the last few days, a brisk demand
was seen in the market yesterday, while
local dealers took an active interest in
absorbing for further stocks. There was
a large amount of provincial rice brought
here from the growing centers in Nan-
king and Wuhu.
The rice holders refused to sell their
goods at the ordinary rate, because Saigon
rice displayed a high price after foreign
exchange rates become high yesterday
morning. According to the official market
rate yesterday, the price of various kinds
of provincial rice moved up by $0.20 to
$0.35 per picul. The total sales to both
local and outport dealers were estimated
at 4,000 bags of Nanking and Wuhu
provincial rice, the former was quoted at
from $15.40 to $16, and the latter stood
at $13.30 per picul.

《字林西报》

1939年7月19日

米市

昨日市场白米售价高企，但全天交易令人满意。市场通过轮船从内地收到8船白米，另有2,000包新米供应通过卡车和铁路从产区运抵此处。

由于昨日外汇汇率高企，洋米价格在市场上表现坚挺，而持米商惜售，对白米要价高昂。结果，低级和二级白米价格较前一日最终成交价每担上涨0.30美元。

尽管天气炎热，所有经营者仍有意购买，吸纳了大量一级常熟白米，价格涨至20美元，较昨日收盘价上涨0.40美元。

尽管过去几天外省大米报价较低，但昨日市场需求旺盛，本地商人积极吸纳以增加库存。有大量外省大米从南京和芜湖等产区运抵此处。

持米商拒绝以普通价格出售货物，因为昨日早晨外汇汇率走高后，西贡米价格显示高位。根据昨日官方市场价，各类外省大米价格每担上涨0.20至0.35美元。卖给本地和外埠商人的总销量估计为4,000包南京和芜湖产外省大米，前者报价在15.40至16美元之间，后者站稳在每担13.30美元。

CHINA PRESS.
JUL 15 1939

Rice Market

Due to large shipments of fresh rice arriving here yesterday, the selling price of white rice was irregularly weak in the market. Local dealers were inactive buyers because of considerable amounts of stocked rice in godowns, while the interior showed no brisk demand and bought fractional amounts throughout the day.

Because cash was wanting for rice collection in the growing centers, rice holders hurried to sell their goods in the market, and offered their stock at low prices, but no big business was done. According to the official quotation, the selling rate of various kinds of white rice dropped heavily. The second-grade white rice fell by $0.40, below the preceding day's final rate, and first-grade Changshu white rice went down to $0.30, or $20.30 per picul.

Provincial rice opened very weak and the price weakened still more in the market. It was a surprise to all that the Wuhu provincial price fell by $0.50 per picul, and Nanking provincial rice went lower by $0.30 than Thursday's closing rate. The market received considerable amounts of fresh supplies of provincial rice yesterday from the growing centers.

Local dealers were not interested in further buying for stock during the hot weather, and the outport dealers were reluctant to absorb for transportations. The total sales in the day was estimated at 2,000 bags of Nanking and Wuhu provincial rice. The former was quoted at $16 and the latter stood at $14 per picul.

《字林西报》（China Press）
1939年7月15日

米市

由于昨日大量新米运抵此地，市场上白米售价走势疲软且不规则。本地商号因栈房内囤积大米数量可观，购货不积极；而内地需求并不旺盛，全天仅零星采购。

由于产区收米缺乏现金，持米者急于在市场抛售货物，低价供应库存，但成交寥寥。据官方报价，各类白米售价大幅下跌。二级白米较前一日最终收盘价下跌0.40元，一级常熟白米下跌0.30元，至每担20.30元。

外省米开盘极弱，市场价位进一步走低。令人惊讶的是，芜湖外省米每担下跌0.50元，南京外省米较周四收盘价下跌0.30元。昨日市场接收了来自产区的相当数量的外省新米供应。

鉴于天气炎热，本地商号无意继续进货囤积，外埠商号也不愿吸纳货物以作转运。当日总销量估计为2,000包南京和芜湖外省米。前者报价为每担16元，后者为每担14元。

JUL 5 1939
Flour And Wheat
No improvement in native flour was
seen in yesterday's market. Selling
amounts were very narrow, because of
shortage of Chinese national currency for
liquidation, while the mills continued to
refuse order cheques for both local and
outport dealers. The outport buyers
bought only fractional amounts for ship-
ment, and local dealers absorbed a few
hundred bags of second-grade product at
$4.65 cash.
Owing to a surplus of native wheat in
the market, the selling price showed lower
yesterday, with few operators interested
in buying. The Chinese mills were not
in the market, and Japanese merchant
dominated. As a result, the Japanese
mills bought 200 bags of Nanking newly-
harvested native wheat at $6.42 per 100
catties, or $0.16 below the previous final
closing rate.

1939年7月5日
面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉市场未见起色。由于缺乏法币进行结算，成交量极为有限，而磨坊继续拒绝接受本地及外埠商号的订单支票。外埠买家仅零星采购以供装运，本地商号以现金每包4.65元的价格吸纳了数百包二级产品。

由于市场上国产小麦供过于求，昨日售价走低，鲜有经营者有意购买。中国磨坊未入市交易，日本商人占据主导。结果，日本磨坊以每百斤6.42元的价格购买了200包南京新收国产小麦，较前一最终收盘价低0.16元。
