《上海泰晤士报》

1939年6月3日

欲购绿茶

进口商安排从浙江购买绿茶

据悉，本地茶商正准备从浙江地区购买大量低品质绿茶，因为目前大量作物可供上市。

这种低等级绿茶不符合国外市场需求，注定用于国内消费。本地茶叶进口商和商人目前正在与其各自的公会安排获取真实证明书，以便在向财政部对外贸易委员会申请将茶叶进口至上海时出示。据报道，面向国内市场的茶叶进口商和商人无需以外汇支付购买款项，但在中国海关当局允许装运之前，必须从对外贸易委员会获得证明书。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
14043
JUN 3 1939
TOOTHBRUSH MAKERS FACING SHORTAGE
Government Ban Upon Handling Bristles Chief Cause

The local Chinese toothbrush manufacturers
are said to be facing an acute shortage of bristles following
the Chinese Government ban on shipments of bristles to
Shanghai, it was reported yesterday.

In view of the situation, Mr. Yu Ya-ching
has sent a petition in the name of the Shanghai Toothbrush
Manufacturers Guild to the Ministry of Economic Affairs
urging that the ban on bristle exports to Shanghai be lifted
in consideration of the future of the industry and the problems
of livelihood of the thousands of workers now employed in the
various factories.

Exportation of white and black bristles to
Shanghai, the petition stated, are requested to be permitted on
condition that the importers can produce bona fide certificates
from the Chamber of Commerce which shall guarantee that such
imports are designed for the use of the factory concerned and
will not be sold to the "enemy"

Following the ban, exports of bristles from
China to foreign countries have been brought under the control
of the Foreign Trade Commission of the Ministry of Finance.
It was previously reported that large quantities of bristle
exported to Shanghai from the inland cities had found their way
to Japan during the past year, and hence the Chinese Government
has deemed it necessary to enforce the present ban.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》
14043
1939年6月3日
牙刷制造商面临短缺
政府禁止处理猪鬃是主要原因

据报道，继中国政府禁止向上海装运猪鬃后，本地中国牙刷制造商据说正面临猪鬃严重短缺的局面。

鉴于此情况，虞洽卿先生以上海牙刷制造业同业公会的名义向经济部递交请愿书，敦促考虑到该行业的未来以及目前在各个工厂受雇的数千名工人的生计问题，解除对向上海出口猪鬃的禁令。

请愿书称，请求允许向上海出口白猪鬃和黑猪鬃，条件是进口商能提供商会出具的真实证明书，保证此类进口旨在供相关工厂使用，且不会出售给“敌人”。

继该禁令之后，中国向外国出口猪鬃已置于财政部对外贸易委员会的控制之下。此前曾有报道指出，过去一年中，从内地城市出口到上海的大量猪鬃流向了日本，因此中国政府认为有必要执行目前的禁令。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES
MAY 31 1989

Closure Of Ports Will
Not Greatly Affect The
Local Food Situation

Cost Of Vegetables, Eggs, Poultry And Pork Is
Expected To Increase, But No Alarming
Shortage Envisaged By Authorities

SHIPPING COMPANIES ARE NOT YET
INFORMED AS ZERO HOUR NEARS

The supply of fresh food to the foreign-controlled areas of
Shanghai will not be greatly affected by the closure of nine
ports along the Kiangsu and Chekiang coast and in the Yangtze
estuary, local authorities stated yesterday.
The men who are rarely heard of, but who, nevertheless,
watch that ample supplies of fresh products are always avail-
able in Shanghai, pointed out that the latest measure by the
Japanese authorities will undoubtedly cause a rise in prices, but
they emphatically discounted all rumours that there is likely
to be an alarming shortage.
While the food situation was at
the back of most discussions yester-
day, up to a late hour in the after-
noon shipping companies which
operate vessels to the ports which
are to be affected by the new order
had received no official informa-
tion that their vessels would be re-
fused clearance papers as from to-
morrow.

Statement By Japanese
At the Japanese Press conference
yesterday afternoon, the Navy
spokesman stated that no official
communication of the new order
had been sent by the Japanese au-
thorities either to the shipping com-
panies or to the consulates of third
Powers. He pointed out that if any
notification to that effect were is-
sued, it would be by the Customs
authorities.
On Monday afternoon it was an-
nounced by the Navy spokesman
that the following nine ports would
be closed to shipping from Shang-
hai: Haimen in Kiangsu, Chitung in
Kiangsu, Haimen in Chekiang,
Hsinghwa in Kiangsu, Siushu, Kan-
king, Chuanchow in Fukien, Hsin-
yangkong and Funing in Kiangsu.
The spokesman at the time con-
tended that the measure was being
introduced as a military necessity
and that the Customs authorities
would refuse clearance papers, act-
ing upon the demand of the Japan-
ese authorities, as the force in oc-
cupation of the local areas.

Effect of Closure
The closure of several of the nine
ports will have very little effect on
Shanghai. The closure of Haimen
in Chekiang will affect the local
supplies of sea foods. Eggs, veget-
ables, poultry and a few pigs also
come from that port. The closure of
Hsinyangkong will play the greatest
hardship, as from this port the
major supply of pigs comes to
Shanghai. This will mainly affect
the local Chinese community.
Authorities pointed out that large
quantities of vegetables, even dur-
ing the present "off season" period,
were coming over daily from Poo-
tung and this is likely to prevent
any shortage. Profiteering will,
of course, be in evidence as unscru-
pulous dealers will take opportunity
to increase their prices, claiming
difficulties of getting supplies into
the foreign areas and owing to in-
creased transportation charges in
case the food supplies have to be
carried by different routes.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年5月31日

港口关闭不会
对本地食品供应状况
造成重大影响

当局预计蔬菜、鸡蛋、家禽和猪肉价格
将上涨，但认为不会出现令人恐慌的短缺

随着最后期限临近，航运公司
尚未收到通知

上海地方当局昨日表示，江苏和浙江沿海及长江口九个港口的关闭，不会对上海外侨控制区的鲜食供应造成重大影响。
那些鲜为人知、却时刻确保上海有充足新鲜产品供应的人士指出，日本当局的最新措施无疑会导致价格上涨，但他们坚决驳斥了所有关于可能出现严重短缺的谣言。
尽管昨天的讨论大多围绕着食品供应问题展开，但直到下午很晚，经营驶往受新令影响港口的船只的航运公司仍未收到官方通知，称其船只将从明天起被拒绝签发结关单。

日本方面的声明
在昨日下午的日本记者招待会上，海军发言人表示，日本当局尚未向航运公司或第三国领事馆发出关于新命令的正式照会。他指出，如果发布此类通知，将由海关当局发出。
周一午后，海军发言人宣布，以下九个港口将禁止来自上海的船只进入：江苏海门、江苏启东、浙江海门、江苏兴化、秀水（音译）、甘京（音译）、福建泉州、江苏新洋港和阜宁。
该发言人当时声称，此举是出于军事需要，海关当局将应占领当地地区的日本当局的要求，拒绝签发结关单。

关闭的影响
这九个港口中几个港口的关闭对上海影响甚微。浙江海门的关闭将影响本地的海产品供应。鸡蛋、蔬菜、家禽和少量生猪也来自该港口。新洋港的关闭将造成最大的困难，因为上海的大部分生猪供应来自该港口。这将主要影响本地华人社群。
当局指出，即使在目前的“淡季”，每天都有大量蔬菜从浦东运来，这可能会防止任何短缺现象。当然，投机倒把行为将会显现，无良商贩将借机抬高价格，声称难以将物资运入外侨区，并且如果食品供应必须通过不同路线运输，运输费用也会增加。

page_data.en:
Tsunming Island, from which large
supplies of cereals come to Shang-
hai, has not been closed and neither
have a dozen or more other small
ports, which will continued to for-
ward their produce to Shanghai.
To Sail To-morrow
Unless a definite order is received
that their vessels will not be per-
mitted to enter the nine ports enu-
merated, the various shipping com-
panies yesterday had not made any
change in their sailing schedules and
were planning to dispatch their ves-
sels as usual. The larger shipping
firms operating along the coast were
only slightly affected by the new
order and when approached yester-
day could not state what their atti-
tude would be.
Also questioned on this problem,
the British Shipping Vice-Consul
stated that he had heard noth-
ing beyond the original order
closing the ports to Shanghai ship-
ping. There had been no further
developments, he continued, and the
Consulate had taken no action. When
asked if a protest was going to be
lodged with the Japanese by the
British, the Shipping Vice-Consul
said that he considered it a problem
to be dealt with by the Governments
at home, and not by the local
authorities.
Questioned further he said that
the order stated that all ships pro-
ceeding to these ports would be stop-
ped, but whether they would, in fact,
was another matter.
Vessels Affected
Some of the vessels affected by
the new order will be the Jardine's
s.s. Liwo, which sails for Haimen and
Chitung, as well as the s.s. Heini,
Patti and Kiangting which call at
Haimen in Kiangsu as well as at
Chitung in the same province.
page_data.zh:
崇明岛并未关闭，上海的大量谷物供应来自该地；此外还有十几个其他小港口也未关闭，它们将继续向上海输送农产品。
明日启航
除非收到明确命令禁止其船只进入上述九个港口，否则各航运公司昨日未对其航行计划做任何更改，并计划照常派遣船只。沿海岸线运营的大型航运公司受新令影响较小，昨日被问及此事时，它们无法说明其态度。
英国航运副领事也就此问题接受了询问，他表示除了最初发布的禁止上海船只进入这些港口的命令外，未听到其他消息。他继续说，事态没有进一步的发展，领事馆也未采取任何行动。当被问及英国是否会向日本提出抗议时，这位航运副领事表示，他认为这是一个应由本国政府而非地方当局处理的问题。
进一步询问时，他说命令规定所有前往这些港口的船只都将被拦截，但是否真的会这样做则是另一回事。
受影响的船只
受新令影响的部分船只包括怡和洋行的“利沃”号轮船（s.s. Liwo），该船驶往海门和启东；以及“黑尼”号（s.s. Heini）、“帕蒂”号（Patti）和“江定”号（Kiangting）轮船，这些船只停靠江苏海门以及同省的启东。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

MAY 3 1 1939

Port Famine Faces
Shanghai

Guerillas Forbid Dealers
To Ship Pigs in Japanese
Vessels

Shanghai may have no pork for
sale at all after two or three days
because the present supply is enough
for about two days' consumption and
farmers raising pigs in north Kiangsu
can no longer transport their stock
to Shanghai if the guerillas there are
serious in carrying out their order
forbidding all pigs to be transported
by Japanese steamers.

At present all steamers carrying
pigs to Shanghai must be "appointed"
by the new Shanghai Cattle Market
in Hongkew, and since the market is
a Japanese sponsored organization
practically all appointed steamers
are Japanese. Enraged by this
monopoly, guerillas in North Kiangsu
have forbidden farmers to transport
their pigs in junks to Japanese
steamers, threatening not only to
confiscate all pigs but also to burn
the junks if the rule is violated.

Thus the Shanghai populace is
being attacked from both the front
and rear, as it were, in the matter of
obtaining a supply of pigs. Pig deal-
ers operating south of the creek have
refused to register with the new
market and therefore they can not
take delivery of the pigs sent to them
by farmers in the interior and de-
tained by the market authorities.
During the past fortnight or so
Shanghai has been getting a small
supply of pigs because of this non-
cooperation movement, but now the
situation is aggravated by the fact
that the guerillas are dealing a death
blow to the business by forbidding
pig raisers to transport pigs to this
port.

The new market is reported to be
trying to control the transportation
of other live stock and this is said
to be part of the economic penetra-
tion programme being followed by
the Asia Development Board. No
official announcement has been made
in this connection, however.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年5月31日

上海面临
港口饥荒

游击队禁止商人
用日本船只运输生猪

由于目前的供应仅够约两天的消费，且如果江苏北部的游击队认真执行其禁止所有生猪由日本轮船运输的命令，那里的养猪农民将无法再把牲畜运往上海，因此两三天后上海可能根本无猪肉可售。

目前，所有运载生猪到上海的轮船必须由虹口的新上海牲畜市场“指定”，由于该市场是一个由日本赞助的组织，实际上所有被指定的轮船都是日本轮船。江苏北部的游击队对这种垄断感到愤怒，禁止农民用舢板将生猪运至日本轮船，并威胁如果违反规定，不仅没收所有生猪，还要烧毁舢板。

因此，在获取生猪供应方面，上海民众可谓腹背受敌。苏州河以南经营的猪贩拒绝在新市场注册，因此他们无法接收内地农民发送给他们、并被市场当局扣留的生猪。在过去两周左右的时间里，由于这种不合作运动，上海获得的生猪供应很少，但现在局势因游击队禁止养猪户将生猪运往本港，从而对该行业给予致命打击而更加恶化。

据报道，新市场正试图控制其他活畜的运输，据说这是亚洲开发委员会正在推行的经济渗透计划的一部分。然而，对此尚未发布官方公告。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 3 1 1939

Local Rice
Stocks Put At
562,192 Bags

Shanghai present stocks of rice
total 562,192 bags, showing an in-
crease of 4,352 bags compared with
the figure for last week, according
to the ninth investigation made by
the provision merchants' guilds, the
Credit Men's Bulletin reported last
night.

From reliable sources, however, it
has been learned that the actual
quantity in stock in Shanghai far
exceeds the figure indicated in the
report of the rice merchants guilds.

Since the outbreak of the current
Sino-Japanese hostilities, it was
stated, Shanghai has literally been
overwhelmed by a flood of idle
wealth, as a result of the influx
of capital from the inland areas.
Those who possess much idle money
have almost invariably speculated in
the commodities market, and in
consequence, much rice has, been
stored up by them, it was said.

At the same time, most shops
and merchants are reported to have
bought and stored up from 10 to
100 piculs each for the consump-
tion of their staff while private
families have hoarded up supplies
sufficient to last for some time.

Meanwhile, fairly large quantities
of provincial rice are continuing
to be brought to Shanghai. In
view of the fact that within the
next month or two fresh crops in
the Pootung and the surrounding
areas will be available, it is generally
anticipated that the current stocks
will be sufficient to last until new
arrivals are received, and that
prices will continue to show an
easier tendency.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年5月31日

本地大米
库存定为
562,192袋

据米业公会进行的第九次调查，《征信新闻》昨晚报道，上海目前的大米库存总量为562,192袋，比上周的数字增加了4,352袋。

然而，从可靠渠道获悉，上海的实际库存量远远超过米业公会报告中显示的數字。

据悉，自当前中日敌对行动爆发以来，由于内地资本涌入，上海实际上充斥着大量闲置资金。拥有大量闲置资金的人几乎无一例外地在商品市场进行投机，因此，据说他们囤积了大量大米。

同时，据报道，大多数商店和商人都购买了10至100担不等的大米储存起来供员工消费，而私人家庭也囤积了足够维持一段时间的供应品。

与此同时，相当数量的外省大米继续运抵上海。鉴于未来一两个月内浦东及周边地区将有新作物上市，人们普遍预期目前的库存足以维持到新货到达，且价格将继续呈现趋缓态势。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 31 1939

Ban On Exports Of
East Chekiang Eggs
To Shanghai Lifted

Fresh eggs, which have been
banned from shipment from
east Chekiang, are now again
permitted to be transported to
Shanghai, according to informa-
tion from local egg merchants
yesterday.
The Chekiang Provincial
Government, the Credit Men's
Bulletin said, has informed
the Ningpo Egg Merchants
Guild that more than 5,000
baskets of fresh eggs stocked
up in the city have been per-
mitted to be exported to Shang-
hai.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年5月31日

取消浙东鸡蛋
运往上海的出口禁令

据昨日本地蛋商提供的消息，此前被禁止从浙东装运的新鲜鸡蛋，现在再次允许运往上海。
《征信新闻》称，浙江省政府已通知宁波蛋业公会，允许将该市囤积的5,000多篮新鲜鸡蛋出口到上海。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

MAY 31 1939

Rice Market

With the weather turning cold in the
last few days, the dealers continue to
absorb rice for their stocks, while the
opening price of the white rice rose irre-
gularly in yesterday's market, with a
favourable business recorded throughout the
day's session.
Rice supplies received by the market
yesterday from the interior totaled seven
junkloads and 4,000 bags brought by
steamer and rail. Local traders took
an active interest in yesterday's market,
and bought a considerable amount of
white rice, although the selling price rose
by $0.40 above the previous closing rate.
The outport dealers also purchased a big
amount of white rice for transportation.
The rice holders took advantage of the
present cold spell to transport a large
amount of rice to the market from the
country for liquidation. The opening
price of white rice was officially quoted
at $17.50 per first-grade picul, or $0.40
above Monday's closing rate.
The price of the provincial rice was
steady yesterday and a satisfactory busi-
ness was done by the dealers. The market
has received a large shipment yesterday
for sale. Both the local and outport
dealers were interested in buying.
Local operators dominated the market
yesterday and bought more than 3,000 bags
of Nanking and Wuhu provincial rice for
their stocks, the former being quoted at
$14.90 and the latter at $14.70. The
low-grade product rose to $12.80.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年5月31日

大米市场

随着近几日天气转凉，经销商继续吸收大米入库，昨日市场白米开盘价不规则上涨，全天交易记录良好。
昨日市场从内地收到的大米供应总计为七舢板装载量以及由轮船和铁路运来的4,000袋。本地交易商对昨日市场表现出浓厚兴趣，购买了大量白米，尽管售价比前一收盘价上涨了0.40美元。外地经销商也购买了大量白米用于运输。
持米者利用当前的寒冷天气，将大量大米从乡村运到市场进行抛售。白米的官方开盘报价为每头等担17.50美元，比周一的收盘价高出0.40美元。
昨日外省大米价格稳定，经销商交易令人满意。市场昨日收到大批货物待售。本地和外地经销商都有购买意向。
本地经营者昨日主导了市场，为其库存购买了3,000多袋南京和芜湖产的外省大米，前者报价为14.90美元，后者为14.70美元。低等级产品涨至12.80美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 31 1939

Flour And Wheat

With a steady liquidation of foreign
flour in yesterday's market, the opening
price of native flour offered by the mills
dropped to $4.35 or $0.05 below the pre-
ceding day's closing rate. Large amounts
of flour were purchased by various dealers.
Because of big shipments of foreign
flour recently brought here, the native
flour has been dropping irregularly in the
last few days, and is expected to continue
its fall for a day or two.
Both the South Sea and North China
dealers absorbed more than 30,000 bags
of native flour at a reasonable price. The
local and the interior traders also bought
20,000 bags at $4.35, paid by order cheque.
Trading in foreign flour in the market
was very dull and slight, although its
price was cheaper than that of the native
flour, falling to $4.20, or $0.15 below
the previous closing rate.
Native wheat was very weak in yester-
day's market, and no big business was
done throughout the day's session, because
local and the interior dealers were not
in the market.
The mills do not desire further native
wheat for their stocks while the outport
dealers bought fractionally for transpor-
tation. The Japanese traders dominated
yesterday's trading and absorbed about
300 bags of Kiangpeh native wheat at
$6.05 in cash.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年5月31日

面粉与小麦

随着昨日市场外国面粉的稳定抛售，磨坊提供的国产面粉开盘价跌至4.35美元，比前一日收盘价低0.05美元。各类经销商购买了大量面粉。
由于近期大量外国面粉运抵此地，国产面粉在近几日不规则下跌，预计还将继续下跌一两天。
南洋和华北经销商以合理的价格吸收了30,000多袋国产面粉。本地和内地交易商也以4.35美元的价格购买了20,000袋，通过指令支票支付。
尽管外国面粉价格比国产面粉便宜，跌至4.20美元，比前一日收盘价低0.15美元，但市场上的外国面粉交易非常清淡且微量。
昨日市场上国产小麦走势非常疲软，全天没有达成大宗交易，因为本地和内地经销商均未入市。
磨坊不希望进一步增加国产小麦库存，而外地经销商仅零星购买用于运输。日本交易商主导了昨日的交易，以现金6.05美元的价格吸收了约300袋江北国产小麦。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

MAY 25 1939

RICE PRICES EASIER
WITH BIG SUPPLY

Increasing Arrivals In
City From Inland Has
Boosted Stocks

Anxiety felt recently over a possible shortage of rice in the local market was considerably allayed following the arrival of heavy shipments from the inland areas, during the past few days, according to Chinese reports yesterday.

The ban on the exportation of cereals from the inland areas to Shanghai, it was further stated, has now been lifted, and with the approach of warmer weather, the rice stock holders have shown a greater willingness to unload their cargo into the local rice market. This has the effect of bringing the prices down appreciably.

Meanwhile, the stocks on hand are said to be fairly adequate, a total 557,840 bags are said to be held by local rice merchants' circles, thus showing an increase of by 4,592 bags as compared with last week, it was revealed yesterday.

Greater stability in the Shanghai rice market is anticipated in the near future, in view of the heavy orders for foreign cereals already placed by local Chinese merchants, according to the report.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年5月25日

大米供应充足
价格趋缓

来自内地的抵沪量增加
推高了库存

据昨日中文媒体报道，过去几天大量货物从内地运抵，大大缓解了近期因本地市场可能出现大米短缺而产生的焦虑。

报道进一步指出，禁止从内地向上海出口谷物的禁令现已解除，随着天气转暖，大米持有者更有意愿将货物投放到本地大米市场。这使得价格显著下降。

与此同时，据悉现有库存相当充足，本地米商圈子持有的总量为557,840包，较上周增加了4,592包，这是昨日披露的数据。

报告称，鉴于本地华商已下达大量外国谷物订单，预计上海大米市场在不久的将来会更加稳定。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

MAY 25 1939

Rice Market

Business in white rice was slight
and dull yesterday and the price
dropped by $0.20 below the previous
day's closing rate. White rice
brought here yesterday from the in-
terior totaled eight junkloads and
4,000 bags brought by steamer and
rail.

Owing to a large amount of rice
in stock, local operators were not
interested in buying further cargoes,
and outport dealers were not in
the market, which made the market
weak. Little trading was done
throughout the day's session.

With the weather becoming
warm, rice holders offered their
stocks for liquidation, but no
dealers were interested.

The opening price of provincial
rice was irregularly lower in yes-
terday's morning market, the first-
grade provincial rice being quoted
at $14.80, or $0.30 below the last
closing price. Although a large
shipment of provincial rice was
brought here yesterday from Wuhu
and the interior, no brisk demand
was reported in the market.

A total of 2,000 bags of Wuhu and
Nanking provincial rice was sold in
yesterday's market.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1939年5月25日

大米市场

昨日白米交易清淡且低迷，价格较前一日收盘价下跌0.20美元。昨日从内地运抵此地的白米共计八船，另有4,000包由轮船和铁路运来。

由于库存大米量大，本地经营者无意购买更多货物，而外埠商人也未入市，导致市场疲软。全天交易寥寥无几。

随着天气变暖，大米持有者提出抛售库存，但无商人感兴趣。

昨日早市外省大米开盘价参差不齐地走低，一等外省大米报价为14.80美元，较最后收盘价低0.30美元。尽管昨日有大量外省大米从芜湖及内地运抵此地，但据报道市场需求并不旺盛。

昨日市场共售出2,000包芜湖和南京产的外省大米。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

MAY 25 1939

Flour And Wheat

The flour market was very dull yesterday, with the dealers offering no flour for stock. Outport dealers awaited improvement and local traders bought a small amount at $0.05 below Tuesday's rate.

According to a report from the market yesterday, the North China dealers have large stocks in godown and would not buy any more flour for the time being. The South Sea traders were not in the market.

With demand falling off, the mills offered a reduced price on No. 5 low-grade flour to outport buyers, the North China operators absorbing 3,000 bags at $3.50.

Local buyers bought 2,000 bags of No. 2 flour at $0.05 below the morning's opening rate.

Mills refused to pay high prices for newly-harvested native wheat. Consequently, the business yesterday was very slight. With a large shipment of foreign wheat recently brought here from Australia, and native wheat continuing to come from the interior, the price remained very weak.

A large shipment of newly-harvested native wheat was transported by the holders directly to the Japanese mills at a good price.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1939年5月25日

面粉与小麦

昨日面粉市场非常冷清，经销商未提供面粉入库。外埠经销商等待行情好转，本地贸易商以低于周二价格0.05美元的价格少量买入。

据昨日市场报告，华北经销商在仓库中拥有大量库存，暂时不会购买更多面粉。南洋商人未出现在市场上。

随着需求下降，磨坊向外埠买家降低5号低档面粉的价格，华北经营者以3.50美元的价格吸纳了3,000包。

本地买家以低于早盘开盘价0.05美元的价格购买了2,000包2号面粉。

磨坊拒绝为新收获的国产小麦支付高价。因此，昨日交易量非常少。由于最近从澳大利亚运抵此地的大量外国小麦，以及国产小麦继续从内地运来，价格依然非常疲软。

大量新收获的国产小麦被持有者以良好的价格直接运往日本磨坊。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 21 1939

Rice Market

Although the white rice brought
here yesterday totalled only five
junkloads and about 3,500 bags from
the interior by steamer and
rail, the opening price in yesterday's
market dropped by $0.30 below the
previous day's rate.

With the price of white rice
rising to $18 in unofficial quotations,
the Committees of Rice and Bean
Guild held a meeting yesterday to
discuss price stabilization.

With an oversupply of cargo in
market, local dealers bought con-
siderable amount from the holders
at $17.50 per picul of first-grade
rice.

Large amounts of provincial rice
will be brought here from the delta
ports and Wuhu early next week.
Local traders absorbed 3,000 bags
of Wuhu rice at from $14 to $15.
No transaction was reported yester-
day for outport dealers. The lowest
grade provincial rice was quoted at
$13.80.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1939年5月21日

大米市场

虽然昨日运抵此地的白米总量仅为五船，以及约3,500包由轮船和铁路从内地运来，但昨日市场的开盘价较前一日价格下跌了0.30美元。

随着白米在非官方报价中涨至18美元，米豆公会委员会昨日召开会议讨论稳定价格事宜。

由于市场货物供过于求，本地经销商以每担17.50美元的价格从持有者手中购买了一等米的大量货物。

下周初，将有大量外省大米从三角洲港口和芜湖运抵此地。本地贸易商以14至15美元的价格吸纳了3,000包芜湖大米。昨日未见外埠经销商的交易报告。最低等级的外省大米报价为13.80美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 19 1939
Rice Market
With a small amount of white
rice brought here yesterday, the
opening price was irregularly
higher in market, rising by $0.50 per
picul over the previous day's rate.
The unofficial quotation was set at
$17.50 for first-grade quality, but no
business was done throughout the
day's session, even the second-class
grade being quoted above the
maximum price, at $15.50. Accord-
ing to a report from the rice com-
mittees, the rice price will continue
to rise in the next few days.
The opening price of provincial
rice went up at yesterday's market,
with a limited amount bought from
Wuhu and the interior. The price
was $0.40 above the last closing
rate. Owing to smaller supply, the
holders would not sell their cargoes
at a cheaper price: as the result,
6,000 bags of provincial rice were
purchased at $15 by local traders.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年5月19日
大米市场
由于昨日运抵此地的白米数量较少，市场开盘价参差不齐地上涨，较前一日价格每担上涨0.50美元。一等品质的非官方报价定为17.50美元，但全天交易期间未达成任何业务，甚至二等品也以15.50美元的价格报价，高于最高限价。据米业委员会报告，未来几天米价将继续上涨。
昨日市场外省大米开盘价上涨，从芜湖和内地购买的数量有限。价格较最后收盘价高出0.40美元。由于供应减少，持有者不愿以更低的价格出售货物：结果，本地贸易商以15美元的价格购买了6,000包外省大米。

page_data.en:
01390
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 19 1939

Flour And Wheat
After few days of restless
dealing, the flour market became
active yesterday, with the price re-
maining dull and firm. Shantung
operators offered some flour for
transportation. Mills were not at-
tracted by the opening price and no
business was done.
The South Sea customers con-
tinued fractional buying for stocks
at a reasonable price. Local and
the interior traders dominated
quotations yesterday and bought a
large amount of second-grade pro-
duct at $4.55.
The native wheat market yester-
day morning was very steady and
firm, as no operators were interest-
ed in trading. Owing to oversupply
of foreign wheat in stock, the mills
took no action. Most of the recently
brought native wheat remained in
godowns. Japanese merchants
stopped buying for the North China
market.
page_data.zh:
01390
《大美晚报》
1939年5月19日

面粉与小麦
经过几天的动荡交易后，昨日面粉市场变得活跃，价格保持沉闷且坚挺。山东经营者提供了一些面粉用于运输。磨坊对开盘价不感兴趣，未达成任何业务。
南洋客户继续以合理的价格零星买入库存。昨日本地和内地贸易商主导了报价，并以4.55美元的价格购买了大量二等产品。
昨日早晨国产小麦市场非常平稳且坚挺，因为没有经营者有兴趣进行交易。由于库存中外国小麦供过于求，磨坊未采取行动。最近运抵的国产小麦大多留在仓库中。日本商人停止为华北市场采购。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
MAY 1 5 1939
08070
Decrease in City's
Rice Supplies
Rice Price Fixing Board
Ask for Foreign Supply;
Prices Rising
The authorities of the foreign
Settlements in Shanghai have been
petitioned by the Rice Price Fixing
Committee to purchase foreign rice
in order to meet the demand in
Shanghai, which has been lessened
as a result of the smaller supply
coming from the interior. The price
of rice continues to soar, causing
anxiety among the Chinese, it being
quoted at between $16.50 and $17
for a picul, showing almost three
dollars' increase as compared with
the officially limited price of $14 for
a picul of the first grade rice which
is already hard to buy in the market.
The question has become so serious
that the committee has deemed it
necessary to petition the authorities
for help so that foreign rice may be
bought in order to increase the ready
stock and also to offset the high price
of the native rice. Informed quar-
ters believe that when the foreign
rice is transported to Shanghai its
price will also be quoted at about
$16 but that if it is exempted from
the import tax it will well serve
the purpose of saving the local
situation.
Exportation Control
The written petitions have been
sent already to the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council and Municipal Council
of the French Concession. Official
reactions towards the question may
be seen to-day and it is even ex-
pected by the Chinese press that the
former Council may discuss the
question at its regular meeting on
Tuesday. This is not the first time
that the authorities have been re-
quested to buy foreign rice. During
the hostilities in Shanghai there was
an acute rice shortage resulting in
many rice riots in front of rice shops
many of which had to be closed
because they had no rice to sell.
Through the efforts made by the
Shanghai Municipal Council Saigon
rice was bought and sent here.
Sometime ago, there was confusion
in the rice market here as the
market had to be closed earlier
because of the increase of price
surpassing the official limit. Execu-
tives of the Rice Merchants Asso-
ciation met and saved the situation
by warning retailers against secretly
increasing their prices and by doing
their best to transport more rice to
Shanghai. The supply was apparent-
ly on the decline, however, and the
executives were forced to fix the
price higher than the official limit.
The reported embargo on rice ex-
portation in Wuhu and the effective
control of rice transportation in
Soochow and Wusih have recently
aggravated the situation and the
merchants have eventually been
forced to petition the authorities for
buying foreign rice.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年5月15日
08070
城市大米供应减少
米价平抑委员会
请求进口外国供应；
价格上涨
上海公共租界当局已收到米价平抑委员会的请愿，要求购买外国大米以满足上海的需求，由于来自内地的供应减少，上海的需求未能得到满足。米价持续飙升，引起华人焦虑，其报价在每担16.50至17美元之间，与官方限定的一等米每担14美元的价格相比，几乎上涨了三美元，而该限定价格在市场上已难以买到。
事态已变得如此严重，以至于委员会认为有必要向当局求助，以便购买外国大米，增加现货库存，并抵消国产大米的高价。知情人士认为，当外国大米运抵上海时，其报价也将约为16美元，但如果免除进口税，将很好地起到挽救本地局势的作用。
出口管制
书面请愿书已发送至上海工部局和法公董局。官方对此事的反应可能在今日显现，中文媒体甚至预期前者工部局可能在周二的例行会议上讨论此事。这并非当局首次被要求购买外国大米。在上海战事期间，曾出现严重的大米短缺，导致米店前发生多次米骚乱，许多米店因无米可卖而被迫关闭。
通过上海工部局的努力，购买了西贡大米并运抵此地。不久前，这里的大米市场出现混乱，由于价格上涨超过官方限额，市场不得不提前关闭。米业同业公会 executives 开会，通过警告零售商不得秘密涨价，并尽力向上海运送更多大米，从而挽救了局势。然而，供应显然在下降，executives 被迫将价格定得高于官方限额。
据报道，芜湖的大米出口禁令以及苏州和无锡对大米运输的有效控制，最近加剧了局势，商人们最终被迫向当局请愿购买外国大米。

page_data.en:
08086
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 1 5 1939
Dealers To Ask
Importation Of
Foreign Rice
Authorities in the foreign-
administered areas will be requested
to import rice from foreign
markets, it was decided Monday
afternoon at a meeting of the Rice
and Grain Association.
If the local authorities agree to
bring in foreign rice, it is believed,
the price of the grain here would
be immediately forced down to its
previous level.
The price as agreed upon by city
officials and rice dealers was $14
per picul for first-grade, but the
unscrupulous practices of certain
dealers and restrictions imposed
upon exporters of the grain in the
Japanese-occupied areas have
allegedly forced the cost of rice to
$15 per picul.
It was also decided at Monday's
meeting that a special investiga-
tion would be instituted by the as-
sociation to determine the parties
guilty of the unscrupulous practices.
The Price Fixing Committee of
the association is continuing its
work of determining the exact
stocks of rice in Shanghai, it was
learned.
page_data.zh:
08086
《大美晚报》
1939年5月15日
经销商将请求
进口
外国大米
周一午后，在米粮业同业公会的一次会议上决定，将请求外国管理区域的当局从国外市场进口大米。
据信，如果地方当局同意引进外国大米，这里的粮价将立即被迫降至之前的水平。
市政府官员和米商商定的价格为每担14美元（一等），但据称某些经销商的不道德行为以及对日占区谷物出口商施加的限制，迫使大米成本涨至每担15美元。
周一的会议还决定，由公会发起一项特别调查，以确定犯有不道德行为的当事方。
据悉，该公会的米价平抑委员会正在继续确定上海大米的确切库存工作。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 9 1939

Rice Market
Yesterday's arrivals here from the outports were very low, totalling only 1,500 bags. The price of first-grade rice barely reached $15 per picul in yesterday's business session. The dealers did not raise their price higher than the maximum price set in a general order issued by the Bean and Rice Guild last Saturday.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1939年5月9日

大米市场
昨日从外埠运抵此地的货物非常少，总计仅1,500包。在昨日的交易时段中，一等大米的价格勉强达到每担15美元。经销商未将价格提高至超过米豆公会上周六发布的一般命令中设定的最高限价。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
MAY 3 1939
Price Of Rice
Still Hangs At
$15 Per Picul
Efforts Of Dealers To
Lower Cost Making
Little Headway
MANIPULATION OF
MARKET FEARED
Reports Made To Local
Authorities By
Merchants
The desperate attempt of local
dealers to check the advancing
cost of rice over the weekend
ended in virtual failure as the
price of the grain yesterday con-
tinued to hover around $15 per
picul, $1 above the official fixed
cost.
Hope was expressed on Saturday
morning when the rice market was
reopened that a downward trend
might be possible, according to well
informed circles, but the situation
assumed a more serious aspect as
the price again hit the level which
was reached on the previous day.
At a meeting held on Friday
afternoon, a few dealers proposed
that special cheap sales of the grain
be held at shops in the poorer
sections of the town, but the plan
was finally defeated in view of the
fact that the grain which might be
designated for such sales was far
too insufficient to bring material
relief to the present exigency.
800,000 Bags Here
Meanwhile, it became known that
although the amount of the grain
being brought in to the Settlement
and Concession from Japanese-
controlled areas had greatly de-
creased in recent weeks, the rice
stock here still totalled over 800,000
bags.
Informed circles were of the
opinion that the rising cost of rice
was due largely to the unscrupulous
manipulation of certain dealers in
the city, in view of the fact that
the grain's supply here was yet far
more than sufficient for local con-
sumption for at least ten weeks to
come.
Following the general meeting on
Friday, representatives of the con-
vening dealers submitted identical
reports to S.M.C., F.M.C. and the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce re-
garding the rice situation in the
city.
Imports Diminishing
Explaining that the importation
of rice from the Japanese-occupied
areas had greatly diminished, the
reports stated that many towns near
Shanghai are now dependent upon
this city for their supply of rice.
The report concluded by request-
ing that "appropriate action be
taken to ameliorate the present
serious situation."
Another decision was reached at
Friday's meeting that special de-
legations be sent to call on officials
of the foreign controlled areas in
order to make a full explanation to
the authorities.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年5月3日
米价
仍维持在
每担15元
米商试图
降低成本的举措
进展甚微
担忧市场
被操纵
商人向地方
当局提交报告

上周末，本地米商为遏制不断上涨的米价所做的绝望尝试几乎以失败告终，昨日米价继续徘徊在每担15元左右，比官方固定价格高出1元。

据消息灵通人士称，周六上午米市重开时，人们曾希望米价可能出现下跌趋势，但随着米价再次达到前一天的水平，局势显得更为严峻。

在周五下午举行的一次会议上，少数米商提议在市内贫困地区的店铺进行特价大米销售，但鉴于指定用于此类销售的大米数量远远不足以对当前的紧急状况提供实质性的缓解，该计划最终未能通过。

本地存米80万包

与此同时，据悉尽管最近几周从日军控制区运入租界和法租界的粮食数量大幅减少，但本地的稻米库存总量仍超过80万包。

消息灵通人士认为，米价上涨很大程度上是由于市内某些不法商人的操纵，因为考虑到这里的粮食供应足以满足本地至少未来十周的消费需求，且绰绰有余。

在周五的大会之后，发起会议的米商代表就本市米市情况，向上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）、上海法租界公董局（F.M.C.）以及上海总商会提交了内容相同的报告。

进口量减少

报告解释说，从日军占领区进口的稻米已大幅减少，并指出上海附近的许多城镇现在依赖本市供应稻米。报告最后请求“采取适当措施以改善目前的严重局势”。

周五的会议还达成另一项决定，即派遣特别代表团拜访外国控制区的官员，以便向当局作出全面解释。

page_data.en:
05798
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 7 1939
Rice Exchange
Reopens After
New Prices Set
Guild Issues Drastic
Order Regulating
Staple Prices
After a day of acute uncertainty,
the Bean and Rice Guild yesterday
issued a general order to the dealers
setting the maximum price of the
first and second grade rice at $15
and $14 respectively.
The issuance of the order follow-
ed the reopening of the rice ex-
change, which was closed on Fri-
day morning as the result of a sen-
sational rise in prices.
In addition to the order regulat-
ing the prices, the Guild also passed
a series of draconic regulations, de-
signed to prevent speculative deal-
ing in the staple.
Among the notable "don'ts" issued
to the dealers were "black market"
trading and unloading of stocks on
the market for speculative purposes.
Intense excitement attended the
opening of the Friday session at
the rice exchange, following the fai-
lure of the control committee to
reach a decision.
With the exchange in an uproar,
it was decided to stop trading, even
at the risk of causing general un-
certainty. Fortunately, the closure
of the exchange was not followed
by the consequences some dealers
feared it might have been.
The guild's order to the dealers
threatened serious punitive action
against those failing to comply
with the new price regulations.
page_data.zh:
05798
《字林西报》
1939年5月7日
米业交易所
在新价格制定后
重新开市
同业公会发布严厉命令
规范主食价格

经过一天的极度不确定后，豆米同业公会昨日向米商发布通令，规定一等和二等米的最高价格分别为15元和14元。

此项命令的发布紧随米业交易所的重开。该交易所因周五上午价格惊人上涨而关闭。

除了规范价格的命令外，公会还通过了一系列严厉的规定，旨在防止对该主食进行投机交易。

向米商发布的 notable “禁令”中包括禁止“黑市”交易以及出于投机目的将库存投放市场。

由于管制委员会未能做出决定，周五米业交易所开盘时气氛极为紧张。

鉴于交易所内一片混乱，即使冒着引起普遍不确定性的风险，也决定停止交易。幸运的是，交易所的关闭并未引发一些米商所担心的后果。

公会对米商的命令威胁称，将对那些不遵守新价格规定的人采取严厉的惩罚行动。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 5 1939

Flour And Wheat
Flour: Mills' quotations yesterday for second grade product rose $.10, the current rate being $4.55 cash. In view of the high cost of production, the mills' sentiment was bullish which accounted for the firmness in the market, although demand was not keen.
Yesterday's total turnover amounted to roughly 50,000 bags. Spot quotations for foreign flour also were increased from $4.50 to $4.55 cash, and displayed a tendency to advance further.
Wheat: With holders still awaiting better opportunities to dispose of their stocks, market remained quiet yesterday.
No orders were reported to have been placed for American wheat which, it was learned, was being offered at US$21.50 per ton.
Incidentally, the firm sentiment displayed by the mills in regard to the disposal of flour was due, it was said, to no small extent to the fear that the cost of foreign wheat would advance further.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年5月5日

面粉与小麦

面粉：昨日面粉厂对二等产品的报价上涨0.10美元，现价为现金4.55美元。鉴于生产成本高昂，面粉厂情绪看涨，这解释了市场的坚挺，尽管需求并不旺盛。
昨日总成交量约为5万包。洋面粉的现货报价也从现金4.50美元增至4.55美元，并显示出进一步上涨的趋势。

小麦：由于持有者仍在等待更好的机会处理其库存，昨日市场保持平静。
据报道，没有下达美国小麦的订单，据悉其报价为每吨21.50美元。
顺便提一下，据说面粉厂在处理面粉方面表现出的坚定情绪，在很大程度上是由于担心外国小麦的成本会进一步上涨。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAY 5 1939

Rice Market

White Rice: Rising trend of the
market yesterday was arrested
following the strong appeal of the
guild circles to the merchants and
the strict prohibition of secret
trading.
In the morning, prices continued
to advance, but as larger traders'
buying activities slackened, a reac-
tion set in, prices losing their
earlier gains.
At closing, medium quality pro-
duct was quoted at $14.50.
Provincial Rice: As appetite of
buyers weakened, more stable con-
ditions were seen in the market
yesterday. With Nanking "special"
being quoted at the high price of
$14 and high grade Wuhu rice at
$13.80, absorbing interests were
dampened. Trading dropped from
almost 10,000 bags on Wednesday to
less than 4,000 bags yesterday.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1939年5月5日

米市

白米：继同业公会圈子强烈呼吁米商并严禁秘密交易后，昨日市场的上涨趋势得以遏制。
上午，价格继续上涨，但随着大买家的购买活动减弱，出现反弹，价格回吐了早先的涨幅。
收盘时，中等质量的产品报价为14.50美元。

外省米：由于买家胃口减弱，昨日市场状况较为稳定。随着南京“特制”米报价高达14元，高等级芜湖米报价为13.80元，吸纳兴趣受挫。交易量从周三的近1万包降至昨日的不足4000包。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 5 1939
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. M. REGISTRY 657... No. S. B. D. Date 5）
Working Classes, Poor People
Hit By Shanghai's
Soaring Cost Of Living
Steady Rise
In Price Of
Rice Recorded
Index Now Approaching
Record Marked Up In
Winter Of 1938
CLOTHING DEARER,
FUEL COSTS LESS
Effect Of Bean Oil
Shortage Seen In
Latest Figures
With a change for the worse in industrial conditions last month, when Shanghai workers averaged a further decrease in wages, the city's poorer classes again had to face a further increase in the cost of living, figures released by the Shanghai Municipal Council revealed yesterday.
Most hard hit were those classes whose daily menu consists of little more than a humble bowl of rice, for which they were compelled to a higher price last month than even the preceding month, when an alarming increase in price was registered.
The effect of a marked shortage in bean oil, and higher costs of transportation was responsible for a rise in the price of another commodity necessary to the poorer classes, and while fuel cost slightly less in April than it did in March, there was an increase in the cost of clothing registered.
Index Figures Given
The general index of the cost of living for Shanghai workers last month set at 164.13 is only 1.68 points short of the position of January, 1938 (165.81), the peak index during the past 21 months since hostilities started. The present rise-phase in the general index began from December, 1938, the figures show, and has extended uninterrupted over a period of five months.
The increase for April is 0.64 per cent., 3.60 per cent., and 49.88 per cent. when compared with the preceding month, the same month last year, and the pre-war month, July, 1937, respectively on 1926 base. However, by taking the general index of the pre-war month, which is 109.51 as the base for comparison (both the general index for July, 1937, and its reciprocal will then be represented by 100,) the index for April, 1939, which is 164.13, will then be represented by 149.88, the reciprocal of which is 66.72. Therefore the purchasing power of a July, 1937, dollar, is worth $0.6672 in April, 1939.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年5月5日
（印：上海公共租界警务处 S. M. 登记处 657... 编号 S. B. D. 日期 5）
工人阶级、贫民
遭受上海生活成本
飙升的打击
记录到
米价稳步
上涨
指数正接近
1938年冬季创下的
纪录
衣物更贵，
燃料成本降低
最新数据显现
豆油短缺的影响

上海市政委员会昨日公布的数据显示，上个月工业状况恶化，上海工人的平均工资进一步下降，城市贫困阶层不得不面对生活成本的进一步增加。

受影响最严重的是那些日常饮食仅为一碗微薄米饭的阶层，他们上个月被迫支付比前个月更高的价格，而前个月的价格已经出现了令人担忧的上涨。

豆油明显短缺以及运输成本上升，导致另一种贫困阶层必需商品的价格上涨；虽然4月份的燃料成本略低于3月份，但衣物成本有所增加。

公布指数数据

上月上海工人生活费用总指数定为164.13，仅比1938年1月（165.81）的水平低1.68点，后者是自敌对行动开始以来过去21个月中的峰值指数。数据显示，总指数的当前上升阶段始于1938年12月，并已连续持续了五个月。

以1926年为基数，4月份的增幅与前一个月、去年同月以及战前月份1937年7月相比，分别为0.64%、3.60%和49.88%。然而，若以战前月份的总指数109.51作为比较基准（此时1937年7月的总指数及其倒数均表示为100），则1939年4月的指数164.13将表示为149.88，其倒数为66.72。因此，1937年7月的一美元的购买力，在1939年4月值0.6672美元。

page_data.en:
05 10

Rice And Oil Up
In the food group indices the most conspicuous rise in price during March was that of rice; for April, soy bean oil. The average retail price of soy bean oil per chin for March was $0.251, and for April. $0.359. The increase was 43.03 per cent. The peak price was, however, as high as $0.480 per chin.
It is reported that prohibition to export soy bean oil from Dairen coupled with manipulation has caused the price to soar and that the price is believed to be the highest during the past 60 years.
When the average retail prices of the month are compared with those of the preceding one, fluctuation is extremely great in a number of commodities, e.g., in the food group, sweet potato was increased by 43.08 per cent., lard 12.85 per cent., fresh pork 10.81 per cent., white sugar 9.60 per cent., turnips 7.41 per cent., soy bean sauce 5.04 per cent.
The increase in the price of pork was due to a further levy of $1.00 per head in the occupied areas. For the different varieties of rice, the increase was from 2.90 to 3.54 per cent.

Clothing Dearer
Demand for clothing materials was active during the month as a result of the ever-growing population. Most items in the clothing group showed a rise, save three. Native sheetings rose 12.15 per cent, fancy twills 10.00 per cent, cotton socks 8.50 per cent., grey shirtings 4.23 per cent., jeans and drills 4.17 per cent., white shirtings 3.73 per cent. Cotton flannel shows a drop of 16.41 per cent., as it is out of season.
The average retail prices of the various items in the fuel and light group showed a general fall during the month. Fire-wood showed a drop of 5.40 per cent., charcoal 4.15 per cent., and coal briquettes 1.93 per cent.
page_data.zh:
05 10

米价与油价上涨

在食品组指数中，3月份价格上涨最显著的是大米；4月份则是豆油。3月份豆油的平均零售价格为每斤0.251美元，4月份为0.359美元。涨幅为43.03%。然而，最高价格曾高达每斤0.480美元。
据报道，禁止从大连出口豆油加上人为操纵，导致价格飙升，据信这是过去60年来的最高价格。

当将该月的平均零售价格与前一个月进行比较时，许多商品的价格波动极大，例如，在食品组中，红薯上涨了43.08%，猪油上涨了12.85%，鲜猪肉上涨了10.81%，白糖上涨了9.60%，萝卜上涨了7.41%，酱油上涨了5.04%。
猪肉价格上涨是由于在占领区每头猪额外征收1.00美元的税款。不同品种的大米价格上涨幅度在2.90%至3.54%之间。

衣物更贵

由于人口不断增长，本月对服装材料的需求活跃。服装组中的大多数项目显示上涨，仅有三项除外。土布上涨12.15%，花斜纹布上涨10.00%，棉袜上涨8.50%，灰平布上涨4.23%，牛仔布和钻布上涨4.17%，白平布上涨3.73%。棉法兰绒因过季下跌16.41%。

燃料和照明组中各项商品的平均零售价格在当月普遍下跌。木柴下跌5.40%，木炭下跌4.15%，煤球下跌1.93%。

CHINA PRESS.
MAY 4 1939
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. I. D. G. 05869 No. 4. A D. From）

Local Rice
Price To Be
Maintained

A resolution to maintain the local rice market at the present maximum level of $14 per shih was reached at a meeting held by the Price-Adjusting Committee in the beginning of this week.

This decision, it was said, was arrived at in view of the fact that although recent arrivals as well as stocks of rice in Shanghai have shown a small decline, there is still sufficient quantity on hand to allay any fear of a shortage. It was, therefore, decided to advise all provision dealers to keep the prices from exceeding the maximum level and at the same time to spare no efforts to accelerate the shipment of fresh supplies from the producing centers.

The present local stocks, according to an investigation made by the committee, amount to a total of 611,153 bags, showing a decline of 41,303 bags compared with the last reported figure. Of this amount the largest quantities are held in the Bank of China and the National Commercial Bank godowns totalling 121,120 and 97,169 bags respectively.

本地米价
将维持
现状

本周初，平价委员会在一次会议上通过了一项决议，将本地米市维持在目前每石14元的最高水平。

据说，做出这一决定是鉴于以下事实：尽管近期抵达上海的米量以及上海的米库存略有下降，但手头仍有足够的数量以消除任何短缺的担忧。因此，决定建议所有粮商保持价格不超过最高水平，同时不遗余力地加快从产地发运新鲜供应品。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

APR 15 1939

Local Pig Market
Established

Livestock Must Be Landed
In Hongkew; Dealers and
Ships to Register

The recent difficult situation confronting pig dealers in Shanghai who have been forced to transport their live pigs from Hsingkong, north Kiangsu, by Japanese steamers and also to pay a tax of $2 per pig was clarified yesterday when it was announced that the Shanghai Cattle Market had officially been established in Hongkew where the Japanese influence is predominant.

It was stated that in order to "fit in with the war-time situation transportation of live stock in Shanghai must be monopolized by one hong" and to that end a large piece of land covering 100 mow has been marked out for the establishment of the new market which is already in process of construction. Pending the completion of the construction, the temporary offices of the market will be located at 52 Yechow Road and in Room 127, 400 North Soochow Road.

All hongs dealing in live stock must register with the new market between April 16 and 30 and although no registration fees will be paid, it was clearly mentioned that all live stock in producing districts destined for Shanghai must be transported by steamers "all of which must be appointed by the market authorities." All live stock will be sold by the market alone. Pig dealers were urged to register in order to "avoid losses."

Steamers to Be "Appointed"

Informed quarters believe that the new Hongkew enterprise will affect many people probably including the general public if there is a change of prices as a result of the control. Formerly, it will be recalled, live pigs and other cattle were transported to Shanghai from interior districts by third party steamers and also by Japanese boats. Sometime ago, armed Japanese parties forced junks carrying pigs to sail to Japanese steamers at the place of loading, namely Hsingkong, and as a result two British steamers, the Christine Moller and Whangpu, had to return to Shanghai without pigs which were to have been shipped here by them.

It will be interesting to see how foreign shipping interests will react towards the newly-monopolized business as steamers transporting live stock must be "appointed" by the new market, but in Chinese circles strong opposition has already been voiced. More than 40 pig hongs, which are members of the Shanghai Pig Hongs Association, have publicly announced their disapproval of the arrangement. They have started a wordy war stating that they would never participate in any "illegal organization" and it will be interesting to watch whether or not their word will be followed by action. They have already threatened to stop business.

It was reliably learnt yesterday, however, that live pigs have been transported to Shanghai during the past few days uninterrupted by tax collectors, but as stated, "registration" has just begun and the situation is keenly watched by cattle dealers.

《字林西报》，

1939年4月15日

本地生猪市场
已建立

牲畜必须在虹口
上岸；商行与
船只须登记

上海猪商近期面临的困境——他们被迫通过日本轮船从江苏北部的兴公（音译，Hsingkong）运输活猪，并需为每头猪缴纳2美元税款——昨日随着上海牛市场在日方势力占主导的虹口正式宣布成立而得以澄清。

据称，为了“适应战时局势，上海的牲畜运输必须由一家商行垄断”，为此已划出一块面积达100亩的土地用于建立新市场，目前建设工作正在进行中。在建设完成之前，市场的临时办事处将设在耶周路（音译，Yechow Road）52号以及北苏州路400号127室。

所有经营牲畜的商行必须在4月16日至30日期间向新市场注册，虽然无需缴纳注册费，但明确指出，所有产自产区并运往上海的牲畜必须通过轮船运输，“且所有轮船必须由市场当局指定”。所有牲畜将仅由该市场进行销售。猪商被敦促进行注册，以“避免损失”。

船只将被“指定”

消息灵通人士认为，如果因管控导致价格变动，这家新的虹口企业将影响许多人，可能包括普通公众。回想以前，活猪和其他牲畜是由第三方轮船以及日本船只从内地地区运往上海的。不久前，武装日本人强迫载有生猪的驳船在装货地（即兴公）驶向日本轮船，结果两艘英国轮船“克里斯汀·莫勒”号（Christine Moller）和“黄埔”号（Whangpu）不得不空载返回上海，未能运出原定在此装船的生猪。

值得关注的是，外国航运利益集团将如何反应这一新近被垄断的业务，因为运输牲畜的轮船必须由新市场“指定”，但在华人圈子里，强烈的反对声音已经发出。超过40家作为上海猪行公会成员的猪行已公开宣布不赞成此项安排。他们发起了一场口水战，声称绝不会参与任何“非法组织”，值得观察的是他们的言论是否会转化为行动。他们已经威胁要停止营业。

然而，昨日可靠消息获悉，在过去几天里，活猪运抵上海的过程未受收税人员干扰，但正如所述，“注册”才刚刚开始，牲畜交易商们正密切关注局势。

（右上角印章内容：S. A. MUNICIPAL POLICE / S. B. REGISTRY / V. S. B. D. / nte...）

SHANGHAI TIMES,
APR 15 1939

Sino-Japanese Combine To
Monopolise Livestock

Shanghai Livestock Association, Capitalized
At $250,000, To Start Operating To-day;
Chinese Dealers Organize “Boycott”

From to-day, all livestock coming into Shanghai will have to pass through the hands of the Shanghai Livestock Association, a Sino-Japanese combine capitalized at $250,000, which, with the help of the Japanese naval and military authorities, will exercise a complete monopoly. "The Shanghai Times" learnt yesterday.

The combine, "The Shanghai Times" was reliably informed yesterday, is the result of some six months of hard work and negotiations by an unnamed foreigner, who—due to the Japanese restrictions—will have nothing further to do with the association, though doubtless he will receive some remuneration for his efforts.

As far as the average householder is concerned, the result of this combine will mean a drop in prices; pork, for instance, will probably drop about 10 cents a pound to start off with, and possibly another 10 cents in the near future. And similarly for all other livestock, including chickens.

Before the hostilities broke out, a pig cost anywhere from 43 to 48 cents to bring to Shanghai, "The Shanghai Times" was told yesterday. Since the outbreak of hostilities, the Customs has levied a duty of $1.50 on each pig, while "taxes" paid to guerrillas, Ta Tao officials, officials who purported to be Ta Tao officials, and others, have brought the import costs up to $11 or more. Pigs at the moment cost $15, the table cost thus being around $26.

As a result of the monopoly, the Japanese authorities have assured the Association that all taxes will now not amount to more than from $5 to $6, including Customs duty.

The association is in the hands of 36 shareholders, 20 of whom are reported to be Chinese and 16 Japanese. The $250,000 capital is made up of $125,000 subscribed by Japanese interests, a similar amount subscribed by Chinese interests. The Association has temporary offices in the Embankment Building which was well guarded yesterday by Japanese and Chinese detectives.

Chinese dealers in Shanghai, however, have held a meeting as a result which they refuse to have any dealings with the Association, on the grounds that it is a Japanese organization, with the Chinese in it merely as a "blind."

To the Association's suggestion that the real trouble is that the dealers see a large profit dwindling away, the dealers retort that once the monopoly is well established and backed by the Japanese military, there is nothing to prevent present prices being doubled on the ground of "prevailing conditions." So far, the dealers are adamant in their refusal to deal with the Association.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年4月15日

中日联合垄断
牲畜业

上海牲畜协会，资本金
25万美元，今日起开始运营；
中国商人组织“抵制”

《上海泰晤士报》昨日获悉，从今天起，所有进入上海的牲畜都必须经过上海牲畜协会之手。这是一个中日联合企业，资本金为25万美元，将在日本海陆军当局的帮助下实行完全垄断。

《上海泰晤士报》昨日从可靠渠道获悉，该联合体是一位 unnamed foreigner（无名外籍人士）经过约六个月的艰苦工作和谈判的结果，此人——由于日本的限制——将不再与该协会有任何关联，尽管毫无疑问他会因其努力获得一些报酬。

就普通住户而言，这种联合体的结果意味着价格下降；例如，猪肉起步阶段可能每磅下降约10美分，并在不久的将来可能再降10美分。同样，包括鸡在内的所有其他牲畜也是如此。

《上海泰晤士报》昨日被告知，在敌对行动爆发前，将一头猪运到上海的成本在43至48美分之间。自敌对行动爆发以来，海关对每头猪征收1.50美元的关税，而支付给游击队、大道政府官员、自称是大道政府官员的人以及其他人的“税款”，使进口成本升至11美元或更多。目前猪的价格为15美元，因此餐桌成本约为26美元。

作为垄断的结果，日本当局已向协会保证，现在包括关税在内的所有税款总额不会超过5至6美元。

该协会由36名股东掌控，据报道其中20名为中国人，16名为日本人。25万美元的资本由日方利益集团认购12.5万美元，中方利益集团认购同等金额。该协会在堤岸大厦设有临时办事处，昨日该处由日本和中国侦探严密把守。

然而，上海的华商举行了一次会议，结果拒绝与该协会进行任何交易，理由是该组织是日本机构，其中的中国人 merely as a "blind"（仅仅作为“幌子”）。

针对协会提出的真正麻烦在于商人看到巨额利润正在缩水的建议，商人们反驳说，一旦垄断确立并得到日本军方的支持，没有什么能阻止以“现行状况”为由将现有价格翻倍。到目前为止，商人们坚决拒绝与该协会打交道。

April 6, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

News Digest and other local newspapers :-

PIG DEALERS AND THE EXTRA TAX

The entire body of pig dealers are
opposing the collection of an extra tax of $2.00 per
head. Pigs are now being transported by the Chiyo Maru
of the Japanese Tairiku Products Company from Sinkiang
to Shanghai in an attempt to monopolize this trade.
Much delay in delivery has thus been caused.
It is learned that Watanabe, manager
of the Tairiku Company, has agreed to reduce the tax
to $1 per head and this has been accepted by the pig
dealers. Yesterday, when the pig dealers went to
Tientsin to take delivery of pigs, it was discovered
about 300 pigs had died. Negotiations for compensation
have been opened by the pig dealers with the Hoo Tei
Hong (通衛行) in Kompo.
While the s.s. Whangpoo of Butterfield
& Swire and the s.s. Christine of Moller Company were
entering Shanghai with a load of more than 2,000 pigs,
the Tairiku Company wanted to collect an extra tax
of $2 per head. This was strongly opposed by the pig
dealers who are refusing to take delivery of the pigs.
The trouble is still unsettled.

当怡和洋行（Butterfield & Swire）的“黄埔”号轮船（s.s. Whangpoo）和莫勒公司（Moller Company）的“克里斯汀”号轮船（s.s. Christine）载着2000多头生猪进入上海时，大陆公司要求征收每头2美元的额外税款。这遭到猪商的强烈反对，他们拒绝提取生猪。纠纷尚未解决。

CHINA PRESS.
APR 4 1939
03556
S. B. REGIST. Y
No S B. D.

Rice Stocks
Said Enough
For Shanghai

Stocks of rice in Shanghai, including those stored in godowns and rice shops, are estimated to total 650,000 bags or about 850,000 to 950,000 shih or piculs, according to information emanating from the local Chinese Rice and Cerea Appraisal Committee.

Disregarding the daily arrivals the existing stock of rice in Shanghai, it is stated, will probably be sufficient to meet local consumption till the end of May. Due to the inclement weather daily arrivals have been slow and of smaller quantities but it is expected that with the improvement in weather conditions and other factors, rice will continue to arrive from Soochow, Wusih Kashing, Wuhu and other producing and distribution centers in larger quantities.

Since the fixing of the maximum price for the best quality rice at $14 by the Appraisal Committee, the market has remained rather steady and although the sentiment prevailing among holders continue to be firm with little intention shown for quick disposal, the prices of all grades of rice are not expected to rise to any appreciable degree in the near future.

The lowering of the price in the producing districts by around $1 per picul is an additional factor making for the easier tendency in the local market, but the reported heavy buying by the Japanese in the occupied areas will doubtless act as a great deterrent.

A surcharge of $.40 per picul over the limit set by the Appraisal Committee is, however, being added by the rice shops in their retail sales, commencing April 1. This surcharge is to cover their commission and other fees. In view of the difficulties experienced by detail shops in making a profit on account of the $14 restriction, the surcharge ruling was passed by the Shanghai Rice Merchants Guild and has obtained the approval of the Appraisal Committee, it is further understood.

称上海大米
库存充足

据本地中国米谷评价委员会发出的消息，上海的大米库存，包括存储在仓库和米店中的大米，估计总数为65万袋，或约85万至95万石（或担）。
据说，撇开每日到货量不谈，上海现有的大米库存可能足以满足本地消费直至5月底。由于天气恶劣，每日到货缓慢且数量较少，但预计随着天气状况和其他因素的改善，大米将继续从苏州、无锡、嘉兴、芜湖以及其他产区和分销中心以更大量的形式抵达。
自从评价委员会将优质大米的最高价格定为14美元以来，市场一直相当稳定，虽然持有者的普遍情绪依然坚挺，几乎没有快速处置的意向，但预计近期各级大米的价格不会出现大幅上涨。
产区价格每担降低约1美元是促使本地市场趋于宽松的一个额外因素，但据报道日军在占领区的大量购买无疑将起到巨大的阻碍作用。
然而，自4月1日起，米店在零售销售中在评价委员会设定的限额之上每担加收0.40美元的附加费。此附加费旨在涵盖其佣金及其他费用。另悉，鉴于米店因14美元的限制而在获利方面遇到困难，上海米业公会通过了这项附加费规定，并已获得评价委员会的批准。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
APR 2 1939
（印：POLICE REGISTRY No. S. [...] Date [...]）

Imports Cause
Local Flour
Price Decline

Shanghai Market Feels
Effect Of Nipponese
Dumping In North

Large quantities of foreign wheat
and flour are being imported into
Shanghai because of the Japanese
control of the wheat-producing dis-
tricts, Chinese circles report.

Flour mills operating in the
International Settlement, such as
the Foh Sing and Fou Foong, have
reportedly been compelled to pur-
chase foreign wheat to meet their
requirements since the Japanese
undertook to restrict the export of
wheat from the occupied areas.

These mills have also been
unable to buy wheat from the
interior because of the embargo
imposed by the Chinese Govern-
ment. It is reported that during
the month of February a total of
250,458 quintals of foreign wheat,
worth some Ch.$2,242,687, were im-
ported into Shanghai, the greater
portion coming from America and
Australia.

In the occupied areas, Japan has
also been buying wheat chiefly for
the use of Japanese flour mills in
North and Central China. Accord-
ing to statistics, a total of 55,631
quintals worth Ch.$440,142 was ex-
ported from the occupied areas to
Japan Proper alone. From January
to February this year this export was
some 12,430 quintals, part of these
having been taken up by Japanese-
operated mills in China.

Japanese flour has recently been
dumped into the North China
market which formerly had provid-
ed the principal outlet for Chinese
flour. This, coupled with the
recent importation of considerable
quantities of foreign flour, has
compelled local flour mills to lower
the prices of their products and to
seek a market elsewhere.

（批：Loo C 3/4）
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1939年4月2日
（印：警务处登记号 S. [...] 日期 [...]）

进口导致
本地面粉
价格下跌

上海市场感受到
日本在华北
倾销的影响

据华人方面报告，由于日本人控制了小麦产区，大量外国小麦和面粉正被进口到上海。

据报道，自日本人着手限制从占领区出口小麦以来，在公共租界运营的面粉厂，如福新（Foh Sing）和阜丰（Fou Foong），已被迫购买外国小麦以满足其需求。

由于中国政府实施的禁运，这些面粉厂也无法从内地购买小麦。据报道，二月份共有250,458公担的外国小麦进口到上海，价值约华币2,242,687元，其中大部分来自美国和澳大利亚。

在占领区，日本也一直在购买小麦，主要供其在华北和华中的日本面粉厂使用。据统计，仅出口到日本本土的小麦总量就达55,631公担，价值华币440,142元。今年一月至二月，这一出口量约为12,430公担，其中部分被在华经营的日本面粉厂所吸纳。

最近，日本面粉被倾销到华北市场，而该市场此前曾是中国面粉的主要销路。加之近期大量进口外国面粉，迫使本地面粉厂降低产品价格并另寻市场。

（批注：Loo C 3/4）

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES
MAR 24 1939

NO RICE SHORTAGE
SEEN LOCALLY
Ample Supplies From
Producing Areas
Reaching Here

No anxiety is now felt for a possi-
ble shortage of rice in Shanghai
following heavy shipments of this
staple produce which have continued
to arrive from the inland areas, ac-
cording to reports yesterday.
The advent of spring, it was point-
ed out in local rice merchants cir-
cles, has brought very clear wea-
ther conditions, and this has greatly
facilitated the shipment of rice to
Shanghai.
In view of this, local holders have
shown themselves to be eager to un-
load their stocks on the market.
However, dealers have been heavily
stocked, and have shown no keen
buying interest, with the result that
prices which recently soared to
above $14, have now returned to
within the $14 level.
Meanwhile, the price stabilization
committee of the Shanghai Chinese
Rice Merchants Guild is continuing
with the plans for keeping a regular
supply of the staple produce to
meet the local normal market re-
quirements and generally attempting
to prevent price fluctuations by
keeping a check over the specula-
tive activities of members of the
guild. The Beans and Cereals
Dealers' Guild is also engaged in
similar measures which are being
enjoined upon its members to ob-
serve.
Once again, the local rice market
is reported to be steadily returning
to normal as a result of the ap-
plication of such preventive meas-
ures.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年3月24日

本地未见
大米短缺
产区充足供应
运抵此处

据昨日报道，随着这种主要农产品持续从内陆地区大量运抵，目前上海方面对可能出现的大米短缺已不再感到担忧。

本地米商圈子指出，春季的到来带来了非常晴朗的天气状况，这极大地便利了大米向上海的运输。

鉴于此，本地持货者表现出急于将库存投放市场的意愿。然而，经销商存货充足，且没有表现出强烈的购买兴趣，结果是，近期飙升至14元以上的大米价格，现已回落至14元水平以内。

与此同时，上海米业公会的价格稳定委员会继续执行计划，以保持主要农产品的定期供应，满足本地正常的市场需求，并总体上试图通过监控公会成员的投机活动来防止价格波动。豆类谷物同业公会也在采取类似措施，并要求其成员遵守。

据报道，由于实施了此类预防措施，本地大米市场再次稳步恢复正常。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAR 2 1939

Price Of Rice Here
Again Exceeds Limit
Of $14 Per Picul

Despite the setting up of the
maximum price by local dealers the
price of rice during the past few
days has again slightly exceeded
the $14 per picul limit.
Circles close to the rice trade in-
dicated that the climbing of the
price was largely due to the rising
cost in transporting the grain from
the inland cities to Shanghai.
Unscrupulous officials in the rice-
producing areas were said to have
deliberately raised the transporta-
tion permits cost for rice from the
former rate of 50 cents per picul
to $1 per picul.
This ruling consequently brought
about a decline in the amount of
rice imported to Shanghai and in-
directly boosted the price of rice
in the local market.
The Price Fixing Committee is
investigating the matter and is
hopeful that in a few days, the
price of rice may be brought back
to normal again.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1939年3月2日

本地米价
再次超过
每石14元的限额

尽管本地经销商设定了最高限价，但在过去几天里，大米价格再次略微超过了每石14元的限额。

接近大米贸易的人士表示，价格上涨主要是由于从内陆城市向上海运输粮食的成本上升所致。

据说，产米区的一些不法官员故意提高大米的运输许可证费用，从原来的每石50分提高到每石1元。

这一规定 consequently 导致进口到上海的大米数量减少，并间接推高了本地市场的大米价格。

物价核定委员会正在调查此事，并希望在大米价格在几天后能再次恢复正常。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
30
Jun 1 6 1959

RICE MARKET MAY
BE NORMAL
Formal Installation Of
Price Stabilization
Committee Here

The local rice market is expect-
ed to return to normal following
the formal installation of the price
stabilization committee of the
Shanghai Rice and Beans Mer-
chants Guild yesterday.
During the past few days, prices
have fluctuated within a wide mar-
gin, first quality rice having been
sold at $15, while prices for second
grade rice soared as high as $13.25
per picul. This abnormal situation,
members of the rice guild explain-
ed, has been due to speculation
among the rice merchants, many
of whom have hoarded their stocks
in anticipation of better prices.
It was further pointed out yes-
terday that if this situation were
to continue, it would work untold
hardships among factory workers,
ricksha pullers, and other labour
elements in the city, although the
other classes of people, who are
generally placed in better circum-
stances, will not feel the pinch so
strongly.
The committee has now been
charged with the responsibility of
fixing and regulating market prices,
which shall not be over $14 per
picul for first quality cereals.
The market condition during the
past two days, following reports of
the decision to form a committee,
has been easier. Speculators have
since been unloading their stocks
on the market, fearing that prices
would drop further. Although, a
few days ago, there were reported
to be in stock around 700,000 bags
of rice, actually less than 200,000
bags were placed on the market,
while the rest were being hoarded
by speculating merchants, it was
revealed yesterday.
The soaring prices in the local
market, meanwhile, have attracted
more rice which is now being ship-
ped into Shanghai from the Yang-
tze and inland areas. It is expect-
ed that after the committee has
set seriously to work, the rice mar-
ket will be restored to normal. An-
other task of the committee is to
devise measures for keeping up a
steady and regular supply of rice
from the interior to Shanghai.

16/3
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
30
1959年6月16日

大米市场可能
恢复正常
本地正式成立
价格稳定委员会

随着上海米豆业公会价格稳定委员会于昨日正式成立，预计本地大米市场将恢复正常。

在过去几天里，价格在很大范围内波动，一级大米售价为15元，而二级大米的价格则飙升至每石13.25元。米业公会成员解释说，这种异常情况是由于米商之间的投机行为造成的，许多米商囤积居奇，期待更好的价格。

昨日进一步指出，如果这种情况持续下去，将给工厂工人、人力车夫和城市中的其他劳工阶层带来难以言说的苦难，尽管其他处境 generally 较好的人群不会如此强烈地感受到压力。

该委员会现在被赋予确定和规范市场价格的职责，一级谷物的价格不得超过每石14元。

在成立委员会的决定传出后的过去两天里，市场状况有所缓和。投机者因担心价格会进一步下跌，此后一直将库存投放市场。昨日披露，虽然几天前据报道库存约有70万袋大米，但实际上投放市场的不足20万袋，其余均由投机商人囤积。

与此同时，本地市场价格飙升吸引了更多大米，目前正从长江流域和内陆地区运往上海。预计在该委员会认真开展工作后，大米市场将恢复正常。委员会的另一项任务是制定措施，保持从内地向上海稳定、定期供应大米。

16/3

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
MAR 16 1939

Rice Prices to Be
Stabilized
Local Association Forms
Special Committee

The Shanghai Rice and Bean
Dealers Association and its affiliated
organizations have jointly held a
meeting at which the Rice Price
Stabilization Committee has been
organized. As a result, retail shops
in Shanghai are required to maintain
the officially fixed price of $14 per
picul of the first grade rice which
was quoted at $15 last week.
The increased price has caused
confusion in the market and anxiety
among the poor for some time past
but it has now been announced that
the new committee will undertake to
fix the price at a reasonable level
and persuade merchants having
direct connections with farmers to
ship rice to Shanghai continuously.
A steadier market has been created
and manipulators are now willing to
unload their cargo from rice boats.

16/3
page_data.zh:
《华北每日新闻》，
1939年3月16日

米价将获
稳定
本地协会成立
特别委员会

上海米豆业同业公会及其附属组织联合召开会议，成立了米价稳定委员会。因此，上海的零售店被要求维持官方核定的一级大米每石14元的价格，而上周该价格为15元。

过去一段时间，价格上涨导致市场混乱和贫困人群的焦虑，但现在宣布，新委员会将致力于将价格固定在合理水平，并说服与农民有直接联系的商人持续向上海运送大米。

市场已变得更加稳定，操纵者现在愿意从米船上卸货。

16/3

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
MAR 1 5 1939
02316

Price-Fixing Body Formed
To Supervise Rice Trade

Seven Organizations Join Hands In An Attempt
To Defeat Profiteers Charged With
Causing Rising Cost Of Grain

In yet another attempt to check speculative manipulation of grain prices, a price-fixing committee was formed yesterday at a joint meeting of the Shanghai Rice and Bean Guild and six related organizations. The joint meeting was called to discuss means of putting a stop to the soaring prices of rice, which reached the $15-per-picul mark over the weekend, and of preventing further profiteering in the grain trade.

It was revealed at the meeting that certain an unnamed Chinese patriotic organization in Shanghai had served warning on the convening organizations, urging them "to censor the practice of certain traders who had been forcing the price up and shipping the grain to the enemy."

600,000 Bags Here

The present rice stock in Shanghai was estimated to total 600,000 bags, which, it was revealed, was sufficient for the city's consumption for a few months.

The proposal that the present $14-per-picul limit for rice be raised to $15 was defeated at the meeting, the majority opinion being that the raised limit will not check profiteering.

The price-fixing committee consists of 15 members. The Rice and Bean Guild and the Rice Dealers Guild will each be represented by five members. Other organizations to be represented include the Rice Transportation Guild and several guilds of rice-producing hsien near Shanghai.

Support Pledged

Meanwhile, support to the proposal of the Rice and Bean Guild and its related organizations was promised by the First District Citizens' Association at its meeting yesterday afternoon.

In a resolution adopted at the meeting the Association urged the sponsoring bodies of the proposal to seek an immediate remedy for the existing "deplorable condition."

In another resolution, instruction was given to the Association that the S.M.C. and F.M.C. be petitioned to pay special attention to the rising cost of living in the city.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年3月15日
02316

成立物价核定机构
以监管大米贸易

七个组织联手试图打击被指控导致粮价上涨的牟取暴利者

为了进一步遏制对粮食价格的投机操纵，上海米豆业公会和六个相关组织在昨日召开的联席会议上成立了一个物价核定委员会。召开此次联席会议旨在讨论制止大米价格飙升（周末达到每石15元）以及防止粮食贸易中进一步牟取暴利的方法。

会议透露，上海某未具名的中国爱国组织已向发起会议的组织发出警告，敦促他们“审查某些商人哄抬价格并将粮食运往敌方的做法”。

本地存有60万袋

据透露，上海目前的大米库存估计总计为60万袋，足以供本市消费数月。

会上否决了将目前大米每石14元的限价提高至15元的提议，多数意见认为提高限价无法遏制牟取暴利的行为。

物价核定委员会由15名成员组成。米豆业公会和大米同业公会各派五名代表。其他受代表的组织包括大米运输公会以及上海附近的几个产米县的同业公会。

承诺支持

与此同时，第一区市民协会在昨日下午的会议上承诺支持米豆业公会及其相关组织的提议。

在会议通过的一项决议中，该协会敦促该提议的发起机构立即补救现有的“悲惨状况”。

在另一项决议中，指示该协会向工部局（S.M.C.）和法公董局（F.M.C.）请愿，要求其特别注意本市生活成本的上升。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAR 13 1939

Rice Prices to Be
Discussed
Further Increase Likely ;
Permission Must be Given
By Authorities

Members of the Shanghai Rice and
Bean Dealers' Association are sche-
duled to hold an important meeting
today to discuss a proposal asking for
a further increase of the price of rice
which has already surpassed the
officially fixed peak mark of $14 for a
picul. Retail rice shops are selling the
first grade rice at $15 for a picul
causing anxiety among the majority of
people here despite the association's
request for maintaining the price at
$14.
In order to have the increased price
officially fixed by their association it
has been urged that a meeting
should be held. Informed quarters
believed that even should the associa-
tion decide in favour of the retailers,
permission must be obtained from
authorities of both foreign settlements
here who were reported to be paying
close attention to the matter. It was
alleged by Chinese press circles that
evidently "manipulators" were behind
the business and that the authorities
were investigating.

Confusion in Market

There has been confusion in the
rice market during the past few days
and last Saturday even the price of
$15 for one picul was surpassed and
the market had to be closed before
noon. This was done despite the as-
sociation's order forbidding a further
increase of price beyond the $14
mark.
A few days before the confusion,
rice merchants, who buy grain from
farmers directly, stopped shipping
rice to Shanghai because of their in-
ability to make money in the busi-
ness as the price quoted in the inter-
ior went up to such a level that it
almost became equal to that quoted
in Shanghai plus the transportation
expenses. The association persuaded
them to continue shipping rice to
Shanghai and they soon resumed
business. But the price in Shanghai
suddenly went up last Friday.
It would appear that since there
is no profit to make if the association's
price limit is maintained some rice
merchants are asking that the peak
price be further increased. Previous
reports were to the effect that the
price went up in the interior because
Japanese and "puppet" officials were
buying the grain in large quantities
and if the report is true there will
be difficulties in finding a remedy
locally.
page_data.zh:
《华北每日新闻》。

1939年3月13日

将讨论
米价
可能进一步上涨；
必须获得
当局许可

上海米豆业同业公会成员计划于今日举行重要会议，讨论一项进一步提髙大米价格的提议，该价格已超过官方核定的每石14元的峰值。尽管公会要求维持14元的价格，但零售米店以每石15元的价格出售一级大米，在此地大多数人中引起了焦虑。

为了使其协会正式核定上涨后的价格，有人敦促召开会议。知情人士认为，即使协会决定支持零售商，也必须获得此地两个外国租界当局的许可，据报道当局正密切关注此事。中文报界圈子声称，显然有“操纵者”在背后运作，当局正在进行调查。

市场混乱

过去几天大米市场出现混乱，上周六甚至超过了每石15元的价格，市场不得不在中午前关闭。尽管公会下令禁止价格进一步超过14元，但仍采取了这一措施。

在混乱发生前几天，直接从农民手中购买粮食的米商停止向上海运送大米，因为他们无法从中获利，因为内地的报价上涨到几乎等于上海报价加上运输费用的水平。公会劝说他们继续向上海运送大米，他们很快恢复了业务。但上周五上海的价格突然上涨。

看来，由于维持公会的限价无利可图，一些米商要求进一步提高峰值价格。此前的报道指出，内地价格上涨是因为日本人和“伪”官员大量购买粮食，如果报道属实，本地将难以找到补救办法。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAR 1 3 1939

Price Of Rice
In Shanghai
Hits New High

City. However, Believed
Facing No Shortage
Of Cereal

Although the price of rice mounted to the $15-per-picul mark during the week-end, Shanghai grain merchants expected no immediate danger of a rice shortage in this city, Chinese reports said yesterday. Far from being an indication of a possible shortage, circles close to the grain trade were of the opinion that the mounting price was the direct result of manipulations by unscrupulous dealers in the city. The present rice stock here was estimated to be well over 700,000 bags.

Officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council were said to have reinforced their inspection force which is entrusted with the duties of eliminating unscrupulous practices in the grain trade.

Meanwhile, as the market price soared beyond the approved limit of $14 per picul, grain merchants in the city were reported to have petitioned the Bean and Rice Guild to endorse a $15-per-picul measure. Action on this petition was reported to have been promised by Guild officials at their meeting this afternoon.

Another proposal advanced by grain dealers supported the importation of Siam and Burma rice to Shanghai. It was believed that with an increased supply of rice, the price would be brought back below to the $14-per-picul level.

Both Municipal and Guild officials, however, were said to have frowned upon the idea of bringing foreign rice into the city in view of the fact that it would cost well above $15 a picul for the imported grain. Poor 1938 harvests in those localities, it was explained, are responsible for the high cost.

The present rice stock in Shanghai is sufficient for the city's consumption for three months, the report asserted.

File
E 13/3
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年3月13日

上海米价
创历史新高

本市。然而，据信
谷物并无短缺之虞

据昨日中文报道，尽管上周末米价涨至每石15美元的水平，但上海粮商预计本市近期不会出现米荒。与认为这可能预示短缺的观点相反，接近粮食贸易圈的人士认为，价格上涨是市内无良商人操纵的直接结果。据估计，目前本市的存米量远超70万袋。

据悉，上海公共租界工部局官员已加强其检查队伍，该队伍负责消除粮食贸易中的无良行为。

与此同时，由于市场价格飙升，超过了每石14美元的核定限额，据报道，本市粮商已向豆米业同业公会请愿，要求认可每石15美元的措施。据报道，公会在今天下午的会议上承诺将对这一请愿采取行动。

粮商提出的另一项建议支持从暹罗和缅甸进口大米到上海。人们相信，随着大米供应量的增加，价格将回落至每石14美元以下的水平。

然而，据说工部局和公会官员均对将外国大米引入本市的主张持反对态度，理由是进口谷物的成本将远高于每石15美元。解释称，这些地区1938年的收成不佳是导致高成本的原因。

报道断言，上海目前的存米量足以维持本市三个月的消费。

March 9, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News (Editorial):

THE RICE SITUATION IN SHANGHAI

It is known to all that directly the sharp increase in the price of rice will affect the livelihood of the people while indirectly it will reflect upon the peace and order of the community. Since the outbreak of hostilities, many persons have been able to make handsome fortunes through their unscrupulous activities in hoarding commodities, but in the case of rice supplies, the situation was different, because shortly after the outbreak of hostilities, the authorities adopted certain restrictions and established the Rice Provisions Control Committee. In addition, the price of rice was fixed at $14 per picul as the maximum, while on the other hand efforts were made to secure rice supplies from other sources. It was due to all these strenuous efforts on the part of the authorities concerned that the supply of rice to the people was effectively maintained and peace and order was efficiently preserved despite the fact that Shanghai was at that time in the war area.

Some time last year a sharp increase in the price of rice was witnessed due to the activities of certain unscrupulous and traitorous merchants for the furtherance of their monetary ends. Now, taking advantage of a decrease in the imports of rice, these unscrupulous persons are making use of the pretext of the Japanese and puppet control of rice supplies to raise the price of the rice. In reality, this is absolutely contrary to the actual facts.

It should be remembered that the prices of all agricultural products, not only rice, in the interior, are regulated by the market prices in Shanghai. Owing to the sudden increase in the price of rice in Shanghai, the dealers in the interior likewise raised the price of their stocks, thereby resulting in an increase in the cost price of the rice, which the rice dealers in Shanghai have to face when making purchases from the interior. This is the natural cause of the prevalence of rumours that the Japanese and the puppet authorities are making direct rice purchases in the interior and are adopting a monopoly over rice. Moreover, though the puppet authorities may have imposed many kinds of taxes over the transportation of rice, they would not be so foolish as to prevent the exportation of rice from the interior as their principal aim is to collect more revenue. Furthermore, according to latest information secured by this paper, there is absolutely no difference in the system of transportation of rice from the guerrilla zones from that of last year. It therefore shows that there is no truth in the rumour that a monopoly is in force in the interior.

Thanks to the efforts of the Rice and Bean Trade Association for the limitation of the price of rice and those of the Rice Provisions Control Committee in advising the dealers to continue purchases from the interior, the rice situation has eased somewhat.

We now offer the following suggestions for preventing an increase in price of rice by unscrupulous rice merchants:-

1939年3月9日。
下午译文。

《中美日报》（社论）：

上海米情

众所周知，米价急剧上涨将直接影响民生，间接影响社会安宁秩序。自战事爆发以来，许多人通过囤积居奇的无良活动发了大财，但在大米供应方面，情况有所不同，因为战事爆发后不久，当局采取了一些限制措施并成立了米粮管理委员会。此外，米价被限定为每石最高14美元，同时努力从其他来源获取大米供应。正是由于有关当局的这些艰苦努力，尽管当时上海处于战区，但仍有效维持了对民众的大米供应，并高效地保持了和平与秩序。

去年某段时间，由于某些无良奸商为谋取金钱利益而进行的活动，米价曾急剧上涨。现在，这些人利用大米进口减少的机会，借口日本人和伪政权控制大米供应来抬高米价。实际上，这完全违背事实。

应当记住，内地所有农产品（不仅是大米）的价格都受上海市场价格的调节。由于上海米价突然上涨，内地商贩也提高了库存价格，从而导致上海米商从内地采购时面临的成本价格上升。这就是谣言盛行的自然原因，即日本人和伪政权在内地直接采购大米并实行垄断。此外，虽然伪政权可能对大米运输征收了多种税款，但他们不会愚蠢到阻止大米从内地出口，因为他们的主要目的是收取更多税收。此外，根据本报获得的最新消息，从游击区运输大米的制度与去年完全相同。因此，这表明内地实行垄断的谣言毫无根据。

得益于豆米业同业公会限制米价的努力，以及米粮管理委员会建议商贩继续从内地采购，米情已有所缓和。

我们现在提出以下建议，以防止无良米商抬高米价：-

page_data.en:
1) In the interests of peace and order, the Rice
Provisions Control Committee should do the same as it
has done before, i.e. maintain the fixed price of
rice, and enforce adjustment of rice supplies in
case of necessity.
2) According to reports appearing in newspapers, there
are at present between 600,000 to 700,000 bags of rice
in stock in Shanghai, sufficient to meet local
requirements for three months. As these bags of rice
were mostly purchased before at normal prices, the
Rice Provisions Control Committee should order the
owners to sell their stocks below the maximum price.
3) Should the owners of these stocks refuse to dispose of
them below this price under the pretext that the stocks
are being used as a mortgage to banks, the Committee
should adopt emergency measures, such as providing
funds to redeem these stocks from the banks on behalf
of the owners and thereafter enforcing a uniform price.
If the above measures fail to produce
effective results, then the method adopted last year should
be enforced, i.e. the authorities of the two Foreign
Settlements should be asked to purchase rice from abroad
for the adjustment of the rice supplies in Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
1) 为了和平与秩序，米粮管理委员会应像以前一样行事，即维持大米固定价格，并在必要时强制调整大米供应。
2) 根据报纸报道，上海目前存有60万至70万袋大米，足以满足本地三个月的需求。由于这些大米大多是在之前以正常价格购买的，米粮管理委员会应命令业主以低于最高限价的价格出售其库存。
3) 如果这些库存的所有者以库存作为银行抵押为借口，拒绝以低于此价格处理库存，委员会应采取紧急措施，例如提供资金代表业主从银行赎回这些库存，随后强制执行统一价格。
如果上述措施未能产生有效结果，则应执行去年采用的方法，即要求两个外国租界的当局从国外购买大米，以调整上海的大米供应。

March 9, 1939.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
S. M. REGISTRY
Morning Transl. No S. B. D.
Date....................

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE RICE QUESTION IN SHANGHAI

The public are paying close attention to the rapid increase in the price of rice in Shanghai.
At 11.30 a.m. yesterday, the Rice Market Control Committee held a meeting, at which some 20 rice merchants from various places were present. Wu Zien-keng (付前耕), Chairman of the Committee, after reporting the particulars relating to the increase in the price of rice during the past few days, persuaded the merchants to sell rice at a fair price out of consideration for the general situation. He entertained the hope that the rice merchants would continue transporting rice to Shanghai to supply the local residents. The rice merchants explained that the cost of rice in the rice producing areas had increased and that there were exorbitant taxes and heavy transportation charges to pay. The meeting terminated at 1 p.m.
After the meeting, the Committee issued a notice maintaining the limit of the price of best quality rice to $14 per picul.
The Rice Shop Owners' Association, at a meeting held at 4 p.m. yesterday, passed a resolution that rice merchants be notified to observe the limited price of rice.

Letter to the Foreign Councils

On March 8, the Bean and Rice Trade Association sent the following letter to the S.M.C. and the French Municipal Council :-
"During the past few months, large quantities of rice have been transported to outports direct from the interior. As a result, the price of rice in the producing areas has risen and the price of best quality rice in Changshu, Wusih and other places has been increased to $12 and $13 per picul. Transportation taxes and other charges of more than $1 are required for the transportation of every picul of rice to Shanghai. Rice merchants, seeing that they cannot make a profit, have ceased to order rice with the result that only small quantities of rice are transported to Shanghai and the price of rice is rising. There are indications that the price of rice will exceed the limited price. The rice merchants have all been advised not to exceed the limited selling price.
"Rice will come to Shanghai in less quantities in future should the price of rice in the producing areas in the interior be subject to further increases. As the stock of rice in this locality will diminish, it is feared that there may be a shortage of rice.
"The Council is always much concerned about the food question and we hereby send this letter reporting the cause of the increase in the price of rice. As a precaution against a shortage of rice, we think that the Council should devise ways and means beforehand to cope with the situation."

1939年3月9日。

上海公共租界
S. M. 登记处
晨译件 编号 S. B. D.
日期....................

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

上海米问题

公众正密切关注上海米价的快速上涨。
昨日上午11时30分，米市场管理委员会召开会议，约有20名各地米商出席。委员会主席吴恩庚（付前耕）在报告了过去几天米价上涨的详细情况后，劝告米商出于大局考虑以公平价格售米。他希望米商能继续向上海运米以供应当地居民。米商解释说，产米区的米价成本上涨，且需支付高昂的税费和沉重的运输费用。会议于下午1时结束。
会后，委员会发布公告，维持上等米每石14美元的限价。
米店业主协会在昨日下午4时举行的会议上通过决议，通知米商遵守米价限额。

致外国理事会的信函

3月8日，豆米业同业公会向上海公共租界工部局和法国公董局发出如下信函：
“过去几个月，大量大米直接从内地运往各口岸。结果，产米区的米价上涨，常熟、无锡等地的上等米价已涨至每石12和13美元。每石大米运往上海需缴纳超过1美元的运输税和其他费用。米商见无利可图，已停止订购大米，导致运抵上海的大米数量稀少，米价上涨。有迹象表明米价将超过限价。已劝告所有米商不要超过限定售价。
“如果内地产米区的米价进一步上涨，未来运抵上海的大米数量将会减少。随着本地存米减少，恐怕会出现米荒。
“理事会一直非常关心粮食问题，特此致函报告米价上涨的原因。为预防米荒，我们认为理事会应事先设法应对这一局面。”
