Hwa Mei Chen Pao and other local newspapers :- 7 MAR. 1939
LIMIT ON THE PRICE OF RICE TO BE MAINTAINED
To discuss the rice situation, the Bean and
Rice Trade Association held a meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday.
Ying Tse-kang (□□□) presided.
It was decided that as there is in Shanghai
a stock of some 700,000 bags of rice, the limit of $14 per
picul should be maintained.
The cause of the rising price is due to direct
purchases of rice from the interior by foreigners. Local
rice merchants refuse to buy as the price in the producing
areas is higher than in Shanghai. There is some anxiety
for should the price in the interior continue to rise the
stocks in Shanghai will become short. It will be wise,
therefore, to inform the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements of this situation and to ask them to take the
necessary steps to purchase Saigon rice.
The price of rice yesterday reached the limit
of $14 per picul. Some 3,000 bags of rice are arriving
here daily and rice dealers are unwilling to sell. There
is a tendency of the price exceeding the limit. Actually
the retail price has already reached $14.50 per picul.
page_data.zh:
《华美晨报》及其他本地报纸： 1939年3月7日
维持米价限额
为讨论米情，豆米业同业公会于昨日下午3时举行会议。
应子康（□□□）主持。
会议决定，鉴于上海存有约70万袋大米，应维持每石14美元的限额。
价格上涨的原因是外国人直接从内地采购大米。本地米商因产地价格高于上海而拒绝购买。人们有些担忧，如果内地价格继续上涨，上海的库存将会短缺。因此，明智的做法是将此情况告知外国租界当局，并请他们采取必要步骤购买西贡米。
昨日米价达到每石14美元的限额。每天约有3,000袋大米运抵此处，但米商不愿出售。价格有超出限额的趋势。实际上，零售价格已达到每石14.50美元。

page_data.en:
Hwa Mei Chen Pao and other local newspapers :-

Traitorous Merchants Are The Cause Of The
High Price Of Rice

According to information secured by a reporter
from bona fide rice merchants, the increase in the price of
rice is due to underhand control of the rice market by
certain traitorous merchants who, in conspiracy with the
Japanese and puppet authorities, are making handsome
profits.

Rumours that the Japanese and puppet
organizations are attempting to control the rice market
are being spread through newspapers in order to make the
price soar, but actually rice transactions in the guerrilla
zones are going on the same as last year. Moreover,
ample supplies of rice are in stock in the Foreign
Settlements.

page_data.zh:
《华美晨报》及其他本地报纸：

奸商是米价高涨的原因

据记者从诚实米商处获得的消息，米价上涨是由于某些奸商暗中控制米市所致，他们与日本人和伪政权勾结，牟取暴利。

有关日本人和伪组织试图控制米市的谣言正通过报纸传播，以使价格飙升，但实际上游击区的大米交易与去年相同。此外，外国租界内有充足的大米库存。

page_data.en:
News Digest and other local newspapers :-
THE CONDITION OF THE RICE MARKET
Within the past few days the price of rice has risen to the limit of $14 per picul. (Actually the price of rice has been on the decline during the past two days). The Bean and Rice Trade Association will hold a meeting in a day or two to discuss the situation.
The recent increase in the price of rice is due to direct purchases from the rice producing areas by the Japanese and puppet authorities. As a consequence rice supplies are becoming smaller and the price has increased. There is in Shanghai a stock of more than 300,000 piculs of rice which can last three months. There is no reason for the price to go up at present. It is hoped that the rice dealers will give the matter consideration.
It is rumoured that at the meeting to be held rice merchants will suggest that the limit of $14 per picul be raised. The Bean and Rice Trade Association, which is responsible for regulating the people's foodstuffs, should deal with the situation wisely.
The Rice Provisions Joint Control Committee organized by the authorities of the Foreign Settlements recently held a meeting at which the opinion was expressed that as the importation of rice is still going on and stocks are ample, there should be no anxiety over supplies of rice.
page_data.zh:
《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：
米市状况
过去几天，米价已涨至每石14美元的限额。（实际上，过去两天米价一直在下跌）。豆米业同业公会将在一两天内举行会议讨论这一情况。
近期米价上涨是由于日本人和伪政权直接从产米区采购所致。结果，大米供应减少，价格上涨。上海存有超过30万石大米，可维持三个月。目前价格上涨没有理由。希望米商对此事予以考虑。
有谣言称，在即将举行的会议上，米商将建议提高每石14美元的限额。负责调节民食的豆米业同业公会应明智地处理这一局面。
由外国租界当局组织的米粮联合管制委员会最近举行了一次会议，会上表示，由于大米进口仍在进行且库存充足，无需担心大米供应。

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAR 7 1939

Rice Price Shows
Increase

Controlled Level Already
Reached: No Shortage But
Inland Purchases Cease

Hope was expressed yesterday by
the Chinese press that authorities of
foreign settlements in Shanghai
would check the increase in the
price of rice which has already
reached the limited level of $14 for
a picul of first grade rice.
Members of the Shanghai Rice and
Bean Merchants' Association were re-
ported to have met yesterday on the
question and it was hinted by one
report that the merchants might
suggest a further increase in price.
The price quoted in the rice
market was $14 but in retail shops
where the middle class people and
the poor obtain their daily quota of
rice the officially limited price was
surpassed. Many Chinese housewives
bought more rice yesterday fearing
that there might be a further in-
crease of price.
Although there is no fear of
immediate shortage of rice in Shang-
hai because there are 650,000 bags
stored in various godowns here,
merchants who directly buy rice
from farmers in the interior have
been reluctant to make purchases
and consequently there has been a
decrease in supply.
The supply of rice in the interior
has been decreased as a result of
big purchases made by the Japanese
and "puppet" officials, it was reported.
In Wusih, it was pointed out, a picul
of rice is worth $12.60 now and plus
the transportation fee the price
would go up to $14.10 after arriving
in Shanghai.
Rice merchants have therefore
been reluctant to ship rice to
Shanghai because it does not pay.
At present the daily arrival of rice
amounts to only 2,000 or sometimes
3,000 piculs. Foreign settlements
alone need 7,000 bags or about 9,000
piculs daily.
At a meeting held yesterday after-
noon, executives of the Shanghai
Rice and Bean Merchants' Association
decided not to increase further the
price of rice which has already
reached the officially limited level,
namely, $14 for a picul of first grade
rice.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年3月7日

米价显示
上涨

已达管制水平：并无短缺，但内地采购停止

上海中文报纸昨日表示希望，上海各外国租界当局能够遏制米价的上涨，目前一级大米每石的价格已达到14美元的限定水平。
据报道，上海米豆业同业公会成员昨日就此问题举行了会议，有报道暗示，商人们可能会建议进一步提价。
米市报价为14美元，但在中产阶级和穷人购买每日定额大米的零售店中，官方限定的价格已被突破。许多中国家庭主妇昨日购买了更多的大米，担心价格会进一步上涨。
虽然由于上海各地仓库储存有65万袋大米，不必担心上海会出现 immediate 的米荒，但直接从内地农民手中购买大米的商人一直不愿采购，因此供应量有所减少。
据报道，由于日本人和“伪”官员的大量采购，内地的稻米供应已经减少。指出在无锡，目前一石大米价值12.60美元，加上运输费，运抵上海后价格将涨至14.10美元。
因此，米商一直不愿将大米运往上海，因为无利可图。
目前，每日抵达的大米数量仅为2,000石，有时为3,000石。仅公共租界每日就需要7,000袋或约9,000石大米。
在昨日下午举行的一次会议上，上海米豆业同业公会的执行委员决定不再进一步提高大米价格，该价格已达到官方限定水平，即一级大米每石14美元。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
FEB 1 7 1939
01787
Local Rice Conditions Are
Reported Satisfactory
Excellent Handling Of Delicate Situation Arising
From Hostilities Results In Coverage Of Costs
And Profit For Refugee Relief In Settlement

At a recent meeting of the Rice
Joint Administrative Committee the
local rice situation was reviewed.
The stock in Shanghai was estimated
at approximately 900,000 zars, ar-
rivals during January averaging
approximately 10,000 zars per day.
The stock in the French Concession
was estimated at 96,000 bags, an in-
crease of 30,000 bags during Decem-
ber and January.
The steady inflow of rice to Shang-
hai had been only slightly affected
by purchases up-country for ship-
ment to Northern Ports and it was
felt that there was no cause for
concern as regards the general
situation.
It was reported to the Committee
that since its last meeting at the
end of November, the Council's re-
serve supply which then stood at
10,606 bags, had been completely
turned over to reduce risk of de-
terioration and sales had been made
of such quantity as showed signs
of being impaired. The balance re-
maining was 6,156 bags and on the
recommendation of the Treasurer
and Controller, in view of the satis-
factory stock position in the city as
outlined above, the Committee un-
animously approved the disposal
forthwith of this balance which is
considered to be negligible in view
of the existing margin of safety.
Results Of Purchases
An estimate of the final result of
the Council's transaction in Saigon
rice was presented to the Committee
by the Treasurer and Controller. It
was noted that 22,740 tons had been
handled, in respect to which the
final credit balance was expected to
be approximately $280,000; in addi-
tion, a further sum of $54,000 had
accrued from fees charged for facili-
ties extended to a number of im-
porters in respect to shipments ar-
ranged by them subsequent to the
Council's decision to refrain from
further purchases for its own ac-
count, such shipments being subject
in all respects to the same measures
of supervision and control.
As regards the disposal of these
funds when finally determined the
Treasurer and Controller proposed
that the latter amount ($54,000)
which was in the nature of fees
collected without risk of loss to the
Council, be transferred direct to
municipal relief funds to augment
those which had been derived from
the Entertainment Voluntary Levy
to be used for direct measures of
refugee relief.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年2月17日
01787
本地米况据报令人满意
妥善处理因敌对行动产生的微妙局势，所得收益覆盖成本并为租界难民救济提供利润

在最近召开的米业联合管理委员会会议上，审查了本地米市状况。估计上海库存约为90万包（zars），一月份平均每日到货量约为1万包（zars）。
法租界的库存估计为9.6万袋，在十二月和一月期间增加了3万袋。
运往上海的大米稳定流入，仅因向上游地区采购以运往北方港口而受到轻微影响，人们认为总体局势无需担忧。
委员会获悉，自十一月底上次会议以来，当时储备量为10,606袋的工部局储备粮已全部周转，以降低变质风险，并已售出那些出现受损迹象的数量。剩余余额为6,156袋，鉴于上述城市库存状况令人满意，根据司库兼总监的建议，委员会一致批准立即处置这一余额，考虑到现有的安全裕度，该余额被视为微不足道。

采购结果
司库兼总监向委员会提交了关于工部局在西贡大米交易中最终结果的估算。据悉，共处理了22,740吨大米，预计最终贷方余额约为28万美元；此外，还有一笔5.4万美元的款项，这是向若干进口商收取的费用，这些进口商在工部局决定不再为自己账户进行采购后，安排了后续装运，这些装运在所有方面均受同样的监督和控制措施约束。

关于这些资金最终确定后的处置问题，司库兼总监提议，将后者金额（5.4万美元），其性质为收取的费用且工部局无亏损风险，直接转入市政救济基金，以增加从娱乐自愿捐税中获得的用于直接难民救济措施的资金。

CHINA PRESS.

JAN 22 1930

Nippon Daily
Appeals For
Wheat Tariff

Immediate adoption of a protective wheat tariff policy by the "Reformed Government" as a measure against alleged maneuvers of Chinese flour-manufacturers and foreign merchants was urged by the Nippon Shimpō in an editorial yesterday.

Under the heading "Imported Wheat Should Be Taxed," the editorial charged that the prevailing system of exemption of wheat from taxation, has led Chinese flour manufacturers in the International Settlement and the French Concession of Shanghai, in co-operation with foreign merchants, to import large quantities of cheap wheat from the United States and Australia. By this action, they are driving Chinese agricultural villages to poverty, the paper alleged.

"This problem is too serious," went on the editorial, "to be disposed of under the excuse that such activities are temporary because of the scarcity of wheat on the market and that it is based upon a purely economic reason that comparatively cheap material is available for production.

"If we study how far such an attitude on the part of Chinese and foreign business men concerned will go in its destructive effects," further said the editorial, "we cannot overlook the fact that a political motive underlies their actions."

《大美晚报》。

1930年1月22日

日本日报
呼吁征收
小麦关税

《日本新报》（Nippon Shimpō）昨日在一篇社论中敦促“维新政府”立即采取保护性小麦关税政策，作为对抗所谓中国面粉制造商和外国商人策略的措施。

在以“进口小麦应征税”为标题的社论中，该报指责现行的小麦免税制度导致上海公共租界和法租界的中国面粉制造商与外国商人合作，从美国和澳大利亚进口大量廉价小麦。该报称，通过这一行动，他们正使中国农村陷入贫困。

社论继续说道：“这个问题太严重了，不能以‘此类活动是因市场小麦短缺而产生的暂时现象’以及‘基于纯粹的经济原因，即可以获得相对廉价的原材料进行生产’为借口来处理。”

社论进一步说道：“如果我们研究有关中外商人的这种态度在其破坏性影响方面会走多远，我们就不能忽视这样一个事实，即他们的行动背后隐藏着政治动机。”

January 19, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

LOCAL PORK BUTCHERS REFUSE TO JOIN PORK MARKET

Most pigs brought to Shanghai are from
Tungchow, Chinkiang, Zongohow and Wusih. Owing to
financial difficulties, the Japanese are collecting a
tax of more than $1 on every pig transported to Shanghai.
A similar tax will be levied in a few days along the ports
north of the Yangtsze. The price of pork in Shanghai
has thus gone up.
In order to control the pork trade in
Shanghai, the Japanese and the puppet authorities intend
to establish a pork market in the neighbourhood of Tinghai
Bridge (定海桥), Yungtszepoo. Local pork shops,
knowing their trickery, are refusing to join the market,
while the Pork Shop Trade Association is warning its
members not to join.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

本地猪肉摊贩拒绝加入猪肉市场

运抵上海的大多数生猪来自通州、镇江、宗孝（音译，Zongohow）和无锡。由于财政困难，日本人对每头运往上海的生猪征收超过1美元的税款。几天后，长江以北的各港口也将征收类似的税款。因此，上海的猪肉价格上涨。
为了控制上海的猪肉贸易，日本人和伪政权当局打算在杨树浦定海桥附近建立一个猪肉市场。本地猪肉店识破其诡计，拒绝加入该市场，而猪肉店同业公会也警告其会员不要加入。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JAN 20 1939

Japanese May Start
Pig Market
Chinese Dealers Refuse to
Co-operate

Besides the Fish Market which is controlling the fishing industry in Shanghai, the Japanese are now reported to be interested in the establishment of a pig market in Tinghai Chiao, Yangtszepoo, but Chinese work dealers in town are stated to have started a movement against the project.
Officials of the Shanghai Pork Dealers Association have been approached by middlemen who persuaded them to participate in the proposed market but they have refused the proposal. Members of the Association are mutually checking each other against becoming a member of the new market, it is stated.
Inconvenience of communications resulting from the hostilities plus the allegedly extorbitant taxes collected by the Japanese and "puppet" officials have already caused an increase of the price of pork. The "transportation" tax for a pig transported to Shanghai from the interior now amounts to more than $1.
Foreshadowing a further increase, it is stated that the new tax will soon be collected in districts in Kiangsu on the northern bank of the Yangtze where most of the pigs for the Shanghai people come from.
Tungchow, Jukao and Tsingkiang in Kiangsu export pigs to Shanghai with Chingkiang, Changchow and Wusih coming next in importance in that respect.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，

1939年1月20日

日本人可能启动
生猪市场
中国商贩拒绝
合作

据报道，除了控制上海渔业的水产市场外，日本人现在也有兴趣在杨树浦定海桥建立生猪市场，但据称市内的中国中间商已发起反对该项目的运动。
上海猪肉商协会的官员曾受到中间人的接洽，劝说他们参与拟议中的市场，但他们拒绝了这一提议。据说，协会成员之间相互监督，防止有人成为新市场的成员。
因敌对行动导致的交通不便，加上据称由日本人和“伪”官员征收的高额税款，已经导致猪肉价格上涨。目前，从内地运往上海的一头生猪的“运输”税已超过1美元。
预示着价格将进一步上涨，据悉，不久将在江苏省长江北岸的地区征收新税，上海市民所需的大多数生猪都来自那里。
江苏的通州、如皋和靖江向上海出口生猪，其次是镇江、常州和无锡。

December 17, 1938.
Morning Translation

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE EXPORTATION OF RICE

Local rice merchants have requested the S.M.C.
to ask the Customs to permit the exportation of rice.
Several rice merchants requested the Customs to allow the
exportation on presentation of the permits issued by the
Council, but the request was rejected by the Japanese
Commissioner of the Customs.
On December 16, Mr. Yu Ya-ching, a Chinese
member of the S.M.C., made the following statement to a
reporter of the Hsien Tai News Agency (現代電訊社):- "The
ban placed by the Customs on the exportation of rice is
due entirely to orders from the Ministry of Finance of
the National Government. The report that the Japanese
authorities are preventing the exportation is not true.
As the highest administrative organ in the International
Settlement, the S.M.C. is naturally paying close attention
to the food supplies of the people. The right to permit
or to refuse the exportation of rice is vested with the
Customs and in this the S.M.C. cannot interfere. There-
fore, the Council has no desire to express any views on
the question."
The Bean and Rice Trade Association held a
meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday and passed the following
resolution :-
"A permit is required from the French Municipal
Council for the exportation of rice from the French
Concession.(The transportation of rice from the French
Concession to the International Settlement also requires
a permit).
"Resolved that a letter be sent to the French
Municipal Council requesting that no permit be required for
the transportation of rice from the French Concession to
the International Settlement."

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

大米出口

本地米商请求工部局要求海关允许大米出口。
几名米商请求海关凭工部局签发的许可证允许出口，但该请求被日本籍税务司拒绝。
12月16日，工部局华董俞亚清先生向现代电讯社记者发表如下声明：“海关禁止大米出口完全是由于国民政府财政部的命令。关于日本当局阻止出口的报道不实。作为公共租界最高行政机构，工部局自然密切关注民众的食品供应。许可或拒绝大米出口的权利属于海关，工部局对此无法干涉。因此，工部局无意就此问题发表任何意见。”
米豆业同业公会于昨日下午3时举行会议，并通过以下决议：-
“从法租界出口大米需要获得法国公董局的许可。（将大米从法租界运往公共租界也需要许可证）。
“决议致函法国公董局，请求免除将大米从法租界运往公共租界所需的许可证。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOV 30 1938

Food Supplies Are
Adequate
Record Deposit in Chilling
Rooms Last Month; Markets
In Hongkew Improve

Shanghai's food situation during October is given considerable attention in the monthly report of the Commissioner of Public Health which reveals the constant supervision maintained by the Department.

Interesting figures regarding the increasing use of the chilling rooms for food storage are given in the report. Admissions for chilling totalled 536,999 lb., as compared with 320,316 lb., for September an increase of 216,683 lb. From beginning of 1938 to date 2,667,211 lb. have passed through the chilling rooms.

Admissions of meat for freezing and cold storage during October amounted to 502,352 lb., as compared with 402,695 lb., for September or an increase of 99,657 lb. Withdrawals totalled 513,512 lb. From the beginning of the year to date, 3,287,588 lb. of meat have been admitted. October's deposit of 502,352 lb. is a record figure.

Milk Supplies

The average daily milk production was 27,965 lb., an increase of 5.77 per cent. and 41.22 per cent. over the figures for September and the corresponding month of last year respectively. The daily production of cream was 220 lb., as compared with 215 lb., for last month, an increase of 2.33 per cent. The number of unsatisfactory samples was 14.93 per cent. (includes three unlicensed), as compared to 26.67 per cent. for last month and 38.44 per cent. for the corresponding month of last year. All Grade "A" (TT) samples were up to standard and only one Grade "A" was below. Grade "B" milk also showed improvement though not to the same extent as the higher grades. Unlicensed samples continued to be 100 per cent., unsatisfactory.

Anthrax caused three deaths, contagious pleuro-pneumonia three, pneumonia one, metritis one, tuberculosis three, panaritium one and other causes 11, making a total of 23. 23 post-mortems were carried out.

Abattoir Figures

A total of 2,853 food animals were slaughtered comprising 894 oxen, 1,909 pigs and 50 horses. A total of 10 carcases, all pork, were rejected. The total number of pigs killed in the two slaughterhouses situated at Chengtu Road amounted to 37,762 an increase of more than 50 per cent. over the corresponding month last year. A total of 23 carcases were rejected. Additional electrical stunners were installed to cope with the increased activities.

The number of pigs imported in October was 47,990 as compared with 32,795 for September, 42,974 for August, 24,551 for July, 31,091 for June and 23,041 for May. Pigs dead on arrival this month numbered 395 (0.725 per cent.) as compared with 525 for September (0.994 per cent.), and 842 for August (1.959 per cent.). 80 moribund and injured pigs were shot on the Bund to prevent suffering. The average price of pork live-weight during October was 27.5 cents a cattie.

Main items of other importations were: Oxen 2,519, goats 6,627, buffalo 568, fowl 3,800 baskets, eggs 32,970 baskets, sea food 6,927 tubs, rice 197,015 bags, wheat 65,733 bags, vegetables 9,164 bags, salt pork 1,296 bags, ground nuts 1,208 bags, beans 21,011 bags, lard 873 tins, wine 1,167 jars, cotton 78,494 bales, cocoons 8,739 bales, peppermint oil 1,114 tins.

The system of fining is having the desired effect, as shippers are conforming more to Department requirements than hitherto. Inspection of 584 boats was carried out during the month, an increase of eight over that of last month. Four new applications for transportation permits were received and approved.

Market Conditions

In the Northern district, the major business is being carried on in the Hongkew Market where the Chinese are daily showing their confidence in conditions by their rapid return to business there. The North Fokien, Purdon and Elgin Road markets are also showing some improvement in trading conditions. The only two markets operating in the Eastern district are the Pingliang Road and Sungpan Road markets. Of these two, Pingliang Road market is handling the larger volume of trade, and conditions in this market are becoming daily more normal. The main market business is still, however, controlled by those markets located in the Central and Western districts.

Food supplies remain adequate and of excellent quality, though prices remain abnormally high due to the particular conditions which exist these days. Supplies of frozen fish have considerably augmented those of fresh fish. Flour and rice supplies remain satisfactory.

The iced suckers and cold drinks hawked in previous months with so much potential danger to public health have now, due to the colder weather, disappeared entirely.
page_data.zh:
00239

《字林西报》，
1938年11月30日

食品供应充足
上月冷藏库入库量创纪录；虹口市场情况好转

公共卫生处处长在月度报告中对上海十月份的食品状况给予了极大关注，报告揭示了该部门持续的监管工作。

报告中提供了关于食品冷藏库使用量增加的有趣数据。冷藏入库总量为536,999磅，而九月份为320,316磅，增加了216,683磅。从1938年初至今，经由冷藏库的食品总量已达2,667,211磅。

十月份冷冻及冷藏肉类的入库量为502,352磅，而九月份为402,695磅，增加了99,657磅。出库总量为513,512磅。从年初至今，肉类入库总量为3,287,588磅。十月份502,352磅的入库量创下了纪录。

牛奶供应

日均牛奶产量为27,965磅，分别比九月份和去年同月的数字增长了5.77%和41.22%。奶油日产量为220磅，而上个月为215磅，增长了2.33%。不合格样本占比为14.93%（包括三个无证样本），而上个月为26.67%，去年同月为38.44%。所有“A”级（TT）样本均符合标准，仅有一个“A”级样本低于标准。“B”级牛奶也有所改善，尽管程度不如较高等级。无证样本继续保持100%不合格。

炭疽病导致3人死亡，传染性胸膜肺炎3人，肺炎1人，子宫炎1人，肺结核3人，瘭疽1人，其他原因11人，共计23人。进行了23次尸检。

屠宰场数据

共屠宰食用动物2,853头，其中包括牛894头，猪1,909头，马50匹。共有10具 carcasses（胴体）被拒收，均为猪肉。位于成都路的两家屠宰场共屠宰猪37,762头，比去年同月增加了50%以上。共有23具胴体被拒收。为了应对增加的业务量，安装了额外的电击晕设备。

十月份进口猪的数量为47,990头，而九月份为32,795头，八月份为42,974头，七月份为24,551头，六月份为31,091头，五月份为23,041头。本月运抵时已死亡的猪数量为395头（0.725%），而九月份为525头（0.994%），八月份为842头（1.959%）。80头垂死和受伤的猪在外滩被枪决，以防止其遭受痛苦。十月份生猪平均价格为每斤27.5分。

其他主要进口项目包括：牛2,519头，山羊6,627只，水牛568头，家禽3,800篮，鸡蛋32,970篮，海产品6,927桶，大米197,015袋，小麦65,733袋，蔬菜9,164袋，咸肉1,296袋，花生1,208袋，豆类21,011袋，猪油873听，酒1,167坛，棉花78,494包，蚕茧8,739包，薄荷油1,114听。

罚款制度正在产生预期效果，因为发货人比以往更遵守部门的要求。本月检查了584艘船只，比上个月增加了八艘。收到并批准了四份新的运输许可证申请。

市场状况

在北区，主要业务在虹口市场进行，中国人通过迅速恢复那里的营业，每日显示出他们对局势的信心。北福建路、蒲登路（Purdon Road）和爱尔近路（Elgin Road）市场的交易状况也有所改善。东区仅有的两个运营市场是平凉路市场和嵩山路（Sungpan Road）市场。在这两个市场中，平凉路市场的交易量较大，该市场的状况日益正常化。然而，主要的市场业务仍由位于中区和西区的市场所控制。

食品供应依然充足且质量优良，尽管由于目前的特殊状况，价格仍然异常高。冻鱼的供应量大增，超过了鲜鱼。面粉和大米的供应令人满意。

前几个月兜售的、对公众健康具有巨大潜在危险的冰棒和冷饮，现在由于天气变冷，已完全消失。

THE EXPORTATION OF RICE

The Association has decided to co-operate with
the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Shanghai Maritime
Customs and the authorities of the Foreign Settlements to
regulate the food supplies for local consumption and for
exportation. As to the date for the resumption of
exportation, it will be fixed after arrangements have been
made with the authorities concerned.
Meanwhile, the representatives submitted
the following letter to the Foreign Councils :-
"On November 9, this Association sent you a
letter giving reasons why the exportation of rice should be
resumed and a set of measures governing exportation. As
these measures seem incomplete, we submit the following
points for your consideration :-
(1) Reason for the Exportation of Rice:
Owing to the good weather this autumn, bumper
harvests have been gathered. At present, there are
about 500,000 bags of rice stored in Shanghai. As the
autumn crop is arriving in ample quantities, there need
be no fear for a shortage. Exportation, therefore,
will not affect the food supplies for Shanghai.
(2) The Price of Rice:
Some time ago, this Association limited the price
of best quality rice to $14 per picul and decided that
exportation is to be suspended when the price exceeds
the limit. The exportation of rice will be limited
to 100,000 bags a month and for the month of November,
50,000 bags only will be allowed to be exported. The
price of rice will be limited as before.
(3) Request for Permits:
The Association some time ago made a suggestion
that any person desiring to export rice must produce
documents issued by the Chamber of Commerce or other
proper bodies with a guarantee from other rice dealers.
The Association requests the Council to issue to this
Association every month permits for the exportation of
rice for distribution among rice merchants. It is
requested that each permit be made to cover 500 bags
of rice; thus for the 100,000 bags of rice each month,
200 permits will be required. For the month of
November, 100 permits will be required. With these
permits and the certificates of this Association, the
Customs authorities will then be requested to authorize
the exportation.
(4) Passes Should Be Abolished:
Since the quantity of rice to be exported is
limited and a permit is required, the Association
requests that the application for passes should be
abolished as it is very troublesome. The Association
will submit to the Council every fortnight a report
on the arrivals and sales of rice.

803719/5
21 11 3

1938年11月18日。晨间译稿。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

大米出口

昨日下午3时，上海豆米业同业公会会员朱子香（Tsu Ts-shiang）和陈子义（Chen Ts-yee）拜访了工部局和法公董局，讨论从上海出口大米的问题。
该公会决定与华人总商会、上海海关税务司署以及租界当局合作，调节供本地消费和出口的食品供应。至于恢复出口的日期，将在与有关当局作出安排后确定。
与此同时，代表们向外国市政机构提交了以下信函：
“本公会于11月9日致函贵方，说明了应恢复大米出口的理由以及一套管理出口的措施。鉴于这些措施似乎不完善，我们提出以下几点供贵方考虑：
(1) 大米出口的理由：
由于今年秋季天气良好，获得了丰收。目前，上海储存的大米约有50万袋。由于秋粮大量上市，无需担心短缺。因此，出口不会影响上海的食品供应。
(2) 大米价格：
不久前，本公会限制上等大米的价格为每担14元，并决定当价格超过此限额时暂停出口。大米出口量限制为每月10万袋，十一月份仅允许出口5万袋。大米价格将像以前一样受到限制。
(3) 申请许可证：
本公会不久前建议，任何希望出口大米的人必须出示由商会或其他适当机构签发的文件，并由其他米商提供担保。本公会请求市政机构每月向本公会签发大米出口许可证，以便分发给米商。请求每份许可证涵盖500袋大米；因此，对于每月10万袋大米，需要200份许可证。对于十一月份，需要100份许可证。凭这些许可证和本公会的证明，将请求海关当局批准出口。
(4) 应废除通行证：
由于出口大米的数量有限且需要许可证，本公会请求废除通行证申请，因为这非常麻烦。本公会每两周向市政机构提交一份关于大米到货和销售情况的报告。

page_data.en:
(5) The Council Requested to Write to the Customs:
The Council is requested to write to the Customs
as soon as an application for the exportation of rice
attached with a permit from the Council and also
a certificate from this Association has been granted.
The Council is requested to consider and
approve the above points without delay.
page_data.zh:
(5) 请求市政机构致函海关：
一旦批准附带市政机构许可证以及本公会证明的大米出口申请，即请求市政机构尽快致函海关。
请求市政机构毫不迟延地审议并批准上述各点。

page_data.en:
November 18, 1938.
Afternoon Translation

Shanghai Daily News (上海日報), a mosquito newspaper :-

EXPORTATION OF RICE : ASSOCIATION AND MERCHANTS DENOUNCED

Recently the authorities of the Shanghai
Maritime Customs frustrated a great plot of the Bean and
Rice Trade Association by refusing to lift the ban on the
exportation of rice.
About ten days ago the price of rice in
Shanghai suddenly rose to about $13 per picul following
the request made by rice merchants for the resumption of
exportation of Chinese rice. Enquiries show that most
of the Chinese rice intended for exportation is to be
transported to North China where the price of rice, as in
Peiping and Tientsin, is about $20 per picul. The real
object of the rice merchants is to manipulate the local
rice market in the hope of making large profits. Their
attempt, should it succeed, will have serious consequences
on the local food problem. Fortunately, the Customs
authorities saw through their intrigues and have
resolutely rejected the request of the rice merchants.
The Bean and Rice Trade Association has
spared no effort to help the rice merchants in securing
permission to export the rice and the affair cannot escape
the attention of intelligent people. It is a shame that
a few members of the local press should have been deceived
into willingly working in favour of the scheme. The "Sing
Sung News Agency" (新声通訊社), which has been misleading
the readers of various newspapers by false reports, openly
alleged on November 16 that the Customs authorities had
rejected the request at the instigation of the puppet
Customs Superintendent and spoke in favour of the rice
merchants. Its object in making such mad statements is
not known.
page_data.zh:
1938年11月18日。
午后译稿

《上海日报》，一家小型报纸：-

大米出口：谴责公会与商人

最近，上海海关税务司署通过拒绝解除大米出口禁令，挫败了豆米业同业公会的一个大阴谋。
大约十天前，在米商要求恢复中国大米出口后，上海米价突然涨至每担约13元。调查显示，大部分拟出口的中国大米将运往华北，那里如北平和天津的米价约为每担20元。米商的真正目的是操纵本地大米市场，以期获取巨额利润。他们的企图如果得逞，将对本地粮食问题产生严重后果。幸运的是，海关当局看穿了他们的诡计，坚决拒绝了米商的请求。
豆米业同业公会不遗余力地帮助米商获得大米出口许可，此事逃不过明智之士的关注。令人羞愧的是，本地新闻界的少数成员被欺骗，自愿为该计划效劳。“新声通讯社”一直通过虚假报道误导各家报纸的读者，于11月16日公然声称海关当局是在傀儡海关税务司的唆使下拒绝了请求，并为米商说话。其发表此类疯狂言论的目的尚不清楚。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
NOV 17 1938

Rice Dealers
Revise Rules
For Exports

Because local Maritime Custom.
authorities refused to lift the em-
bargo on the export of domestic
rice, regulations for interport trade
were revised by the Shanghai Rice
Dealers' Association supervisors
committee members yesterday after-
noon.

It was believed that the authori-
ties rejected the export request
owing to the local food problem, and
the association decided yesterday
to reduce the amount of rice to be
exported from 200,000 to 100,000
bags per month. For the month of
November, the Association will ask
for the export of only 5,000 bags.

It was reported during the meet-
ing yesterday that in principle the
Customs authorities consented to the
export of domestic rice but sug-
gested a limit. Representatives of
the association will make further
negotiations today with the au-
thorities.

It was decided that if interport
exportation is granted the As-
sociation will submit a detailed
report to the Customs authorities
every fortnight on the amount of
the stock exported and its destina-
tion.

The relief levy of one cent for
every bag of rice exported was
increased to five cents, it was de-
cided in the meeting yesterday, and
if the local price of first grade rice
reaches $14 per picul, the old em-
bargo will be enforced again.

（批：File 5/8 R.G. 18/11）
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》
1938年11月17日

米商
修订出口规则

由于本地海关当局拒绝解除对国产大米出口的禁令，上海米业同业公会监理委员会成员于昨日下午修订了埠际贸易法规。

据信，当局因本地粮食问题而拒绝了出口请求，公会昨日决定将每月出口大米数量从20万袋减少到10万袋。对于十一月份，公会将只申请出口5,000袋。

据报在昨日的会议上，海关当局原则上同意出口国产大米，但建议设定限额。公会代表将于今日与当局进行进一步谈判。

会议决定，如果获准进行埠际出口，公会每两周向海关当局提交一份详细报告，说明出口库存数量及其目的地。

会议昨日决定，将每袋出口大米的救济捐从一分增加到五分，如果一级大米的本地价格达到每担14元，将再次执行旧的禁令。

（批注：档案 5/8 R.G. 18/11）

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
NOV 4 1938
Price Of Local
Domestic Rice
Hits New Low
Rice Dealers To Hold
General Meeting ,
Next Week

With the appearance on the local
market of domestic rice of the final
harvest of the year, the Shanghai
Rice Dealers' Association will hold
a general meeting next week to dis-
cuss the local rice situation and the
control of rice export, it was learn-
ed yesterday.
Several months ago, in early
August, fear was entertained by
local rice dealers that Shanghai
would face a shortage of rice for
the winter, but this is now found
untrue.
Favorable weather conditions
have resulted in the prosperous
harvest of the crop grown in the
near interior, especially Wusih and
Changshu. Because of the large
consignments of rice shipped from
these two rice producing centers to
Shanghai within the past few
weeks, local prices of domestic rice
are hitting a new low.

Price Drop Felt

This major drop was especially
felt about a fortnight ago when
Wusih rice, formerly selling $12 per
shih (approximately 160 catties)
dropped to $9.80. Now this rice is
selling at $11.60. THE CHINA PRESS
learned from a well-known rice
dealer yesterday.
Changshu rice, which sold for $12
in August, was reported again sell-
ing at this price, after a drop to
$11.40 about two weeks ago, it was
learned.
Because of the comparatively
small rice supply this year, China
has been importing a considerable
amount of the crop from abroad,
especially from Saigon, Siam and
Annam.

Imports Increase

While during the first 10 months
of last year, China only imported
$33,134,387 worth of foreign rice, the
imports of rice for this year's cor-
responding period show a steep in-
crease, amounting to $110,282,253,
Chinese papers reported yesterday.
Of late, however, by virtue of the
policy of the National Government
in the control of international
trade, the imports of rice have de-
clined. In the first season of the
year, the imports amounted to
$27,938,993; in the second season it
swelled to $56,516,956, while in the
third season it dropped again to
$25,826,344, the reports added.
At the impending meeting the
Shanghai Rice Dealers' Association
will discuss the possibility of ex-
porting domestic rice to Chinese
ports which has hitherto been pro-
hibited by the Association as a
means to control the local rice
situation.
A date will be definitely set for
the commencement of exporting
domestic rice to Chinese ports in
the coming meeting, it was reported.

（批：P
Xie
8/11）
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
1938年11月4日
国产米价
创新低
米商将于
下周召开大会

据悉，随着本年度最后一季收获的国产米出现在本地市场，上海米业公会将于下周召开全体大会，讨论本地米市情况及大米出口管制事宜。
数月前，即8月初，本地米商曾担心上海将面临冬季缺米局面，但现已证实此虑不实。
得益于有利的天气条件，邻近内地尤其是无锡和常熟的作物丰收。由于过去几周内从这两个大米产地运抵上海的大批米货，本地国产米价正创下新低。

感受到的价格下跌

据《字林西报》昨日从一位知名米商处获悉，这一大幅下跌在约两周前尤为明显，当时无锡米从前每石（约合160斤）售价12美元跌至9.80美元。目前该米售价为11.60美元。
据悉，常熟米8月份售价为12美元，约两周前曾跌至11.40美元，据报道目前又回升至12美元。
由于今年大米供应相对较少，中国一直从国外进口大量大米，尤其是来自西贡、暹罗和安南的大米。

进口增加

据中文报纸昨日报道，去年前10个月，中国仅进口价值33,134,387美元的外国大米，而今年同期的大米进口量显示急剧增加，总额达110,282,253美元。
然而，近期由于国民政府实施国际贸易管制政策，大米进口量有所下降。报道补充称，今年第一季进口额为27,938,993美元；第二季激增至56,516,956美元；第三季则再次降至25,826,344美元。
在即将召开的会议上，上海米业公会将讨论向其他中国港口出口国产米的可能性，此前公会为控制本地米市情况一直禁止此类出口。
据报道，在即将到来的会议上，将确定开始向其他中国港口出口国产米的具体日期。

（批：P
谢
8/11）

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
OCT 20 1938

Rice Prices
Record Major
Drop Locally

Because of the large consignments of rice shipped from the interior to Shanghai within the past week, local prices of domestic rice are hitting new lows, the Ta Wan Pao reported last night.

Wusih rice, which used to sell $12 per shih (equivalent to about 160 catties), is reported selling $9.80, while the Changshu rice has dropped from $12 to $11.40 per shih.

Until recently it was feared by many here that Shanghai would be short of rice for the next few months. Local dealers were reported to have petitioned the Chinese Government to permit them to import rice from abroad.

Last Thursday, as many as 6,000 bags of rice were shipped here from Changshu and Wusih, two rice-producing centers. More quantities of the crop were reported to have arrived here last Friday and Saturday.

Earlier Chinese reports stated that local rice trade has thrived since the hostilities. The number of rice dealers has increased from 1,700— to about 2,700, it was reported. Daily consumption has also increased from 8,000 to more than 9,000 shih.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
1938年10月20日

米价
本地录得
大幅下跌

据《大晚报》昨晚报道，由于过去一周内从内地运抵上海的大批米货，本地国产米价正创下新低。
据报道，无锡米从前每石（约合160斤）售价12美元，现售价为9.80美元，而常熟米已从每石12美元跌至11.40美元。
直到最近，本地许多人仍担心上海在未来几个月会出现米荒。据报道，本地米商已请愿中国政府允许他们从国外进口大米。
上周四，多达6,000袋大米从两个产米中心常熟和无锡运抵此地。据报道，上周五和周六又有更多大米运抵此地。
早前的中文报道称，自战事爆发以来，本地米业繁荣。据报道，米商数量已从1,700家增加至约2,700家。每日消费量也从8,000石增加至9,000多石。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,
SEP 2 4 1938
No Shortage
Of Food For
This Winter
Areas Of Supply Being
Opened Up At Many
Points Inland
SHANTUNG BEEF FOUND
IN LARGE QUANTITY
A plentiful supply of food-stuffs of all kinds will be available in Shanghai during the coming winter, it is reported. The opinion is also expressed that prices will remain steady and that no marked increase over those prevailing at present may be expected.
It is understood that with the return of more or less normal conditions to certain areas in China upon which Shanghai is dependent for its supply of foodstuffs, the situation is much better as a whole than it was last year. According to Mr. P. Veidt, Superintendent of Markets, meat is now being brought here from the vicinity of Nanking as well as from Shantung.
The principal source of supply for beef is Shantung and anything which tends to disrupt normal shipments is likely to create a serious shortage here. It is therefore of considerable importance that cattle are being sent from some of the most productive areas in the province.
With regard to the supply of fruit and vegetables, it stated that farmers in this area have been able to get large quantities of produce into the foreign areas. Large quantities of fruit have also been brought over from Japan, especially pears, apples and grapes.
The only difficulty in this connection is the fact that the prices for Japanese fruit are rising rapidly, possibly due to the fact that the demand is very heavy this year from the army in China. An abundant supply of apples has been shipped from Chefoo to Shanghai this year and Korean apples have also proven especially good.
Supply of Rice
Japanese onions are arriving almost by the shipload and are said to be finding a very good market in Shanghai. There is also a boom in bananas in Shanghai at the present time, it being estimated that from 10 to 13 tons are arriving daily. Most of the bananas are being brought in from Singapore and Manila, the first class "fig" variety coming from the latter port.
It is stated that there is also a very large supply of fish available and incoming boats have been so well-loaded that the cold-storage godowns are now filled up. There is no fear of a shortage of pork as an adequate supply from Nantung continues to be available, and, what is perhaps most important, there is little likelihood of a rice shortage.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，
1938年9月24日
今冬
食物无虞
内陆多处
供应区正在开放
发现大量
山东牛肉

据报道，上海在今冬期间将有充足的各种食品供应。另有观点认为，物价将保持稳定，预计不会出现较当前水平显著上涨的情况。
据悉，随着上海赖以获取食品供应的中国某些地区状况恢复大致正常，整体局势比去年大为改善。据市场主管 P. Veidt 先生称，目前肉类正从南京附近以及山东运抵此地。
牛肉的主要供应来源是山东，任何可能扰乱正常运输的因素都可能导致此地出现严重短缺。因此，从该省一些最高产的地区运送牛只至此具有相当重要的意义。
关于水果和蔬菜的供应，报道称该地区的农民已能够将大量农产品运入租界区域。大量水果也从日本运来，尤其是梨、苹果和葡萄。
在此方面的唯一困难在于，日本水果的价格迅速上涨，这可能是由于今年在华日军的需求非常旺盛所致。今年已有大量苹果从烟台运抵上海，朝鲜苹果也被证明品质尤佳。

大米供应

日本洋葱几乎整船整船地运抵，据说在上海销路很好。目前上海的香蕉交易也十分兴旺，估计每天抵达10至13吨。大多数香蕉来自新加坡和马尼拉，其中一等“无花果”品种来自后者港口。
称鱼类供应也非常充足， incoming boats（入境船只）装载满满，以致冷藏仓库现已爆满。无需担心猪肉短缺，因为南通的供应持续充足，而且或许最重要的是，出现大米短缺的可能性很小。

page_data.en:
August 4, 1938.
Afternoon Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

MEETING OF BEAN AND RICE TRADE ASSOCIATION

With a view to regulating foodstuffs in
Shanghai, the local Bean and Rice Trade Association
recently strictly prohibited the exportation of Chinese
rice, while efforts were made to facilitate the arrival
of rice supplies in Shanghai. As difficulties are being
experienced in transporting rice to Shanghai due to the
blockade of the surrounding districts by the Japanese,
the price of rice is gradually rising and has reached
the limit of $14 per picul.
The Association held an urgent meeting at
3 p.m. yesterday in the office of the Cereal Trade
Association on Avenue Edward VII, which was attended by
14 members of its Executive and Supervisory Committees
and was presided over by Mr. Ying Ts-kong (邢志剛).
Investigations made by an official of the
Association revealed that there are about 400,000 bags
of rice in stock in Shanghai, comprising of 196,000 bags
of Chinese held by rice shops, 50,000 bags of Saigon rice
and about 200,000 bags of rice stored by private individuals.
The supplies of rice from the interior are scarce, but they
have not been totally cut off; therefore, for the time
being there is no cause for alarm.
The meeting resolved to appeal to the S.M.C.
and the F.M.C. to continue to order rice from Saigon and
to reject requests to extend the price limit as it is
unwarranted.
page_data.zh:
1938年8月4日。
下午译件

《标准报》及其他本地报纸：-

豆米同业公会会议

为规范上海食品供应，本地豆米同业公会近期严禁国产大米出口，同时努力促进大米供应运抵上海。由于日军封锁周边地区，导致向上海运输大米遇到困难，米价逐渐上涨，已达到每担14美元的限价。
公会于昨日下午3时在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）粮业同业公会办公室召开紧急会议，其执行委员会和监察委员会共14名成员出席，由邢志剛（Ying Ts-kong）先生主持。
经公会官员调查，上海现有库存大米约40万袋，其中包括米店持有的19.6万袋国产米、5万袋西贡米以及私人储存的约20万袋大米。内地大米供应虽稀缺，但并未完全断绝；因此，目前无需恐慌。
会议决议呼吁工部局（S.M.C.）和法公董局（F.M.C.）继续从西贡订购大米，并拒绝提高限价的请求，因为此举毫无理由。

REASONS FOR THE HIGH PRICE OF RICE 


Due to the unreasonably rapid increase in the 
price of rice during the past few days, the question of 
rice supplies to local residents will again become as 
serious as it was two months ago. This is svidently 
due to manipulation and hoarding on the part of certain 
elements and it is deemed necessary that investigations 
Should be made and punishment be meted out upon such 
elements. 

The following information has been secured by 
the Dah Chung News Agency ( _ Wt )t- 

At this time when the S.M.C. and various local 
authoritative’ bédies are planning the construction of 
granaries for the storage of rice as a means to prevent 
a@ shortage of rice supplies in spring next year, the price 
of the "Kan Mee" has suddenly gone up to over $40 per 
picul during the past three or four days. This sharp 
increase in the price of rice is undoubtedly not due to 
obstruction or to shortage of stocks, as rice supplies 
are still pouring into Shanghai continuously from the 
suburban areas. Moreover, according to a high official 
of the S.M.C., there are at present at least 224,000 pniculs 
of rice in stock in Shanghai. It is therefore quite 
evident that the recent sharp increase in the price of rice 
is due to manipulation on the part of certain elements 
who are doing this purposely for the sake of profiteering. 

It is learned that with a view to preventing 
a shortage of rice supplies for residents as well as for 
the purpose of maintaining peace and order, the S.MeC. is 
making discreet enquiries into the actual facts responsible 
for this rapid increase and will take severe measures 
against such activities as soon as definite proof has been 
established. 

The authorities of the Foreign Settlements have 
been requested by the Citizens' Federation to pay special 
attention to such activities, while the Chamber of Commerce 
and the Rice Trade Guild have been asked by the local 
authoritative banking and industrial circles to take 
effective measures against activities of manipulation and 
hoarding so as to appease the anxiety of the public. It 
is hoped that by doing this the avarice for profits of the 
traitorous merchants will be somewhat checked. 


According to two local leading rice uwexchants, 
there is no explanation for the sudden rise of the price 
of rice during the past few days other than that of 
manipulation for profiteering on the part of certain 
elements. The reports that this increase is due to non- 
arrivals of rice and shortage of rice stocks or due to 
the shortage of rice supplies in Japan are simply intended 
to mislead the public. At present between seven and eight 
thousand bags of rice arrive in Shanghai every day, while 
the daily consumption in Shanghai is only 7,000 bags. 
Moreover, there are sufficient stocks of rice in Shanghai. 

In connection with the report that the Jap-nese 
are making purchases of rice in the interior, it will be 
noted that most of the purchases they make consist of the 
Wuhu "see-mee;" this in no way affects the rice supplies 
to Shanghai as the rice transported here from the regions 
along the Nanking-Shanghai Railway comprise mostly "kan-mee." 
It is, therefore, not difficult to see why there has 
prevailed a sharp rise in the price of rice of this c tegory. 

When asked by the reporter of the news agency 
about the truth of the rumour that a company had been 
established jointly by certain speculators with the object 
of undertaking large-scale manipulation of the rice mart, 
the two rice merchants replied that they were in ignorance 
but stated that the rice trading circles were now making 
discreet enquiries into this fact and were devising ways 
and means to put a stop to future trouble in connection 
with the question of rice supplies. 

It will be remembered that on November 19 a 
meeting was held by the Rice Mart Control Committee, at 
which it was resolved that efforts be made to prevent rice 
brokers from engaging in deliberate enhancement of the 
price of rice at the rice mart. This action on the part of 
the Committee has checked somewhat the activities of the 
unscrupulous elements. 

More than 7,000 bags of rice arrived here 
yesterday and, thanks to this, the price of all grades of 
"kan-mee" marked a drop of about $2 per picul yesterday, 
ig eg of the "see-mee" showed a decline of about $1.30 
per picul.

‘The Rice Shortage: 


A Correspondent’s Anxiety 


To the Editor of the 
“NortH-Curva Dany News" 

Six,—The recent rise in price of. 
rice has badly hit the already wretch- 
ed Chinese residents of this city, 
especially those of middle and lower 
classes. A picul of rice costing $36 
or so is) unprecedented and is cer- 
tainly beyond the averuge buying 


power of the man in the street. 

As we generally know, a great 
portion of the present Shanghai re- 
Sidents are refugees from the in- 
terior, These people have been fiv- 


ing either on their previous savings 
or by the support of their relatives 
or friends. That their conditions 
are pitiful is too well-known to 
need mentioning. Ever since the 
beginning of this year, a number of 
these people have been returning to 
their native towns on account of the 
nigh cost of living prevailing in this 
city, This exodus is observed to 
have come to its crowning point dur- 
ing the past several months. Ac-; 
cording to a recent report published 
{in the Jocal papers, the number of 
| residents in the International Settle- 
[ment and French Concession in 
[Shanghai has been reduced by one 
million since the beginning of this 
year and further reduction is ex- 
pected towards the end of current 
year, The huge reduction in number 
otf residents will probably give one 
some impression as to the seriousness , 
of the local economical condition. 

In this connection, it might as well 
be pointed out that residents in 
Hongkew and Yangtszepoo districts 
have been greatly increased since the 
beginning of this year. This is un- 
doubtedly due to the cheaper rent 
and lower price of daily necessities 
prevailing in these areas compared ' 
with those in the Settlement and! 
Concession. The reduction in num- 
ber of residents in the Settlement and 
Concession has given rise to some 
anxiety among the local business and 
financial circles. Business in general 
was flourishing last year. Some busi- 
nes is said to have reaped such a huge 
profit that they have had never en- 
-joyed before. Further, a considerable 
number of new shops have: sprung 
up last year to meet the increasing 
demand on the part of population. 

A contrast of conditions of current 
year to that of last leads one to 
worry very much about the future 
of this metropolis. As a sequel to 
the reduction of residents in the 
Settlement and Concession business 
firms are the first to suffer. The fall 
in value of Chinese dollars has in- 
‘creased the prices of various. com- 
modities to such a degree that they 
‘are, generally beyond the reach of 
working class. Among those the most 
laird hit one are, of course, the im-' 
port firms. Some import firms have |} 
practically no business to do since 
the fall of dollar,'and as the time is 
going on there seems no alternative 
| for them but to close up the business. 
Firms other than this category 
though are less. unfortunate, but the 
difference is only. in degree. 


The situation is aggravated by the 
recent rise in price of rice, which is 
the prelude to the general increase 
in price of practically every kind of 
commodity. With the exception of a 
few wealthy class, most people are 
unable to afford the sky-high price 
and are being in a state of disaster. 
Notwithstanding the pains we suffer, 
the prices of rice and other com- 
modities show no sign of dropping 
down: instead there is every pos- 
sibility of their going up. The 
ultimate result will be that there 
will be no buying power on the 
part of population to meet the 
high price. If the present situa- 
tion were allowed to continue 
unabated the time would not be long 
before the business world in Shang- 
hai come to a general depression, if 
not bankruptcy. 

In speaking of this, I have no in- 
tention to exaggerate the situation. I 
simply bring the grave situation to 
the notice of those responsible for 
the maintenance of peace and order 
of this city. I doubt if our City 
Fathers are giving due attention to 
this matter and devising ways and 
means to relieve the present string- 
ency. 

Li CHun.

the existing situation, and that every- 
thing possible will be done to alleviate , 
it, but it is necessary to remember 
that to find a solution is not likely to 
prove so easy as was the case of the 
rice shortage shortly after the out- 
break of hostilities.—Eb,

community. Rice has soared to over $40

factors behind the actual shortage of 
grain, but it must still be hoped that

difficulties will be overcome. If it is not 
the great fall in the exchange value of

ties. Owing to the crisis in Europe there

value which others are prepared to 


accept. 


When landlords, compradores, retail- 
fers, and public utility concerns which

say) it sounds not so bad, because we 
have always thought that that was about 
a fair figure. But the fact of the matter 
is that that workman or servant is getting

.becoming tragically ridiculous. What | 
jShanghai as a whole is faced with is the 
;necessity of general revision in terms of 
the dollar’s real worth. If we were all

so painfully experienced by others else-

for in terms of the dollar's current buying | 
capacity. As matters are, vast numbers j

ee which cannot persist for long |

While the politically minded — talk | 
Blibly about the “China situation.” the! 
actual conditions in Shanghai are giving 
rise to a great deal of anxiety to people 
on the spot. The report for May issued 
by the Industrial Section of the Shanghai 
Municipal Council shows the mounting 
cost of living and the growing plight of 
the workers. Tne further drop in. tiie 
value of the Chinese dollar, owing to the! 
withdrawal cf support by the Anglo- | 
Chinese Stubilization Fund, has struck an! 
additional blow at large numbers of | 
people in this town who are dependent 
upon the preservation of the value of the 
Chinese dollar at aw reasonable figure to 
make ends incet. The explanation given 
to Reuter in Hongkong by authoritative 
circles on the subject of this action is 
worthy of special note. It is to the effect 
that the “Control temporarily withdrew 
its support to allow the exchange value 
of the detlar to be adjusted to a better 
econom.c Jevel, and thereby bring the 
balance of trade into equilibrium.” “As 
will be vremerabered,” it goes on, “a 
similar step was taken in June, 1938, and 
when the level of cightpence was found, 
it was successfully maintained for a 
period of twelve months. It is confidently 
believed that a new level has now been 
found, and can be strongly maintained.” 
Some days must elapse, we presume, 
before that level is definitely known, but 
if it is to be little more than sixpence, it 
is obvious that there must be heavy losses 
on the part of many people in Shanghai. 
before things are readjusted for ordinary 
business purposes. Unfortunately, for 
many wage earners, both foreigners and 
Chinese, there is little hope of an early 
readjustment which will co. pensate for 
the very low level which the Chinese 
dollar now seems likely to take up. Even 
the poorest class of Chinese workers who 
do not buy any foreign goods cannot 
wholly escape, for reductions in the 
foreign exchange value of currencies of 
this nature must affect everyone 
ultimately and go right down to the 
lowest grades of society. There is little 
doubt that the prices of local goods and 
services will have to be raised consider- 
ably and that some time must elapse 
before business is able to feel at ease 
under a new set of conditions. Still 
“worse, however, is the uncertainty as to 
future developments, and particularly the 
fear that the dollar will decline further, 
even if it should be pegged again for 
a time by the Stabilization -Fund at 
‘around sixpence or sixpence-halfpenny. 
This fear is enhanced. by the realization 
that the British Government's Participa- 
tion in the Stabilization Fund is rather a 
gesture of goodwill to those who are 
working in China under adverse conditions 
than an obligation on the part of Great 
Britain. Only the conclusion of the’ 
| Sino-Japanese hostilities can, it seems to 
us,\ bring about conditions: ¢ conducive to 
real’ ‘health: in > commerce and a Sidley. 2H

continues to worry many of the less 
privileged people in Shanghai, the political 
situation also casts its shadow of anxiciy 
on the scene. The troubles in Pootung 
culminating in the death of Mr. R. M.

certainly not improved feeling betyeen

unprejudiced person reacts to all this

able by all parties. Of this, unfortunately,
